tom_tat: According to the book Luong Cao Tang Truyen, Ma Ha Ky Vuc was originally from Thien Truc. He went from Thien Truc to Funan (Cambodia), through Giao Chau...
noi_dung: 10. Mahajivaka (Mahajivaka)According to the book Luong Cao Tang Truyen, Ma Ha Ky Vuc was originally from Thien Truc. He went from Thien Truc to Funan (Cambodia), to Giao Chau (Vietnam), and then to Guangzhou at the end of the reign of Jin Hui De (290-306). One time, when he arrived at Tuong Duong, he wanted to get on a boat to cross the river. However, the boat owner saw that he was dressed in rags so he did not let him on. As soon as the boat arrived at the river wharf, he saw Him standing on the riverbank with two tigers. Everyone was horrified. From then on, many people followed him to study Buddhism. Coming to Luoyang, he used strange medical methods to cure incurable diseases, causing all patients to recover. Later, because of the war, he left Luoyang and returned to Thien Truc. In the book Co Chau Phap Van Buddha Bon Hanh Ngu Luc (a collection of stories about the history of Vietnamese Buddhism), Zen master Vien Chieu recorded: "During the time when Han Linh De ruled our country (Vietnam), there was a monk named Ky Vuc, leading a disciple named Khau Da La. Ky Vuc held a branch of poplar in his hand and went everywhere. Finally, he came to Luy Lau land. There, there was a monk who often practiced meditation. He invited his teacher and his disciples. Ky Vuc went home to rest. However, only Khau Da La stayed, while Ky Vuc continued to go east. After a month, Khau Da La also left. However, the other monk made a vow to practice Buddhism and stayed behind. Khau Da La often stood on one leg and chanted the sutras continuously for seven days In the west, there was a loud sound, so the group came to find it. Finally, they discovered a sutra book under a large tree (where Khau Da La often stood and recited sutras)."

tom_tat: Chi Khiem's ​​name is Cung Minh, nicknamed Viet, and comes from Dai Nhuc Chi country. During the reign of Emperor Lingdi of Han, his father led hundreds of people to the land of Han...
noi_dung:
11. Chi KhiemChi Khiem's ​​name is Cung Minh, nicknamed Viet, and comes from Dai Nhuc Chi country. During the reign of Emperor Lingdi of Han, his father led hundreds of people to the land of Han, and changed his name to Chi. Chi Khiem was originally a lay person. When he was ten years old, he studied the scriptures and had a sharper intelligence than others. At the age of thirteen, he studied Sanskrit books and became fluent in the languages ​​of six countries. During the reign of Emperor Ling of Han, his disciple Chi Sam, Chi Luong, went to Central Earth. Chi Khiem then followed Chi Luong to study Buddhism. At the end of the Eastern Han Dynasty, Chi Khiem fled to the country of Wu. I thought I would go to the south to take refuge, but I still encountered hardship. At that time, Chi Khiem and a few dozen compatriots went to Ngo land. They have to sleep on the road with blankets. In the group there was a guest; he didn't have a blanket to cover himself with. Seeing the cold weather, Chi Khiem called him over to cover him with a blanket to avoid the cold. In the middle of the night, the other guest secretly took Chi Khiem's ​​blanket and went away. In the morning, his companions saw this and asked Chi Khiem where the blanket had gone. Chi Khiem replied:

- A stranger took it away last night!

They asked:

- Why don't you scream?

- If I had shouted, you would have had to tie up or punish the thief. Why do you harm everyone or kill others just because of a blanket?

Ngo Ton Quyen heard the scholar's reputation and his outstanding intellectual talent, so he summoned Chi Khiem to attend him and asked him about the depths of the Buddhist teachings. Chi Khiem responded fluently and clearly to the scriptures that were difficult to understand and many questions, depending on his ability. Hearing this, Ngo Ton Quyen was very happy, so he appointed Chi Khiem as a Doctor, responsible for teaching the eastern palace. At that time, there were many scriptures transmitted to Wu, but most of them were in Sanskrit, so it was difficult for people to understand the meaning. Because he was fluent in Chinese and Sanskrit, as well as the languages ​​of six countries, Chi Khiem collected many types of sutras and translated them into Chinese himself. Chi Khiem translated about twenty-seven sutras, along with annotating sutras such as Lieu Bon Sanh Tu. When the crown prince ascended the throne, Chi Khiem went into seclusion on Khuong Ai mountain, ignoring all worldly matters. Chi Khiem also followed Truc Phap Lan and received the five precepts, and lived there for sixty years until his death.

According to the book 'Exit Tripitaka', from the reign of Ngo Ton Quyen, the reign of Hoang Vo (222) to the reign of Ngo Ton Luong, the reign of Kien Hung (252-253), Chi Khiem translated more than thirty sutras as follows: Dai Bat Ne Hoan (2 volumes), Doan Ung Bon Khoi (2 volumes), Tieu A Sai Mat (2 volumes), Hue An (1 volume), Bon Nghiep (1 volume), Dhammapada (2 volumes), Tu Lai (1 volume), Tu A Mat (1 volume), Vi Mat Tri (1 volume), Amitabha (2 volumes), Nguyet Minh Dong Tu (1 volume), Karma Succeeding (2 volumes), Ananda Tu Su (1 volume), Sai Ma Kiet (1 volume), Uda La Mau (1 volume), That Nu (1 volume), Bat Master (1 volume), Thich Ma Nam (1 volume), Bat Sao (1 volume), Minh Do (4 volumes), Old Woman (1 volume), Trai Sutra (1 volume), Four Vows (1 volume), Repentance (1 volume), Sage Virtue (1 volume), The Buddha's Practice of the Thirty Verses (1 volume), Liu Bon's Birth and Death (1 volume), Duy Minh Nhi's Twenty Verses (1 volume). These are the classics translated by Chi Khiem, and listed by Mr. Dao An. According to Tang Huu, Chi Khiem translated six other sutras such as the Shurangama Sutra (2 volumes), Dragon Thi Nu (1 volume), Phap Kinh (2 volumes), Loc Tu (1 volume), Twelve Doors of the Great Direction (1 volume), Lai Tra Hoa La (1 volume).

Chi Khiem's ​​way of interpreting the sutras is very flexible and fluent. In the past, most of the translated scriptures had a lot of Sanskrit words, so it was very difficult to read. Later, Chi Khiem translated the sutra according to his ideas and then reviewed them to match the meaning of the sutra. If the translation idea is consistent with the text of the scriptures, then the original text will be maintained without any further changes, so the text will rarely contain Sanskrit words.

tom_tat: Mr. Duy De Nan, originally from Thien Truc, had a family background that believed in pagan fire worship. One time, a monk practiced Hinayana teachings, but often practiced...
noi_dung:
12. Venerable Duy De Nan (Vighna)Mr. Duy De Nan, originally from Thien Truc, had a family background that believed in pagan fire worship. One time, a monk who practiced Hinayana teachings, but often practiced Taoism, went out as a beggar and encountered the dark sky. When he arrived at Duy De Nan's house, this monk intended to ask for shelter for the night. Because Duy De Nan's family believed in paganism, they were suspicious of the monk and did not allow him to stay in the house. The monk then rested overnight outside on the road. That night, the monk recited the mantra, causing the fire in Duy De Nan's house to go out. Terrified, Duy De Nan's family ran out and asked the monk to come into the house to make offerings. The monk then recited the mantra, causing the fire to burn again. Witnessing this extraordinary supernatural power, Venerable Duyen Nan immediately started believing in the Buddha Dharma, then left home to become a monk, followed that monk to study the three canonical teachings, and excelled in the Four Agama Sutras. Later, Venerable Duy De Nan traveled all over the country.

During the reign of Ngo Hoang Vo (224), Duy De Nan and his fellow student Truc Luat Viem went to Vo Xuong, bringing with them the Dam Bat Sutra in Sanskrit, the Dhammapada Sutra. At that time, Ngo Si requested to translate the sutra. Although Mr. Duy De Nan and Truc Luat Viem were not fluent in Chinese, they still tried to translate, keeping the original meaning, so the writing was very simple and rudimentary. At the end of Tan Hue's reign, the monk Phap Lap translated it into five volumes, and the monk Phap Cu recorded it.

tieu_de: 13. Venerable Bach Thi Le Mat Da La (Srimitra)
tom_tat: Mr. Bach Thi Le Mat Da La, or Thi Le Mat (translated as Kiet Huu) from the Western Regions. Contemporaries often called him 'Highly Venerated Dharma Master'. He...
noi_dung:
13. Venerable Bach Thi Le Mat Da La (Srimitra)Mr. Bach Thi Le Mat Da La, or Thi Le Mat (translated as Kiet Huu) from the Western Regions. Contemporaries often called him 'Highly Venerated Dharma Master'. He was originally the teacher of the great translator of the Western Jin Dynasty, Truc Phap Ho. Then how great is Thi Le Mat (or Truc Cao Toa)! Thi Le Mat was originally a prince of the Western Region, but he ceded the throne to his younger brother, then secretly studied Buddhism, then understood the great religion, so he became a monk. He has outstanding genius and intelligence, unlike ordinary people.

During the reign of Western Jin Emperor Huai, during the reign of Yongjia (307-312), he came to Central Earth. At that time, at a time when the Five Lakes and sixteen countries were fighting, he crossed the Truong Giang River, went to the south, and temporarily stayed at Kien So Pagoda (in Nanjing city). As soon as Prime Minister Vuong Dao met him, he felt that this was not an ordinary person, but recognized him as 'Nga Boi Trung Nhan (favored close friend)'. Since then, his reputation was resounding, so he often interacted with mandarins and noble scholars, such as Yu Luong, Chu Di, Ta Con, Vuong Don, etc.

Contemporaries wanted to comment on Him, but there was no way to do so. At that time, Hoang Di asked Chu Di about this. Chu Di replied:

- Mr. Thi Le Mat is a noble and elegant figure.

Hoan Di also said:

- When I was young, I met Mr. Thi Le Mat. His spirit is rich and prosperous; What an outstanding character, making everyone admire him.

The first person to meet Him was King Dao (267-330). Vuong Dao was originally a loyal servant of Emperor Nguyen, Emperor Minh, and Emperor Thanh, and was prime minister of Emperor Thanh. When Vuong Dao came to his residence to visit, he took off his outer robe and threw it on the ground, then spoke to him. Not long after King Dao arrived, Bien Khon also came to visit him. When Bien Khong was about to arrive, he adjusted his posture, sat upright and waited for him. Others saw this and asked why He had such a strange gesture. He said:

- Vuong Dao likes to 'enthrone the gods'. Bian Khong judges people by looking at their doubts. That's why I have two different attitudes.

Therefore, contemporaries praised him for knowing how to use the method to suit the person facing him.

His personality is very generous and tolerant, not fussy about details. When he arrived in Central Earth, he did not learn Chinese, so anyone who wanted to converse with him needed a translator. However, often without waiting for the translator to translate, He can clearly understand the words of the other person, which means he is able to know that person's psychology.

Chu Di (269-322) also often interacted with him. Chu Di is a person with a clear mind and a talented personality. Chu Di was originally a Boc Xa mandarin, so he often selected talented people to bring to the court as mandarins. When he first met him, Chu Di said:

- If it is a time of peace and prosperity, this sage must be chosen, without any regrets!"

Later, Chu Di was killed by Vuong Ban, so he came to his house to pay his respects. He sat facing Chu Di's children, chanting Sanskrit; The clear sound echoed through the heavens. He recited thousands of mantras again, and the sound echoed far away, but his face remained as normal. After reciting, he wiped away his tears, his expression was calm and normal, not showing any sadness. He doesn't care about happiness, sadness, or anger. Vuong Dao often said:

- Foreign countries only have this one talent!

The great general Vuong Xu Chong heard that Vuong Dao, Chu Di, etc. all praised him, so he came to pay his respects. As soon as he met Him, he immediately began to worship Him.

Vuong Dao's grandson, Vuong Man, once studied secret mantra with him, and often listened to the monk Devata preach the sutras. Vuong Man often wrote prefaces to classics.

He always recited the mantra, which was very effective. Previously, in the Jiangdong region, there had never been a mantra. Thanks to him translating the sutra "Confucian King", mantra was introduced to the Buddhist masses. In the book 'Exit Tripitaka', there are two sutras on secret mantras that he translated, the Great Confucius King's Mantra, and the Confucius King's Mantra. In addition, he also translated many sutras on secret sects. Currently, in the twenty-first volume of Dai Chanh Tan Tu, there are also ten volumes translated by him as follows: 1/ Buddha's Teaching of the Empowerment of the Seven Thousand Divine Kings Protecting the Body Sutra; 2/ Buddha's Teaching of the Empowerment of the Twelve Thousand Divine Kings Protecting the Body of the Body Sutra; 3/ Buddha's Teaching of the Empowerment of the Five Precepts of the Five Precepts Protecting the Body Sutra; 4/ Buddha's Teaching of the Empowerment of the Hundred Kings Protecting the Body Mantra; Left and Right Sutra; 6/ Buddha's Teaching on Empowerment of the Four Directions Mantra; 7/ Buddha's Teaching on the Empowerment of the Great Mantra of the Five Directions; 8/ Buddha's Teaching on the Empowerment of the Great Mantra of the Five Directions 11/ Buddha's Teaching on the Initiation of Praying for Rebirth in the Ten Pure Lands; 12/ Buddha's Teaching on the Initiation of Exorcising the Sins of Birth and Death and Enlightenment.

During the reign of Eastern Jin Emperor Cheng, in the reign of Ham Khang (334-342), he became naturalized citizen, living more than eighty years old. Because he had once practiced asceticism at Thach Tu Vong, his body was buried there. People at that time, hearing that he passed away, shed tears of mourning. Admiring his teaching merits, King Tan Thanh De built a rosary at his grave. Later, a foreign monk came to Kinh Su and built a pagoda right at the grave of Thi Le Mat. Ta Con in Tran District provided financial support to build the pagoda, and to remember the merits of Mr. Thi Le Mat, the pagoda was called Cao Toa Tu.

tom_tat: Before Kumarajiva's time, the person most instrumental in spreading Mahayana teachings was the great translator Truc Phap Ho. Again, although there is...
noi_dung:
14. Truc Phap HoBefore Kumarajiva's time, the person most instrumental in spreading Mahayana teachings was the great translator Truc Phap Ho. Again, although there are many translators who interpret the classics of the digital series, the one who has the most merit is Mr. Truc Phap Ho.

Mr. Truc Phap Ho is also called Dam Ma La Sat (Dharmaraksa), a native of Dai Nhuc Chi country, his family background resides in Dun Hoang district, he became a monk at the age of eight, studying with a foreign monk named Truc Cao Toa. Because he studied with a Thien Truc monk, he took the name Truc. He often recited sutras with thousands of words. Because of his determination to study, he did not care about hardships and traveled miles to find teachers to study. He understood six sutras and thoroughly understood the treatises of hundreds of religions, so his knowledge was very profound. As for people in the world, even though they are praised, criticized or scolded, they are still not moved. Nature is gentle and pure.

Because he knew that in the capital Lac Duong, there were no Mahayana sutras such as Phuong Dang and Prajna, so he was determined to establish his will and propagate the great path. He followed his teacher through the countries of the Western Regions, so he became fluent in thirty-six languages, and mastered the script of Thien Truc and the Western Regions, laying the basic foundation for later translation of the scriptures. Because he prayed the Prajnaparamita Sutra, from Don Hoang, he went to Vu Dien.

In the past, Chau Si Hanh copied the original Sanskrit text of the Prajnaparamita Sutra in the country of Vu Dien. At that time, Vu Dien, which was the center of Mahayana Buddhism, developed strongly. From the country of Vu Dien, he went to Sa Lac, then around the north of Tay Vuc (the southern avenue of Thien Son mountain), to the country of Quy Tu, and back to Dun Hoang. At his translation ashram, there were lay people from Quy Tu country such as Bach Nguyen Tin, Bach Phap Cu, etc.

From the Western Regions, he brought many Sanskrit scriptures to Chang'an in 266, then returned to Dunhuang. From 274 to 283, he secluded himself in the deep mountains and forests, diligently practiced the Dharma at Ngoai Kien Pagoda in Thanh Mon, and used his virtuous power to transform the four directions, so thousands of monks followed him to study the Dharma. On the fourteenth day of the tenth month in the year 284, at Don Hoang, he finished translating the Sutras of the Cultivation of the Path and the A Duy Viet Chi Gia. In 286, he brought many Sanskrit scriptures back to Chang'an. Because on the way, he translated the sutras while walking, so when he arrived at Truong An, he finished translating the Pho Sieu sutra. For more than twenty years in Truong An, he enthusiastically and actively engaged in the career of translating classics.

During the reign of Emperor Hue of the Western Jin Dynasty, due to the chaos of the king, wars and killings did not stop. Furthermore, the Ho clan continuously invaded the North China region, and besieged Luoyang city. In the eleventh month of the reign of Yongxing (304), Emperor Hui was forced to move the capital to Chang'an. In the year of Quang Hi (306), in May, Ky Tu led the Tien Ti army to invade Truong An, killing more than two hundred thousand people, causing blood to flow all over the river. The capital Truong An became desolate. People are hungry and miserable. The world is in utter chaos.

Even though he encountered times of chaos, he still did not stop the work of translating the scriptures. During the time he translated the sutras, the copyist was Phap Cu. Between the reigns of Emperor Hui and Emperor Huai (290-312), Phap Cu translated the Lau Than Sutra, and together with Phap Lap translated the Dhammapada Sutra and Phuoc Dien Sutra.

Among those people, there was Truc Phap Thua, the most trusted disciple of Truc Phap Ho. Truc Phap Thua followed Truc Phap Ho and received novice ordination from a young age. Since the first time Truc Phap Ho came to Truong An, Truc Phap Thua always accompanied him, helping to translate the sutras and propagate the Dharma. In Don Hoang, Truc Phap Thua built a pagoda and tried his best to promote Buddhism, causing the correct teaching to be spread throughout the Western Regions. When Truc Phap Ho returned to Don Hoang, Truc Phap Thua helped translate the Sutras of Cultivation of the Path and A Duy Viet Chi.

Truc Phap Ho was a great translator, translating classics in ancient times. Throughout his life, he focused on the career of translating classics. In parallel, there are two anecdotes about Him.

The first anecdote: Throughout his life, he was tirelessly attentive and devoted to the career of translating the classics. At the end of Emperor Jin Wu's reign (263-274), he lived in seclusion in the mountains and valleys. There is a clear blue water stream on the mountain, where woodcutters often rinse their mouths and bathe, making the water unclean. Some time later, the water stream dried up. He anxiously stood beside the dry stream and said to himself:

- The water flowing here is dry. There is no way to live on my own. Must go somewhere else!

As soon as he finished speaking, the green water suddenly flowed out again.

Later, in Truong An, he built a pagoda at the eastern gate of the citadel, and diligently practiced Buddhism. At that time, more than a thousand people admired his morality. In the book 'Cao Tang Truyen' and 'Khai Nguyen Luc', Mr. Chi Don praised Mr. Truc Phap Ho as follows: "Mr. Truc Phap Ho has a calm and quiet mind, gentleness, and profound morality."

He is a great translator, deeply explaining obscure teachings. The anecdote about the dried water suddenly flowing again symbolizes His outstanding divine power.

Second anecdote: Truc Phap Thua followed him and became a novice monk since he was eight years old. One time, some noble people wanted to test his spiritual power, so they went to his residence and borrowed two hundred thousand dong. Hearing them ask for loans, he just stood silently without responding. At that time, the thirteen-year-old novice monk Truc Phap Thua told the guests:

- The Venerable Master's heart has accepted your request!

Hearing this, the guests said goodbye and left. Truc Phap Thua immediately told him:

- Look at their faces, they didn't come here to borrow money, but just wanted to test the Venerable's magic power!

He said:

- I also think so!

The second day, the other guests returned, and brought with them more than a hundred people, to ask him to give the five precepts, and to reiterate their intention to borrow money. The reason why they came to borrow money was because someone said that He had two hundred thousand gold coins. However, this money was not borrowed by Him, but only donated by believers or supported in the work of translating the scriptures. This is completely different from the classic translation career of Kumarajiva and Xuanzang. The two of them were supported and sponsored by the powerful king. Hearing that guests wanted to borrow money, he immediately promised to do so without any regrets. This shows His deep morality, not being greedy for material wealth.

Tan Ton Xuoc in his treatise Dao Hien highly praised his virtue. Later, he passed away at the age of seventy-eight.

During the Western Han Dynasty, the translators translated the sutras, listed as follows: Monk Cuong Luong Lau Chi translated one set, one volume of sutras. The monk An Phap Kham translated five volumes and sixteen volumes. The monk Vo La Xoa translated one set, thirty volumes. Monk Bach Phap To translated sixteen volumes and eighteen volumes. Monk Thich Phap Lap translated four volumes, twelve volumes. Monk Thich Phap Cu translated forty volumes and fifty volumes. The monk Chi Phap Do translated four volumes and five volumes. Monk Nhuoc La Nghiem translated one set and one volume. Upasaka Truc Thuc Lan translated two volumes, five volumes. Thanh believer Nhiep Thua Vien translated two volumes and three volumes. Thanh believer Nhiep Dao Chan translated twenty-four volumes and thirty-six volumes.

Translators are not necessarily only monks, but lay people also contribute.

noi_dung:
15. Buddha Do Trung - Hung Long Buddha DharmaHe was originally from the Western Regions, belonging to the Quy Tu country. His customary name is Bach, a young monk, gentle and sincere but studious; Reciting scriptures up to hundreds of thousands of words; Regarding literature, he has a thorough understanding of the meaning and interpretation, and is quick to understand. When I had not yet been to Central Earth, although I had never read the Confucian histories and classic scriptures, when discussing with scholars, they were all in accordance with the intention. Regarding education, He once said:

- I have been to Ke Tan country twice to receive teachings from famous masters, so now I have this ability.

The people of the Western Region unanimously proclaimed that he had attained enlightenment.

During the reign of Emperor Jinhuai, the fourth year of Yongjia (310), he came to Luoyang. He has the will to propagate Buddhism, has supernatural powers, and the ability to command ghosts and spirits; Rubbing fat in the palm of your hand will make you see things thousands of miles away; predict future events; When I heard the sound of the spirit calling, I immediately knew what was going to happen; nothing but inspiration. His original intention was to build a pagoda, but when Liu Dieu was raising troops in the Central Plains, causing chaos among the Buddhist monks, he temporarily suspended that wish and hid himself in the wild countryside, to observe the changing times, hoping to find an opportunity to promote Buddhism.

(Talking about history, after the Han and Wei dynasties, the foreign people in the north surrendered to the Chinese court. But in the Eastern Han Dynasty, they established the Xiongnu state, with Liu Yuan as emperor. Liu Uyen died (310), his son Liu Thong ascended the throne, then led the army to attack Luoyang citadel in the reign of Jin Huai De (311). At that time, Liu Thong's younger brother Liu Dieu and Wang Di destroyed Luoyang citadel and captured Luoyang citadel. Killed Emperor Hoai of Tan, then led his army to attack Chang'an citadel, killing Emperor Man De (316), causing the Jin Dynasty to perish. There was chaos in the country, so the country was divided into Early Trieu and Later Trieu. Later, Thach Lac in Later Trieu killed Liu Dieu and Vuong Nhi of Former Trieu, and subdued the Hu clans such as Khuong Nhung, then proclaimed himself Thien Vuong.

Lang Nha Vuong Due was a descendant of Sima Y. He went to build a business in the south at Kien Nghiep (Nanjing), founded the Eastern Jin dynasty, and called himself Emperor Tan.)

Thach Lac's army in Tan Sat, Ha Nam province, often killed countless civilians to show off their prestige. Buddhist monks were also persecuted quite a bit. Witnessing this situation, Buddha Do Trung felt compassion and pity for the suffering living beings. He intended to use Buddhism to influence Thach Lac, so first he went to the house of Quach Hac Luoc (the general of Thach Lac), persuaded him and forced him to take refuge in the Three Jewels and take the five precepts. From then on, every time Thach Lac's army went into battle, Quach Hac Luoc predicted victory or defeat. This made Thach Lac suspicious and asked:

- I don't feel that you have outstanding strategic talent, but every time you're about to send troops, you know what's going on, what's the point?

Quach Hac Luoc said:

- The General's heavenly army now has divine support. That monk's magic was extremely clever. He often said that the General would rule the Central Plains, and that he himself would be the national teacher. The victory and defeat of the king and queen that I know in advance are all thanks to the advice of that monk.

Hearing that, Thach Lac was happy and said:

- God gives good fate!

Having finished speaking, he ordered to invite Buddha Do Trung to come and ask about the spiritual effects of the Buddha's teachings, and asked to see the magic displayed. Knowing clearly that Thach Lac did not understand the profound meaning of Buddha Dharma, he only used magic to demonstrate the profound Buddhist path. He said:

- Although the Way is high and profound and difficult to understand, the most recent events can be used as proof.

Having finished speaking, he asked to bring out a basin of water, then offered incense and recited mantras. Later, a blue lotus flower appeared from the tub, shining with an unusual color. Seeing this, Thach Lac was convinced. Taking advantage of that opportunity, He reminded Thach Lac:

- As a king, one must use virtue to give to the people, then four ghosts such as unicorn, phoenix, tortoise, and dragon will appear to represent good omens. If politics has many bad things, and the righteous path declines, then comets will appear and bad things will arise, which represents bad things. These strange omens all correspond to gentle or tyrannical politics. In the past, this often happened, and noble people who clearly understood the principles of heaven warned it.

Hearing these admonitions, Thach Lac immediately received faith. From then on, for every ten people about to be killed, nine were spared, and imbued with the grace of Buddhism. Because Thach Lac followed his advice to carry out politics, in the Central Plains, the majority of the Ho clan and the Han clan believed in Buddhism. From then on, he tried his best to advise Thach Lac on military and political issues, and prophesied terrible things. Therefore, towards His strange divine power, Thach Lac was very respectful and awed, so he often called Him the Great Venerable.

One time, Thach Lac returned from Catpo to Ha Bac, passing through Phuong Dau. At night, someone planned to attack the barracks. Anticipating this, he called Quach Hac Luoc and said:

- Someone will come and steal the dragon robe. Please notify Thach Lac to prepare early.

At night, indeed, something happened as He predicted. However, thanks to careful preparations, Thach Lac escaped death. One night, because he wanted to test his supernatural powers, Thach Lac put on his armor and sat down with a knife, then sent someone to tell him:

- It's dark, General Thach doesn't know what to do!

The official sent by Thach Lac, as soon as he arrived, before he could say anything, he said:

- Everything is peaceful, and there are no bandits coming, but why is Thach Lac armed and preparing for battle?

From then on, Thach Lac respected him even more.

Another time, Thach Lac suddenly became angry with the monks, so he wanted to kill him and tried to accuse him. The prophet knew of this intention, so at Quach Hac Luoc's house, he told the disciples:

- If Thach Lac sends someone to find me, answer that you don't know!

Not long after, the people sent by Thach Lac couldn't find him at Quach Hac Luoc's house, so they returned to report. Thach Lac was frightened and exclaimed:

- Because I had evil thoughts towards the Saint, he left!

Therefore, Thach Lac kept tossing and turning all night, only wishing to see Him again. Knowing that Thach Lac had regained his mind, the next morning he came to see him. As soon as he saw Him, Thach Lac happily asked:

- Where did you go last night?

He said:

- Because the Great King was angry yesterday, the old monk temporarily stayed away. Now, the Great King has regained his mind, so the old monk returned here to meet.

Hearing these words, Thach Lac was not only amazed but also endlessly happy.

One time, the water source leading from the northwest of the Xiangguo citadel moat, about five miles long, suddenly dried up. Thach Lac asked him if it was possible to make the water flow again. He replied:

- Just summoning the dragon will solve the problem?

Because Thach Lac's given name is 'Long' (dragon), he thought he was joking and said:

- Because the dragon cannot open the water vein, that's why I asked him!

He said:

- I speak the truth, not joking. At the source of the water, there is a dragon in seclusion. Just summon it, and the water will flow abundantly.

Therefore, He led his disciples to the source of the stream. There, the water had dried up a long time ago, and there were clearly printed traces of passing wheels. The disciples are afraid that they will not be able to open the water vein. However, he approved his intention, sat upright on a tree stump, offered incense, prayed, and recited mantras. Just like that, after three days, water suddenly flowed from the dry stream. A small dragon, about five meters long, crawled out from the stream. As soon as he saw the dragon, his followers scrambled to see it. He said:

- Dragon has poisonous gas, don't go near it!

Soon the Tuong Quoc moat was filled with water. Sitting alone there, He said:

- Two days later, a servant who will cause earth-shattering chaos will arrive.

The reason is because Tiet Hop, from Tuong Quoc, has two very arrogant and arrogant children. One time, they deceived and teased a servant of the Tien Ti tribe, so he became angry and had evil thoughts, so he carelessly killed the younger child, and then locked the older child in the room. The man was about to run in to save him when he brandished his knife and threatened that if anyone came near he would kill that child. Guy said:

- Take me back to my homeland. On the contrary, I will die with this boy here.

People inside and outside the city were shocked and shocked, so they ran to see and surrounded Tiet Hao's house. Thach Lac also went there himself and said:

- Please send this servant back to his native country, then you can hope to preserve your son's life. That is the best choice. If the national law has been declared, disaster will come. I advise you to put aside your personal feelings and think carefully. National laws are not amended because of this!

Therefore, Tiet Hop sent someone to arrest the servant. The servant was angry, quickly killed his son and left himself tied up. Because of this, the Tien Ti tribe, Doan Ba, led an army to attack Thach Lac. Doan Ba's military reputation was very strong, making Thach Lac very worried and afraid, so he had to pray to him to find a plan to oppose the enemy. He said:

- Yesterday the spirit in the temple suddenly cried out that early tomorrow morning, Doan Ba ​​would be arrested.

Thach Lac went up to the citadel to check the military situation, saw Doan Ba's troops surrounded in rows and rows outside the citadel, so he was terrified and said:

- The enemy army was so crowded that it shook the earth. How could Doan Ba ​​be captured? Buddha Do Trung probably only comforted me!

Feeling uneasy, Thach Lac sent someone to ask him about his military situation. He said:

- Don't doubt it, Doan Ba ​​has been arrested!

Because there was an army of Thach Lac sneaking out of the city to ambush. When Doan Ba ​​was coming, they caught him.

Capturing the enemy general, he advised Thach Lac to release Doan Ba ​​back to his native country. Thach Lac followed his teachings, so he benefited later.

At that time, Liu Thong had just passed away and his younger brother Liu Dieu succeeded him, changing the country's name to Tien Trieu and the reign name Kien Nguyen Quang So. In the eighth year of Quang So, Liu Dieu sent his younger brother, King Liu Nhac, to lead a large army to attack Shi Lac. Thach Lac then sent Thach Ho to bring troops to resist. After the two sides fought in the west of Lac Duong city, Liu Nhac, defeated, had to retreat to Thach Luong valley, then sent his army to defend firmly. Unable to destroy the attack, Thach Ho then pulled his army to the surrounding area, set up tents and resolutely waited for Liu Nhac. The two sides kept fighting without winning or losing.

One day, with his disciples just entering the door of Tu Quan pagoda, he said:

- Feel sorry for Liu Nhac!

The crowd didn't understand anything, so they asked. He said:

- Yesterday at the hour of the pig, Liu Nhac was arrested.

Moments later, news of the battle came back, as expected.

In the 11th year of Quang So, Liu Dieu personally led a large army to destroy Lac Duong citadel. Thach Lac intended to personally bring troops to resist, but the courtiers all advised that there was no need to take risks. Thach Lac then came to ask him what he should do. He said:

- 'If you send troops, you will capture Liu Dieu' is the language of the Yet tribe.

At that time, the military officer heard that and believed his prediction, so he invited Thach Lac to personally lead the army. Thach Lac then held Thach Hoang to defend Tuong Quoc citadel, then led a large army to Luoyang. While the two sides were fighting, Liu Dieu's army was suddenly scattered. Liu Dieu's horse also fell into the water. Taking advantage of the opportunity, Thach Kham sent troops to surround Liu Dieu, then brought him back to meet Thach Lac. At that time, in the city, He rubbed his hands with oil, and then there appeared among the rioting soldiers, a man with his hands tied. He then told Thach Hoang that that person was Liu Dieu.

After pacifying Liu Dieu, Thach Lac proclaimed himself Trieu Thien Vuong and changed his reign name to Kien Binh, meaning he became king of Later Trieu. At that time, it was the fifth year of Ham Hoa, the reign of Eastern Jin Thanh De (330).

One time, Thach Thong intended to rebel, and he knew this clearly, so he told Thach Lac:

- This year there are worms in the onion plants, so they cannot be eaten. Please, Great King, issue an order banning people from eating onions.

Therefore, Thach Lac wrote an edict, forbidding people from eating onions. Because 'real pine' (ie onion tree), which has the same sound as Thach Thong's name, upon hearing that decree, Thach Thong knew the plot had been revealed. In August, for fear of being arrested, Thach Thong fled to another place. Thach Lac later learned clearly about the situation, so he respected him even more. Whatever matters arise, Thach Lac discusses them with Him and then carries them out.

Thach Ban was originally the son of Thach Ho and was loved very much by Thach Lac. One time, Thach Ban had a fever and died. Thach Lac said sadly:

- I have heard that once the crown prince of Quach Quoc country died, Thien Thuoc brought him back to life. The Venerable Master is a god in the country. Tell Him this. He will definitely turn misfortune into blessing.

Therefore, Thach Lac sent someone to invite him to come. He used a poplar branch to wave over Thach Ban's head and chanted the mantra. Moments later, Thach Ban came back to life, then slowly became healthy as usual. From then on, Thach Ban often stayed in the temple. Every year on the eighth day of the fourth month, Buddha's birthday, Thach Lac himself goes to the temple to attend the Buddha bathing ceremony to pray for blessings.

In the fourth year of Kien Binh (333), in April, the sky was clear and cloudy, there was no wind, but the spirit on the tower suddenly made a dull sound. He told the crowd:

- Linh said that there was a great funeral in the country. I'm afraid it will happen this year.

That year, in July, Thach Lac died and was succeeded by Thach Hoang. Not long after, Thach Ho deposed Thach Hoang and took the throne himself, then moved the capital from Tuong Quoc to Nghiep Do (ie Lam Chuong district, Ha Nam province), changing the reign name to Kien Vo. Thach Ho was even more devoted and devoted to serving him than Shi Lek, so he issued the decree:

- The Great Venerable is the great national treasure of the royal court. He never received any honor or glory. From now on, you must weave silk and brocade to make your robes, and decorate your palanquin with flowers to make your carriage. On the day of the court festival, when the Great Venerable ascended to the palace, the mandarins had to carry the palanquin, and the crown prince and his servants also had to carry him to the palace. The main movement is that 'The Great Venerable' has come. All sitting mandarins had to stand up to welcome him to show his noble dignity and honor.

Thach Ho again sent Ty Khong Quy Nong to come to the temple early and late to greet him. The Crown Prince and his vassals came every five days to pay homage to him, to show their utmost respect.

One day, while residing at a temple in Nghiep Do city, he sent his disciple Phap Thuong to Tuong Quoc to call back another disciple, Phap Ta. On the way, Phap Thuong met Phap Ta at Luong Co citadel, so they stayed overnight in the same place. At night, they discussed together about His unusual deeds. The next morning, the two broke up. Phap Ta returned to Nghiep Do. He smiled and said:

- Last night, you and Phap Thuong discussed my affairs, right? The ancients said that just because we don't see each other, we don't have a heart of respect. Just because you live alone, don't let your mind relax in the precepts.

Hearing these words, Phap Ta was terrified and repented. Therefore, people often remind each other:

- Don't give rise to evil thoughts! Aren't you afraid that the Great Venerable will know!

Crown Prince Thach Thuy has two children in Tuong Quoc. He once told Thach Thuy:

- The Crown Prince's child is about to get seriously ill. Go over there quickly and take care.

Thach Thuy sent someone to visit, and it was as he said; One of his children is seriously ill and bedridden. Therefore, Thach Thuy invited physician Doan Thang and foreign monks to diagnose the disease. They all said they could cure Thach Thuy's child's illness. He told his disciple Phap Nha:

- Even saints from the world cannot save Thach Thuy's sick child, let alone those people!

Three days later, indeed, Thach Thuy's child passed away. Thach Thuy was passionate about alcohol and intended to rebel, but was still afraid of his magical powers, afraid of being discovered, so he told his servant Hac Vu:

- The Venerable has great supernatural powers. I'm afraid that the Venerable will find out what I'm doing. So, tomorrow when the Venerable comes, you will eliminate me.

On the full moon day of every month, he often visited Thach Ho. That time, before leaving, he told Tang Hue:

- Last night, God told me that tomorrow if there is an climax, I will definitely not visit anyone! Before I want to leave, please remind me not to go anywhere else!

Every time he entered the court, he had to come and see Thach Thuy. Seeing that he had entered the court, Thach Thuy asked him to come to the palace. Remembering the previous advice, Tang Hue immediately pulled his robe as a signal. He said:

- There is no other solution. It's impossible not to go!

After arriving at the eastern palace, as soon as he sat down, he said goodbye. Thach Thuy was determined to keep it, but he refused, so the assassination plot failed. Returning to the temple, he lamented:

- The Crown Prince's rebellious appearance has formed. I want to speak but it's difficult to speak, and I want to endure but it's difficult to endure.

At that time, He only used hidden words to warn Thach Ho. However, Thach Ho did not understand at all. Only when the Crown Prince's plot to rebel broke out, did Thach Ho understand the intention of His hidden words of warning.

Later, Quach Hac Luoc led his army to conquer the Khuong clan in Bac Son and Truong An. In the middle of the road, they were ambushed by Khuong people. At that time, he was sitting in the main hall, with his disciple Phap Thuong standing next to him. He suddenly changed his face and said:

- Quach Hac Luoc is currently in trouble.

Having finished speaking, he told the monks to chant prayers and prayers. Not long after, He said to himself:

- Only by going southeast can you escape. Going anywhere else will be in danger.

Having finished speaking, he then prayed to continue. A moment later, He said:

- Escaped!

A few months later, Quach Hac Luoc returned to the capital as a monk, and recounted the incident in the army of the Khuong clan. He headed southeast for refuge. However, the horse was exhausted, so it thought it would probably be captured. Luckily, there was a person under his command who brought a horse to him and said:

- Please exchange the general's horse for me. Whether or not you can escape the siege depends only on fate.

Thanks to riding that horse, Quach Hac Luoc escaped the siege. Calculating the date, that day was when he was praying.

Knowing Thach Ho's rough temperament, he often used Buddhist theory and supernatural powers based on the spirit of compassion to remind him of his actions.

Thach Ho's two great ministers were Truong Ly and Truong Lang, who were wealthy and noble, believed in Buddhism, and built temples. He told them:

- When doing Buddhist work, you must have a compassionate, pure mind and not be greedy. Although Dan Viet believes in the great dharma, but his greed has not stopped, his desires are insatiable, he has never known self-control, he has accumulated endless wealth, so he will suffer sins in this life, so how can he hope to receive blessings?

The most important fundamental spirit when doing Buddhist work is that the mind must be compassionate, pure, and not greedy. He reminded Truong Ly and Truong Lang of these words because although they had faith in making offerings to the Three Jewels and building pagodas, they were all based on insatiable greed, worrying about accumulating wealth without limit, and often killing birds and animals. Therefore, if you commit a crime right in this life, even if you need to pray, how can blessings come?

Later, Truong Ly and Truong Lang were sentenced to death because they were freely dissolute and violated national law.

Thach Ho's son, the great prince Thach Ban, took office in You Chau Muc, often recruiting evil people and doing many unjust things. He told Thach Ho:

- Yesterday, the angel told me to quickly bring the horse back, otherwise it would be rotten in the fall.

Thach Ho did not understand what he meant, so he ordered the horses that were running around to be captured and locked in stables. In the fall, when people reported Thach Ban's cruel actions, Thach Ho was angry, so he summoned him back, then ordered him to kill Thach Ban's mother, Te Thi, and to punish Thach Bin with three hundred lashes. Thach Ho personally supervised the punishment. However, seeing that his subordinates punished Thach Ban too lightly, Thach Ho ordered all five hundred people to be killed. Seeing that Thach Ho killed so many people, he advised:

- The mind cannot be too liberal! Dead people cannot come back to life! According to ritual regulations, Thien Tu cannot personally kill people, because he will hurt his virtue. Why did the Great King personally execute the execution?

Hearing this, Thach Ho finally stopped.

Later, the Eastern Jin army counterattacked, fighting on three fronts at Truong An, Tan An, and Lac Duong. The military sent a letter to report that the situation was critical. Thach Ho angrily said:

- I believe in Buddhism and make offerings to monks. Now that there is a foreign invasion, what is the Buddha's response?

The next day, Shi Ho questioned him about this matter. He said:

- The previous Great King was originally a great merchant. He once came to Ke Tan Hanh to make offerings to the monks' conference. At that time, there were sixty Arhats in the Assembly, and I was also among them. At that time, a person who had attained enlightenment said that after his death, this master would first take on the body of a chicken, and then be born as a king in the Middle Earth. Currently, the Great King has become king, so isn't it due to blessings? On the battlefield, winning or losing is normal. Why do you resent the Three Jewels and give rise to cruel thoughts because of this?

Hearing these words, Thach Ho understood and realized his mistake, so he knelt down to apologize and repent. Thach Ho asked him again:

- What is the basic essence of Buddhism?

He replied:

- Buddhism does not kill people!

- I was originally the king of the world. Without using punishment, there is no way to fulfill the important responsibility of reminding the people in the country. I went against the precept against killing and killed people, and then practiced Buddhism. If so, will we reap good rewards?

- Great King, when doing Buddhist work, you must use your whole body to pay homage, and use your mind to follow the teachings, promoting the Three Jewels. Furthermore, there should be no acts of tyranny or killing of innocent people. For those who are cruel and evil, whose crimes are everywhere, if we cannot use the Dharma to make them turn their minds to goodness, then we cannot help but kill them, and we cannot help but punish them. Must kill those who should be killed. We must punish those who should be punished. If the Great King were to arbitrarily kill innocent people, then the blessings and blessings from making offerings to the Three Jewels or building pagodas would not be able to rescue the disaster. Therefore, I hope that Your Majesty will use compassion to care for the people. If that is the case, not only will the Buddha Dharma be eternally prosperous, but the Great King's blessings will also be lasting.

His wish was to teach Thach Ho and the Buddhists to know little and to awaken the spirit of compassion. Although he did not completely follow all of his teachings, Thach Ho also did many good deeds, bringing great benefits to the people.

One year, there was a great drought from January to June. Thach Ho sent the crown prince to Tay Phu village in Lam Chuong to pray for rain, but the prayer still failed. Therefore, Thach Ho asked him to pray for rain. Soon, against the blue sky, two white dragons flew around the herd, praying for rain, and then in an instant the rain poured down like a waterfall. Farmers within a thousand miles, had a good harvest that year. Arrogant people who do not believe in Buddha's teachings, when they hear about His miracles, must worship and slowly accept the teachings.

He often sent his disciples to the West Region to buy incense. After that disciple left for a few days, he suddenly told his disciples:

- I saw that he was about to be murdered by the robbers over there.

Having finished speaking, he offered incense and prayed. When he returned, the other disciple reported:

- On the way to Tay Vuc to buy incense, I was surrounded by robbers who intended to kill me. Suddenly, a strange scent came, causing the robbers to scream in panic: 'The rescue team is here', then ran away, so my life remained.

When Thach Ho came to Lam Chuong to repair an old tower. There, a tray appeared. He said:

- In Lam Chuong citadel, there is a tower of King Ashoka. Under the ground there is still a tray and a Buddha statue. There, trees grow very luxuriantly. Let someone go there and dig it up.

Having finished speaking, he drew a map. Shi Hu then sent someone to dig there and actually found a tray and a Buddha statue.

One time, knowing that Thach Ho wanted to lead his army to conquer the country of Yen, he advised:

- Yen's fortunes are not over yet. If the Great King leads his army to conquer, I'm afraid it will be difficult to succeed.

Shi Hu did not listen to his advice, but continued to lead his army to attack the country of Yen, and was defeated and had to pull his army back. From then on, Thach Ho trusted his words even more.

Along with the industry of building pagodas, preaching sutras and preaching Dharma, and educating people with the Thach family, Buddha Do Trung also converted them into monks. The first Chinese monk to go to the Western Regions to seek Dharma during the Three Kingdoms period was Chau Si Hanh. At that time, very few Chinese people became monks. The vast majority are monks from Thien Truc, Tay Vuc, Khuong Cu, Quy Tu, Ke Tan, who came to Trung Tho to propagate Buddhism or translate scriptures. Belief in Buddhism is limited to lay Buddhists only. Thanks to the inspiring virtue of Buddha Do Trung, Buddhist followers raced to donate material to build temples, and competed to become monks, so they could not avoid being abused by some monks.

Since Emperor Han Ming saw the manifestation of gods, he began to send people to the Western Regions to seek Dharma, but the court did not officially allow the Chinese to believe in worshiping Buddhism, as follows: "Only the people of the Western Regions, who set up monasteries in Do Ap, believe in worshiping Buddha as a god."

Building pagodas, making offerings to monks, doing Buddhist work, is limited to people from the Western Regions, and only accepts monks from the Western Regions, not allowing Chinese people to become monks. Cao Wei's reign also followed the same regime as that of the Eastern Han Dynasty.

Originally from the Ho tribe in the north, with customs and institutions different from the Chinese, when entering Central Earth and ascending the throne, Shi Ho issued a decree: "Buddha is a foreign god, not a god that the kings in Central Earth believe in worshiping. I was born on the border, had good fortune, and became king in Central Earth. Regarding sacrifices, I have sovereignty here, so for sacrifices I must follow the customs of the Central Earth. Buddha is my god, so the people must believe in it. Only by following the king can it become a permanent rule. If there is no harm, there is no need to follow the regime of the previous kings, but prohibit Chinese people, Chinese people, and Man people, if anyone wishes to renounce worldliness and practice Buddhism, then I will grant them permission to become monks.

This decree was issued in response to the statement of the royal mandarin, Vuong Do. He once submitted a petition (335) asking Thach Ho to strictly forbid the people of the Later Dynasty from worshiping and worshiping Buddha; punish those who violate this law, and force Chinese monks to return to the world because Buddha is only a foreign god, not the god that previous kings believed in.

Due to this decree, those who want to become monks and nuns are approved. In the reign of Tai Ninh of the Eastern Jin Dynasty (323-326), and in the reign of Kien Vo of the Later Zhao Dynasty of Shi Hu (335), the court officially allowed Chinese people to become monks. (Previously, although monks from the Zhao state were famous for being monks, they still often dressed like commoners.) The thirty-fifth book of the Sui Dynasty Sutra Sutra, wrote: "During the early years of the Wei Huang Dynasty, the people of Central Earth began to follow the Buddha's precepts and shave their hair to become monks."

In the past, Chinese people became monks only on their own initiative and without official permission from the court, like Chau Si Hanh and Truc Tham (brothers of Prime Minister Vuong Don, during the reign of King Tan Thai Xuong).

One day, he and his disciple Dao An went to the palace. While sitting, He suddenly shouted:

- Change U Chau! There is a fire!

Having finished speaking, He then asked to take out the wine, then sprinkled the wine on the ground as if to put out a fire. A moment later, He smiled and said:

- Fire rescue is done!

When Thach Ho saw this incident, he did not understand the story, so he sent someone to You Chau to investigate, and was informed:

- That day, a fire broke out at the west gate, southwest of Dieu Van Mat Dong. At that time, clouds suddenly came, then rain fell, causing the fire to be extinguished, and in the rainwater, there was a slight smell of alcohol.

In Wei district, there was a wanderer whose name no one knew. He only wore burlap and begged for food at the market in the district city, so everyone called him 'Ma Nhu'. His language is very strange, and he acts like a crazy person. Every time I asked for rice, I refused to eat it. I crushed it and left it at the intersection, telling myself that I would feed it to the horses of heaven. Governor Ta Bat in Trieu Hung, knowing clearly about his behavior, arrested him and then handed him over to Thach Ho. Previously, He had predicted this and told Thach Ho:

- Two hundred miles east of here, one day there will be a person who is not like a normal person. Please don't harm that person.

A few days later, Ta Bat sent the army to bring this person here. Thach Ho replied to that person, without saying anything special, except for the sentence:

- His Royal Highness is finally a pillar under the palace.

Hearing this, Thach Ho did not understand anything, so he took him to see him. As soon as they met, he talked with that person all day and night. The disciples did not understand anything about the content of the discussions, they only felt like they were discussing things hundreds of years ago. Later, Thach Ho sent troops to take that person back to Wei Huyen. As soon as the car left the city, that person got out and walked, saying that he wanted to visit his friends, and then made an appointment with the military officials to meet at Hekou Bridge. The military officer driving the horse-drawn carriage had not yet reached Hekou Bridge when he saw that person standing on the bridge.

He had a disciple, Dao Tan, who was erudite and knowledgeable in external scriptures and was highly respected by Thach Ho.

In the fourteenth year of Kien Vo (348), Shi Hu's children Thach Tuyen and Thach Thao wanted to kill each other. One time, Thach Tuyen came to the temple and sat next to him. At that time, the spirit on the Buddha tower suddenly echoed. He told Thach Tuyen:

- Do you understand what the spirit is saying? Linh said that Ho Tu was lost.

Thach people were originally from the Yet clan, so they were called Ho Tu. Happiness means the mind of the soul flying away. When Thach Tuyen heard this, his face turned pale and he asked:

- What does that mean?

He said:

- When I practice and do Buddhist work, I should always live in seclusion in the mountains and valleys, but instead I wear silk clothes and eat luxurious foods. Is this the enjoyment of happiness (pleasure)?

Thach Thao went to the temple to meet him again. As soon as we met, he glared, causing Thach Thao to panic, so he asked why. He said:

- I saw a strong smell of blood on his body.

However, both Thach Tuyen and Thach Thao did not understand his words. In August of that year, he told his disciples to clean the hermitage, strictly observe the precepts, and then temporarily entered into hermitage in Dong Cac.

Thach Ho and Queen Do Thi asked why he lived like that. He said:

- The robbers are right next to you. In less than ten days, there will be rebellion. To the west of the Buddha Tower, that is, to the east of this Dong Cac, there will be bloodshed. No matter what the Great King and Queen do, do not go to the east!

The Queen said:

- The Venerable Master is so confused! How can there be an enemy here?

He said:

- Human desire is the enemy. When you get old, you often become confused and lethargic. However, just keeping young people from falling into a coma is enough!

Two days later, Thach Tuyen indeed sent people to kill Thach Thao right in the temple. Thach Tuyen had the intention that during the funeral ceremony for Thach Thao, he would kill Thach Ho as well. Thanks to listening to his words of caution, Thach Ho avoided great disaster. Thach Tuyen's plot to rebel was later revealed, so he was imprisoned and brutally imprisoned by Thach Ho's family. Seeing that, he advised Thach Ho:

- Thach Tuyen is also the son of the Great King. Ha must have just finished mourning a child, creating another disaster! If the Great King gradually reduces his anger and uses the virtue of kindness, he will enjoy more than sixty years of prosperity. If he decides to kill him, Thach Tuyen will turn into a comet and burn Nghiep Do palace.

Thach Ho refused to listen to his honest words, but ordered an iron ring to be tightened around Thach Tuyen's abdomen and firewood to be burned alive. Thach Ho also took more than three hundred of Thach Tuyen's royal family, ran him over in a car, and threw his body into the Chuong Ha River, causing blood to flow profusely. He knew this could not be saved, so he told his disciples to stop performing the festival.

No matter how many words of advice he used, Thach Ho's violent personality was difficult to change.

A few months later, suddenly a horse, whose mane had burn marks, ran from Trung Duong gate to Hien Duong gate, then ran to the northwest, then disappeared. Seeing this, He said:

- Disaster is coming!

In November, Thach Ho held a banquet for his officials in front of Thai Vo palace. He suddenly raised his voice and chanted:

- Palace! Palace! The thorn tree has become a forest, tearing people's clothes!

Sure enough, right on the rock outside the palace, a thorn tree suddenly grew. Returning to the temple, he looked up at the Buddha statue and lamented:

- How sad! From now on there is no more respect!

Ask yourself again and answer yourself:

- Can it last for three years?

- Impossible! Impossible!

- Can it be maintained, two years, one year, one hundred days, one month?

- Impossible!

At this point, he stopped saying another word, then returned to his room and told Phap To:

- In the Year of the Tiger, chaos gradually arose. In the year of Ky Hoi, the Thach family perished. Before this disaster arises, I must enter nirvana soon.

Having finished speaking, he asked his disciples to send a farewell letter to Thach Ho:

- All things must of course change, and the body and life are the same, they cannot last forever. I am the same, so I want to enter nirvana. When I was alive, I was grateful to the Great King for your kindness and hospitality, so now I especially report from you.

Thach Ho sadly said:

- Without hearing what illness the Venerable has, why do you want to become a citizen?

Having finished speaking, Thach Ho himself came to greet him. He said:

- Death and life are immutable arguments. The length of one's lifespan is also determined by intention, it cannot be extended by oneself. When studying religion, one must focus on virtue and integrity. Virtue lies in not being lazy or lazy. If virtue is not defective, then death is the same as birth. Acting contrary to the righteous path in order to attain eternal longevity is not my wish. Even though the Great King had the heart to pay respect to the Buddha's teachings and build magnificent temples, he implemented a tyrannical policy, clearly betraying the holy teachings. If you don't wake up and change, you will never be blessed. If I repent often, change my mind, and show kindness and virtue to the good people, making the country's fortunes last forever and everyone admiring and admiring the religion, then I will have no regrets even if I die!

Thach Ho sobbed, knowing he would pass away, so he ordered someone to build a tomb. On the eighth day of the twelfth month in the year 348, Buddha Do Trung passed away at Nghiep Cung Pagoda, at the age of one hundred and seventeen years. Scholars throughout the country are sad and sad like a national funeral.

After Phat Do Trung passed away, Thach Lac buried him in Lam Chuong, west of Sai Mach. Thach Ho also personally shrouded his body into the coffin, then brought his staff, robe and bowl to put it inside.

When Nhiem Man was the assistant director, he opened the coffin and saw only a staff and alms bowl, but no body. The people said to each other:

- During the month that Buddha Do Trung passed away, someone saw him by the river.

Hearing this, Thach Ho became suspicious that he had not passed away yet, so he went to open the coffin, but did not see the body.

There was a hole in His left chest, forty centimeters deep, all the way to his stomach. While still alive, the intestines in his stomach often flowed out, so he used flowers to stop them. Reading the scriptures at night, he opened the flower and suddenly a halo of light shone, making the whole room bright. During his teenage years, he often went to the water, took out his intestines, washed them, and then put them back in his stomach as before.

Not long after Buddha Do Trung entered citizenship, Luong Duc rebelled. The next year, Shi Hu died, Ran Man usurped the throne, changed the country's name to Wei, so history called it Ran Wei. Ascending the throne, Nhiem Man killed the entire Thach family. The meaning of Nhiem Man's middle name is 'thorn tree', in accordance with the prophecy of Buddha Do Trung in the past: "thorns become forests, piercing people's clothes."

As soon as the war broke out, he felt sorry for the innocent people who were killed, so he displayed his supernatural powers to influence Shi Le in Tuong Quoc and Shi Ho in Nghiep Do. He used secret mantras to save many living beings, and used scent to save people in danger; He heard the sound of the spirit calling and sat in one place and knew about luck, so he was revered and admired by Thach Lac and Thach Ho. His descendants, Thach Tuyen and Thach Thao, also often came to ask for advice. He kindly advised the Thach people with their violent temperament, imbuing the people with grace.

If it weren't for Buddha Do Trung, with the violent and violent temperament of Thach Lac and Thach Ho, countless innocent people's lives would have been torn to pieces, and it would have been difficult for pen and ink to record them all. Regarding Thach Lac and Thach Ho, he often spent a lot of effort and energy to remind and encourage them that they should use the Buddhist spirit of compassion, joy, and forgiveness to rule the country and the people. He used divine power to save hell on earth at that time. The kings of the Five Lakes and sixteen countries often killed people like cows and buffaloes without distinction. Buddhism advocates not killing. Over many generations, the Ho tribe has often believed in Buddhism, so they have reduced their violent habits. That is the positive contribution of Buddhism at the time.

His body is eight meters tall, his gestures are gentle and gentle. He understood all the profound scriptures and was well versed in secular books and scriptures. When lecturing the sutras, he only proposed the tone, allowing the audience to naturally understand the beginning and the end, and clearly understand the meaning.

Buddha Do Trung's religious life not only used divine power to convert kings, lords and subjects, but also often focused on preaching sutras and preaching the Dharma, and founding temples. Cao Tang Truyen wrote: "Buddha Do Trung thoroughly explained the profound sutras and understood the world."

Although he was not a great translator like Truc Phap Ho, he had a deep understanding of the true meaning of the sutras and the worldly treatises.

When explaining the scriptures, he was able to accurately express the basic principles, making the listeners clearly understand the meaning of the literature from beginning to end. Not only did he use profound words to explain the scriptures, but he also applied the spirit of compassion, joy, and forgiveness to the masses, and devotedly rescued them in times of hardship, disaster, and danger.

His propagation of Buddhism not only had a wide influence throughout Central Earth but also spread to Thien Truc, causing dozens of famous monks from Thien Truc, Khuong Cu, etc. to travel countless miles, wade through countless deserts, and climb mountains and wade streams to pray for teachings like Buddha Dieu, Subhuti, etc. In the country, Dao An, Truc Phap Nha, etc. also crossed mountains and rivers. Come and listen to him preach the sutras and preach the Dharma. All of them are filled with wonderful, mystical and profound principles.

Buddha Do Trung once said:

- The place where I was born is more than nine hundred thousand miles from Nghiep Do; left home to become a Christian for one hundred and nine years; teeth never touch wine; Do not eat rice after noon; If you do not follow the precepts, do not practice; There is no desire, and there is no constant desire; There are more than a hundred people who come to seek enlightenment from far away regions; There are hundreds of thousands of followers from one generation to the next; built eight hundred and ninety-three pagodas throughout Central Earth; Dharma propagation flourished, unlike the previous ones.

Buddha Do Tung Tac said that the place of birth was more than nine hundred thousand miles away from Nghiep Do, which is Thien Truc. He had one hundred and nine lower layers. He passed away at the age of one hundred and seventeen (348), that is, he became a monk at the age of eight. He arrived in Luoyang at the age of seventy-nine, at the end of the Western Jin Dynasty, the fourth year of Yongjia (310).

'Do not touch the teeth when drinking wine, do not eat after noon, do not practice if it is not in accordance with the precepts, do not be greedy, do not seek anything', proving that Buddha Do Trung not only has full supernatural magical powers, but also personally worships and strictly observes practical precepts. Not drinking alcohol means keeping the precept of not drinking alcohol. Not eating rice after noon means observing the precept of not eating at the wrong time. All actions do not go against the precepts, and do not give rise to desires or desires.

Mr. Dao An once went to Nghiep Do city to study precepts under the court of Buddha Do Trung. However, Mr. Dao An only learned a little part, not completely. Mr. Dao An encountered chaos again, so he kept running for refuge. In the year 370, Mr. Dao An came from Tuong Duong to Chang'an. He heard the foreign monk, Dam Ma, recite the Hinayana Abhidharma precepts, so he increased his knowledge of precepts. Later, Venerable Dao An again asked the monk Truc Phap Niem in Luong Chau to write the precepts in Sanskrit, and asked Venerable Dao Hien to translate, Hue Thuong took notes. The translation from summer to winter was complete, so there was a whole set of bhikkhu precepts. Since this book of precepts was translated, it has become clear that the previous books of precepts were mostly wrong. Mr. Dao An considered Buddhist precepts and rituals in Central Earth to be equally important, so he seriously practiced them. Therefore, when propagating the Dharma, Mr. Dao An paid special attention to precepts. In fact, it was Mr. Dao An who inherited the teachings of Mr. Buddha Do Trung.

Buddha Do Trung told himself that there were hundreds of thousands of followers, and he established eight hundred and ninety-three temples. Buddha Do Trung's work of propagating Buddhism in Central Earth was truly great and rare. Thanks to witnessing firsthand the extraordinary and extraordinary miraculous powers of Buddha Do Trung, believers raced to donate material to build the pagoda. Because he had no desires or desires, he never kept money privately, but only used all the donated resources to build pagodas and stupas, propagate Buddhism, and make Buddhism flourish throughout the Central region.

Not only did he build temples, but he also practiced Buddhist rituals such as celebrating Buddha's birthday. According to Cao Tang Truyen, on the occasion of Buddha's birthday, on the eighth day of the fourth month, Thach Lac often personally went to the temple to attend the Buddha's bathing ceremony. Because he used divine power to save Thach Ban's life, Thach Lac often entrusted his children and grandchildren to the temple, allowing those children to be inspired by the Buddha's teachings, so that they could later believe and practice them.

During the time of Thach Lac, Trung Tho initiated a great statue ceremony on Buddha's birthday, the eighth day of the fourth month. The book Dong Tan Mausoleum, Nghiep Trung Ky, writes: "Thach Lac often made four-wheeled carts out of sandalwood, more than ten meters wide, more than two hundred meters long; made a golden Buddha statue, placed on the cart; on it was a picture of nine dragons spraying water. He also made wooden Taoists, using his hands to rub the Buddha's belly; and made more than ten wooden Taoists, over two meters tall, all dressed in robes, walking around and worshiping the Buddha, and then personally placing incense in the incense burner. Just like a real person, when the car runs, the wooden person follows, and when the car stops, everything stops."

Thach Lac had people make chariots out of sandalwood, then made nine water-spewing dragons and wooden Taoists who rubbed the Buddha's belly to represent the act of bathing the Buddha. Make more than ten monks out of wood, wear robes, walk around on all four sides, and offer incense and worship, to express the wish for peace and happiness in the world.

Inheriting the custom of making statues of the Five Lakes and sixteen countries in Northern China, Northern Wei King Thai Vo De, reigning as Dinh Do Dai Dong, in the years he first ascended the throne, also made statues like that on Buddha's birthday. Wei Shu Thich Lao Chi, wrote: "As soon as The Patriarch ascended the throne, he also followed the deeds of Thai To and Thai Tong, often discussing Buddha Dharma with highly virtuous monks. On the eighth day of the fourth month, a parade of Buddha statues was held on all the roads. The king himself sat on the city gate, scattered flowers as offerings, and even worshiped."

During the Eastern Han Dynasty, Buddhism was introduced into China from King So Vuong Ying, Zac Dung, Han Emperor, etc. They considered Buddhism to be the same as Taoism, so it became Buddhism in the fairy form or Buddhism in the form of Taoism, with the most important things being praying for rain or curing diseases. During the Three Kingdoms period, Truc Phap Ho and Chi Khiem translated many sutras, but for the masses, it was very difficult to absorb and understand the meaning of Buddhism. They only worship pure reason, not greed. Therefore, they only need to pray to Buddhism for things like praying for rain, healing illnesses, or showing strange signs of inspiration. Responding to the people's desire to admire the strange mystical arts, Buddha Do Trung came to North China and used his magical powers to convert them. If Buddha Do Trung only specializes in translating sutras, then I'm afraid his work of propagating Buddhism will be less effective.

The great disciples of Buddha Do Trung.

noi_dung:
15A. Mr. Buddha DieuBuddha Dieu came from Thien Truc to study with Buddha Do Trung, and often resided at Thuong Son Pagoda. Buddha Dieu also has strange supernatural powers, and has shown many kinds of miraculous changes like Buddha Do Trung. He also once entered a tiger's den on the mountain and predicted the moment of his death. Later, he suddenly passed away. Over the next few years, eight lay disciples went to Son Tay to cut wood and saw Buddha Dieu sitting on a high rock. They were horrified and asked:

- The Venerable is still alive!

He replied:

- I'm alive!

Returning, they found His burial place, then opened the coffin, but did not find the body.

(Buddhist Buddha Dieu and Nghiem Phat Dieu are completely different. Phat Dieu is from Thien Truc, and is a disciple of Buddha Do Trung. Nghiem Phat Dieu is a Chinese who once translated the Dharma Kinh Sutra with the novice Thap Hue Chuong Cu in the reign of Emperor Lingdi of Han.)

Among the great disciples of Buddha Do Trung, the most prominent were Dao An, Truc Phap Nha, and Tang Lang.

noi_dung:
15B. Venerable Dao'an - Established the foundation of Chinese BuddhismDuring the Eastern Han Dynasty, the translators Thien Truc, who began to translate the classics from Sanskrit into Chinese, were An The Gao and Chi Lau Ca Sam. In terms of spreading and translating Hinayana scriptures, An The Cao is the most outstanding person, so he is forever respected and admired by the world.

An anthology of prefaces and lists of copies of the sutras by Mr. An The Gao and other translators in the early days of Buddhism, Mr. Dao An. Dao An's position in early Buddhism was very important. Indeed, the three great men of early Buddhism were Buddha Do Trung, Kumarajiva, and Dao An.

Mr. Dao An was born in the reign of Vinh Gia, at the end of the Western Jin Dynasty (312), from Phu Lieu in Thuong Son (near Chanh Dinh district, He Bac province). At that time, because the Five Lakes and sixteen countries occupied the North China region, famous monks and scholars slowly migrated south, to the Yangtze River basin in Jianye (Nanjing). The culture in the north also moved to the south, so the culture in North China gradually declined.

At that time, Buddhism developed in the Thuong Son region. According to 'Bhikkhu Nyu Truyen', book one is written about Bhikkhu Tri Hien. The nun was originally from Thuong Son, surnamed Trieu; Father's name is Tran. Prefect Do Ba originally believed in Hoang Lao's religion but hated Buddhism. At that time, King Phu Kien ordered an investigation of the monastery. Do Ba took the opportunity to inspect the pagoda and saw nun Tri Hien's elegant appearance and clear voice, so he had an evil mind. Therefore, Do Ba ordered nun Tri Hien to live alone, then forced them to have sex. Nun Tri Hien refused, preferring to die than break the precepts. Do Ba was angry and took a knife to attack, slashing nun Tri Hien more than twenty times, making it impossible for her to walk. After leaving for a while, Do Ba suddenly came to his senses and repented. From then on, Do Ba diligently practiced vegetarianism and kept the precepts, earning King Phu Kien's respect. Do Ba also often sews robes and clothes to make offerings to the monks.

This story proves that in Thuong Son at the time Dao An was born, Buddhism was widely developed, so there were monks and nuns practicing the religion.

Because his parents died early, Mr. Dao An was raised into a good man by his brother Confucius.

At the age of seven, Mr. Dao An understood the meaning of the Five Classics. As for the books, he immediately remembered them clearly after just looking at them once or twice, making the people in the area very respectful. Although his nature is clear, his appearance is very ugly. On His biceps, there is a large lump of flesh, an inch round, that can be pulled up or down. Because of that, later generations called him Bodhisattva Mudra.

When he became a monk at the age of twelve, his teacher looked down on him, so he only told him to go work in the fields. For three consecutive years, he worked diligently, without any resentment or resentment. During that time, he strictly maintained the precepts and did not violate any pride. A few years later, he asked his original teacher to teach him the scriptures. The original teacher then gave him the Sutra of the Elder Commentary, which had more than five thousand words. He took the sutra out into the field. Taking advantage of the break, he looked through this set of sutras, then in the evening returned to the temple, gave it back to his master, and requested another set of sutras. The original teacher blamed:

- Yesterday I gave you this sutra. Before I could read it thoroughly, I quickly returned it to Me. Why do you want another book?

He said:

- I have memorized that sutra, and can recite it myself!

The original teacher was half-believing and half-skeptical when he heard this, but he also gave him the Sutra, The Sutra of Light and Bright Concentration, which has about a hundred thousand words. (This sutra was translated into two different versions by Chi Lau Ca Sam and Chi Dieu. This is a sutra belonging to the Mahayana system, so the meaning is profound and not easy to understand. Currently it is included in the Tan Tu Tripitaka, Mahayana Sutra, volume fifteen. This sutra is also called the Samadhi of the Accomplished Instrument of Light.)

Just like before, in just one day, Mr. Dao An finished memorizing the Sutra of the Master of Light and Concentration, so he returned to the temple and returned it to his original teacher. This made the teacher even more suspicious, so he asked Mr. Dao An to read it again. He then recited it thoroughly, not missing a word. When the original teacher saw that, he was very surprised and recognized Mr. Dao An's talent. Later, Mr. Dao An followed his original teacher and received full ordination. Before receiving full ordination, he met monk Tang Tien. According to the fifth book 'The Legend of Cao Monk', Master Tang Tien was from Ky Chau, a disciple of Thuong Son Nhuan. He and Master Tang Tien were very compatible, so before parting they made an appointment:

- When you get old, don't forget your classmates!

After receiving the full precepts, his master told him to go consult and learn the Dharma from Buddha Do Trung. At that time, at a time when the Five Lakes and sixteen countries were fighting and causing chaos everywhere, he fled to the Son Tay region for refuge. In the preface to the Dao Dia Sutra, he wrote that he was born during the time of the destruction of the Western Jin. When the Huns invaded the North China region, his master died and separated from his Dharma friends, so he took refuge in Son Tay, in the Tan Son mountain.
