At that time, the monk Chi Dam preached at Nhan Mon, the monk Truc Tang Phu (a Thien Truc person, maintained strict precepts, studied treatises, and understood the scriptures) at Nghiep Do, the monk Truc Phap Te in Thai Duong (Bamboo Phap Te was the writer of the book 'Gao Dat Samana's Story', and was a major disciple of Truc Phap Tiem), together with him studied the Dao Dia sutra and the Amitabha Sutra. Next, he went to Thuong Minh pagoda in Kinh Chau, developed a belief in Maitreya Bodhisattva, then went to Prefaceng mountain to meet monk Tang Tien (his old Dharma friend in Thuong Son) who was in retreat there.

In the year 335, he came close to Buddha Do Trung at a temple in Nghiep Do city. At that time, he was twenty-five years old, and Phat Do Trung was one hundred and four years old. At that time, Thach Ho moved the capital to Nghiep Do. As soon as he saw Mr. Dao An, Mr. Phat Do Trung praised him continuously, and talked all day long. Seeing His ugly appearance, the masses felt disdain. Buddha Do Trung then told them:

- This person has profound knowledge and far-reaching scholarship that none of you can match!

He believed in Buddha Do Trung as his teacher. Every time he finished preaching the sutra, Buddha Do Trung asked him to preach again, but the crowd did not believe him. One time, the masses said together:

- Waiting for Kun Lon (showing Mr. Dao An's dark face) to discuss, we decided to question him until we lose.

As soon as he finished preaching Buddha Do Trung's words, the crowd kept asking questions. To the deep doubts of the mass of fellow students, each and every one of His Holiness answered and explained clearly, so everyone was impressed and said:

- Taoist Bi's words terrified four villages.

He followed his teacher for fourteen years, until Buddha Do Trung passed away in the year 348. Buddha Do Trung explained the important points of the scriptures, so he deeply understood them. Furthermore, thanks to learning the majestic and virtuous teachings of Buddha Do Trung, he always focused on the precepts. According to the preface on the Bhikkhu's precepts, Mr. Dao An wrote about the Buddha's teachings in the book 'Exit Tripitaka' as follows: "The three dharmas of precepts, meditation, and wisdom are called the gateway to the path, and are the important dharma to enter Nirvana. Precepts are the cessation of three evil deeds. Meditation prevents and prevents scattered thoughts. Wisdom is a wonderful medicine to save all illnesses. Only by completing these three dharmas can one attain enlightenment. Using these three methods is also consistent with the religion. Whether at home or as a monk, the first thing is to keep the precepts as the basis. Therefore, the Tathagata takes the precepts as the most important thing in the teachings In foreign countries, the precepts are also respected. Each temple has a person who holds the precepts position and preaches the precepts to the public every month. From dusk to morning, they recite all the sutras and encourage each other to maintain the precepts. If anyone violates the precepts, they will be immediately expelled.

He wrote again: "The first great dharma was transmitted to Dong Do not long ago. The monks have received the precepts since the reign of Qin Shi Huang, but the translators of the precepts are very rare, so the previous people only passed on to the next. During the Venerable Do's reign, most of it was corrected! I lived in Nghiep Do and studied a few parts, but it was not complete, and then I encountered a chaotic life, what a pity!"

At that time, he used to reside at Hang Son mountain, but also often went back and forth to Nghiep Do. When he arrived at Hang Son mountain in Thai Hanh, he built a temple and changed his secular clothes, becoming the clothes of a monk. From then on, the temple on Hang Son mountain was his center for propagating Buddhism. Prefect Lo Ham in Vo Ba, heard of his reputation for noble morality, so he asked the monk Man Kien to invite him to open the sutras. However, he refused, but Lo Ham kept asking, so in the end he had to lecture on the sutra. Because he was one who had the strength to study the sutras and had a reputation for profound morality, monks and laity flocked to listen to the sutras. Every time he preached the sutras, everyone praised him. At that time, Hue Vien was twenty-one years old, and Hue Tri was eighteen years old. They went to Hang Son together to become disciples of Dao An. According to the sixth book 'The Story of Cao Tang', Hue Vien originally wanted to go to Jiangdong to follow Pham Tuyen Tu to study the hidden dharma. However, because the war was spreading everywhere, Hue Vien could not go south. Luckily, Mr. Hue Vien met Mr. Dao An at Quan Ta. As soon as he met Mr. Dao An, Mr. Hue Vien happily said:

- This person is My Teacher!

Thach Ho died, Thach Dao succeeded him, then sent the monk Tru Xuong Bo to welcome him to stay at Hoa Lam Vien, and build a monastery there. Staying there for a while, he felt that the fate of the Later Trieu Dynasty was about to reach a critical point, so he led his followers to leave Hoa Lam Vien and go to Khien Khau mountain. Sure enough, Ran Min rebelled in 350, leading to the destruction of Later Zhao. He told them:

- Nowadays, natural disasters, pests are raging, and thieves are rebelling on all sides. We are gathered here together, living together is very difficult and difficult, but we cannot disperse and separate. What a dilemma!

Therefore, he led his followers to the Royal Palace in Nu Lam mountain, then worked in the fields to make a living. However, because that place was not safe, he soon led his followers across the Yellow River to Luc Hon, residing in a cave, picking wild fruits and vegetables to make a living, but still not giving up his studies. However, the suffering is not over yet. At that time, Yen Dich and Mo Dung Tuan led troops to attack Nhiem Man. The army besieged Luc Hon, so he alone took refuge in the south at Tuong Duong. When the crowd came to Tan Da, but that place was not peaceful, he said:

- Currently, we are facing bad times, war and chaos. Without a king to protect and protect, the work of propagating Buddhism would be difficult to complete. Educate as many sentient beings as possible. If the king supports it, this will be easy.

They all said:

- In all things, we listen to Your words.

He told Truc Phap Thai to go to Duong Chau, and said:

- There are many wise men there. They all worship Buddhism.

The reason he said this was because in a chaotic situation, if he wanted to maintain the Sangha, he needed the support of a great benefactor. Therefore, he led his followers to Tuong Duong.

According to the fifth book 'The Tale of Cao Tang', Truc Phap Thai was a dharma student with him in his youth. At that time, Truc Phap Thai and him fled to Tan Da. Later, he told Truc Phap Thai to go to the capital. When saying goodbye, Truc Phap Thai said:

- The Dharma Master propagates teachings and resides in the Northwest region. I have to go to the southeast to propagate Buddhism. Each of us has a different place to preach the Dharma. Today, we solemnly say goodbye. See you in the future in the Pure Land.

Afterwards, Truc Phap Thai went down to Duong Chau with more than forty disciples such as Dam Nhat, Dam Nhi, etc. At Duong Khau on the east side of the Truong Giang River, on the way to Duong Chau, Truc Phap Thai became seriously ill, so he had to stay there. Chanh Tri Hoan On was ruling Kinh Chau, so he sent someone to bring offerings to Truc Phap Thai. Mr. Dao An also sent his disciple Hue Vien to inquire about Truc Phap Thai's illness.

He again told Truc Phap Hoa to go to Sichuan to practice meditation:

- The mountains there are majestic and magnificent, it is a very good place to practice.

According to the book 'Cao Tang Truyen', Master Truc Phap Hoa was Dao An's fellow student when he was young. Master Truc Phap Hoa is famous for his virtue of respect and humility. The teacher followed Dao An's teachings, and because he wanted to preserve the congregation from being scattered, he led his disciples into the Sichuan region. There, the reputation of Master Truc Phap Hoa became even more famous. Later, when he heard that Tuong Duong was in turmoil, he left Sichuan, went to Truong An, and lived at Duong Binh Pagoda. Next, Master Truc Phap Hoa and Venerable Dao An went over Tang Lang's Kim Du cup.

Having just broken up with monks Truc Phap Thai and Truc Phap Hoa, he led more than five hundred followers like Hue Vien, etc. straight to Tuong Duong, hoping to find a spacious ashram that could accommodate hundreds of followers. That year, he was over fifty years old.

One time, just past the Bach Ha River, it was dark and then a heavy rain fell. He and his followers had no shelter, so they just continued walking straight through the rain. On the way, they passed a house. In front of the house there are two pillars; In the middle there hangs a grass basin, with a capacity of about one square meter. Seeing this, He called out loudly:

- Lam Bach Thang!

The owner ran out in horror, because his name was Lam Bach Thang. We had never met before and were called by our correct names, so this owner was very impressed with His divine power and warmly welcomed us. The crowd later asked:

- How do you know the owner's identity?

He said:

- Two pillars come together to form 'Lam'. In the middle there hangs a tub of grass, with a capacity of about one cubit, which is 'Bach Thang' (one cubit is equal to one hundred surplus of rice). Hop Lai into Lam Bach Thang!

Arriving at Tuong Duong, he immediately began the work of propagating Buddhism. At that time, general Hoan Lang Tu, who was conquering the west, was stationed in Giang Lang and sent people to invite him to temporarily stay in Giang Lang. Then, the governor of Tuong Duong, Chau Tu, invited him to return to Tuong Duong. Seeing that Bach Ma pagoda was too narrow and could not accommodate all the monks, Chau Tu helped him build Dan Khe pagoda. Later, many famous people came to help build the temple. In addition, he also built a five-story Buddha tower and created more than four hundred monk rooms. The governor in Luong Chau sent tens of thousands of pounds of bronze for him to create a sixteen-meter tall Buddha statue with a radiant appearance. Former Qin King Phu Kien also sent officials to buy gold and silver to create a seven-meter high reclining Buddha statue. There is also a gold Buddha statue, a jade Maitreya Buddha statue, a brocade Buddha statue, and a brocade Buddha statue. Every time there is a dharma conference to preach the sutras, Buddha statues are placed in the lecture hall, and then arranged with phan treasures; The pearls surrounding the Buddha statue shine with sparkling golden light. The believers who came to attend the Dharma conference to preach the sutras could not help but feel sincere reverence and worship. However, there was a bronze statue brought back from abroad, but the image was very strange, so the public could not bear to worship. He said:

- This statue is very dignified, but it has a disproportionate bun on its head.

Having finished speaking, he told his disciples to take this statue to the smithy and fix its bun. Forging for a while, suddenly there was light shining from all directions, making the whole room bright. Looking closely at the bun, I saw a relic lying in it. The crowd witnessed this with their own eyes, so they repented together and became respectful. He told the crowd:

- Each Buddha statue has a different appearance, but all of them are inherently full of many spiritual inspirations. Therefore, there is no need to bother making changes.

Therefore, he told his disciples to stop fixing the Buddha's bun. He already knew that there would be relics in the bun, so he deliberately told his disciples to forge the Buddha's bun, hoping to instruct them. This story has been passed down for generations. Therefore, we know clearly that at Dan Khe Pagoda, in addition to the Shakyamuni Buddha statue, there are many other Buddha statues, and also relics.

Xiangyang is not only a traffic connection between North China and Central China, but also a strategically important place. Famous artists of the time often gather there. Therefore, there were many of His disciples there. In total, he stayed in Tuong Duong for about fifteen years. There, he preached the Prajnaparamita Sutra many times. This sutra was brought by Chau Si Hanh's disciple, Phat Nhu Dan, from Vu Dien country to Luoyang, and then translated by the monks Vo Xoa La and Truc Thuc Lan. He also annotated and summarized the book Quang Tan Prajnaparamita translated by monk Truc Phap Ho.

A noble man named Tap Tac Si lived in Tuong Duong, had great eloquence, and was famous at that time. He had also heard about His virtue. Knowing that he had come to Tuong Duong, he went to pay his respects. As soon as he sat down, he called himself 'Tu Hai Tap Tac Si', meaning his eloquent talent, no one in the world could compete with him. He then replied 'Di Thien Thich Dao An', which means that in all the world, there is only one Dao An. His writing style and his are compatible. Contemporaries referred to the symmetrical pair of famous scholars and monks. As soon as Tap Tac Si arrived at the temple, he met the boy festival, so he brought more than ten pears. He took those pears, cut them into small pieces, and then distributed them to the crowd. Regarding his education and morality, and the way the congregation maintained the precepts according to regulations, he admired and praised him constantly, so he called him an 'extraordinary Taoist'. In a letter sent to prime minister Kien Khang, he wrote: "Here there is a magician Dao An, an extremely outstanding Buddhist. He leads hundreds of followers, appoints committees to lecture on sutras, or conducts sacrificial ceremonies. He acts diligently, and does not use magical powers or magic to bewitch and terrorize the eyes and ears of others. He also never used authority or force to rule over small people, but the followers all respected each other, and always respected each other. always adhere to the precepts and regulations in their practice and practice. I have never seen such a Dharma monk, knowledgeable in internal and external scriptures, pure in the calculation of yin and yang, and leisurely in the Dharma. He is the same as Phap Lan, Phap Dao, etc.

His noble and virtuous name resounded everywhere, causing Eastern Jin Emperor Hieu Vo to also issue a letter of praise: "The Dharma Master Dao An is extremely virtuous, has converted morality, not only saves living beings at present but also sets a shining example for posterity."

Emperor Hieu Vo worshiped and offered him many gifts, and treated him like a king. Not only did Eastern Jin Emperor Hieu Vo Martial in the south worship him, but Former Qin Fu Kien in the north also said:

- Tuong Duong has Thich Dao An, called the spirit. I want to summon the Wizard here to help rule the country. Later, Phu Kien sent troops to attack Tuong Duong, capturing Dao An and Chau Tu. Phu Kien told the explosive general Quyen Duc:

- I used a hundred thousand troops to attack Tuong Duong, but I only got half of them!

Quyen Duc asked:

- Who is that?

- Dharma Master Dao An is one person, and Tap Tac Si is half a person.

Therefore, it is clear how much the kings and people of his time respected Him!

Phu Kien then invited him to become the abbot of Ngu Trong Pagoda in Truong An. When leaving Tuong Duong, he told his disciples like Hue Vien, etc. to go to Giang Nam region, and went alone to Truong An. Although he said he would disperse his followers, when he arrived at Truong An, thousands of monks flocked to Ngu Trong pagoda to study under his court. Therefore, his industry of spreading Buddhism spread everywhere. Thanks to his profound virtue, he did such extensive Buddhist work.

As soon as Phu Kien established the country, there was still chaos in the country, but gradually all four directions were pacified. The eastern border area reached Thuong Hai, the west bordered Quy Tu country, the south included Tuong Duong, the north reached Han Han, leaving only Kien Nghiep (the capital of Eastern Jin) that had not yet submitted. Every time he talked with courtiers, Phu Kien clearly stated his intention to unify the Giang Ta region. Phu Kien's younger brother, Phu Dung, and courtiers such as Thach Viet, Nguyen Thieu, etc., all sadly advised them not to start an army because they could not change Phu Kien's mind. Therefore, they came to ask him to advise Phu Kien:

- The Lord wants to use troops to attack Dong Tan. Why don't you (Dao An) give advice for the people?

He immediately came to advise, but Phu Kien still did not listen.

One time, Phu Kien went out to Dong Uyen garden and invited him to go on a journey with him. Official Quyen Duc said:

- I heard that when Thien Tu is away from home, only mandarins can follow. When Mr. Dao An became a monk, why did he and Thien Tu travel far away together?

Phu Kien got angry and said:

- The morality of Dharma Master Dao An is truly admirable. The whole world and I are not as good as the Dharma Master, not to mention how the price of going to a long distance is not commensurate with the Dharma Master's morality!

Therefore, Phu Kien sent Quyen Duc to invite him to the throne.

When he heard the name of Kumarajiva in Tay Vuc, he kindly advised Phu Kien to quickly request that holy monk to come to Trung Tho to translate the sutras. On the contrary, Kumarajiva had also heard of Dao An's heroic reputation, so he often said that Dao An was a saint in the East. Twenty years after Mr. Dao An became naturalized, Mr. Kumarajiva went to Central Earth.

Not only was he proficient in poetry, but he was also proficient in internal and external classics, yin and yang, math, and other studies. Therefore, the aristocracy in Truong An also used to be close to Him to learn, and often said:

- Without studying with Mr. Dao An, it is difficult to understand the meaning!

For four years in Chang'an, he preached the Prajnaparamita Sutra twice each year. In August 382, ​​he went to Nghiep Do to perform the ceremony for his original teacher, Buddha Do Trung. At Nghiep Do pagoda, he also invited the Dharma Master Kumarajiva Buddha to read the Four Agama Sutras in Sanskrit, then invited Truc Phat Niem and Truc Phat Ho to translate. He again invited two Venerable Bamboo Buddha Niem and Bamboo Phat Ho to translate the Vairocana Sutra, and then write the preface for that sutra himself. In 383, Venerable Sangha Bat Trang translated the commentary on Ping Ba Sa, the commentary on Abhidhamma and Prajnaparamita, and the Sutra on Ba Tu Tan Tap; Mr. Dam Ma Nan De translated the Sangha Nhat A Ham Sutra; Venerable Dao An wrote the preface to those commentaries. Abhidhamma Prajnaparamita is the most complete treatise of the Hinayana Pitaka. Therefore, with regard to the Tripitaka, he thoroughly understood all three canons of sutras, rules, and treatises.

Chinese Buddhism worships the Venerable Tan Dau Lo (or Pindola - Pindola -, meaning Immovable, and is one of the sixteen Arhats, who does not enter Nirvana but lives forever in the world. The Venerable often appears at religious gatherings to demonstrate and support the dharma conference) starting with Dao An. Because Mr. Dao An commented on many sutras, every time he annotated any sutra, he prayed for the Three Jewels' blessings. However, because the responsibility of exegeting the scriptures was heavy, and he was afraid that it would not be in accordance with the Buddha's will, he made a vow:

- If my notes do not contradict the Buddha's intention, then please show auspicious signs to confirm.

One night, he dreamed of a Pham monk with white hair and long eyelashes who said:

- Your comments on the scriptures are in accordance with Buddha's ideas. I was originally a monk who did not enter Nirvana in the Western Regions. I will support you in propagating Buddhism. For my sake, prepare to make offerings.

Therefore, Mr. Dao An set up a ceremony for the monks to make offerings to the Venerable Tan Dau Lo.

Twenty years after Mr. Dao An became a citizen, Mr. Prajna Da La and Mr. Kumarajiva translated the book Ten Reciting Rules. At that time, his disciple Hue Vien knew that the monk his master had dreamed of in the past was the Venerable Tan Dau Lo. From then on, it was customary to make offerings to Venerable Tan Dau Lo.

Later, Tan Phu Kien refused to listen to his advice, so he sent Binh Duong Cong Phu Dung to lead two hundred and fifty thousand vanguard troops, while he himself led six hundred thousand troops to march south. King Jin sent Chinh Lo, general Ta Thach, and royal historian Ta Huyen in Tu Chau to lead troops to resist. As a result, Phu Kien's army was defeated at Bat Cong Mountain. History calls it the battle of Phi Thuy. The Eastern Jin army chased and killed the Phu Kien army. Phu Dung was also fatally injured. In the end, Phu Kien alone rode his horse back to Truong An, only to be killed by Murong Sung, causing the destruction of the Former Jin dynasty. Because he refused to listen to his advice about conquering the south, Phu Kien lost his country and lost his life.

At that time, at the temple, he and his disciples like Phap Ngo, etc. knelt before the statue of Maitreya Buddha, vowing to be reborn in the Tushita heaven. On the twenty-seventh day of the first month in the year 384, the twenty-first year of Kien Nguyen, suddenly a monk with an ugly and dirty appearance came to the temple and asked to stay overnight. Because there was no room left in the temple, arrangements were made for the monk to rest in the lecture hall. That night, Venerable Duy Na saw that strange monk flying back and forth from the window, so he was horrified and rushed to tell him the news. Immediately, he went to the lecture hall to worship and ask the foreign monk's purpose for coming to the temple. The monk replied:

- Because I want to save you, I came here!

He said:

- My sins are so heavy, how can I be saved?

- Of course I can save you! However, one must wash and bathe the statue of a holy monk to be able to have his wish fulfilled!

Having finished speaking, the monk then showed him how to practice wood training. He received and asked the monk where he lived. The monk then pointed up to the sky, towards the northwest, then suddenly the clouds and mist there disappeared, and the solemn and wonderful landscape of the Tu Suat heaven appeared completely before his eyes. Late at night, several dozen people in the temple also saw the sights of Tu Suat heaven clearly. He followed the teachings and prepared all the Dharma tools to perform the woodwork ceremony. At that time, suddenly there were a few dozen unusual young monks running into the temple to play, and then in a moment, they performed the woodwork ceremony themselves. That is the premonition of Maitreya Buddha.

On the eighth day of the second month in the year 385, without any illness, he told his disciples:

- We have to go!

Having finished speaking, He passed away. The coffin was buried at Ngu Cap Pagoda in Truong An.

Before he passed away, there was a hermit named Vuong Gia who often came back to greet him. He told the King:

- The world is so chaotic. Disaster often strikes the body! Please leave this world with Me!

Vuong Gia replied:

- It's true what He said. However, I still have some outstanding debt. Please go first.

At that time, Dao Truong led his army to attack Truong An. The troops of Dao Truong and Phu Dang fought fiercely with each other but could not decide who won or lost. At that time, Dao Truong summoned Vuong Gia and asked:

- Can I take the throne?

Vuong Gia said:

- Get it.

Hearing this, Dao Truong became angry and said:

- If it's okay then say it's okay. Why do you say that strategy can be obtained?

Having finished speaking, Dao Truong beheaded Vuong Gia. That is the debt that the Vuong Gia must pay. As soon as Dao Truong died, his son Dao Hung defeated Phu Dang and became emperor. The self-name of King Dao Hung is 'Luoc'. That is the meaning of what Vuong Gia said when he won the throne.

His disciple is Dam Gioi. In the fifth book 'The Tale of Cao Tang', it is recorded that, in old age and illness, he often recites the name of Maitreya Buddha. Mr. Dam Gioi's disciple, Tri Chanh, asked:

- Why doesn't Master make a vow to be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss?

Mr. Dam Gioi said:

- In the past, I, along with the Venerable Master (Mr. Dao An) and eight other brothers, vowed to be reborn in the Tushita heaven. Venerable Dao An and my fellow monks have passed away, only I remain here. Right now, it is time for me to urgently pray for rebirth in the Tushita heaven.

As soon as he finished speaking, a ray of light shone throughout his whole body, making Mr. Dam Gioi's appearance peaceful and bright, and then he peacefully passed away. Dam Gioi's grave was also built right next to Dao An's grave.

In addition, his old Dharma friend, Truc Phap Phu, at Thuong Minh Pagoda in Kinh Chau, also often prayed to be reborn in the Dau Suat heaven, praying to see Tu Thi.

Regarding the precepts, Mr. Dao An once said:

- Precepts are the basic foundation for enlightenment. In the Tripitaka, precepts occupy the most important position.

During the Three Kingdoms period, Cao Wei period, Dam Ma Ca La translated the Tang Ky Luat, and together with Emperor Dam translated the Four Parts Law. Next, the two of them set the Yet Ma Dharma and actually practiced the ordination. During his lifetime, Dao An was still not complete. While residing in Nghiep Do, Mr. Dao An tried his best to study the precepts, but because of the war, his wish was not fulfilled. When he arrived at Tuong Duong and then passed through Truong An, Mr. Dao An met the monk Dam Ma Thi, who specialized in precepts, so he was very happy. Therefore, he requested the monk Dam Ma Thi to recite the 'Ten Recitations of the Great Bhikkhu Precepts', and asked the monk Truc Phat Niem and Truc Dao Hien to translate. Furthermore, when the monk Supreme Patriarch from Cau Di country brought back the book 'Ten Recitations of Bhikkhus' Precepts', Venerable Dao An also invited two monks Truc Phat Niem and Truc Dao Hien to translate that book. According to the book 'Cao Tang Truyen', Mr. Dao An wrote the following rules for monks and nuns to practice: "The formality of monks and nuns, that is, the practice ritual, has three rules: The first is the dharma of pilgrimage, sitting on the throne, the upper scriptures are preached. The second is the dharma of the six times of practicing the religion, eating and chanting at the right time. The third is the practice of the dharma of Bodhisattva, scribbling, repentance, etc. All pagodas and monasteries in the world must follow this method."

The content of this statement is not clear, so the book 'Simplified History of the Sangha' in the Song Dynasty explains as follows: "The first is to go on a pilgrimage and sit down to preach the sutras. The second is to repent for the six times. The third is to practice the Bodhisattva dharmas."

As for pilgrimage, there are two types: First, pilgrimage is also an act of almsgiving, that is, offering incense to Buddha, to express thorough sincerity; People sitting in high positions (seniors) must diligently practice this practice; At the dharma conference, seriously practice this. Second, pilgrimage simply means offering incense. Next, 'meditation at the top' means that if the monks are small, they sit and practice meditation, but if the monks are high, they go up to the throne to preach sutras. Holding the platform to preach sutras is a Buddhist ritual that originated from Dao An. Before going up to preach the sutras, you must offer incense to Buddha. 'The Upper Lecture Sutra' means to preach in sentences. When preaching the sutra, we must plan and clearly distinguish three parts: the introduction, the main sect, and the circulation. It must be in the same order as the narrative and explanation. Furthermore, at the altar to preach the sutras, a Buddha statue must be installed and a phan treasure garland should be hung.

Second, the six times of repentance, that is, during the six times (morning, noon, afternoon, evening, early evening, midnight, late night) you must meditate and worship the Buddhas. You must go from the right to circumambulate the Buddha. This is a ritual of the Thien Truc people. In addition, Mr. Dao An also wrote the repentance ceremony for the monks and nuns in six periods of practice.

In terms of eating, only eat once a day at noon. 'Ordering the Dharma Session' means chanting the Buddha's name at any time.

Third, practicing Bodhisattva, that is, monks gather at the precept hall every fortnight and perform repentance rituals before reciting the precepts. If any monk violates the precepts, he must come before the monks to confess and beg for repentance. The monks judge and judge according to the world's importance. Next, a monk stepped up to the throne and read the precepts, while the others had to gather to listen. This is the Dharma taught by the World-Honored One. In Central Earth, initiated by Dao An, the Bodhisattva Dharma was truly implemented, and had a great influence on the Buddhist Sangha later on.

Before Dao An's lifetime, Chinese monks were often given Dharma names by worldly teachers, so they were mixed without limits. He advocated that the original teacher of Buddhists is Shakyamuni Buddha, so monks must take the name Shakyamuni. He said:

- The original teacher, no one is more noble than the Shakyamuni family.

At first, no one paid attention to His words. Later, when the Tang Nhat A Ham Sutra was translated into Chinese, people clearly understood that Buddha taught:

- When rivers flow into the sea, they no longer have the names of rivers. Therefore, although the customary names are different, the monks must all be called 'Thich' race.

This clearly shows that his words are in accordance with the scriptures, so from then on, the monks all took the surname Thich as their head.

Saying goodbye to Mr. Dao An at Tan Da, Master Truc Phap Thai went to Duong Chau, became the abbot of Ngoa Quan Pagoda in Kien Nghiep citadel, and was respected and respected by the Eastern Jin kings, and gathered more than a thousand followers, so the Dharma propagation industry developed widely.

Master Truc Phap Hoa said goodbye to Mr. Dao An at Tan Da, then went to Thuc land, then returned to Truong An with Mr. Dao An to actively edit the translated canonical books.

Mr. Dao An was born in a time of war and chaos everywhere. Not only is food scarce, but even life is always at risk. Living in that time of chaos, although he had to flee here and there many times, Mr. Dao An was still determined to practice without interruption, and devoted himself to propagating Buddhism, training high monks such as Mr. Hue Vien, Mr. Dam Duc, etc., and educating followers, building pagodas and temples like the tower pagoda in Hang Son, seven meditation halls in the east of Thuong Minh pagoda, Dan Khe pagoda in Tuong Duong with fifty monasteries. Besides these careers, Mr. Dao An also diligently annotated the scriptures, helping researchers clearly grasp the true meaning of the scriptures. He also established the basic religious foundation for the Sangha according to the precepts.

Before Mr. Dao An's time, Chinese Buddhism was still young, only in its early stages. The work of translating the classics was started by Mr. An The Cao and Chi Lau Ca Sam, and then many other translators joined in. However, for those who have the mind to study and practice, when reading the classics translated in the early days, it is mostly difficult to grasp the meaning, let alone achieve the profound meaning. Therefore, the book 'Exit Tripitaka' records Dao An's words as follows: "The sutras have been translated for a long time, but the text of the sutras is old and sometimes erroneous, causing the profound meaning to be lost and obscured. Each time the sutra is lectured, we only discuss the meaning roughly."

According to this, the early period of Chinese Buddhism, in terms of translating the classics, was almost mature. However, ancient translations often have many mistakes, so the profound meaning is lost, and the meaning is not clearly understood. Therefore, speakers of ancient translated scriptures often explain the general idea or just recite them. Therefore, the meaning of the scriptures is not clearly understood.

To understand the true meaning of the sutras, Chau Si Hanh had to go to the country of Vu Dien to seek the text of the Prajnaparamita Sutra in Sanskrit. However, the translation of this sutra has not yet exposed the profound meaning, so when preaching, Mr. Dao An only preached the general idea. Therefore, for Buddhist scholars, Dao An deeply sympathized with this difficulty, so he determined to research the true meaning, then proposed the profound and wonderful weaknesses of the scriptures by commenting. According to the book 'Exit Tripitaka', Venerable Dao An annotated and summarized the sutras as follows: Light Tan Prajna interpretation (1 volume), Light Tan Prajna extracts the middle interpretation (1 volume), Radiation Prajnaparamita extracts standard rituals (1 volume), Radiance Prajnaparamita extracts summary explanations (2 volumes), Radiance Prajnaparamita with complete interpretation (1 volume), Dao Hanh Sutra with mantras (1 volume), Great Twelve Doors Mantra (2 volumes), Minor Twelve Doors Mantra (1 volume), Liu Bon Birth and Death Sutra (1 volume), Secret Explanation of the Vajra Sutra (1 volume), Mind Retention Brahma Sutra (1 volume), Perfection of the Thousand Life and Four Thousand Heavens Sutra of Infinite Wisdom (1 volume), Human Origin and Desire Sutra with Explanation (1 volume), An Ban Thu Yin Sutra (1 volume), Amitabha Sutra of Entering the Great Path Mantra (2 volumes). The Earth Sutra Mantra (1 volume), the Ten Dhammapada Meanings (1 volume), the Meaning Commentary Mantra (1 volume), the Abhidharma Ninety-Heaven Commentary on the Sutras (1 volume), the Commentary on the Thirty-Two Characters (1 volume).

Mr. Dao An authored the following books: Three Realms of Gods of Chaos Hao Tap Luc (1 volume), General Assembly Sutra Table of Contents (1 volume), Da Sa Thai Can (1 volume), Response to the Dharma of Similarities (2 volumes), Western Vuc Chi (1 volume).

In fact, in the history of Chinese Buddhism, Dao An is hailed as the First Patriarch of sutra commentary. Therefore, in the book 'Exit Tripitaka' it is written: "Clarifying the meaning of ancient scriptures, starting from Mr. Dao An."

Not only commenting on the sutras, Mr. Dao An also composed and composed many preface articles, to recount how the sutras were translated through the process, where this sutra came from, what the title of the sutra is, etc. For each treatise on the canon, Mr. Dao An expressed his own interpretation. His prefaces, rewritten in the book 'Exit Tripitaka' are as follows: An Ban Mantra, Amitabha Sutra, Amitabha Sutra, Human Origin of Desire Sutra, Lieu Bon Samsara Sutra, Twelve Doors Sutra, Great Twelve Doors Sutra, Dao Hanh Sutra, Synopsis of the Hop Phong Light-Sun Sutra, Maha Prajna Paramita Sutra, Tang Nhat A Ham Sutra, Tao Earth Sutras, Ten Dhammapada Meanings, Abhidharma, Binh Ba Sa, Bhikkhu Dai Gioi.

The book 'Exit Tripitaka' writes: "First, Venerable Dao An recorded the sutras, because he wanted to promote the Dharma. Venerable Dao An also invited foreign monks such as Sangha Bat Trung, Dam Ma Nan De, Sangha Deva, etc. to translate many sutras, then together with his junior brother Truc Phap Hoa, they selected the text and carefully examined the meanings of the sutras. The sutras. The newly translated dictionary has been edited and edited like that."

This shows that Venerable Dao An often invited foreign monks to translate the sutras and together with his brother Truc Phap Hoa, edited and revised the text to determine the true meaning of the sutras.

There are three difficult things when translating: First, when the Buddha was still alive, he preached the Dharma according to the people's instincts and nature. The customs of the times change depending on time. Therefore, refining ancient texts to fit current texts is difficult. Second, it is difficult for ordinary people to estimate the realm of saints and sages. The Buddha's teachings have been taught for thousands of years and hundreds of generations, so translating them to the Buddha's liking and making it easy for ordinary people of the Dharma-Ending Age to understand the Buddha's words is very difficult. Third, the first collection of sutras right after the Buddha entered Nirvana was by Venerable Mahakasyapa convening five hundred great Arhats, and Venerable Ananda and Venerable Upa Ly simultaneously re-proclaimed the Buddha's teachings, a thousand years have passed. Therefore, in today's life it is difficult to review the scriptures for changes, additions or deletions.

Therefore, according to Mr. Dao An's stance, when translating the sutras, the meaning of the Sanskrit scriptures must be kept intact.

In addition, Mr. Dao An was also instrumental in writing a table of contents for the translated sutras, making it easier for scholars to look up the translator, date, etc., such as the Index of the General Assembly of the Sangha. Master Hue Kieu later followed that and wrote more. The teacher wrote: "From the Han and Wei dynasties to the Eastern Jin, the scriptures were translated quite a bit, but the name of the translator, the date, and the title of the sutras were not clearly stated, making it difficult for later people to look up. Therefore, Venerable Dao An collected all the lists, wrote a chronology, translator, era, chapter, new and old, and compiled them into a sutra. From then on, the scriptures had a place to rely on, truly thanks to Venerable Dao An. Scholars in all four directions They all raced to learn from Mr. Dao An."

According to this, throughout the dynasties, monks and lay people from the Western Regions to China translated at their convenience, so the translations were often chaotic. Not only are the translations sometimes lacking in detail, but the translator and the era are not clearly recorded. Therefore, Venerable Dao An reviewed the newly translated sutras, clearly wrote the name of the translator, era, place, and judged to distinguish between true and false sutras, completing the work of editing the table of contents.

However, the book 'Sutta Summary' was lost and could not be found. Currently, in the book 'Exit Tripitaka' by monk Monk Huu, from volume two to volume five, there is a summary of the content and details of the book 'Sutta of the General Assembly Sutra Table of Contents'. Therefore, the table of contents of the ancient scriptures is still in the book 'Exit Tripitaka' by Master Tang Huu. If it weren't for Mr. Dao An's book 'Sutras of the General Assembly', I'm afraid it would have been difficult for Master Sangha to compose the book 'Exit Tripitaka'.

In addition, Mr. Dao An also wrote the book 'Pure Land Commentary', but unfortunately it has now been lost. Although he had never been to the Western Regions, thanks to his scholarly intelligence, Mr. Dao An recorded the geography, products, people, and current situation of Buddhism in the Western Regions, passed down orally by monks and lay practitioners of the Western Regions, and wrote it into the record 'Western Regions', very accurately.

tieu_de: 15B.1. Mr. Hue Vien - First Patriarch of the Pure Land Sect
tom_tat: Dao An's chief disciple is of course Hue Vien. Mr. Hue Vien was originally a top disciple, and the most powerful right-hand man of Mr. Dao An....
noi_dung:
15B.1. Mr. Hue Vien - First Patriarch of the Pure Land SectDao An's chief disciple is of course Hue Vien. Mr. Hue Vien was originally a top disciple and the most powerful right-hand man of Mr. Dao An. When chaos broke out in Tuong Duong, Hue Vien and a few dozen disciples went to Mount Lo Son to practice. Thanks to his dedicated efforts, Mr. Hue Vien succeeded in researching and cultivating the three disciplines of concentration and wisdom. Regarding the aspects of establishing the basic foundation for Buddhists to develop faith and practice, most of them are thanks to the merits of Hue Vien, typically the founding of the Pure Land sect, reciting the Buddha's name to pray for rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

In the year 401, Kumarajiva entered Chang'an, translated the scriptures and spread the ideas of Khong Prajna Prajna of Nagarjuna and Devadava.

At that time, in Lo Son, Mr. Hue Vien strictly maintained the precepts, practiced meditation, and secretly nurtured talented and virtuous monks. He inherited the method of meditation and Bodhisattva principles founded by Mr. Dao An.

He was born in 334, originally from Lau Phien in Nhan Mon, with the last name Co, coming from a lineage of scholars. When he was born, it was at the time when Buddha Do Trung was being worshiped by Shi Lac and Shi Hu of Later Zhao, and was their advisor. Later, he followed Dao An, a disciple of Buddha Do Trung, to study Buddhism. At that time, Shi Ho allowed Chinese people to officially become monks. At that time, although in the eyes of the Chinese people, Thach Ho was an unscrupulous monarch, but he greatly valued literature, so in Nghiep Do he founded the five scholarly classics, the strongest of which was Confucianism.

During his youth, he not only received Confucian education, but was also deeply influenced by Buddhist thought. Even though he was young, he studied tirelessly; His divine nature truly surpasses that of mortals. At the age of thirteen, he followed his uncle Linh Co to Hua Xuong, Luo Duong to study. Therefore, he learned the Six Classical Sutras and Lao Zhuang's thoughts. His uncle's secret intention was that he wanted him to pursue official positions and make his sect shine. From the age of thirteen to twenty-one was the period when he specialized in studying classics. His demeanor and knowledge are sublime, and he is a talented Confucian scholar, making ordinary people admire him.

Before 350, Buddha Do Trung passed away, and Sang Lang entered Mount Tai. As soon as Thach Ho died, Central Earth was in chaos, enemies emerged like locusts, causing the people to suffer hunger and thirst, and even eat each other. Therefore, the majority of famous scholars and monks often migrate to the Giang Nam region. At the age of twenty-one, he also decided to go to Giang Nam, follow Pham Tuyen Tu, and learn hidden magic. However, the situation at that time was chaotic, causing the road to the south to be cut off, so he could not fulfill his wish. On the way, he heard the reputation of Mr. Dao An promoting Buddhism at Thai Hanh mountain, so he changed his mind and went there to consult and study. At that time, accompanying him was his younger brother Hue Tri. As soon as he met Mr. Dao An, he immediately showed respect and joy and said:

- This is my teacher!

When he heard Mr. Dao An preach the Prajna Sutra, Mr. Hue Vien suddenly became enlightened and said:

- The doctrines of Confucianism, Taoism, and Hundred Schools are all nonsense!

Therefore, he decided to throw away all the teachings of Taoism and Confucianism, become a monk along with his younger brother Hue Tri, and follow Dao An to study Buddhism. From then on, Mr. Hue Vien always followed Mr. Dao An for twenty-five years. After becoming a monk, he diligently practiced diligently, keenly studied and recited the scriptures, became wise, mastered the great Dharma, and took upon himself the responsibility of propagating the Dharma. For a person, like Mr. Hue Vien, who is well-versed in Lao Zhuang's thought and the ancient scriptures to renounce the world and become a monk, one must have a strong mind to do so.

In the past, only because his uncle provided him with money, he was able to study safely. Becoming a monk, no one supported him, so he was poor and miserable, to the point of not having money to buy fabric to make robes, or clothes to wear in the cold winter. However, when it comes to practice, brother Hue Vien is never lazy. A fellow monk, Dam Duc, knew about this and helped them with money. Knowing that Hue Vien was inherently extraordinary and would become a dragon statue in the future, and knowing that Dam Duc supported him financially, Mr. Dao An praised:

- Dam Duc is truly a person who knows others well!

Dam Duc became a monk at the age of sixteen, and later followed Dao An to Dan Khe Pagoda, and then to revive Truong Sa Pagoda in Giang Lang.

Hue Vien's spirit is high and profound, his will to always seek the great path, different from ordinary people. Therefore, Mr. Dao An praised:

- The Dharma was passed down in Dong Do, thanks to this Hue Vien place!

It is true that this statement is true, in the history of Chinese Buddhism, Hue Vien left behind a great career, allowing the basic foundation that Dao An had laid to be widely developed.

Thanks to hearing Mr. Dao An preach the Prajnaparamita Sutra, Mr. Hue Vien decided to throw away his Lao Trang knowledge and become a monk to study Buddhism. In his letter responding to the hermit Liu Di Dan, he wrote that in retrospect, he had focused his attention on the secular learning of Confucianism, mistakenly taking it as the ultimate truth in the world, but after looking at Lao Zhuang's thought, he realized that Confucianism was nothing more than a vain discussion that changed with the situation. Furthermore, when I first studied Buddhism, I judged for myself that the teachings of Buddhism were infinitely more profound and profound than Lao Trang's thoughts.

One time, at the age of twenty-four, he took the stage to preach the Prajnaparamita Sutra. A certain person, because he did not understand the meaning of 'Real General', came to ask. He used Lao Trang's writing to explain the essential points, and explain doubts, so that the other person could understand the essence. From then on, Mr. Dao An specifically allowed him to use classical sentences to explain Buddhism. Fellow monks such as Phap Ngo, Dam Huy, etc. also attended that sutra lecture and were very impressed with him.

Phap Ngo, disciple of Dao An, had 'extraordinary enlightenment' and great ability. In 377, at Truong Sa Pagoda in Giang Lang, Phap Ngo taught more than four hundred disciples.

Dam Huy became a monk at the age of sixteen. Even though he is not yet an adult, he has already appeared on the forum to lecture on the sutras. Later, Dam Huy became an outstanding disciple of Dao An at Thuong Minh Pagoda in Kinh Chau. Outstanding disciples of Mr. Dao An such as Phap Ngo and Dam Huy, etc. often admired Mr. Hue Vien's talent. This shows how high Hue Vien's outstanding talent was.

While staying at Hang Son mountain, because of the Nhiem Man riot (340), the society was insecure, so Mr. Dao An had to go to Vuong-hoc in Nu Ngot mountain. There, he took refuge not long before crossing the Yellow River to Luc Hon. Encountering natural disasters, food shortages, and at the same time Mo Dung Tuan was besieging Luc Hon, Dao An had to move to Tan Da. That place was also insecure, so Dao An told his younger brother Truc Phap Thai to go to Duong Chau, and Truc Phap Hoa to go to Thuc land, then lead his disciples to Tuong Duong. At that time, Mr. Dao An was fifty-four years old, and Mr. Hue Vien was thirty-two years old. For twenty-five years, Hue Vien always followed Dao An closely to practice and study the Prajnaparamita Sutra, the An Ban Thu Yen Sutra, the Amitabha Sutra, etc. to lay the foundation for practice and Hinayana meditation practice. For Mr. Dao An, the Mahayana Prajnaparamita Sutra and Hinayana meditation are both teachings passed down by Shakyamuni Buddha, without any contradiction. The teachings are based on Mahayana scriptures. In terms of practice, use the Hinayana scriptures as the protocol.

During his stay in Tuong Duong, Hue Vien's understanding was similar to Mr. Dao An.

In 378, King Fu Kien of Qin sent troops to capture Tuong Duong. The Thai governor of Luong Chau was a well-defended Chau Tu, but the following year Tuong Duong fell. Chau Tu was taken to Truong An. Out of respect, Phu Kien also invited Dao An to Truong An. Therefore, Mr. Dao An's congregation was forced to disperse. During the farewell, Mr. Dao An kindly advised all his long-time disciples, but never said a word to Mr. Hue Vien. Therefore, Mr. Hue Vien knelt down and said:

- I am the only one who has not been taught by you. Why am I different from other monk brothers?

Mr. Dao An smiled and replied:

- For a talented person like you, what else do you have to worry about? So I don't need to tell you anything.

From then on, to Mr. Hue Vien, Mr. Dao An no longer taught anything. After that, Venerable Hue Vien and Hue Tri, along with several dozen disciples, came to stay at Thuong Minh Pagoda in Kinh Chau. At that time, Mr. Dao An's disciple, Monk Monk, was holding the position of abbot of Thuong Minh Pagoda. This temple, for Dao An's disciples, is truly a monastery that gives rise to superior dharma conditions. There, Dam Duc was offered offerings to Truong Sa pagoda by the governor of Truong Sa, Thang Ham.

Not long after staying at Thuong Minh Pagoda in Kinh Chau, Mr. Hue Vien went to La Phu Mountain. Previously, La Phu mountain was the place that Mr. Dao An appointed for Mr. Hue Vien and his brother Hue Vinh to reside and practice together. On the way south, at Tam Duong in Jiangxi, we saw Lo Son mountain, quiet and extraordinary; It is truly a wonderful practice landscape that can help you calm your mind and meditate. Therefore, Mr. Hue Vien chose Long Tuyen monastery as a place to reside and practice. Because the monastery is far from the source of the stream, there is a lack of water. Mr. Hue Vien then went outside, propped his staff on the ground, and said:

- If I have a relationship with this mountain, then this place will suddenly flow into the stream.

As soon as he finished speaking, a clear stream suddenly appeared from the ground. Not long after, the Tam Duong area suffered from drought. Mr. Hue Vien then went near the pond and chanted the Sea Dragon King Sutra. While chanting, suddenly a bamboo boat flew straight up into the sky from the middle of the lake, then rain poured down, causing the people to reap a good harvest. From then on, Long Tuyen Vihara was renamed Long Tuyen Pagoda.

At that time, seeing that the monastery was cramped, his fellow disciple Hue Vinh invited Hue Vien to come and stay with him at Tam Lam pagoda. The deputy historian Hoan Y also said:

- Lord Hue Vien went to the south to propagate the Dharma. The monks followed him, becoming more and more numerous. Although I wanted to make offerings, I couldn't help it. The monastery was too narrow.

Therefore, he built another pagoda on the east side of Lo Son mountain, which history called Dong Lam pagoda, to serve as a residence for Mr. Hue Vien.

One time, when a monk from Thien Truc described the statue of Buddha saving a poisonous dragon, Hue Vien went behind the mountain, next to the stream, chose a place to build a hermitage, called Buddha Image Hall (influenced by the architecture of the main hall in the style of Thien Truc or Tay Vuc country), then according to the description, he imagined and drew a Buddha statue. Looking from a distance, it looks like the Buddha statue is sometimes hidden and sometimes appears in clouds and smoke.

One time, a fisherman told the governor of Guangzhou, Dao Khan, that he often saw a strange light shining on the sea surface for ten consecutive days. When Dao Khan heard that, he personally went there to take a look. He saw the Buddha statue created by King Ashoka floating on the sea and radiating light. Therefore, he requested Han Khe Pagoda in Vo Xuong. One day, Master Tang Tran, the abbot of Han Khe Pagoda, left the pagoda for Ha Khau. At night, I dreamed that Han Khe pagoda burned down, but only the room worshiping the Buddha statue, thanks to the dragon gods surrounding and protecting it, was still intact. Waking up, Master Tang Tran quickly returned to the temple and saw that everything had burned down, but only the room where the Buddha statue was left intact. Later, Dao Khan went to Giang Chau to accept the position of deputy historian, so he sent someone to invite him back. As soon as the Buddha statue was placed, the boat sank. Dao Khan from a young age was famous as a talented martial artist. However, because he lacked a faithful mind and only requested the image with power, it did not work as expected. Later, Dao Khan's son, Dao Pham, heard that Hue Vien founded Dong Lam Pagoda, so he wholeheartedly invited the Buddha statue to that pagoda to worship. In the past, the Buddha statue was so heavy that it caused the boat to sink, but now thanks to sincerity, the Buddha statue is light, so it was brought back to the temple. This story displays the miraculous power and profound virtue of Hue Yuan.

At Dong Lam Pagoda, Mr. Hue Vien also established a meditation hall, so that meditation practitioners could meditate together.

In 385, Dao An became a naturalized citizen in Chang'an. In 386, Hue Vien finished building Dong Lam pagoda. In 383, the monk Sangha Deba came to Chang'an and translated the Abhidharma Abhidharma. After the demise of Later Qin Fu Kien, the monk Sangha Deba along with Phap Hoa came to Lac Duong. Reviewing the old translations, he found that there were many mistakes, so Phap Hoa asked monk Devata to correct them. During the Dao Hung dynasty, Phap Hoa returned to Truong An.

Before Mr. Dao An's lifetime, there were translators who translated the treatises of the Sarvastivada sect, but they were not yet completed. Because he had collected sutras, Venerable Hue Vien always wanted to request foreign monks to translate those sutras. Hearing that the monk Sangha Devadā had come to Luoyang, Hui Yuan invited him to Loshan in the year 391. There, the monk Sangha Devadā translated the Abhidharma Abhidhamma by Phap Thang and the Three Dhammapada Sutras by The Sage. These two treatises belong to the Sarvastivada sect. However, the writings of the monk Devata Sangha are very simple, unpolished, only focusing on keeping the original idea. Because he had studied the Hinayana Abhidhamma treatise under the court of Dao An, Venerable Hue Vien considered these two volumes of sutras as treasures, and worked hard to sharpen and polish the text.

Although Mr. Hue Vien liked to practice meditation, meditation in the Giang Nam region was very rare, so he sent his disciples Phap Tinh and Phap Lanh to the Western Regions to search for scriptures on meditation. Later, Zen dharma was transmitted to Central Earth, brought by the monk Buddha Da Bat Da La (disciple of the great monk Zen master Buddha Dai Tien).

Tri Nghiem was originally Chinese. He went to Ke Tan country, studied meditation with the monk Dai Tien Buddha for three years, and attained enlightenment for ten years. Tri Nghiem's ​​meditation was often praised by the great Zen master Buddha Dai Tien. The people of Ke Tan country, seeing Tri Nghiem's ​​sincerity in seeking the Dharma, also praised him very much. At that time, the monk Buddha Dai Tien practiced many scriptures on meditation. Due to Tri Nghiem's ​​sincere request, Da Bat Da La Buddha agreed to go to the East to spread the Zen method.

Regarding the Hinayana meditation scriptures, in the Han Dynasty, An The Gao translated the Twelve Doors Sutra, An Ban Thu Y. However, the Mahayana meditation scriptures have not yet been completely translated. Later, at the request of Zeng Rui, Kumarajiva translated the book Zazen Samadhi. This sutra has forty-three verses, created by Kumarajiva. The last twenty verses were created by Mr. Ma Minh. For this set of orthodox Zen sutras, Mr. Hue Vien devoted himself to practice and practice.

Later, in Central Earth, the meditation sutras that the Buddhist monk Dai Tien often practiced were translated by the Buddhist monk Da Bat Da La. Crossing the sea from Ke Tan country to Thanh Chau in Shandong peninsula, Da Bat Da La passed through Truong An. However, Kumarajiva's disciple, Dao Hang, presented a petition to the court, saying that Buddha Dabat Da La's speech was crude, only bewitching the people, going against the Buddha's precepts, etc., so he could not stay in Chang'an. Hearing these words, Dabat Da La Buddha said that his body was as small as a duckweed, but he came and went freely. However, because the wish was not fulfilled, I felt regretful. Later, Buddha Dabat Da La along with Hui Quan and more than forty others arrived at Lo Son in the year 411. As for Dao Hang's refutation at Truong An, it was the disciples' fault, not Buddha Da Bat Da La's fault. For a long time, I had heard about the reputation of Buddha Da Bat Da La, and heard that this monk was coming to Lo Son mountain, so Mr. Hue Vien was very happy to welcome him. Next, Mr. Hue Vien wrote a poem asking his disciple Dam Ung to give it to King Dao Hung and the monks at Truong An, to exonerate Buddha Da Bat Da La. In addition, Hue Vien also invited Buddha Da Bat Da La to translate the Sutra on the Convenient Practice of Meditation.

The Zen Sutras translated by Da Bat Da La Buddha served as the basic foundation for the prosperity of Zen Buddhism in the Jiangnan region. In the past, the meditation sutras translated by An The Cao and Truc Phap Ho were initiated into practice by Tang Tien and Dam Du. When Tri Nghiem went to the Western Regions to seek the Dharma, he invited Buddha Da Bat Da La to come to Central Earth. From then on, Central Earth had newly translated meditation scriptures, which were then inherited and practiced by Huyen Cao and Huyen Thieu.

In Giang Nam, because Mr. Hue Vien practiced meditation skillfully, meditation also flourished. The meditation sutras translated by Da Bat Da La Buddha greatly influenced Mr. Hue Vien's practice of meditation. Furthermore, the Prajnaparamita and Buddha Image Cave were built before the establishment of Dong Lam Pagoda, both due to the influence of Da Bat Da La Buddha's ideology.

According to legend, at Nam Son mountain in Na Gia Ha La country (Nagarahara) there is a shadow of Buddha. This news was transmitted by word of mouth by Buddhist monk Dabat Da La and Sangha Deva, and written down by Phap Hien after the pilgrimage to Thien Truc. Believing in the words of these people, Hue Vien could deeply understand that the connection between Buddha and sentient beings transcends space and time. He was convinced that if he could paint the Buddha's image, it would cause the viewer to initiate the mind of contemplating the Buddha, that is, seeing the Buddha and giving rise to true faith. Therefore, he determined to build the Buddha Image Cave (a cave with the image of Buddha).

Founder of the Buddha Recitation Society (also called White Lotus Society because on the east and west sides near Prajna Dai Dai there are two white lotus ponds, hence that title. At the same time, the lotus flower also symbolizes the body and mind of the practitioner; when achieving liberation, it means overcoming the mud and afflictions;) Mr. Hue Vien is revered by posterity as the first ancestor of the Pure Land. In the seventh month of the year 402, Huiyuan and one hundred and twenty-three people such as Liu Dimin, Truong Ye, Dieu Tich Chi, etc. (mostly lay people), gathered in front of the statue of Amitabha Buddha at Prajnaparamita monastery, vowing to practice reciting the Buddha's Samadhi (according to the Ban Chu Samadhi Sutra) to pray for rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Believers gather there, believing that good and evil retribution permeates all three lifetimes, and is difficult to eliminate. Therefore, day and night they diligently cultivate pure karma, single-mindedly reciting Amitabha Buddha's name, to pray for rebirth. First, each person practices individually. Later, Venerable Hue Vien gathered everyone in the Buddhist Recitation Society to practice reciting the Buddha's name together so that it would be effective as soon as possible. Venerable Hue Vien also wrote the article Dharma Xa Tiet Do Tu (now no longer available) to prescribe the practice of reciting Buddha's name for monks and lay people.

In the article 'Reciting the Buddha's Samadhi and Poems', Venerable Hue Vien wrote that it is called Samadhi because thoughts and emotions are focused single-mindedly, eliminating all delusions. If your thoughts are single, your will will not be scattered, so delusions will be eliminated, your breathing will be light, your spirit will be calm, allowing you to see everything clearly. The merit of reciting the Buddha's name is immeasurable, and practicing it is easy. Reciting the Buddha's name samadhi is very suitable for the Buddha's compassionate vow to save sentient beings. Reciting the Buddha's name leaves the discriminating mind, which means entering samadhi. If you enter the samadhi of reciting the Buddha's name and see the Buddha, your afflictions will be eliminated, and your deep karma will also be cut off. Comparing Buddha recitation samadhi with other samadhis, this dharma is the most superior. Hue Vien's policy is that when reciting the Buddha's name, one must see the Buddha in samadhi.

In the book 'Mahayana Mahayana', there are recorded discussions and questions and answers about reciting the Buddha's name samadhi between Kumarajiva and Huiyuan. In fact, Hue Yuan's method of reciting the Buddha's name is based on the chapter on Reciting the Buddha's name in the Ban Chu Samadhi Sutra. The Conduct of Conduct in the Ban Chu Samadhi Sutra discusses the Samadhi of reciting the Buddha's name. In it, it is clearly stated that reciting the Buddha's name is like seeing the Buddha in a dream, and asking about the Buddha, eliminating all doubts. That means the Buddha appears in concentration due to achieving Buddha recitation samadhi, similar to seeing the Buddha in a dream. It all comes from the mind. The Ban Chu Samadhi Sutra teaches that if one follows the precepts and practices without violating them, then thanks to the practitioner's power and the supernatural powers of the Buddhas, one will attain concentration.

Regarding seeing Buddhas when attaining Buddha-recitation samadhi, Kumarajiva said that there are three cases: First, Bodhisattvas have attained heavenly eyes and heavenly ears, and can go throughout the ten directions, asking Buddhas to preach the Dharma to eliminate doubts. Second, people who do not have supernatural powers, but by constantly reciting Amitabha Buddha's name and focusing their minds on one place, will be able to see the Buddha and eliminate doubts. Third, practice reciting the Buddha's name, whether you have been separated from desire or not, and you can see Buddha statues in your past, present, and future lives in your dreams. Those are three types of concentration, and all are called Buddha-recitation samadhi.

Ban Chu Samadhi is a very effective practice method for Bodhisattvas who have not yet separated from desire. This is the basic method of practice, which makes you concentrate on reciting Buddha's name, attain samadhi, and see Buddha. The Ban Chu Samadhi Sutra teaches that people who practice reciting the Buddha's name, determined to leave words behind, focus only on one mind, often remember to recite Amitabha Buddha in the Western world, emitting bright light to illuminate all ten directions. It is often said in the sutras that the bodies of all Buddhas are born of conditions, have no self-nature, are ultimately static, and are illusory and transformed. Understanding this way, reciting the Buddha's name and attaining samadhi means seeing the Buddha, which is true and not false.

At that time, because the Infinite Life Sutra had not yet been translated, Hue Vien only relied on the Ban Chu Samadhi Sutra translated by Chi Lau Ca Sam to practice reciting the Buddha's name.

In 402, Hue Yuan founded the Buddhist Recitation Society, which attracted many hermits. At that time, the Hu clan nations in the North China region continued to rise and fall one after another. The Eastern Jin Dynasty in Jiangnan also suffered extreme decline: Ton An rebelled; Hoan Huyen plotted rebellion. That is a sign of the demise of a dynasty. People who are fed up with the world are rioting and taking refuge in the increasingly crowded mountains and forests. In addition, at the time when the Eastern Jin Dynasty was first established, the seclusion-oriented Thanh Talk movement was very successful, and at Hoi Ke in Giang Nam, the initiator was Chi Don. At the end of the Eastern Jin Dynasty, due to Ton An's rebellion, society was in turmoil and insecurity. Therefore, Lo Son, a mountain located in the Truong Giang River basin, is a place where hermits often pay attention. Not only does it have a quiet and mysterious landscape, but Lo Son is also a place that does not submit to the power of the royal court, and where Mr. Hue Vien often resides. Although Hoan Huyen ordered the Buddhist monks to be reorganized, he did not dare to touch Lo Son. Therefore, people with the will to live in seclusion often race to Lo Son to practice under Hue Vien's court.

Liu Di Dan was originally a district official. Admiring Hue Vien's reputation and virtue, after his mother passed away, he went to Mount Lo Son to practice Buddhism. He was the one who, along with other Dharma friends, made a vow to recite Buddha's name and pray for rebirth. Half a year later, thanks to always diligently reciting Buddha's name, Liu Di Dan attained Buddha-reciting samadhi, so while walking on the road, he saw the Buddha appearing in the void, emitting bright light, illuminating the whole sky and earth. He again saw his own body radiating yellow light, was covered by robes, and bathed in the precious lotus pond.

Later, Liu Di Dan wrote the book Bach Lien Xa Tse Van. In it, Liu Di Dan said that if you often visualize and recite the Buddha's name, it is very easy to be blessed by Buddha's divine power, samādhi power, and the merits and vows of the Buddha, causing you to quickly achieve your karma.

Later, Venerable Hue Vien and King Hoan Huyen discussed the adjustment of the Buddhist Sangha and the practice of monks not needing to pay homage to the king. Thanks to him, the Sangha at Lo Son keeps the precepts very seriously, along with the practice of cultivating Buddha's name, becoming more and more solid. In addition, at the age of sixty-eight, seeing that life is impermanent, Hue Vien switched his study of Prajnaparamita to reciting the Buddha's name in samadhi, hoping to be reborn at the time of his death. Therefore, because they admired Hue Vien's practice of reciting the Buddha's name, many people flocked to Lo Son.

Contemporaries often praised eighteen wise men in Lo Son such as: Venerable Hue Vien, Venerable Buddha Da Bat Da La, Venerable Buddha Da Xa, Dao Sanh, Hue Vinh, Hue Tri, Tang Due, Dam Thuan, Dam Hang, Dao Binh, Dao Kinh, Dam Than, Liu Di Dan, Loi Thu Tong, Zhou Tich Chi, Nam Duong Tong Binh, Nam Duong Truong Da, Nam Duong Truong Thuyen.

Venerable Huiyuan and Kumarajiva asked and answered each other, which later generations wrote as 'Mahayana Mahayana Meaning Chuong', or questions and answers about the essential meaning of Mahayana between Huiyuan and Kumarajiva.

1/ Questions and answers about the true dharmakaya

Mr. Hui Vien asked: The sutras say that the dharma body is neither coming nor going, neither born nor destroyed, and is similar to nirvana, which the Bodhisattva dharma body can see. If so, why is the dharma body different from the physical body?

Kumarajiva replied: Buddha's Dharma body is born from the Dharma nature. The physical body is the transformed body of Buddha, different from the dharma body. The true form of the dharmakaya is the same as nirvana, which is non-doing and non-creation.

Hearing these words, Mr. Hue Vien confirmed: a/ The true form of the dharmakaya is neither coming nor going, and is the same as nirvana of tranquility. b/ The Dharma body is not the body of the four elements and five senses, like the moonlight illuminating the bottom of the water, or like a mirror reflecting images. c/ Dharmakaya is Buddha nature, eternal and unchanging.

2/ Venerable Hue Vien again asked about the true dharmakaya.

Kumarajiva replied: The Hinayana uses the thirty-seven teaching aids, the ten powers, the eighteen unattainable dharmas, and the Buddha's sterilized merits to claim that this is the dharmakaya. The dharmakaya of the Mahayana is without birth and death, with no path of speech, with the same form of nirvana and tranquility, with no outflows of merit, etc. The two types of fetters (afflictions), the two types of obstacles, and all conditioned dharmas, are all illusory and unreal. The Bodhisattva's Dharma body, although it is said to have four elements and five senses, is not the same as the body's changes, and does not have birth and death, appearing everywhere.

3/ Questions and answers about the true dharmakaya.

Mr. Hue Vien asked: Many scriptures say that the Buddha has a full body, is radiant, and is dignified and incomparable. So is the true dharmakaya like that?

Kumarajiva replied: The Secret Sutra teaches that the Buddha's body is not fixed, is free, and appears according to the fate of living beings; This means that each living being sees the Buddha's form differently.

4/ Questions and answers about the lifespan of the true dharmakaya.

Hue Yuan asked: The lifespan of ordinary beings is determined by karma. Where does the Bodhisattva's dharma body decide?

Kumarajiva replied: There are two types of dharmakaya. First, the dharma nature is eternal and unchanging, like space, and separate from all reasoning about the conditioned and the unconditioned. Second, when the Bodhisattva has not yet become a Buddha, but has attained the six penetrations, that is called the dharmakaya. Whether there is a Buddha or no Buddha is born, the dharma nature always remains indestructible.

5/ Questions and answers about practicing to achieve thirty-two good signs.

Hue Vien asked: If a person wants to achieve the thirty-two marks, should he use his body of afflictions and karma to cultivate, or should he use his dharma body to cultivate? If we use a body full of afflictions and karma to cultivate, then the body is already full of afflictions and karma, how can it cultivate the thirty-two good signs? If you use the dharma body to practice, then the dharma body does not have enough verbal karma, so how can you practice? The purpose of practice is to become Buddha. So is the Buddha a true dharma body or a transformed body?

Kumarajiva replied: Although we can use the hypothesis to call the dharmakaya, we cannot seek it based on form. Only when the mind's eyes are pure can one see the Buddha. Even the Bodhisattva of the Ten Levels has not yet seen the true Dharmakaya. Only Buddhas with full Buddha eyes can see.

In Central Earth at that time, there was still no theory of permanent nirvana, only discussing the length and shortness of life span. Regarding this reason, Mr. Hue Vien said:

- Buddha is inherently great, so he does not change. Because there is no change, why is life still long and short?

Therefore, he authored the book 'Dharma nature'. King Dao Tan greatly admired his majesty, morality, and intelligence, so he often wrote poems to request and make offerings constantly, and ordered Dao Sung to present him with a jade Buddha statue. The book Dai Tri Do Luan had just finished being translated. King Dao Tan specially sent someone to bring this treatise to Lo Son mountain, asking him to write a foreword. Seeing that the text of this treatise is very long and has profound meanings, not convenient for beginners to study and study, so he wrote more sections and summaries of the essential meaning, making it into twenty volumes, and also wrote a preface, to clearly indicate the tone, saving scholars a little trouble.

When conquering An Trung Kham, the army passed by Lo Son. Hoan Huyen sent people to invite him down the mountain. He then said that because he was sick, he refused to go down the mountain. Hoan Huyen had to go up the mountain himself. At that time, the left and right mandarins of Hoan Huyen said:

- Previously, An Trung Kham once went to the mountain to pay homage to Hue Vien. I hope that after entering the mountain, Your Majesty will not worship Hue Vien.

Hoan Huyen replied:

- An Trung Kham is about to die, why compare with me!

As soon as he climbed the mountain, Hoan Huyen suddenly bowed respectfully and asked him:

- Confucianism says that the body's hair and hair live with the parents, so one should not dare to harm them. Why did the Great Master cut off his beard and hair?

He replied:

- Confucian scholars establish themselves, so they must preserve their appearance. Practicing Buddhism in Buddhism only preserves the mind's nature. The principle of establishing oneself and practicing religion are not the same.

Hoan Huyen heard this and praised him endlessly. I wanted to ask, but I couldn't open my mouth. A moment later, Hoan Huyen asked:

- Do you have any blessings, Master?

He said:

- May the Great King be at peace, and so will his opponents!

Hoan Huyen praised:

- I have never met someone like the Great Master in my life!

After trying to gain power, Hoan Huyen wanted to pull him in to gain more support, so he wrote a persuasive letter, advising him to follow the government and become an official. However, he wrote a letter of refusal. Not long after, seeing that there were bad things in the Buddha's house, Hoan Huyen ordered some monks to return to the secular world, saying:

- Except for monks who often propagate Buddhism, or strictly maintain the precepts, everyone else must return to the secular world. Lo Son is the residence of monks, so there is no need to check.

Knowing that Hoan Huyen was forcing the monks to return to the secular world, he wrote a letter to him: "Buddhism has been degenerate and has been defiled for a long time. Every time I think about this, it makes my heart restless. I think to myself that this is not the will of heaven, but caused by human beings. Nowadays, I see that the elimination of miscellaneous monks is truly in accordance with the will of heaven, it is only necessary that everything must be clear and clear; upright people can correct those who are evil and hypocritical. These inhumane people will leave the world on their own. If so, the order to eliminate the self-indulgent monks will be effective. Then, the evil people will not have the opportunity to do careless and ignorant things. From then on, Buddhism and the secular tradition will flourish, and the Three Jewels will also flourish."

Because the text of the decree was not yet complete, Hoan Huyen happily received his comments.

tieu_de: 15B.2. His disciples Dao An (Hue Tri, Hue Vinh, Dam Duc...)
tom_tat: Emperor Jin Cheng ascended the throne at a young age, so Yu Bing was his assistant. Duu Bang believes that monks must worship the king, but the minister Linh Ha...
noi_dung:
15B.2. His disciples Dao An (Hue Tri, Hue Vinh, Dam Duc...)Emperor Jin Cheng ascended the throne at a young age, so Yu Bing was his assistant. Duu Bang believes that monks must worship the king, but minister Linh Ha Sung, minister Tru Duc, etc. all disagree. At that time, the historians in the court all agreed with the opinions of Linh Ha Sung, Tru Duc, etc. At that time, the political system was in turmoil, so people did not know where to turn. Staying at Co Thuc, Hoan Huyen wrote a poem to him, saying that monks must pay respect to the emperor: "Monks who do not respect royalty are not in accordance with the situation."

Mr. Hue Vien wrote a poem in response: "Why do we call ourselves monks? Because monks open up the path to liberation for foolish people. We must forget the self, then we will be liberated together with people in the world. The wise men and ordinary people also want that benefit. Furthermore, the robe is not the royal garment. The alms bowl is also not an item of the royal court. The monk is a person who has escaped the world, so he cannot respect the king."

Although Hoan Huyen persistently maintained his opinion, after reading his poetry, he had to step back. After ascending the throne, Hoan Huyen immediately issued an order:

- Buddha Dharma is wonderful and vast, something ordinary people cannot expect to know. Today I have ascended the throne. Because in order to show respect for Buddhism, I decree that from now on, monks do not need to pay homage to the king.

For more than thirty years, his body did not leave the mountain, and his feet did not enter the homes of worldly people. Every time you send off guests, take Ho Khe as the limit, then return. On the sixth day of the eighth month in the year 416, Hue Vien fell ill and passed away without eating or drinking, at the age of eighty-three. Religions near and far mourn.

Hue Yuan's writings such as treatises, writings, engravings, praises, poems, letters, there are ten volumes and more than fifty verses, are recorded in the book 'Exit Tripitaka' as follows: Lo Son
