The work of propagating the Dharma in Lo Son began with Mr. Hue Vien, and three more monks came there to support: Hue Tri, Hue Vinh, and Dam Ung.

II. Venerable Hue Tri also resided and diligently propagated the Dharma in Lo Son for more than fifty years. Later, Mr. Hue Tri went to Thuc land, became the abbot of Long Uyen Pagoda, and widely propagated Buddhism.

III. Mr. Hue Vinh resided at Tay Lam Pagoda in Lo Son, educating many disciples.

IV. Hue Sung. After Mr. Dao An became a citizen, Mr. Hue Sung went to Lo Son to assist Mr. Hue Vien in propagating the Dharma.

In addition, there are three disciples of Mr. Dao An such as: Dam Duc, Phap Ngo, Dam Huy, who often propagate the Dharma in Kinh Chau. Due to the efforts and dedication of these three disciples, Buddhism in Kinh Chau region developed widely.

V. Dam Duc.

When Venerable Dao An was still in Tuong Duong, the prefect Dang Xa in Truong Sa established a pagoda there, then requested Venerable Dao An to send his disciples there to become abbots. Venerable Dao An told Venerable Dam Duc:

- The monk in Kinh So wanted to ask for a master to educate the people there. Besides me, who else is there?

Therefore, Venerable Dam Duc obeyed his orders and went south, then became an abbot at Truong Sa Pagoda. When the bandits raided Giang Lang, Master Dam Duc fled to the Thuong Minh area and established Thuong Minh pagoda there. Giang Lang area was peaceful, then Master Dam Duc returned to Truong Sa Pagoda. Master Dam Duc followed Master Dao An and became a monk at the age of sixteen. He strictly maintained the precepts and studied the Tripitaka thoroughly. When he arrived in Shu, Master Dam Duc was respected and respected by the royal historian Mao Cu, and offered food. One time, because there were eggs in the rice, Master Dam Cu took them out before using them. Seeing his actions of strictly maintaining the precepts, Mao Cu was even more respectful, offering thousands of measures of rice to Master Dam Duc. Truong Sa Pagoda later became an important center of Buddhism in the Giang Lang region.

VI. Phap Ngo also often went to Truong Sa Pagoda to preach sutras and preach the Dharma. Under Master Phap Ngo's throne were more than four hundred disciples.

VII. Dam Huy.

When the war broke out in Tuong Duong, Master Dam Huy and Master Dao An left that area. On the way, Master Dam Huy stayed at Thuong Minh Pagoda (built by Master Dam Duc) in Kinh Chau. There, Master Dam Huy drew a picture of Mr. Dao An's appearance to worship. Since then, believers in Giang Lang area often turn to the west (ie Truong An) to worship Bodhisattva Mudra (ie Dao An).

VIII. Master Dao Lap was originally a disciple of Mr. Dao An in Truong An. Master Dao Lap often meditates alone in a mountain cave. He often sat for seven days without getting up. Later, Master Dao Lap suddenly came down from the mountain, gathered with the monks, and opened the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra. A few days later, he was no longer sick but passed away.

Those are the typical great disciples among the thousands of monastic disciples of Mr. Dao An. They strictly maintained the precepts, practiced meditation to attain great wisdom, and received the teachings of Dao An, then devoted themselves to propagating Buddhism in Truong An, Lo Son, Kinh Chau, Thuc Xuyen, etc.

tom_tat: C. Mr. Truc Phap Nha.
noi_dung:
15C. Mr. Truc Phap NhaC. Mr. Truc Phap Nha.

He is from Ha Gian, dignified and dignified, has a noble demeanor, has a peaceful and free mind, and is not attached to anything. When I was young, I often studied Thien Truong Kinh, Bach Gia history, and other foreign texts. When he grew up, he understood the teachings of Buddhism. Thanks to receiving the teachings of Buddha Do Trung, Truc Phap Nha easily understood the meaning of Buddhism. Because he had mastered Lao Trang's thoughts as a child, a number of great scholars, mandarins, and famous scholars respected him very much and often followed him to study the religion. His disciples are all people who have been successful in studying external scriptures, but there are still many doubts about the teachings of Buddhism. Therefore, he, along with Master Khuong Phap Lang, etc., harmonized the teachings of Buddhism with the historical sutras of hundreds of scholars, the term Lao Trang, to explain Buddhism, calling that method 'Cach Nghia'. For example, he often uses Lao Trang's word 'emptiness' to explain the Buddhist word 'emptiness'. Use the language of ancient books to express the meaning of Buddhism. Later, Venerable Ty Phu, Dam Tuong, etc. applied this method of 'Methodism' to teach his disciples.

Because he has clearly understood the profound meanings, regardless of external scriptures or internal scriptures, he has the ability to communicate and discuss and preach. At that time, he often discussed with Dao An and Truc Phap Thai the mystical meanings and hidden meanings of the scriptures, to clarify the essential meaning of the Buddha's teachings. Later, he established a temple in Cao Ba and gathered hundreds of followers.

In the beginning, Buddhism was widely transmitted to the scholarly class in Central Earth largely thanks to the 'Cach Nghia' method. Therefore, the representative of 'Divine Buddhism' was Truc Phap Nha in the Eastern Jin period.

Dam Tap, a disciple of Truc Phap Nha, used his teacher's teachings as the foundation for spreading Buddhism, so he was highly respected by Thach Tuyen of Later Trieu.

tieu_de: 15D. Mr. Tang Lang at Mount Thai Son
tom_tat: D. Zeng Lang at Mount Tai, revived Buddhism in Shandong.
noi_dung:
15D. Mr. Tang Lang at Mount Thai SonD. Zeng Lang at Mount Tai, revived Buddhism in Shandong.

Mr. Tang Lang was originally from Kinh Trieu. When I was young, I used to travel everywhere to learn about the teachings of noble people, and closely followed the teachings of Buddha Do Trung. One time, while talking with his Dharma friends on the road, He told them:

- In your temple, it seems like someone came to steal things.

Hearing that, they quickly returned to the temple, caught the thief, but had not lost anything. He also has the same supernatural power as Buddha Do Trung. As an adult, he returned to Quan Trung, specializing in preaching sutras, mainly the Prajnaparamita Sutra (translated by Truc Thuc Lan in 291). He maintained the precepts, wore burlap, had aspirations beyond the secular world, was profound in learning, and contemplated good and bad deeds.

During the pre-Qin Dynasty, Fu Kien, in the year of the Yellow Water Era (351), he lived at Mount Tai. On the mountain, there is a mountain valley, called Kim Du, where the surrounding landscape of forests, mountains and streams is very majestic. Therefore, he established a thatched hermitage in that place. Hearing his reputation, more than a hundred people flocked to seek enlightenment. Due to their sincere devotion, He responded without tiring. On Thai Son mountain, there is also a Taoist hermit named Truong Trung. He also had disciples, but he often used his body to educate them.

Mr. Dao An and Truc Phap Hoa once visited him at Kim Du cup. That time, on the way to climb to the top of Thai Son mountain to reach Kim Du cup, seeing the towering mountain, Master Truc Phap Hoa lamented:

- This mountain is so high, and there are so many people who travel up here. If you accidentally slip, you will leave this world and not know where to go!

Mr. Dao An said:

- Hey Dharma Master! As long as the spiritual mind is strong and steadfast, why worry about where you will go in the next life? If the mind has no religion, then there will be such sadness!

King Phu Kien of the Pre-Qin Dynasty sent an envoy to Thai Son, inviting the hermit Truong Trung to return to court. After the audience, Phu Kien gave him robes, but Truong Trung did not accept it, but told the story and unusual movements of Tang Lang to the king. Phu Kien then sent an envoy with a letter to request him to return to the capital. The poem reads: "The Emperor respectfully visits the Most Venerable Sangha. The Great Saint's sublime spirit protects and educates all living beings, like the ocean and high mountains that constantly nurture and give birth to all living beings, and like the heavens and earth that nurture and nurture all living things, sustaining birth and death. This spirit is called Trung Tich. I hope to meet the Saint Sangha in the future. Strictly because the road is thousands of miles long, it cannot be far from the price. Now, I will order the official to take the carriage to welcome him. Please come to Kinh Ba city. I also offer a few pounds of gold to paint the Buddha statue, and thirty tons of thin silk, along with three servants, to serve and clean up for you..."

Along with this, the royal messengers also brought gifts and slaves to make offerings and serve him. He then refused to accept the gifts, and wrote a letter to Phu Kien: "... The poor man had already become a monk, his mind was dry in the deep forests and cold mountains, his spirit was weak, he had never been able to propagate Buddhism. No poor man knew that His Highness sent a letter from afar to inquire about the mountains, then kindly summoned him back to the capital. The poor man was truly grateful for the grace of the Holy Supreme. However, because of his weak strength, he could not endure the long journey. and receive these offerings."

This is an expression of his attitude of not having the chance to enjoy the king's grace, but only preferring to reside in the mountains and forests to keep his pure practice.

When he wanted to regulate the Buddhist Sangha, Fu Kien issued a decree: "The Dharma Master's moral precepts are the highest; the disciples also strictly maintain pure precepts. Therefore, for the congregation at Kun Lun Mountain (ie Mount Tai), there is no need to investigate."

Just like his original teacher, Phat Do Trung, Tang Lang strictly maintained the precepts carefully, so he was respected and respected by Phu Kien. Later, Phu Kien attacked Tuong Duong, then invited Dao An to return to Truong An (as mentioned above).

He was also respected by King Tuoba Khue (386-409) of the Ho clan, who sent envoys to bring offerings to Mount Taishan such as silk, silver alms bowls, etc.

King Dao Hung (393-415) of the Later Qin Dynasty also sent envoys to bring three levels of golden altars, a set of sutras, and a treasure to Thai Son mountain to make offerings to him.

King Dong Jin, Emperor Hieu Vo, also sent letters to visit him. After the Pre-Qin state of Fu Kien was destroyed, the Hebei region was governed by Later Yen Mo Dung Thuy, and the Henan region was governed by Later Yen Murong Duc. These two kings also sent letters and offerings to Him. Mo Dung Thuy sent messengers to bring poems and offerings. The poem reads: "May soldiers no longer kill each other, so that all four seas will be peaceful. Now, out of respect, send messengers to bring one hundred bundles of silk, fifty kilograms of cotton, and three sets of robes, to pray for him to pray for peace in the world."

Nam Yen Mo Dung Duc wrote a poem: "I was originally unvirtuous, was born as a foreigner, entered a time of chaos, and suddenly inherited the throne, all thanks to the Venerable Master and the great gods' blessings. Therefore, not only did I send an envoy to bring silk offerings, but also gave him the title of Dong Te Vuong, granted to the two districts of Thai An and Truong Thanh in Shandong. The letter did not write the whole idea. Please understand my mind!"

Through these words, it is clear that Mr. Tang Lang was given the title Dong Te Vuong by Mo Dung Duc, and was given two districts to build pagodas, monasteries and stupas, and was exempted from taxes to create merit.

When he came to Kim Du valley to set up a thatched hermitage, he often practiced meditation and manifested divine powers to control tigers and save people in the area. However, tigers are usually the reincarnations of mountain gods. He conquered the tiger, which means he made the mountain god believe in Buddha's teachings. Because of his reputation for conquering tigers, contemporaries often called him 'Tang Gonggu'.

Although Tang Lang did not leave behind any writings, he used his body to educate and transform his followers, and used his magical powers and mechanical intelligence to save kings. The thatched hut in his Kim Du cup was later built into Than Thong Pagoda, and was the gathering place for Zen masters and scholars to practice, typically Zen Master Tang Y (who attained Sotapanna status), Zen Master Hang Ma Tang (disciple of Than Tu), etc. Zen Master Hang Ma Tang also used a non-scriptural form to teach his followers like Tang Lang there. The Zen Master also praised Tang Lang as 'A Luu Zen Master'.

tom_tat: Deva Sangha is also called Deva Sangha; The Chinese translation is We Thien. His original nature is Cu Dam, from Ke Tan country. After becoming a monk, practicing...
noi_dung:
16. Sanghadeva (Sanghadeva)Deva Sangha is also called Deva Sangha; The Chinese translation is We Thien. His original nature is Cu Dam, from Ke Tan country. After becoming a monk, he practiced diligently, not caring about the distance of thousands of miles, but went to visit the master to receive his karma. Quickly master the three organs, sutras, and treatises, and his forte is specializing in 'The Abhidharma of the Mind'. With regard to the profound and subtle principles of the sutras, one can attain complete enlightenment. He often recited the treatise 'Three Dhammapadas', and took it as an essential method to enter Buddhism. His style is noble; gentle and humble gestures and actions; Be diligent in teaching your disciples without getting tired. In the pre-Qin dynasty, Fu Kien, during the reign of Kien Nguyen (365-384), he went to Chang'an to promote Buddhism.

At that time, the monk Sangha Bat Trang translated the book 'Ba Tu Tan Ngu'. The monk Dam Ma Nan De translated the Trung A Ham Sutra, the Sangha Nhat A Ham Sutra, the Pi Dam Quang Thuyet Sutra, the Three Dhammapada treatise, etc. At that time, because of the Murong Sung riot, the translation work was interrupted. Furthermore, because of the chaotic circumstances, the translators had to wander everywhere, causing the newly translated sutras to be unable to be edited or edited, causing the text and meaning to be greatly distorted. At that time, Mr. Dao An had just become a naturalized citizen, so no one had the heart to rectify the scriptures that had just been translated. Therefore, Venerable Deva and Truc Phap came to Lac Duong in harmony. At that place, for about five years, thanks to his understanding of Chinese, Venerable Deva Bodhisattva studied and corrected errors and omissions in the new translations all day long. Truc Phap Hoa later also invited Venerable Deva to translate the Abhidharma.

Not long after, Later Qin Dao Hung entered Chang'an, and became devoted to Buddhism, so the main teaching was revived. Knowing this news, Truc Phap Hoa returned to Truong An. Venerable Deva Bo then went to the Giang Nam region, then was invited by Venerable Hue Vien to go to Lo Son mountain to preach the sutra and preach the Dharma. At Prajñātā in Lo Son, at the request of Venerable Huiyuan, Venerable Devadā translated the book 'Abhidharma of the Mind', and 'Review of the Three Dharmas'. The translation is preserved intact, and the meaning is very clear. In 397, he left Lo Son and went to Kien Khang (ie Nanjing), the capital of the Eastern Jin Dynasty. At that time, princes and famous men often visited and had friendly relations with him. The royal guard Vuong Tuan believed in Buddhism, often built monasteries, gathered people, and propagated the true teachings. Hearing that Venerable Devadā had come to the Sutra, Vuong Tuan immediately invited him to the monastery to preach the Abhidhamma Sutra, causing famous monks from everywhere to flock there. Thanks to his mastery of the sutras and his precise and clear interpretation of the scriptures, when he developed the meaning, his followers joyfully understood it.

In the winter of that year, Vuong Tuan and more than forty learned monks together invited Venerable Deva to translate the Middle Agama Sutra. At that time, monk Sangha La Xoa (from Ke Tan country) read Sanskrit, and Venerable Deva translated it into Chinese.

Thanks to his thorough understanding of the Buddhist scriptures, his keen understanding of the customs and practices of people in the Western Regions and the Eastern Region, and his ability to speak in accordance with his basic instincts, his Dharma preaching industry had a strong influence in the Jiangnan region, causing many people to flock to seek the Dharma. Later, no one knew where and when Devadāra passed away.

tom_tat: Mr. Dam Ma Nan De (translated as Phap Hi), was originally from Dau Khu Lac (ie Earth Hoa La country or Dai Nhuc Chi, where people often believe in the teachings of small...
noi_dung:
17. DharmanandiMr. Dam Ma Nan De (translated as Phap Hi), was originally from Dau Khu Lac (ie Earth Hoa La country or Dai Nhuc Chi, where the Hinayana teachings are often believed). He became a monk at a young age. Intellectual, intelligent, diligent, often diligently reciting and reading the sutras, looking at all three collections of scriptures, likes to study and study the two sutras Tang Nhat A Ham and Trung A Ham, his knowledge is wide and deep, and he is well-versed in all dharmas, making scholars at home and abroad, far and near, admire him.

When he was young, he often traveled all over the country, and had the will and ambition to go to Dong Do to propagate the Dharma. In the reign of Kien Nguyen (365-384), the reign of Qin Fu Kien, he came to Chang'an. Hearing his reputation, many famous scholars came to study. As soon as Tan Phu Kien met him, he received him with a warm welcome.

Because at that time Central Earth did not have four volumes of the A Ham Sutra, the governor Trieu Chanh wanted to ask him to translate the Sutra. At that time, Murong Sung rebelled and raised troops to attack Tan Phu Kien, causing chaos in Truong An. Due to his admiration for Buddhism and his determination to sacrifice himself for the sake of Buddhism, the chief minister Trieu Chanh asked Dao An Van to gather famous monks in Truong An and asked Dam Ma Nan De to translate Trung A Ham, Tang Nhat A Ham, Bhikkhu Tam, Tam Phap Do, etc. In total, Dam Ma Nan De translated one hundred and six volumes. Venerable Dam Ma Nan De is truly an expert on the A Ham Sutra. At that time, Master Truc Phat Niem translated, and Master Hue Sung took notes. From summer until spring of next year it will be completed. Mr. Dao An and Truc Phap Hoa jointly censored and refined the text.

In May, year 385, Dao Truong besieged Chang'an, causing turmoil. Venerable Dam Ma Nan De then left Truong An, returned to the Western Regions, and then no one knew where he passed away.

tom_tat: Ti Ma La Xaa, translated as Eyeless Eye. He is from Ke Tan country. Calm personality, but strong will. After becoming a monk, he diligently practiced...
noi_dung:
18. Venerable Timamaksas (Vimalaksas)Ti Ma La Xaa, translated as Eyeless Eye. He is from Ke Tan country. Calm personality, but strong will. After becoming a monk, he diligently practiced asceticism. First, he promoted the Vinaya in the country of Quy Tu. Scholars in the West strive to study Buddhism. Kumarajiva also followed Timala Xoa to receive precepts. Because the country of Quy Tu was plagued by war in 382, ​​he sought refuge in the country of Uddiyana. Hearing that Kumarajiva was promoting the Sutra Pitaka in Chang'an, Venerable Tim Ma La Xoa also wanted to go to Dong Do to promote the superior Bhikkhuni Canon. Therefore, he carried his staff and crossed many dangerous deserts and mountains to reach Truong An in the year 406. There, Tim Ma La Xa was still respected by Kumarajiva as a master.

After Kumarajiva became naturalized citizen, Timāla Xoa traveled to Tho Xuan and resided at Thach Gian Pagoda. A large number of disciples followed him to study the Vinaya, causing the Bhikkhunī Dharma to be promoted and flourished.

Kumarajiva translated the entire set of the Ten Vinaya Rules, containing fifty-eight volumes. The final set of Vinaya is called the Dharma of Understanding the Precepts and the Dharma Accomplishments of Goodness. Because of that meaning, this series is called Thien Tung. Coming to Thach Gian pagoda, Tim Ma Na Xoa wrote sixty-one more volumes, and renamed the final set of Vinaya Sutras as Bhikkhuni Chant.

Later, at Tan Tu pagoda in Giang Lang, he went to the throne to lecture on the Ten Tung Laws. Thanks to his fluency in Chinese, it was easy for listeners to understand. The wonderful duty of non-action is strongly promoted. Those who extract literature and seek reason gather under His court as numerous as a forest. The Vinaya Pitaka was widely propagated thanks to Tim Ma La Xoa.

At Dao Trang pagoda, thanks to penetrating the Vinaya Pitaka taught by Tim Ma La Xoa, Hue Quan recorded the light and heavy prohibitions in the precepts, compiled them into two volumes, and then brought them to the monk. Monks and nuns there were racing to transmit and copy. At that time, scholars often said:

- As soon as Tim Ma La Xoa said a word, Hue Quan immediately copied it all down.

At that time, copies of the words of Tim Ma La Xoa's explanations were treasured by everyone like precious gems.

Tim Ma La Xoa often stayed away from the world and cultivated virtue in a peaceful place. At the age of seventy-seven, Tim Ma La Xoa became naturalized citizen at Thach Gian Pagoda in Tho Xuan. Tim Ma La Xoa was originally the eye of the world, so he was praised by people as Thanh Nhan Lawyer.

tom_tat: Da Da Xa Buddha, translated as Enlightenment. He is from Ke Tan country, belongs to the Brahmin lineage, and his family often believes in pagans. One time, there was a...
noi_dung:
19. Buddha Da Xa (Buddhayasas)Da Da Xa Buddha, translated as Enlightenment. He is from Ke Tan country, belongs to the Brahmin lineage, and his family often believes in pagans. One time, a monk came to his house to beg for alms. The father was angry, so he sent someone to beat the monk. At that time, the father's limbs were sore, so he could not work as usual. Therefore, he went to ask the Monks. They said:

- Because you offended the sage, you were punished by the devil.

Hearing this, he bowed to the monk to ask for repentance. After a few days, the pain in my arms and legs gradually improved. Witnessing this with his own eyes, Buddha Da Da Xa followed the monk and became a monk at the age of thirteen. Buddha Da Da Xa often followed his master into remote wilderness areas. One time, as soon as he saw a tiger coming from afar, the original teacher was scared and wanted to run away, but Buddha Da Da Xa said:

- This tiger has already eaten its fill. It doesn't kill people anymore!

Sure enough, the tiger slowly walked away. Moving forward, they saw human bones that had just been eaten by tigers, lying haphazardly, with blood and pus spread everywhere. Through this, his original teacher was very surprised. At the age of fifteen, every day he recited three hundred thousand words. He often went out on the side of the road next to the temple to read and recite sutras. There was an Arahant who, out of respect for his intelligence and diligence, often shared the food that was offered to him by believers. At the age of nineteen, he recited millions of Mahayana and Hinayana sutras. However, because he was arrogant, even though he was old enough, the monks still did not allow him to receive full ordination, that is, he was still a novice monk. He still followed the ancient way of learning the Five Insights, worldly magic, etc. At the age of twenty-seven, he received full ordination, and often recited and read the sutras without taking his hand off the sutra. Every time he meditated, he sat for hours without paying attention. He always practiced diligently and diligently like that.

Later, he came to Sa Lac country. One time, the king offered alms to three thousand monks. He was also among those monks. At that time, Prince Dat Ma Phat Da (translated as Phap Tu), seeing his neat and dignified appearance, asked where he came from. He then responded clearly. The Crown Prince was happy, invited him to stay in the inner palace, and warmly treated him. Kumarajiva, when he came to Sa Lac country, also worshiped and studied with Buddha Da Da Xa. When Kumarajiva followed his mother back to Quy Tu country, Buddha Da Xa still resided in Sa Lac country.

Some time later, the king of Sa Lac kingdom passed away, and crown prince Dat Ma Phat Da ascended the throne. At that time, Tan Phu Kien ordered Lu Quang to lead troops to attack Quy Tu country. The King of Quy Tu quickly sent a letter to Sa Lac to ask for reinforcements. King Dat Ma Phat Da himself led reinforcements to Quy Tu country, only keeping Buddha Da Da Xa and the crown prince to prevent future events. Before King Dat Ma Phat Da's reinforcements arrived, Quy Tu was invaded by Lu Quang. Therefore, King Dat Ma Phat Da led his army back to his homeland and told about Lu Quang's capture of Kumarajiva. Buddha Da Da Xa then lamented:

- I have met Kumarajiva, but I am not satisfied. Kumarajiva suffered this misfortune; We don't know when we will meet again.

For more than ten years, Buddha Da Da Xa propagated in the eastern region of Quy Tu country, causing the Buddha Dharma to flourish. At that time, while being held by Lu Quang in Co Tang, Kumarajiva wrote a poem to greet Buddha Da Da Xa. Although he wanted to go to Co Tang, Buddha Da Da Xa was detained by the people in the country, so he had to stay for a few more years. Finally, He told his disciples:

- I want to go to Co Tang to meet Kumarajiva. So tonight let's secretly pack our bags and go.

The disciples said:

- I'm just afraid that when morning comes, I'll be taken back.

He then poured water into a medicine bottle, recited the mantra a few dozen times, and then with his disciples used that water to wash his feet. That night, he and his disciples set out, traveling as fast as the wind, covering hundreds of miles. When he stopped, he asked his disciples how they felt. They replied:

- Just hearing the wind blowing makes my eyes water.

He blessed the mantra again and gave it to them to wash their feet. The next morning, the nation chased after him, but he and his disciples had traveled more than a hundred miles, so there was no way to catch up. When Gautama Buddha arrived in Coza in the year 402, Kumarajiva had already arrived in Chang'an. Hearing that King Dao Hung forced Kumarajiva to take concubines, Buddha Da Da Xa lamented:

- Kumarajiva is like silk cotton. Why did you leave it in the thorny grass forest?

Hearing that Buddha Da Da Xa had come to Co Tang, Kumarajiva advised King Dao Hung to invite him to Truong An. However, King Dao Hung still did not listen. On behalf of King Dao Hung to translate the sutras, Kumarajiva said:

- People who propagate the Dharma must have the ability to understand literature and meaning. Although poor people know the written word, they have not yet fully understood the scriptures. Only Buddha Da Da Xa has deeply understood the mysterious meaning and is currently residing in Co Tang. Your Highness, please summon us to Truong An.

Hearing this, King Dao Hung sent an envoy to invite Buddha Da Da Xa to Truong An, and gave him a generous gift. He does not accept offerings. King Dao Hung then arranged for Buddha Da Da Xa to live in Tieu Dieu Vien and then make offerings. However, Buddha Da Da Xa still did not receive the food, but instead brought his bowl and alms to the street to beg for alms.

One time, after translating the Ten Pillars Sutra, Kumarajiva still hesitated and had doubts, and did not dare to write for more than a month. At that time, Buddha Da Da Xa suddenly came. Therefore, Kumarajiva and Buddha Daxa discussed and decided the meaning. More than three thousand monks and laity all respected Buddha Da Da Xa. Because of his thorough understanding and clear explanation of the book Ty Ba Sa, the masses unanimously called Buddha Da Da Xa Dich Ty Ba Sa. Because Buddha Da Da Xa was the teacher of Kumarajiva, the masses also proclaimed him Maha Bhikkhu Sa. Even though he received four offerings and the bowls and robes filled all three rooms, Buddha Da Da Xa still did not pay any attention to it. Seeing this, King Dao Hung sent someone to bring all these things in exchange for money to build a pagoda in the south of Truong An citadel for him to live in.

Once requested by Dao Sang, Buddha Da Da Xa recited the code of Dam Vo Duc law, which has more than fifty thousand words. King Dao Hung suspected that there were mistakes in the text, so he censored it. For two days, King Dao Hung could not find a single wrong word, so he admired even more the transcendent memory of Buddha Da Da Xa.

In 410, Buddha Da Da Xa translated forty volumes of the Four Parts of Law, the Long A Ham Sutra, etc. The monk Truc Phat Niem in Luong Chau translated it into Chinese. Monk Dao Ham took notes. In the year 413, Buddha Da Da Xa stopped preaching and translating sutras, and said goodbye to his old country. King Dao Hung offered ten thousand bundles of cloth, but he did not accept it. The monks Dao Ham and Truc Phat Niem offered him thousands of bundles of silk. More than five hundred famous and virtuous monks all offered him many gifts.

Returning to Ke Tan country, Buddha Da Da Xa obtained a copy of the Void Store Sutra and sent it to the monks in Luong Chau. Later, no one knew where Buddha Da Da Xa passed away.

tom_tat: Kumarajiva is translated in Chinese as 'Dong Tho', which means that despite his young age, he is mature in virtue. Kumarajiva's name was originally Kumarajiva. Because...
noi_dung:
20. KumarajivaKumarajiva is translated in Chinese as 'Dong Tho', which means that despite his young age, he is mature in virtue. Kumarajiva's name was originally Kumarajiva. Because the names of Westerners often use their parents' names. His father's name was Kumarajiva, and his mother's name was Ky Ba, so the two names were combined to become Kumarajiva. His ancestors originally resided in the country of Thien Truc, were born around the year 340, and the family's generations were often high officials in the court. His grandfather, Dat Da, had a generous personality, was outstanding among the masses, and was respected by the nation. His father, Kumarajiva, was intelligent and virtuous. When he was about to inherit the position of Prime Minister, he resigned and became a monk, headed southeast, crossed Thong Lanh mountain, to reach Quy Tu (Kuchar). Before entering the border of Quy Tu country, the king of that country heard Kumarajiva's reputation as renouncing glory and wealth to become a monk, so he felt boundless respect, went out to receive him, and then respected him as a national teacher. The kingdoms in Tay Vuc, because they respect monks, often have the custom of honoring them as national monks.

The king has a younger sister, in her twenties, talented and intelligent, who reads the scriptures once and then understands them clearly. After hearing them once, she remembers them. On her face there was a red mole, which hermits often said was a good sign and would give birth to a noble son. Therefore, the kings competed to bring marriage offerings, but she was not satisfied. However, as soon as she saw Kumarajiva, she agreed to be his wife. The king knew what his sister meant, so he forced Kumarajiva to marry her. Not long after they got married, they gave birth to Kumarajiva. When Kumarajiva was still in the womb, Mrs. Ky Ba had many extraordinary abilities. From the moment she became pregnant with Kumarajiva, her wisdom and enlightenment were beyond the ordinary. Hearing that many famous monks had attained enlightenment in Tuoc Le Forest, she, along with the women of the royal family and noble families, and nuns practicing and attaining enlightenment, went there to pay respects to the monks and request Dharma to listen to the sutras. Dai Tung Lam Tuoc Le originally lived in the country of Kien Da La (Gandhara), where there was a famous tower called Tuoc Ly Phu Do. While listening to the sutras, she understood Thien Truc's language, and answered many difficult questions without hesitation. Everyone found it strange. An Arhat named Dat Ma Cu Sa said:

- This is an omen that she is definitely pregnant with a person of great wisdom. In the past, when the Venerable Sariputta was still in his mother's womb, he made his mother's eloquence without hindrance. That is a specific proof of prediction.

When Kumarajiva was born, his mother could not know Thien Truc's language. Some time later, his mother expressed her intention to become a monk, but his father did not allow it. Not long after, she gave birth to another son, named Phat Sa De Ba. One time, on the occasion of going outside the city for an excursion, she saw bones and bones scattered everywhere in the cemetery. She deeply felt the causes of suffering, emptiness, and impermanence, so she determined to become a monk. She vowed that if she did not shave her head and become a nun, she would stop eating and drinking until she died. Just like that, for six days, her breathing gradually became exhausted. His Father saw that her heart was determined, so he fulfilled her wish and allowed her to become a monk. She still didn't believe it; It wasn't until someone else shaved my hair that I started eating and drinking again. She immediately went to the temple, received precepts and learned meditation. From then on, she practiced diligently without any hesitation, so she quickly attained the first stage of Sotapanna.

When he was seven years old, Kumarajiva also followed his mother to become a monk, and followed his master to read and recite scriptures. Every day, he recited a thousand verses. Each verse has thirty-two words. A total of thirty-two thousand words. His original teacher often gave him the Abhidhamma scriptures, and with just a brief explanation, he immediately understood them without any hindrance. Therefore, the prodigy Kumarajiva memorized all the Abhidharma sutras.

Because his mother came from a royal family, the people of Quy Tu made offerings to her very generously. Afraid that this would affect his concentration in practice, she soon took him to another country. At the age of nine, he followed his mother across the Tan Dau River to reach Ke Tan country. (Buddha Do Trung was born in Quy Tu country, then went to Ke Tan country to study. That was a common custom at that time. Ke Tan country was originally a place where Sarvāstivāda doctrine was very popular. In the second half of the fourth century, there were many monks who brought the original sutras and doctrines of Sarvāstivāda from Ke Tan country to Middle Earth, typically Venerable Devadā brought the Sangha Nhat A Ham sutra, Trung A Ham sutra, and A Ham sutra from Ke Tan country. Bhikkhu Prajnaparamita, the Abhidharma commentary. Venerable Ma Da Xa brought the Abhidharma commentary. In addition, Phat Nha Da La and Tim Ma La Xa brought the book Tathagata Da La translated the Avatamsaka Sutra and the Tan Infinite Life Sutra. In 411, Dam Vo Sam translated the Mahaparinirvana Sutra and other Mahayana sutras. Therefore, it can be judged that when Kumarajiva came to Ke Tan, the Hinayana sutras and the new Mahayana sutras were widely circulated.)

There, there was a highly virtuous monk named Bandhudatta, who was the younger brother of the king of Ke Tan. He had extensive education, a generous mind, and scholarly intelligence, a rare thing in his time. Dharma Master Pan Dat Da was the forty-ninth patriarch to continue the tradition of Sarvāstivāda doctrine. As for the three Vinaya sutras and the nine collections, they are all thoroughly understood. From morning to noon, my hand wrote thousands of verses. From noon to evening, one can memorize thousands of verses. His reputation is famous throughout the kingdoms in the Western Regions. Everyone respects him as a great scholar.

When he arrived in Ke Tan country, Kumarajiva paid homage and worshiped him, and followed the monk Pan Dat Da to learn scriptures such as Ka Tang, Zhong A Ham, Chang A Ham, etc. Kumarajiva could also memorize four hundred thousand words in a day. Dharma master Ban Dau Dat Da often praised Cuu Ma La Thap's genius and talent, so his reputation quickly spread to the ears of the King of Ke Tan. Therefore, the king of Ke Tan invited Kumarajiva to the palace, then gathered non-Buddhist commentators to compete in debate together. Seeing that Kumarajiva was young, before the debate began, the pagan commentators looked down on him with contempt, as was evident through their questions and answers. He did not show any fear. Every time a sentence is raised, the opponent cannot find a way to refute it. Later, the pagan commentators were all convinced. Through that debate, the king of Ke Tan treated him even more favorably, made generous offerings, and sent five great monks and ten novice monks to the temple to serve him.

At the age of twelve, his mother took him back to Quy Tu country. On the way, they passed Bac Son mountain in Dai Nhuc Chi country and met an Arhat. As soon as he saw Kumarajiva, the Arhat knew that this was not a human being, so he told his mother:

- You should carefully protect this novice monk. If you don't break the precepts by the age of thirty-five, you will be able to promote great dharma and save countless sentient beings, no different from the patriarch Upa Cuc Da. Otherwise, you will not achieve anything, but just be an ordinary magician of superior intelligence.

One time, when he came to the country of Kashgar, he saw an alms bowl of the Buddha, so he put it on his head and started thinking:

- Strange! This bowl is so big, but when you put it on your head, it doesn't feel heavy?

As soon as that thought arose, he felt that his alms bowl was extremely heavy. When his mother asked the reason, he replied:

- Just because I started the mind to distinguish between heavy and light bowls.

(In the book Tay Vuc Ky, Mr. Dao An wrote: "In Sa Lac country there is a statue of Buddha Moc Duc, made of sandalwood, brought from the west, placed in the palace to make offerings."

He went here and saw that in the middle of the fourth century, Buddhism was introduced into the Sa Lac country, so the king had a statue of Moc Duc Buddha to make offerings at the royal palace. In the early fifth century, the monk Tri Manh once went there to worship the relics. The fifteenth volume of 'Exit Tripitaka' records: "Furthermore, in that country, the Buddha's alms bowl was seen to be purple-blue in color and bright on all four sides. Venerable Tri Manh offered flowers, bowed and made a vow that if the alms bowl had spiritual inspiration, it could be heavy and light. After making the vow, Venerable Tri Manh lifted the alms bowl, then slowly felt that the alms bowl was heavy and could not be held, so he had to put it down. While putting it down, Venerable Tri Manh feels like the bowl is lighter again."

The belief in worshiping Buddha's alms bowl is widely spread from Thien Truc to countries in Tay Vuc. Therefore, Kumarajiva himself personally experienced the inspiration of the Buddha's alms bowl.)

In the first year of his stay in the country of Sa Lac, Kumarajiva learned to discuss the Abhidhamma, the Luc Tuc Sutra, the Anguttara Sutra, and clearly understood the doctrine of the Sarvastivada.

The country of Sa Lac had a Tripitaka magician named Hy Kien. He heard about Kumarajiva's reputation and told the king of that country:

- Please, Your Majesty, do not despise that novice monk, but please invite him to court to preach the sutras and preach the Dharma, then two good things will be achieved: First, the monks of our country, when they hear the Dharma sermons of that novice monk, they will feel that they are not up to par, so they will definitely feel ashamed and try to practice. Second, the king of Quy Tu will definitely understand that our country's generous treatment and respect for Kumarajiva is also a sign of respect for the country of Quy Tu. If that is the case, then the two countries will have peaceful relations.

Listening to the words of the magician Hy Kien, the king of Sa Lac agreed to the request, so he set up a great Dharma conference and invited Kumarajiva to rise to the throne to preach the Zhuan Dharma Sutra. When the King of Quy Tu heard this news, he sent an envoy to bring gifts of gratitude, making the relationship between the two countries even closer.

Although he was a prodigy, he did not take it as complacency, but often focused on studying the Tripitaka, the original Buddhist scriptures, and studying the theory of Nhiet Thiet Huu, and then went one step further to study classical logic such as the Vedic Ham Da treatise, the Four Vedic Treatises, the Five Insights treatise (clarity, cunning wisdom, medical direction, human wisdom, inner wisdom), yin and yang mathematics, medicine, astronomy and astrology. Picking and predicting bad luck.

At Sa Lac, Kumarajiva followed the monk Tu Loi Da To Ma (Surya-Soma) to study Mahayana dharma. The book 'Hundred Treatises' writes: "The monk Tu Loi Da To Ma was originally a prince of Sa Lac country, became a monk and studied the Mahayana dharma. In terms of education, the positions of the Hinayana and Mahayana teachings are completely different. Kumarajiva originally practiced the Hinayana teachings, but from the moment he met the monk Tu Loi Da To Ma and often interacted intimately, his vision of the Mahayana dharma was opened. Initially, to educate, the monk Tu Loi Da To Ma came. In front of the door of Kumarajiva's room, he deliberately read the Anuttara Sutra out loud, with the meaning that everything was empty. From afar, he heard this sutra, so the next morning Kumarajiva asked the monk Tu Loi Da To Ma:

- What prayer did you read yesterday?

Monk Tu Loi Da To Ma said:

- That is the Mahayana sutra.

- What's the meaning?

- Talking about everything is nothing.

- Everything in front of you is real, so why call it nothing?

- If your eyes see something, then may I ask, is there any thing that lasts for a long time?

- What remains is the nature of seeing.

- If seeing is the nature of existence, then why can't we see with our own eyes? Again, is the eye made up of one pole of particles or many poles of particles? If it is said to be composed of a pole of particles, then seeing is also an pole of particles. If one pole of motes cannot be seen, then of course many poles of motes cannot be seen. In addition, if the microscopic dust has a form, it must have the full nature of being large or small. However, if it is vast, it cannot be extremely microscopic. Without the full nature of vastness and narrowness, how can it be called having form?

At this very word, Kumarajiva could not respond, so he remained silent. Using the theory of Sarvāstivāda theory, Kumarajiva believed that the eye faculty is a real dharma. The monk Tu Loi Da To Ma replied that the eye base was originally created by a combination of conditions and did not really exist. This is the debate between Sarvāstivāda and Khongānāda theory. Kumarajiva gradually realized the principles of Mahayana dharma, so he lamented to himself:

- In the past, when I studied the Hinayana method, I often did not know that there was gold inside, but only believed that bronze was precious.

Thanks to that, Kumarajiva began to follow the monk Tu Loi Dat Ma to study Mahayana scriptures such as the Central Commentary, Bach Treatise, Twelve Doors Commentary, etc. From then on, Kumarajiva completely turned to the Mahayana dharma, and considered it an important part of his practice.

Some time later, he followed his mother to the Tianshan mountain range of the country of Wensu (Ush), located north of the country of Guici. In that country, there was a Taoist monk with unimpeded eloquence, whose reputation was famous throughout neighboring countries. One time, he beat the drum and announced to everyone:

- If anyone can argue against me, I will cut off his head to apologize.

Hearing this, He went to reason with him. As a result, the Taoist had to admit that he was conquered, so he bowed and took refuge in him. From then on, his reputation resonated throughout the kingdoms in the Western Regions, causing King Quy Tu to personally go to On Tuc to invite him back to his native country. From then on, he often lectured on the platform. Scholars from all over the world all admired and admired him.

A Kiet Da Mat De, a princess of Quy Tu country, became a nun, recited the sutras, attained profound meditation, attained the second level of Arhatship, and then gathered in public, asking him to explain the profound meaning of the Phuong Quang sutra. Therefore, he took the throne to preach the Dharma, extolling the principle that 'all have no self' and that the warm precepts 'are only false, not real'. When the crowd heard these words, they were delighted and praised.

At the age of twenty, Kumarajiva followed the monk Vimaraksa, an outstanding scholar of jurisprudence, and received full ordination at the royal palace. The monk Ti Ma La Xoa was originally from Ke Tan country, but he went to Quy Tu country to propagate the Vinaya Pitaka, so scholars from all over the world were racing to study. Kumarajiva followed the monk Ti Ma La Xa to study the Ten Recitation Rules.

Later, his mother told King Bach Thong of Quy Tu country:

- The nation is about to collapse. I have to leave this place.

She asked Kumarajiva again:

- The Phuong Dang Sutra and other Mahayana sutras should be transmitted to Dong Do, with only you alone! However, for the child there is no benefit, so how to calculate it?

He said:

- The Bodhisattva path is to benefit others, to forget yourself. If the Dharma is passed down and allows people to perceive and become enlightened, then even if they experience hardship and burning fire, they will still not regret it.

When she arrived at Thien Truc, she attained the three Arhat results (ie A Na Ham fruit).

One time, residing at Tan Tu pagoda in Quy Tu country, he was about to open the Prajnaparamita Sutra to read and recite it, but evil spirits came to disturb him, causing the scriptures to turn into blank sheets of paper. Seeing that he was being harassed by evil spirits, he remained determined not to change his mind and kept reciting, so in the end the evil spirits had to retreat, and the scriptures appeared again. Another time, while reading Mahayana scriptures at Dai Tung Lam Tuoc Le, he suddenly heard a voice in the temple saying:

- You are a great wise man, so why are you still reading and reciting scriptures?

He said:

- Hey little devil! Please go somewhere else quickly. My mind is as solid as the earth, nothing makes it move.

Thanks to the application of wisdom and prajna, his practice stance did not change even when he encountered demons.

For the next two years, he remained in Quy Tu to recite Mahayana sutras and study the profound and wonderful teachings. The King of Quy Tu established a lion throne, spread brocade silk on the seat, and then invited him to preach on the altar. He said:

- My teacher has not yet grasped the essence of the Mahayana sutras. I want to go there myself to preach the Mahayana teachings, so I cannot stay here for long.

However, because he heard the reputation of Kumarajiva and knew that the king of Quy Tu believed in Buddhism, the monk Ban Dau Dama did not manage to travel thousands of miles to Quy Tu country. The King of Quy Tu asked the monk Pan Datama:

- Why did the Great Master come all the way to my kingdom?

The monk Pan Datama replied:

- There are two reasons: First, I heard that my disciple Kumarajiva had great enlightenment. Second, because I heard that the Great King protects and propagates Buddhism, I did not care about the distance and came to your country.

Hearing that the original master had come, it was very consistent with his wishes, so his heart was filled with joy. Knowing that his teacher did not believe in the Sutra of Our Lady's Question before, he preached this sutra again, to promote the principle that cause and effect are false so that his original teacher could not hear it. The original teacher teaches the Hinayana, for some reason the disciple believes in the Mahayana and does not meditate. Therefore, after listening to Kumarajiva's teaching, the original teacher asked:

- In the teachings of the Mahayana, what have you experienced that makes you worship like that?

He said:

- The profound meaning of the Mahayana teachings explains that everything is empty. Hinayana teachings, because they are often stuck on names and appearances, are still largely limited.

- You say everything is no. This argument is scary! If you let go of something, it still exists, so why do you like a place that is empty? For example, a foolish person wants to ask a worker to weave a thin green sheet for him. After weaving, the worker showed it to him. He said that the fabric was still rough and not yet soft, because the shape was still visible. The weaver was angry, pointed to the sky, and said that it was the softest cloth. The foolish person asks why he can't see it. The weaver replied that he was too weak to see. Hearing this, the crazy man was filled with joy and admiration. You say no no, same thing.

He was still resolute, quoting the scriptures, not tired of explaining it to his original teacher. During a month of debating about Mahayana teachings, the original teacher finally fully understood his teachings. Therefore, the monk Pandatatta solemnly bowed to Kumarajiva and said:

- I am your Hinayana teacher. You are my teacher of Mahayana.

The kings of the Western Regions, out of admiration and respect, every time he ascended the throne to preach, they would kneel right next to the pulpit.

At that time, Quy Tu country was the stronghold of Theravada Buddhism. Two Chinese monks, the Supreme Patriarch and Dam Sung, requested this version of the bhikkhu precepts from the monk Buddha Do Thiet Di, a senior monk, the ruler of the four great forest branches such as Van Mo Lam, Tan Tu, Tan Lam, and Sangha Lam; In total there were more than three hundred and fifty monks. All scholars of the A Ham Sutra follow the teachings of Elder Buddha Do Thiet Di. At that time, there were also great monks there such as: Dat Mo Lam (with 170 monks), Bac Thuong Chi Le Lam (with 50 monks), Kiem Mo Vuong Tan Lam (with 60 monks), Tuc Tuc Vuong Lam (with 70 monks). The king also built the Tan Tang Lam temple, which has about ninety monks. This is where Kumarajiva often resides. In addition, there are nunneries such as A Le Lam (180 nuns), Luan Nha Thien Lam (50 nuns), A Le Bat Lam (30 nuns). The Bhikkhus in these three nunneries are mostly royal women who came to practice, and they all received precepts from Elder Buddha Do Thiet Di. The practice regulations in nunneries are very strict and austere. This Bhikkhu must keep all five hundred precepts. Every three months, these Bhikkhus have to change their place of residence. When going out, you must have three companions. If you go out without anyone accompanying you, you will be kicked out of the nunnery.

Buddha Do Trung also studied in this country. Monk Bach Thi Le Mat Da also brought esoteric scriptures from here to China.

In the past, Kumarajiva was also a disciple of the monk Buddha Do Thiet Di. In the second half of the fourth century, Mahayana scriptures such as the Lotus Sutra, Vimalakirti Sutra, Amitabha Sutra, and the Khong Quan teachings developed rapidly and strongly due to the teachings of Kumarajiva, after studying in Sa Lac country. Hearing the explanations of Kumarajiva, the monk Buddha Tathagata believed in the teachings of the Mahayana. Therefore, between Kumarajiva and the monk Buddha Tathagata there is also a relationship of 'both teacher and student'.

After he came to Co Tang, the Mahayana teachings gradually weakened. Because there was no one to promote them, the Hinayana teachings regained dominance. Dharma Master Dat Ma Bat Da (translated as Phap Hien), a native of Quy Tu country, has an intelligent nature, understands all three classics, knows many foreign languages, but believes that the Hinayana dharma is the ultimate, so he becomes arrogant and slanders the Mahayana scriptures. At that time, monk Tu Loi Da To Ma (the Mahayana teacher of Kumarajiva), came from Sa Lac country to Quy Tu to preach the Lotus Sutra, and was able to conquer Dat Ma Bat Da and turn to Mahayana. Later, because of the lack of famous Mahayana monks, Hinayana monks with strict precepts, from Ke Tan country often went to Quy Tu country to spread the Dharma, so gradually the whole country respected Hinayana teachings.

Soon, Kumarajiva's reputation spread to Central Earth.

At that time, in Central Earth, it was the time when the Sixteen Kingdoms of the Five Lakes and the Former Qin Dynasty Fu Kien had great power. In the domestic Buddhist world, Phu Kien had heard about Dao An's reputation in Tuong Duong, so he later invited him to Truong An to propagate the Dharma.

In the thirteenth year of Kien Nguyen (377), in the first month, a royal official observed the stars and reported to Phu Kien:

- Abroad, if stars appear in the wilderness, there must be a wise man, and in the future he will come to Central Earth to support the country.

Phu Kien says:

- I heard that in the Western Regions there is Kumarajiva. So, that's the taste.

One time, the king of Tien Do, Xa Su, and the brother of the king of Quy Tu, Huu Mat Da, both entered the court and told Phu Kien:

- The Western Regions have many precious pearls and jewels. I request the Great King to dispatch troops to pacify them and make them submit to them.

According to the eighth volume of the 'Exit Tripitaka', in the preface to the Maha Prajnaparamita Sutra, Dao An wrote that the king of Former Capital, Xa Su, came to Central Earth in the first month, the eighteenth year of Kien Nguyen (382), and brought with him a national teacher named Kumarajiva (Kuma rabhadra), and presented a Great Product with four hundred and twenty thousand words, and twenty thousand as tribute. verse.

Listening to the words of two foreign princes, in September 382, ​​Phu Kien sent the arrogant general Lu Quang to lead seventy thousand troops to invade the Western Regions. When Lu Quang was about to depart from Truong An, Phu Kien sent Lu Quang off at Kien Chuong palace, saying:

- The emperor rules the country according to the orders of heaven, so he must base his love on the people. Why do you have the ambition to conquer your neighbors? I take the king's way as my weak point, so because I admire a virtuous man, I send my army to conquer. I heard that in the Western Regions there was a strange man named Kumarajiva, who was profound in understanding dharma, clearly understanding the yin and yang and stars, making later scholars worship him. I think to myself that he is a precious sage of the nation. If you can destroy the Quy Tu kingdom, immediately bring Kumarajiva back.

Before Lu Quang's army arrived at Quy Tu, Kumarajiva told King Bach Thong:

- The country's fortunes have reached a decline. Soon there will be enemies coming from the east. Please welcome them respectfully, Your Majesty, and do not fight.

King Bach Thong refused to listen to him and continued to lead his army to fight Lu Quang. In December 383, Lu Quang led his army to surround Quy Tu citadel, but did not enter. In May 384, King Bach Thong took advantage of that opportunity and sent people to ask for reinforcements from neighboring countries such as Sa Lac, On Tuc, etc. However, in July 384, Lu Quang sent troops into the city, killing tens of thousands of souls. King Bach Thong also died in battle. Lu Quang's army entered the citadel and saw that the citadel had three floors, round and wide like Truong An citadel. In the city there are thousands of temple towers. King Bach Thong's palace was as magnificent as the palace of the gods. After conquering the citadel, Lu Quang installed King Bach Thong's younger brother, Bach Chan, on the throne. Seeing that the monk that Phu Kien worshiped was still young, Lu Quang, because he was not a Buddhist and only had a rude and cruel nature, forced Kumarajiva to drink wine, and then forced him to marry the princess in the palace, but he refused. Seeing that, Lu Quang said:

- A virtuous person cannot surpass his father. The Venerable's father was once married, so why did the Venerable persist in not wanting to get married?

Having finished speaking, Lu Quang forced him to drink wine again, then locked him in a secret room with the princess. After that, Lu Quang forced him to ride a buffalo and a horse, and used many ways to humiliate him. However, He tried to endure the bitter torture and humiliation, without giving rise to any resentment or fear. In the end, his perseverance in keeping the precepts and enduring many tortures made Lu Quang feel regretful and no longer had to be brutally executed.

After pacifying Quy Tu country, Lu Quang did not hear any news about the country, so he suspected that there was a war in the country, so he stayed there. Although he was still detained, Lu Quang gradually trusted him. In January 385, Lu Guang summoned his servants to the palace and asked if he should return to his homeland or not. Because the majority of people wanted to return, Lu Quang decided to return to China. In March 385, Lu Guang led more than twenty thousand troops, along with them, he stole many beautiful girls, gold, silver, jewels, exotic birds, beasts, handsome horses, etc. back to China. At that time, Kumarajiva was also captured.

From the Tay Vuc desert, going east, the roads are craggy and dangerous. One time, on the way back, Lu Quang stopped his army to rest at the foot of a mountain. At that time, he told Lu Quang:

- We cannot stop here, because it is very unfavorable, we must move our troops up the mountain.

Lu Quang did not care to listen to His words. At night, heavy rain poured down, water poured down from the mountain and flooded dozens of meters, drowning thousands of soldiers. From then on, Lu Quang knew of His prophetic talent. He said again:

- This is a dangerous and evil place. Don't stay too long, but quickly return to your country. On the way, you will definitely meet a blessed land.

Through the terrible accident, Lu Quang did not dare to disobey His words. As soon as Lu Quang arrived at Luong Chau, he heard that Phu Kien had been murdered by Dao Truong, so the three troops wore white clothes and mourned for three months. Lu Quang immediately sent troops to invade Luong Chau, then proclaimed himself Emperor Van Chieu, founded the Later Luong Dynasty, the reign name was Kien Nguyen Thai An.

In January 387, a hurricane arose in Co Tang. Kumarajiva told Lu Guang:

- This is a bad wind, there will probably be rebellion, but later it will naturally be pacified.

Not long after, Luong Qian and Peng Hoang continuously rebelled, but Lu Quang was able to suppress them. Banh Hoang was originally a governor in Truong Dich, and a military general who followed Lu Quang to conquer Quy Tu. In 388, in the third month, the Vo Oai governor, Do Tan, was killed by Lu Quang. Next, Lu Quang took the loyal mandarins with him to conquer the Western Regions in the past and beheaded them all.

In February 396, Lu Quang officially ascended the throne, proclaimed himself Thien Vuong, granted amnesty, changed the reign name to Lan Gia, established Thach Thi as queen and her son Lu Thieu as crown prince. Naturally, it has all the institutions of an independent country. In 397, Lu Quang changed his reign name to Long Phi.

At that time, Nam Thanh and Mong Ton both honored Doan Nghiep as king at Truong Dich and established the Northern Liang state (397-439).

Later, Lu Soan led fifty thousand troops to attack Northern Liang. Contemporaries all said that Doan Nghiep's army was a mixed army. Lu Soan will definitely win. Lu Guang asked Kumarajiva to check the military situation. He said:

- Looking at this military deployment, we probably won't win.

Indeed, Lu Soan's army was defeated at Hop Ly, so he had to pull back.

Lu Quang had a lieutenant governor named Truong Tu, who was talented, had a gentle personality, and had extensive knowledge. One time, he was seriously ill, so Lu Quang invited famous doctors to treat him. A foreigner, named La Xoa, told himself that he could cure the disease. Lu Quang heard that and happily rewarded him with gifts. Knowing that La Xoa was cheating to get money, he told Truong Tu:

- La Xoa has no medical talent, only cheats to get money. Human life is hidden and unknown. Let me see how your fortune is predicted!

Having finished speaking, He tied five-colored silk strings together, burned them to ashes, then dropped them into the water, saying:

- If the ash floats to the surface of the water and then coalesces into a string shape like before, the illness will not heal!

A moment later, the ash floated up and gathered into a string shape like before. As He prophesied, La Xoa had no way to cure his illness, so within a few days, Truong Tu passed away.

Later, Lu Quang fell ill and died. Crown Prince Lu Chieu ascended the throne, but he was a foolish person. Lu Soan then killed Lu Chieu to take the throne and changed his reign name to Ham Ninh. Lu Soan has a rough personality, does not like to read books but only loves alcohol, is insatiably promiscuous, and often likes to go hunting. In 399, many strange signs appeared in the country: A pig gave birth to three-headed piglets; A dragon rose from the well and lay in front of the palace. Lu Soan thought it was a good omen, so he called that place Long Phi Palace. Next, a black dragon rose from the gate of the Nine Palaces in Duong Duong, so Lu Soan changed the Nine Palaces to Cuu Long Hung. Seeing these strange phenomena, He told Lu Soan:

- Recently, dragons have appeared continuously, and demon pigs have shown strange signs. Dragons are inherently yin and come in and out depending on the weather. As has often appeared now, this is a sign of disaster to come, there will probably be treason. Your Highness, please practice self-discipline and cultivate virtue to change the mind of heaven, then you can avoid disaster.

Lu Soan refused to listen to His advice. One time, while playing chess with him, Lu Soan won a chess piece and laughed and said:

- Cut off Ho No's head! (Chinese people often call people from the North or Western Regions the Ho tribe).

He said:

- Ho Nu's head cannot be cut off, I'm afraid that Ho No will behead someone else!

He said this with profound meaning, but Lu Soan did not understand. The reason is because Lu Quang has a younger brother, Lu Bao. Lu Bao had a son, Lu Sieu, and Lu Sieu's middle name was Ho No. Later, Lu Sieu killed Lu Soan, then crowned his brother Lu Long as king. Only then did everyone know His prediction.

In Luong Kinh, he served as an advisor to Lu Quang and Lu Soan. Regarding supernatural abilities, yin and yang, and divination, Kumarajiva is equally talented as Buddha Do Cheng. However, father and son Lu Quang and Lu Soan did not have the heart to propagate Buddhism, so he had no way to practice the religion.

After Lu Thieu passed away, his wife Truong Thi became a nun. Because Lu Long had the evil intention of forcing her, Truong Thi firmly refused to be humiliated, so she jumped from a high building to the ground and committed suicide, while still reciting the sutras. This clearly shows that the Buddhist congregation existed at that time.

At that time, in Northern Liang, Mong Ton ascended the throne, and was very devoted to Buddhism, so Buddhism was very popular. In 421, the Tay Luong dynasty was destroyed, Mong Ton sent troops to invade, all the way to Dun Hoang.

According to the book 'Apocryphal Book Thich Lao Chi', since the reign of Truong Quy (256-314), people of Liangzhou have always believed in Buddhism. Luong Chau was an important transportation route, so many monks from Thien Truc or Western countries to Central Earth had to pass through there. That place is obviously also a transportation route for languages, that is, Thien Truc, Chinese, and other languages ​​in Central Asian countries are all practiced. Therefore, monks from Thien Truc or Tay Vuc can learn Chinese to translate the sutras; Typically, Dam Vo Sam stayed there for three years to learn Chinese and then translate the scriptures. On the contrary, Chinese monks can also learn the language of Thien Truc or Tay Vuc before going there to practice. Therefore, during the sixteen years of being detained in Luong Chau, Kumarajiva of course became fluent in Chinese, to prepare for the later work of translating the classics.

At Truong An, admiring his virtue, monk Tang Trieu (378-414) traveled there to study the classic teachings.

After killing Phu Kien, Dao Truong ascended the throne and proclaimed himself emperor at Quan Trung. Hearing Kumarajiva's reputation, Dao Truong requested him several times. However, Lu Quang and Lu Soan, his father and son, saw that he was talented and virtuous, and were afraid of Dao Truong's schemes, so they did not let him go to Truong An. Dao Truong died, his son Dao Hung succeeded him.

Dao Hung uses virtue to rule the people, and strongly worships the Three Jewels. He often set up Dharma conferences to make offerings to monks, preach sutras and sermons, causing great Dharma to flourish everywhere, so out of every ten people, there were more than five devout people who became monks. At Chang'an at that time there were more than five thousand monks. There are about a thousand meditating monks. In Vinh Quy Ly built a tower to worship Buddha. In the inner palace, a Bat Nha station was set up.

In 401, in the fifth month, Dao Hung sent Dao Thac Duc to lead an army to attack Lu Long. By September of that year, Lu Long submitted to Later Qin. In the third year of Hongshui (401), on the twentieth day of the twelfth month, Kumarajiva was welcomed by King Dao Hung to Chang'an. King Dao Hung received the ceremony from a national teacher to treat him well, and often happily talked with him all day long without stopping.

In January 402, at Tay Minh Pavilion and Tieu Dieu Vien, Kumarajiva began translating the sutras.

Buddhism from the Early Han, Later Han, Wei, and Jin periods, the classics were gradually translated a lot. However, translators such as Chi Khiem, Truc Phap Lan, etc. often use the 'Cach Nghia' method (which means using the academic terms of Confucianism and Taoism to explain Buddhist scriptures) to translate the scriptures. Therefore, the meaning of the scriptures is not clear.

Seeing this, King Dao Hung asked Kumarajiva to translate the sutras and reproduce the translated sutras. He recited many sutras by heart, had thoroughly researched them, and was fluent in Chinese, which made the translation work even more convenient. He looked through the translated sutras and discovered that there were many mistakes. As discussed previously, translators in the past often used too many Confucian and Taoist terms, thus losing the basic meaning of Buddhism, and also not compatible with the original Sanskrit.

Hearing the fame of Kumarajiva, famous monks from all over flocked to Chang'an to study the essential teachings of Buddhism and assist in translating the sutras, a total of more than three thousand, such as Tang Trieu, Dao Sanh, Dao Dung, Tang Due, Zeng Tuyen, Dao Luu, etc. Among them were four famous monks called Quan Trung Tu Saints such as Dao Sanh, Tang Trieu, Dao Dung, and Tang Due. Mr. Hue Vien's disciples such as Hue Quan, Hue On, etc. also left Lo Son and went to Truong An to listen to him preach. At that time, the two most important Buddhist centers were Chang'an, where Kumarajiva resided, and Loshan, where Huiyuan lived. Kumarajiva and Huiyuan often sent letters to each other to discuss Buddhist principles.

At Tieu Dieu Vien, he was able to translate the Sutras of Zazen Samadhi, Amitabha, Wise Hand, Great Prajnaparamita, Great Wisdom, etc. When translating the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra, Kumarajiva translated directly from Sanskrit, then King Dao Hung took the old translation to investigate, making the disagreements between the new and old translations compatible.

King Dao Hung realized that the profound Buddhist teachings, which often promote virtue and kindness, were truly a boat to escape the sea of ​​suffering. Therefore, he selected excerpts from the nine sutras, and focused on the twelve principles of cause and effect, before writing the book 'The Three Worlds', to show that cause and effect are absolutely not wrong. All the princes and ministers praised it as a masterpiece. General Dao Hien in Thuong Son and left general Dao Sung in An Thanh all devoted their hearts to worshiping Buddhism, and often invited him to preach sutras and sermons at Truong An Great Temple. Therefore, it is clear that the Later Qin royal family all worshiped Buddhism.

From 401 to 405, he translated the sutras at Tieu Dao Institute. From the year 406, he went to Chang'an Dai Temple and translated the Lotus Sutra, the Lotus Sutra, Vimalakirti, the Middle Treatise, the Twelve Doors, the Truthful Treatise, etc.

Since coming to Truong An, he has always been busy translating the classics.

Kumarajiva thoroughly understands people's emotions, his personality is outstanding, and his abilities are unmatched; charitable, kind, gentle, and courteous; sacrifice his life to teach his students. For more than ten years in Truong An, he tirelessly promoted the Mahayana Buddhist principles. He again invited his teachers such as the monk Ti Ma La Xa and Phat Da Da Xa to Truong An; show warm kindness to the senior monks. It is truly full of the qualifications of a great man.

Responding to the requests of the king and court officials, he often ascended to the throne to preach sutras. Highly virtuous monks from all over the world at that time often came to Truong An to listen to him preach the sutras and preach the Dharma. Dharma Master Dao Sanh, the abbot of Long Quang pagoda, although he had thoroughly understood the meaning of the scriptures and thoroughly understood all the essential instructions, but still had doubts about the old translations of the scriptures, so he did not manage to travel thousands of miles and went to Truong An to ask him for guidance. Master Hue Vien lived in the town of Lo Son mountain, studied thoroughly the classics, was a great master among famous monks, but still had many doubts, so he often wrote poems to ask for guidance.

King Dao Hung often told him:

- The Great Master's intelligence is unique, his understanding is superb, no one in the world can compare to him. If one day it was lost, wouldn't that mean the seed of dharma would be cut off?

Therefore, King Dao Hung brought ten beautiful women, forced him to accept them, then ordered people to build a separate room, and made generous offerings. Therefore, every time he preached the sutras, he often said:

-For example, a pure lotus flower emerges from the mud. Once you've picked the flowers, don't throw them back into the mud!

He hopes to warn practitioners to be careful not to break the precepts.

In the past, in the country of Quy Tu, he followed the lawyer Ti Ma La Xoa to receive ordination. Later, when he arrived in Central Earth, lawyer Tim Ma La Xoa asked him:

- You and China really have a deep relationship. How much does the person who follows you receive Dharma get?

He said:

- The scriptures in China are not yet complete. Most of the new sutras are translated by me. Three thousand disciples often follow me to receive Dharma. However, because of heavy karma, I do not dare to receive their respect.

Before entering natural law, he summoned his disciples and said:

- I have translated more than three hundred volumes of Buddhist scriptures. Except for one set of the Ten Vinaya Rules which is incomplete, all other scriptures preserve the original meaning. I hope you will pass on those sutras to future generations to propagate the Dharma. Now, in front of everyone, I make a vow: If the scriptures I have translated are not mistaken, then when I immolate this body, the fire cannot burn my tongue.

In the Later Qin Dynasty, the eleventh year of Hongshui (409), on the twentieth day of the eighth month, Kumarajiva entered citizenship in Chang'an. The body was placed in Tieu Dieu Vien, then the court and monks cremated according to Thien Truc rituals. After his body was burned to ashes, everyone saw that Kumarajiva's tongue was still intact. This proves his ancient vow to translate the scriptures without error. Therefore, people all over the world praised his great translation work.

After Kumarajiva entered citizenship, the congregation of three thousand followers gradually disintegrated, because it had lost a teacher. Lawyer Ti Ma La Xoa left Truong An to reside in Tho Xuan. Buddha Da Da Xa was satisfied and returned to Ke Tan country. Master Dao Sanh also went to Giang Nam. Buddha Dabat Da La and his congregation, Kumarajiva, Hue Quan, went to Lo Son. Although the congregation disbanded, Kumarajiva's work in translating the classics always shines brightly in the history of Chinese Buddhism, and his works of research and explanation will forever propagate to posterity.

Mahayana scriptures have been translated many times by translators such as Chi Lau Ca Sam (Later Han), Khuong Tang Hoi, Chi Khiem (Ngo-Three Kingdoms), Truc Phap Ho (Western Jin). However, most of the translations have not yet completed the text, and the text has not fully expressed the meaning of the sutra. Therefore, after reviewing the old translations, Kumarajiva edited and translated the new version, thanks to which his name resonated in the history of sutra translation.

At that time, he received the support of King Dao Hung and many talented philosophical disciples who devoted their efforts to assist in translating ashrams, so he achieved a great career of translating classics in a short period of time. It's all thanks to His sublime talent and dignity. Regarding the three Hinayana sutras, from a young age he studied in Ke Tan country, then went to Sa Lac country to study Mahayana teachings, so in Quy Tu country he was thorough and knew many Hinayana and Mahayana scriptures. During the sixteen years he was detained in Luong Chau, he made an effort to study Chinese, so translating the classics from Sanskrit into Chinese was easy. According to the book 'Exodus Tripitaka', the sutras translated by him are as follows: New Great Product (24 volumes), New Small Great Product (7 volumes), New Dharma Flower (7 volumes), New Sage Kiep (7 volumes), Flower Hand (10 volumes), New Vimalakirti (3 volumes), New Shurangama (2 volumes), Ten Pillars (5 volumes), Self-Rich Meaning (4 volumes), Experiencing the World (4 volumes), King of Self-Satisfaction (2 volumes), Buddha Pitaka (3 volumes), Bodhisattva Pitaka (3 volumes), Proclaiming the Buddha's Merit (3 volumes), Infinite Life (1 volume), Maitreya's Lower Birth (1 volume), Maitreya Buddhahood (1 volume), Vajra Prajnaparamita (1 volume), Dharma Non-actions (1 volume), Manjushri Enlightenment (1 volume), Amitabha Buddha (1 volume), Contemplation of the Twelve Causes and Conditions (1 volume), Bodhisattva Aghasa (1 volume) volumes), Essentials of Zen Dharma (2 volumes), Samadhi of Zazen Meditation (3 volumes), Miscellaneous Examples (1 volume, compiled by Bhikkhu Dao Luoc), Treatise on Great Wisdom (100 volumes), Treatise on Truthfulness (16 volumes), Ten Pillars (10 volumes), Middle Treatise (4 volumes), Treatise on the Twelve Doors (1 volume), Bach Treatise (2 volumes), Ten Disciplines (61 volumes), Ten Recitations of Bhikkhu Precepts (1 volume), Essential Meditation Dharma (3 volumes).

Disciple of Kumarajiva.

The master who fully ordained him was the monk Ti Ma La Xoa. When he passed through Central Earth, he asked:

- You have a deep relationship with China, so how many people have followed you to receive teachings?

He said:

- Because the dharma treatises in China were not yet complete, most of them were translated by me, and three thousand people followed me to study the Dharma.

At that time, at the ashrams translating the sutras, there were usually at least five hundred monks assisting him in translating. Sometimes there are eight hundred; Even when translating the Tu-ich Sutra, a total of more than two thousand monks participated. Among his disciples, he was called Ten Triet such as: Tang Trieu, Tang Due, Dao Sanh, Dao Dung, Dam Anh, Hue Nghiem, Hue Quan, Dao Tieu, Dao Thuong, etc. These were the monks who often followed him closely, edited the scriptures, listened to him preach the sutras, and participated in discussions. From 401 to 409, the Buddhist community in Chang'an all followed his leadership. Even Buddhist monk Da Bat Da La strictly followed the precepts, practiced meditation, and had a great and complete style in the spiritual world, but was not as influential as his congregation, so he later went to live in seclusion at Lo Son. Therefore, it is clear how strong the power of His congregation was at that time. In 401, he went to Chang'an; The youngest disciple is Tang Trieu, twenty years old; The oldest disciple is Phap Hoa, seventy years old.

The latter proclaimed his four great disciples as the 'Four Saints' such as Tang Trieu, Tang Due, Dao Sanh, and Dao Dung. 'Eight Paths' are Dao Sanh, Sangha million, Dao Dung, Sangha Due, Dao Peng, Dao Anh, Hue Nghiem, Hue Quan. 'Eight Tunes' plus Dao Hang and Dao Tieu become 'Ten Triet'. Among the talented and handsome disciples, Hue Sanh once initiated the theory of 'Cynic Ðà has Buddha Nature' along with the theory of Nirvana Sutra. During the Liu Song Dynasty, activities in the Giang Nam region were Hue Quan and Hue Nghiem. The founder of Thanh That Tong was Sang Dao. The founder of Tam Luan Tong was Tang Sung.

noi_dung:
20A. Mr. Dao Sanh - Theory of Sudden EnlightenmentA. Mr. Dao Sanh, theory of sudden enlightenment.

Dao Sanh's family name is Wei, Cu Loc people, residing in Banh Thanh, his family has spent many generations as mandarins in the court. His father worked as a district official in Quang Thich, was respected by the people, and was praised as a great benefactor. During the Eastern Jin period, Quang Thanh district belonged to the Pengcheng state.

Dao Sanh was intelligent and enlightened when he was young, had wisdom like a god, and excelled beyond ordinary people, so he was greatly loved by his father. Later, he met Truc Phap Thai (320-387) and he became a monk and practiced Buddhism.

In the year 365, the third year of Hung Ninh, Truc Phap Thai followed Dao An to Tuong Duong, then went to Kien Khang in Kinh Chau, and opened a forum to preach sutras at Ngoa Quan pagoda. At that time, Emperor Gian Van De (371-372) was in office. Ngoa Quan Pagoda was built during the Hung Ninh era (363-365). At that time, Ngoa Quan Pagoda was just a street tower. Truc Phap Thai went there, built more monk rooms, and after looking at the terrain, built the same gate. On the day Truc Phap Thai opened the sutra, thousands of people from the Tam Ngo area came to listen to the sermon.

Since entering the Buddha's door, Dao Sanh's extraordinary intelligence has increasingly become evident. Regarding the deep meaning of the scriptures, Dao Sanh researched it himself and realized the reason clearly. At the age of fifteen, Dao Sanh sat in the throne and listened to Truc Phap Thai lecture on the sutras.
