He thoroughly understood the content, then went up to the throne to lecture and discuss with the monks and famous scholars of his time; words as solid as pearls. At the age of twenty, his reputation for lecturing on the classics spread far and wide, causing princes and aristocrats to admire him and travel thousands of miles to listen to the Dharma.

Dao Sanh treated those who received him with gifts in a gentle and careful manner. Calm personality, deep and strong spirit. When he was young, Dao Sanh once went to Lo Son mountain. Feeling that the Buddha Dharma was profound, he determined to live there in seclusion to study the teachings. He often told himself that he must clearly understand the meaning of the scriptures in order to enter the door of Buddhism, so he should study and examine the scriptures thoroughly.

In the year 391, in response to Huiyuan's request, the monk Sanghadeva went to Lo Son mountain to translate the Abhidharma doctrine of the Hinayana. On that occasion, Dao Sanh and Hui Vien came close to the monk Sangha Deva to study the doctrine of the Sarvastivada School. After seven years of staying at Mount Lo Son, Dao Sanh, along with Sang Due, Hui Quan, and Hue Nghiem, went to Truong An to follow Kumarajiva to study the Prajnaparamita teachings of the Mahayana. A few years later, when discussing with the monks, Dao Sanh was praised by them as a miraculous genius with extraordinary intelligence, making the monks respect him. At Tieu Dien Vien, Dao Sanh and Dao Dung debated teachings hundreds of times. When the crowd heard Dao Sanh's sharp words, they all praised and admired the wise and intelligent man.

As soon as Kumarajiva became naturalized citizen, Dao Sanh returned to Kien Khang (Nan Kinh) and stayed at Thanh Vien pagoda. This pagoda was originally the garden of Queen Tru Thi in the Eastern Jin dynasty, and was built by her, so it was named Thanh Vien. The main hall of Thanh Vien pagoda was later struck by lightning, then a dragon flew from inside the pagoda into the sky, causing the surrounding area to radiate light, so the pagoda was renamed Long Quang Tu. At that time, the residents at Thanh Vien pagoda were all famous monks.

One time, Emperor Wu of Song held a banquet for the monks. To show his respect, Emperor Wu of Song personally went into the kitchen to cook, forgetting the time. After noon, the party opened. According to the precepts, after noon, monks are not allowed to eat rice. Therefore, no one in the public dares to have a party. Seeing this, Emperor Wu of Song said:

- The sun is just at noon, not yet past noon!

However, the masses remained silent, no one dared to violate the precepts. Dao Sanh said:

- The sun is in the sky, and now the sky (heaven, only for the king; the king according to the Chinese concept is Thien Tu) points at noon, so it must be right at noon.

Having finished speaking, Dao Sanh took the bowl and ate. The crowd looked at each other, then happily followed Dao Sanh and ate. Everyone praised Dao Sanh's diligence in adapting to the opportunity to handle matters. Famous scholars such as Vuong Hoang Nhan Duyen, etc. all admired his style, so they often came to inquire about Buddha's teachings. King Tong Van De also often visited him out of respect and admiration.

Having considered the teachings for a long time, he finally realized the essence of the scriptures beyond language, so he lamented to himself:

- Images exist by expressing thoughts. Once the concept is opened, the form certainly no longer exists. Language is used to explain meaning. Once the meaning is understood, there is no need to be attached to the linguistic form. Since Buddhism spread to Central Earth, many sutras have been translated, but most people only rely on the written word, so few people clearly see the complete meaning of Buddhism. After getting the fish, you should leave the basket, only then can you fully understand the true principles of Buddha Dharma.

Therefore, after reviewing all the internal and external scriptures, researching and examining the cause-and-effect relationship, he finally wrote the logic 'Doing good deeds does not seek retribution', 'Achieving enlightenment to become a Buddha', and before writing the books 'The Two Noble Truths', 'The Treatise on Buddha Nature's Existence', 'The Formless Law of the Dharmakaya', 'The Buddha's Pure Land Commentary', 'The Treatise on Dependent Existence', etc., are all filled with many reasons, and overflowing with profound intentions. However, this action led to continuous opposition and attacks by conservatives on the text, because of the fear that Dao Sanh changed the meaning of the scriptures. In addition, there was another incident that caused Dao Sanh to be kicked out of the Buddhist scriptures by the monks as follows:

At that time, the 'Great Parinirvana' sutra had not yet been transmitted to the south, but only six volumes of 'Ne Hoan Sutra' were transmitted to the scribes. The six books preach that all sentient beings have Buddha nature, except for the Icchantika class (i.e., all good roots are cut off). However, Mr. Dao Sanh, after thoroughly studying, analyzing and exploring the meanings of the scriptures, and penetrating into the hidden places, proposed the policy that 'Ichchantika people also have Buddha nature.'

This theory was criticized by those who followed the old school, saying it was an evil theory that fascinated the world. More and more people criticize and resent His doctrine. Everyone thought that only by expelling Dao Sanh from the capital could that evil doctrine be stopped. Knowing that there was no way to convince everyone at this time, in front of the crowd, Mr. Dao Sanh solemnly made his vow:

- If my policy goes against the teachings of the Buddhist scriptures, I vow that if I manifest, I will immediately feel leprosy. My theory, if it is in accordance with the right path, then I pray that when I give up this body, I will ascend to the throne of a lion.

Having finished speaking, he dusted off his robes and left the capital to go to Huqiu Mountain in the east of Wu. In ten days, hundreds of disciples were collected. According to the twenty-sixth book 'Buddhist Records', while staying at Tiger Mountain, Dao Sanh preached the Nirvana Sutra to the rocks. He preached that Icchantika also had Buddha nature, so the rocks nodded. This story is called 'Dao Sanh preaches the Dharma, the rocks nod.'

During the summer, the main hall of Thanh Vien Pagoda was suddenly struck by lightning, then suddenly a dragon flew out of there into the void, then disappeared, but its shadow still remained on the western wall of the pagoda. Therefore, the monks changed the pagoda's name to Long Quang. Then someone said:

- If the dragon has flown away, Dao Sanh must have gone far away.

Not long after, when he reached Lo Son mountain, he was greatly admired and respected by the monks in the mountain. The Mahaparinirvana Sutra was later transmitted to the scribes by Phap Hien who brought the Sanskrit text from Thien Truc, and then hundreds of monks and monks jointly translated it into Chinese. After being translated, everyone learned that the sutra confirms that Icchantika also has Buddha nature; This argument corresponds to Mr. Dao Sanh's ancient policy.

Mr. Dao Sanh then brought the newly translated Nirvana Sutra to explain to the masses. The monks in the Buddhist scriptures knew that Dao Sanh's doctrine was in accordance with the scriptures, so they welcomed him back to Long Quang pagoda to preach the Dharma. In general, this doctrine of Dao Sanh was accepted by the monks about two years before he became a citizen.

In 434, at Dong Lam Pagoda in Lo Son, he again composed the book 'Phap Hoa Sutra'. In winter, he ascended the throne to preach the Dharma, his expression was quiet, his voice was resounding. He argued one after another, his arguments were wonderful, causing his listeners to experience abundant Dharma joy. As soon as he finished preaching, he picked up the wand and threw it on the ground, then sat on the throne, his appearance serious, naturally passed away, but his expression was as usual, his appearance was like entering concentration. This sign corresponds to His ancient vow:

- When you give up this retribution body, you will ascend to the lion throne and pass away.

The news of Mr. Dao Sanh's naturalization had just spread, no matter monks or lay people far and near, everyone felt sympathy and regret. The monks at the Buddhist monk, with deep shame and shame, admired the teachings of Mr. Dao Sanh in the past. Later, followers buried Dao Sanh's body at Lo Son mountain.

Mr. Dao Sanh wrote a lot. The book 'Exit Tripitaka' records as follows: 1/ Vimalakirti Sutra Meaning and Commentary (when composing the book Vimalakirti Sutra, Tang Trieu not only quoted Kumarajiva's explanations, but also used Dao Sanh's commentaries on this sutra); 2/ The Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sutra (2 volumes. In the Sutta Pitaka, the volume 'Mahayana Four Commentaries on Mysterious Meanings' quotes Dao Sanh's commentary on this sutra); 3/ Ne Complete Sutra of Meanings; 4/ Skit piece Sutra Meaning Sutra; 5/ Good Life Retribution; 6/ Achieving Buddha's Enlightenment; 7/ The Two Truths; 8/ Buddha Nature Existence; 9/ Formless Dharmakāya; 10/ Buddha's Pure Land Commentary; 11/ Treatise on Dependent Origination; 12/ Nirvana Thirty-Six Questions; 13/ Thich Bat Tru First Mind, Duc Thu Ne Hoan Nghia; 14/ Understanding Buddha's Nature and Meaning; 15/ Truc Dao Sanh responded to Vuong Van with one hand, Truc Dao Sanh responded to Vuong Hoang Don's Book of Enlightenment; 16/ Asking about the Taoist monks of Buddha Nghia and Pham Ba Luan; 17/ The Sangha of the Monks asked questions; 18/ Pham Trong asks Dao Sanh to return to the Three Hands; 19/ Pho Quy responded to Pham Ba Luan's letter.

According to the treatise 'The Formless Dharma Body', Mr. Dao Sanh wrote: "If the Buddha had a form, many contradictions would arise. The form is inherently impermanent. If the Buddha had a form, then the Buddha would also be impermanent, so contrary to the theory that the Buddha is eternal. Furthermore, if the Buddha has a form, and the form is limited, so the Buddha is also limited; this contradicts the reason that the Buddha is unlimited. In addition, if form depends on the Buddha, then form depends on the Buddha. must not change, because Buddha is eternal and immutable. Having form means having to change; that is natural, so this policy cannot be established.

Discussing the argument 'Buddha has no Pure Land', Mr. Dao Sanh wrote: "For the sake of teaching and receiving sentient beings, the Pure Land is used. Buddha does not have a body; it is only because he wants to express it through language that he is called Buddha. Buddha does not have a realm of land, only because of expediency does he have a Pure Land, to make sentient beings rely on. According to the stance of the first noble truth, Buddha does not have a realm of land, and also has no realm. No Pure Land exists. The Pure Land is a means, then the retribution due to good deeds is also a means."

According to the argument 'Good Without Retribution, Mr. Dao Sanh wrote: "The principle of a monk is to be selfless, not to seek merit; that is the manifestation of the principle of non-action; and to seek benefits, there is no merit. This principle is the same as absolute goodness. Doing good deeds does not expect the reward of merit or benefit."

Dao Sanh's thought 'Good deeds have no merit' is similar to Bodhidharma's answer 'No merit' to Emperor Liang Wu.

Regarding the principle of 'Slowly Enlightenment to Become a Buddha', Mr. Dao Sanh wrote: "Sudden enlightenment is the ultimate understanding of non-dual enlightenment, that is, in accordance with the principle of non-duality. Non-dual enlightenment is the principle of indistinguishability. Non-dual enlightenment is true wisdom that cannot be seen. This true wisdom is combined with the principle of indistinguishability, which is called sudden enlightenment. Understanding is enlightenment. Written explanation is faith. Faith and understanding are not real. Once enlightened, faith immediately falls away. This is This is a natural principle, for example, if the fruit is ripe, it must fall. Enlightenment is not an inherent nature, so we must rely on faith to arise in accordance with the layers of inspiration. When enlightenment reaches the point of cutting off afflictions, then faith becomes useless. The saints often advise practitioners that when they are close to enlightenment, they must try their best, that is, they will reach enlightenment.

Truth is natural, not done, not created. Buddha nature is equal and quietly shines. Non-action means not lying. Often illuminated means not hidden. Full non-dual wisdom is in accordance with the principle of indistinguishability. Suddenly gaining insight, the ice suddenly melts, that is called sudden enlightenment. However, once enlightened, one must gradually practice.

'Knowing clearly one thought' refers to suddenly realizing all-knowing wisdom. Thanks to gradual practice, omniscience is attained. First, practice is based on the direct mind, then the final point is to achieve omniscience. Here, it is explained that attainment is necessarily sudden enlightenment, and that practice must be achieved gradually."

tieu_de: 20B. Master Tang Trieu - An interpreter of Prajna's thought
tom_tat: B. Master Tang Trieu, an interpreter of Prajna's thought.
noi_dung:
20B. Master Tang Trieu - An interpreter of Prajna's thoughtB. Master Tang Trieu, an interpreter of Prajna's thought.

Zeng Zhao's book 'Trieu Treatise' had a great influence on the history of Chinese Buddhist thought. Tang Trieu was originally a talented disciple of Kumarajiva, and was the one who accurately understood Nagarjuna's idea of ​​Khong Quan.

Tang Trieu was born in 385, originally from Kinh Bac, studied with Kumarajiva for more than ten years, and also participated in the work of translating classics in Chang'an. When I was still at home, because my family was poor and had to write for others, I read and read historical scriptures, understood classical scriptures, loved mystical scholarship, and knew Lao Zhuang's thoughts well. At that time, Lao Trang's thoughts were circulating everywhere. When he was young, Tang Trieu once read Lao Tzu's Tao Te Ching, but did not feel satisfied. Although I understand clearly, the path of 'peace of mind and liberation' is still not clear:

- In this book, the discussion is so complete and accurate, it makes people wake up a bit. However, it is essential to teach how spirituality can have a place of direction and eliminate the shackles of worldliness. Therefore, the content in this book is not considered perfect.

When I came across the Vimalakirti Sutra, I was extremely happy and said:

- This is where we know where to turn!

Thanks to that opportunity, Tang Trieu developed the intention to become a monk. Zeng Trieu studied Dao An's Prajnaparamita Sutra, making it the focus of his practice and understanding of the sutras, so even though he was only twenty years old, his reputation resonated throughout Truong An. Because of the teenager's fame, some people were jealous and came to Truong An and Tang Trieu to debate. Although he is young, his thoughts are profound and he is eloquent and eloquent. Truong An is a place where talented people gather, but Tang Trieu comes in and out like no one else.

Although he was imbued with Lao Tzu's thoughts and the Vimalakirti Sutra, he had just heard about Kumarajiva's virtue in Luong Chau, so Zeng Trieu did not care about traveling thousands of miles, but went there to study in the year 398. At that time, regarding Kumarajiva's Khong Quan teachings, Monk Trieu was as hungry as seeing a feast, so he absorbed it quickly. As for the Middle Treatise and the Twelve Doors that Kumarajiva had just translated, the talented monk Tang Trieu tried his best to accept it. Therefore, Kumarajiva often praised Tang Trieu, who was a young monk of outstanding talent and maturity in teachings.

When Kumarajiva was invited by King Dao Hung to Truong An, of course Tang Trieu also followed. King Dao Hung ordered Tang Trieu and Tang Due to reside in Tieu Dien Vien and assist Kumarajiva in translating the sutras.

Looking through the old translations, there were mistakes, so Zeng Trieu often asked Kumarajiva; Thanks to that, there is enlightenment. Regarding the teachings of the treatises authored by Nagarjuna and Devadava, Zeng Trieu accepted them all, and devoted all his attention to seeking the exact explanation of Prajnaparamita and Khong Nghia. These teachings are completely different from Lao Trang's ideology. After completing the translation of the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra, the Hundred Treatises, and the Great Wisdom Sutra, Kumarajiva annotated and explained clearly those sutras. Thanks to that, Monk Trieu received the principles of Prajnaparamita and Mahayana Emptiness, so he felt inspired to compose from the previous articles and commentaries, and wrote the book 'Prajna Without Wisdom', to promote the doctrine of Prajna Emptiness. According to Tang Trieu, Prajna Khong Nghia is the basic teaching of Buddha, and the explanation of Prajna is the basic thought of Buddhism. The book 'Prajna of No Wisdom' also displays Kumarajiva's teachings on the essence of Khong Quan philosophy. This book 'Prajna of Wisdom', quotes philosophy from sutras such as: Radiant Prajna Sutra, Prajnaparamita Sutra of Path and Conduct, Vimalakirti Sutra, and the Hundred Commentaries, etc.

At the end of the summer of 407, Dao Sanh brought Zeng Trieu's book 'Prajna of the Infinite Wisdom' to Lo Son Mountain, then gave it to Liu Di Min to review. After reading, Liu Di Dan praised:

- Who would have thought that among the clergy there would be a man like 'Ha Yen (the founder of mystical logic in the Eastern Jin dynasty) like this?

After being shown this treatise by Liu Di Dan, Hue Vien praised:

- Never before have I seen such brilliant literature!

Knowing that this treatise was not ordinary, Mr. Hue Vien and Liu Di Dan studied it thoroughly. From then on, Liu Di Dan often wrote poems to Tang Trieu to ask about the meaning of Prajna. During the last six years of his life, Tang Trieu often practiced diligently despite many illnesses, which made Hue Vien very respectful.

Under the court of Kumarajiva, Sangha received the teachings of Khong Quan from Nagarjuna and Devadava, so he was endlessly grateful. In Chang'an, receiving Liu Yimin's 'Reciting the Buddha's Samadhi' and Huiyuan's 'Samadhi', Tang Trieu returned the favor and sent them the newly translated Vimalakirti Sutra, with additional comments. Hui Yuan had read the book 'Prajna of Wisdom' and the book 'Commentary to the Vimalakirti Sutra' given to him by Zeng Trieu, so he had a profound understanding of Kumarajiva's teachings of Emptiness.

Zeng Zhao became a naturalized citizen when he was only thirty-one years old, in 414.

The works previously narrated by Zeng Trieu are as follows: Prajnaparamita of Wisdom, Abhidharma of Absolute Emptiness, Abhidharma of Objects of Heaven, Nibbāna of the Nameless, True Abhidharma of the Six-True Staff, Vimalakirti Sutra, Vimalakirti Sutra, Truong A Ham Sutra, Hundred Treatises, Da Liu Di Dan Shu.

tom_tat: C. Sangha Rui, Primordial Analytical Form Teachings.
noi_dung:
20C. Tang Rui - Teacher General AnalysisC. Sangha Rui, Primordial Analytical Form Teachings.

Zeng Rui was from Changle in Wei County and became a monk at a young age. At the age of eighteen, he became a disciple of shaman Tang Hien. At the age of twenty-two, he mastered the scriptures. When Zeng Lang lectured on the Radiance Sutra, Zeng Rui often proposed questions for questioning and criticism. For this reason, Tang Lang and Tang Hien became friends. Tang Lang told Tang Hien:

- Tang Due, senior brother's disciple, is so smart!

At the age of twenty-four, he went abroad to seek enlightenment. When he arrived at the Tay Thuc border area, he was captured and forced to herd goats. The merchant saw his appearance and suspected that he was a monk, so he inquired about the meaning of the scriptures. From Tay Thuc, Tang Due went to Yunnan, passed through Giao Chi (Vietnam), then came into contact with traders and followed them to southern Thien Truc. Thanks to that, his knowledge of Sanskrit is very outstanding. At the age of twenty-seven, his wandering life ended.

At the age of twenty-eight, Zeng Due once went to Dao An's court in Chang'an, and helped Dao An with royalties for the translation of the Four A Ham Sutras. At the age of thirty-three, when the Qin dynasty was destroyed, along with the naturalization of Dao An, Tang Due took refuge in Lo Son mountain and studied the method of reciting Buddha's name under Hue Vien's court.

Not long after entering Lo Son, he heard that Kumarajiva had come to Truong An, so Tang Due immediately went to seek enlightenment. At Chang'an, at the request of Zeng Rui, Kumarajiva translated the book 'Essentials of Zen Dharma'. Tang Due's noble personality and profound knowledge earned respect from King Dao Hung and Dao Sung. Dao Sung praised Tang Due as the subordinate of Nghiep Ve (the land of Wei Huyen, where Tang Due came from), while King Dao Hung honored Tang Due as the leader and representative flag of the four seas. When Kumarajiva translated the Lotus Sutra, Tang Rui brightened and refined his beautiful prose.

After finishing translating the book 'Truthful Treatise, Kumarajiva Thap told Sangha Rui:

- This essay has seven places to break the words of the Bhikkhu, but only where the essay's distinction is not clear. If you don't need to ask me, but have the ability to discern those seven places, then you can be called talented!

Monk Rui had no doubts, he proposed those seven places very easily, causing Kumarajiva to praise:

- I specialize in translating classics, so you can understand them clearly. Really no regrets!

Zeng Rui wrote many prefaces for the sutras translated by Kumarajiva, such as: Little Product Sutra (fourth), Phap Hoa Sutra (ninth), Self-wit Sutra (eleven), Vairocana Sutra (fourteenth), Self-Consciousness Sutra (fifteenth), Avalokiteshvara Sutra (thirteen).

After Kumarajiva entered the natural state, Tang Due slowly turned towards the method of praying for rebirth in the Western world. At the end of the Later Qin Dynasty, due to the chaos of the religion, Tang Due went to Jiangnan to take refuge, and studied under Hue Vien's court at Lo Son. In 416, Hue Vien became a naturalized citizen, Tang Due did not aim to stay at Lo Son, but went to the capital Kien Nghiep in Jiangnan, abbot of Dieu Y pagoda. In 420, when he was nearly seventy years old, Zeng Due often preached sutras and sermons. King Nghi Khang in Pengcheng appealed three times, only then Tang Due accepted him as his disciple. In response to Ta Linh Yun's request, Tang Due wrote the book 'Twenty-Sound Instructions' to demonstrate the similarity between Sanskrit and Chinese. At that time, Tang Due also wrote the book 'Du Nghi'.

Since coming to Lo Son, Tang Due has always wished to be reborn in the Western world. When he knew that his life was about to end, he followed the disciples and said:

- At birth, I often vow to be reborn in the West. Think to yourself that the three actions of body, speech, and mind never go against the precepts, so you will definitely be reborn, without the slightest doubt. May the great mercy (Amitabha Buddha), filled with compassion, cause all lifetimes to be reborn in the Western world because of the dharma!

Having finished speaking, he went into the monk's room, took a bath, offered incense, worshiped, clasped his hands facing the West and passed away. That day, in Tang Due's monk's room, a cloud of five-colored incense suddenly appeared. It was the year 433; Tang Rui lived to be eighty-five years old.

Tang Due's thoughts are most clearly expressed through the book 'Du Nghi'. While working as a disciple of Kumarajiva at Chang'an, Tang Due studied the essence of the Prajnaparamita Sutra and the Lotus Sutra. While in Jiangnan, he encountered the Mahaprajnaparamita sutra brought back by Mr. Fa Hien from the Western Regions. Tang Due studied and compared the relationship of the three sutras of Prajnaparamita, Phap Hoa and Nehuan, and then wrote the treatise 'Du Nghi' to respond to the doubts of scholars. In addition, Truc Phap Do, because of his belief in Hinayana teachings, often rejected the Mahayana sutras translated by Kumarajiva. Hui Dao and Dam Lac questioned and slandered Mahayana scriptures such as the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra, Lotus Sutra, etc., so in Chang'an, they committed countless crimes, leading to public criticism. Due to defaming the Nirvana Sutra in Chang'an and Pengcheng, Zeng Uyen's tongue was burned, which he realized was the retribution for defaming the Sutra. Tang Uyen originally followed Tang Sung to study the Truth Commentary and the Pi-Dam, and became a scholar of the Truth Truth Commentary.

Seeing the defamation of Mahayana scriptures, Tang Due felt extremely sad. In order to support righteousness and suppress evil, Tang Due wrote the treatise 'Duc Nghi' to illustrate the meaning of the Prajnaparamita Sutra, Phap Hoa and Ne Hoan (i.e. Nirvana), with special focus on the Ne Hoan Sutra.

At the time of Kumarajiva, the Nehuan Sutra had not yet been translated, but only the Dharmakaya Sutra, which clearly explained the types of dharmakaya of the Buddhas. Kumarajiva said that sentient beings who listen to Buddha's teachings have a true self, and all have Buddha nature, which is already complete!

The Lotus Sutra advocates that everyone who sees the Buddha with knowledge and knowledge will become Buddhas, but has not yet shown the reason that all sentient beings will become Buddhas.

The Great Prajnaparamita Sutra was brought by Mr. Phap Hien from Thien Truc to Duong Do, then gathered by more than a hundred monks of great virtue to translate it. The Nehuan Sutra brought new teachings to Chinese Buddhism: The Buddha nature of all living beings exists; All sentient beings have Buddha nature. The Lotus Sutra has never explained this clearly. Tang Due advocated that the Dharmakaya in the Dharmakaya Sutra is equivalent to the Buddha nature of the Nehuan Sutra, and wrote the book 'Examples of Nghi'. For its decisive judgment on teachings, this treatise has an important position in the history of Chinese Buddhism.

tieu_de: 20D. The disciples of Kumarajiva (Dao Dung, Dam Anh, Dao Hang...)
tom_tat: D. Master Dao Dung.
noi_dung:
20D. The disciples of Kumarajiva (Dao Dung, Dam Anh, Dao Hang...)D. Master Dao Dung.

Dao Dung is one of the four great disciples of Kumarajiva. According to the sixth book 'Cao Tang's Story', Dao Dung was from Lam Lu in Can Do, became a monk at the age of twelve, and was loved by his original teacher for his talent, so he told him to memorize 'The Analects'. From then until the age of thirty, depending on your heart's desire, study the internal and external classics. Hearing that Kumarajiva came to Chang'an, Dao Dung immediately went to the court to study the Dharma. Kumarajiva introduced Dao Dung to King Dao Hung:

- This person especially has the Shakyamuni seed and is super intelligent.

King Dao Hung then invited Dao Dung to Tieu Dieu Vien to assist in the translation. At Dao Dung's request, Kumarajiva translated the book 'Bodhisattva Precepts'. When he was old, Kumarajiva translated the book The Middle Treatise, then Dao Dung lectured and analyzed the literature, making the translated language neat and smooth. Kumarajiva told Dao Dung to preach the Lotus Sutra that had just been translated, and praised:

- The prosperity of Buddhism is thanks to this amazing person Dao Dung!

At that time, a Brahmin from Thien Truc came to Truong An, specializing in arguing with Chinese monks. Knowing clearly that except for Dao Dung, no one among his disciples was capable of debating with this Brahmin, so Kumarajiva sent Dao Dung to debate. Because he had never read a pagan's books, Dao Dung asked someone to copy the Brahman's sutras and arguments, then memorized them in his mind. The discussion hall was publicly held with the participation of King Dao Hung, his dukes, martial arts officials, and monks in Truong An. Brahman knew that his theory was not as good as that of Dao Dung, so he boasted that he had read many sutras. Therefore, Dao Dung also proposed a list of historical scriptures three times greater than the number of other Brahmans. Seeing this, Kumarajiva told that brahmin:

- You probably don't know that China has such scholars, yet you carelessly come all the way here to compete!

That Brahman was ashamed of himself, so he bowed down to Dao Dung and begged for repentance. After a few days, no one knew where the Brahmin went. This story shows that Dao Dung's academic and intellectual abilities are extraordinary.

Dao Dung attended Kumarajiva for about fifteen years. Because of that change, and later because Kumarajiva was naturalized, Dao Dung left Truong An to go to Peng Thanh, at the age of fifty. There, Dao Dung continued to preach the sutras and preach the Dharma, making his reputation far and wide; More than a thousand people often come to ask questions, and more than three hundred disciples often study closely. At the age of seventy-four, Dao Dung became naturalized citizen in Banh Thanh. Dao Dung wrote commentaries on the Lotus Sutra, Golden Light, Ten Grounds, Vimalakirti, etc.

Cao Tang Truyen, the eighth volume wrote: "The sublime virtues and great contributions of Dao Dung, Zeng Trieu, Dao Hang, and Dam Anh, greatly influenced Buddhism in Chang'an."

E. Teacher Dam Anh.

Dam Anh was originally from the north. He did not often converse with others. He only lived in poverty and studied. He often preached the Dharma Flower Sutra and the Prajnaparamita Sutra (translated by Mr. Truc Phap Ho), whose lay audience had more than a thousand people. Arriving at Truong An, Dam Anh was warmly treated by King Dao Hung. When Kumarajiva entered Chang'an, Dam Anh came close to the court to study religion, at the age of sixty (older than Kumarajiva). Kumarajiva said to King Dao Hung:

- Dam Anh is a monk who represents great purity and virtue.

Therefore, King Dao Hung ordered Dam Anh to go to Tieu Dieu Vien to assist in translating the scriptures.

When the commentary on Truthfulness was finished being translated, Dam Anh and Kumarajiva discussed and answered the entire idea. Because he had lectured on the Dharma Flower Sutra (translated by Truc Phap Ho), Kumarajiva had just finished translating the New Dharma Flower Sutra when Dam Anh devoted himself to editing this sutra, and wrote four volumes of commentaries on its profound and wonderful meanings. According to the story, Dam Anh directly participated in translating or commenting on sutras such as the Treatise on Truth, the Middle Treatise, and the Lotus Sutra.

Kumarajiva had just become naturalized citizens, and Dam Anh went into retreat at Son Lam pagoda, hoping to preserve his temper and strive to practice, so that even though he was old, his spirit would still be prosperous. Dam Anh finally became a naturalized citizen at the age of seventy.

Among Kumarajiva's disciples, there were not only excellent translators and commentators, but also people with full political intelligence such as Dao Heng (346-417) and Dao Tieu.

G. Master Dao Hang and Dao Tieu.

Dao Hang is from Lam Dien. At the age of nine, the hermit Truong Trung predicted:

- This boy has all the characteristics of a great man. If you live in the secular world, you will become a Prime Minister, but if you become a monk, you will become a high monk, making the Buddha Dharma shine brightly.

When he was young, Dao Hang soon mourned his father. When he was twenty years old, his mother also passed away, so he became a monk. When Kumarajiva entered Chang'an, Dao Heng immediately came close to him and participated in the translation work. Dao Hang and Dao Tieu were more talented than others, so their fame was famous throughout Truong An. Knowing that the two were talented in political knowledge, King Dao Hung sent Dao Hien to find a way to advise them to return to the secular world and request support to support the throne. King Dao Hung also often wrote poems directly asking them to support the court.

At that time, King Dao Hung often needed to ask talented people to help the country, and also summoned hermits from the mountains and forests to the capital to assist. Due to the encouragement of King Dao Hung, the hermit Tang Lu returned to the secular world and returned to the court to take office. However, the main subjects of King Dao Hung were Dao Hang and Dao Tieu. Although they had some reputation, and knew that the world was impermanent, and showed that they were monks, Dao Hang and Dao Tieu sincerely rejected King Dao Hung's request. Because the time was important, King Dao Hung three times summoned two lieutenants to his court. However, the two still refused, and wrote a poem to King Dao Hung to express their will: "We have been practicing Buddhism since childhood. We want to use our foolish minds to become enlightened, put on our small bodies and wear Dharma clothes to save sentient beings. This small wish, the Holy Supreme has mercy on us. Even though we say we want to propagate the Bodhisattva way, but according to the vision of a monk, our strength is really limited, so it is difficult to answer. comply with the Supreme Lord's decree!"

Seeing that he could not advise the two, King Dao Hung wrote a poem asking Kumarajiva to advise them to return to the world to help him. This shows that Dao Hung's court did not have enough great advisors, so it looked up to Dao Hang and Dao Tieu.

King Dao Hung wrote a poem to Dao Tuyen (who took on the responsibility of censoring the monks in the country): "Although Dao Hang and Dao Tieu are monks, they have enough talent to regulate worldly affairs. Hopefully they will follow My wishes."

Regarding the fact that King Dao Hung three times requested Dao Hang and Dao Tieu to serve in the government, Kumarajiva, Tang Tuyen, etc. realized that these two could not take off their robes and take care of court affairs, so they wrote poems to present to King Dao Hung: "Buddhist monks must take the practice of discipline and practice as the most important thing. Monks must be monks. People who become monks cannot do anything useful in worldly politics. There, the two monks, Dao Hang and Dao Tieu, only had a small wish to keep their duty.

Thanks to Mr. Kumarajiva, Sangjun, etc., offering tributes, the royal court approved Dao Hang and Dao Tieu to continue to become monks and practice the religion. Dao Hang said gratefully:

- There is an ancient saying: 'People who seek wealth for their own benefit make the devil dislike them. A person who makes himself famous is committing suicide', this is not an empty statement.

After Kumarajiva passed away, Dao Heng went into a mountain valley to meditate; eat wild vegetables, drink spring water, wear simple robes, practice meditation, cut off association with the world, and then become naturalized at the age of seventy-two (417). Dao Hang's predecessors were the books 'Thich Bo Luan' and 'Hundred Elements'. Dao Tieu wrote two books, 'Sariputta Abhidharma Tu' and 'Diaeu Vuong Kieu Van.'

The book 'Thich Bac Luan' was written by Dao Hang in his old age, to satirize the rejection of Buddhism and monks by two Taoist monks named Vien and Ha.

tom_tat: Buddha Da Bat Da La, translated as Giac Hien in Chinese, is from the country of Ca Duy La Ve (Nepali), and is a descendant of the Shakyamuni lineage...
noi_dung:
21. Buddha Da La (Buddhadhadra)Buddha Da Bat Da La, translated as Giac Hien in China, was from the country of Ca Duy La Ve (Nepali), a descendant of the Shakyamuni lineage, born in the year 359. Because his paternal ancestor, Dat Ma De Ba (translated in Chinese as Giac Thien) often went to northern Thien Truc to trade, his family migrated to live in the country of Ca Duy La Ve. At the age of three, his father passed away, and then at the age of five, his mother also passed away. Therefore, he was raised by his uncle's family. The monk Patriarch Kumarajiva knew that Buddha Da Bat Da La was very intelligent and diligent, so he asked his uncle to let him become a monk. At the age of seventeen, his daily work was to memorize sutras. The verses that fellow students had to learn in a month, for him it only took a day to memorize.

After receiving the full precepts, he became even more diligent in practicing meditation and precepts, and learned extensively about the scriptures. He and the monk Sangha Dat Da went to study abroad in Ke Tan country. Although they were of the same age, monk Sangha Datta greatly admired his outstanding talent, but did not know what realm he had reached. One time, while he was in retreat and meditating, Sangha Datta suddenly saw him coming and asked where he came from. He replied:

- I just went to Tu Suat heaven to worship Bodhisattva Maitreya and then returned here.

Having finished speaking, Buddha Da Bat Da La immediately disappeared. Only then did the monk Sangha Dat Da know that Buddha Da Bat Da La was a saint incarnate, so it was impossible to know his realm. Later, because he often saw his strange actions, Sangha Dat Da asked and found out that he had attained the status of Arahant 'No Complete' (i.e. A Na Ham).

He often liked to travel around neighboring countries to propagate Buddhism and observe people's customs. At that time, a Chinese monk, Tri Nghiem, went to Ke Tan country and saw that the monks were pure, so he wanted to invite the monks to come to China. The teacher often said:

- Chinese monks have the heart to seek Buddha Dharma, but have never met true great masters, so they cannot comprehend the Dharma.

Master Tri Nghiem traveled here and there, asking people in Ke Tan country who had the dignity and virtue to propagate Buddhism in Dong Do. We all say:

- There was a monk named Buddha Da Bat Da La, born in Thien Truc, whose family had always believed in Buddhism, became a monk at a young age, mastered the Buddhist scriptures, and had studied with the great Zen master Buddha Dai Tien.

At that time, Buddha Dai Tien also told Tri Nghiem:

- Only Buddha Da Bat Da La has the ability to promote Buddha Dharma and make a large number of monks inspired.

Due to Tri Nghiem's ​​sincere request, he agreed to go and preach the Dharma in Central Earth. After paying his respects to Master Buddha Dai Tien, he climbed over Thong Linh mountain, traveled through many mountains, rivers and deserts, passing through six countries. The kings there all made generous offerings after learning of his wish to propagate Buddhism. Three years later, he came to Giao Chau (Vietnam). Next, he got on the boat and continued his journey. One time, on the way to Giao Chau, the boat arrived at an island. Then he told the boat owner:

- You can stop at this island.

Boat owner said:

- The boat is moving with the wind on the sea and cannot easily stop here, because the passengers' time is very important.

Having finished speaking, the boat owner still let the boat run. After two hundred miles, suddenly encountering a storm, the boat was blown back to that island. When they were on the boat, they learned of his miraculous talent, so they worshiped him and listened to his instructions. When the wind was favorable, the boat owner decided to let the boat sail. He said:

- Can't depart!

Because the boat owner knew about His miracle, he listened and did not dare to set off lightly. Not long after, there was news that the boats that had previously set out to sea had all sunk. One night, He suddenly told the boat owner to set out to sea, but he did not listen. There was no other way, he alone unfurled the sails and let the boat sail out to sea. Moments later, the boats staying on that island were all plundered by pirates. Soon, the boat arrived at Qingzhou, east of Lai County in Central Earth. Hearing that Kumarajiva had come to Chang'an, he immediately went there to pay his respects. As soon as he met Buddha Dabatda La, Kumarajiva was very happy, and then they talked together. Buddha Dabat Da La asked Kumarajiva:

- There is nothing special about your explanation of the scriptures, but why does it attract so many people and make your reputation famous everywhere?

Kumarajiva replied:

- Because they have a deep relationship with me, they are respected. However, my talent and virtue are not commensurate with that reputation.

Whenever there was any doubt, Kumarajiva would discuss and resolve it with Buddha Dabatda La. However, because of the profound and superficial differences in their practice, the thoughts of the two Buddhas, Dabatda La and Kumarajiva, were also different, causing debates to often arise. One time, the Crown Prince of Later Qin, Dao Hoang, invited him to preach the Dharma. The monks gathered at the eastern palace to listen to sutras and discuss. At that time, the two Buddhas Dabatda La and Kumarajiva discussed the issue of 'Extreme Vi'. Kumarajiva asked:

- Why do we believe that all dharmas are inherently empty?

Buddha Da Bat Da La said:

- Matter is composed of countless microscopic particles, but has no self-nature, so it is all empty.

- If we use countless microscopic particles to form matter and say it is inherently empty, how can we prove that an extremely microscopic particle does not exist? - Many of us often preach to destroy microscopic particles. But, I don't use it that way.

- So are microscopic particles immortal?

- Looking at an extremely harmful mote, you will see that many mote particles will be destroyed. Looking at the perspective of many microscopic particles, one microscopic particle will be destroyed.

A few days later, the monks in Truong An again invited him to preach the Dharma. He said:

- All things have no self-nature. Only when conditions are sufficient will they arise. Because there is one microscopic particle, there are many microscopic particles. Extremely microscopic particles do not have an independent self-nature, so they are all empty.

King Dao Tan often made offerings to more than three thousand monks, so he had a very strong influence. He lived a quiet, frugal life, unlike the monks who often moved in and out of noble places. One time, He told them:

- I see five boats departing from Thien Truc and coming here.

This news was spread to the public, causing the monks in Truong An to all say that he spoke words that bewitched the masses. In Truong An, he widely propagated Zen Buddhism, causing Zen practitioners everywhere to hear its reputation come and practice. Because among the disciples there is a clear distinction between high and low, deep and shallow, so some disciples lie, pretend to be His name and do dirty things. One time, there was a disciple who told himself that he had attained Ana Ham, but he had never pressed the public to test it. This caused the monks in Truong An to continuously slander him. Due to fear of personal injury, His disciples had to hide and disperse. However, Mr. Giac remained leisurely and unmoved. Kumarajiva's disciple Dao Hang sent a letter to him, writing:

- Buddha never preached the Dharma he had attained. First, he told himself that there were five boats coming here; It's really a false illusion. Next, they went crazy again, bewitching the masses. That is a violation of the precepts of great false speech, so it cannot stay here. Please go somewhere else quickly.

He said:

- My body is as small as a foam, I come and go freely and easily. However, I only regret that my wish to propagate Buddhism has not been fulfilled.

Along with more than forty disciples, Hue Quan, etc., he left Truong An, but his demeanor was still calm and relaxed, without any sadness. Those who knew of his talent all regretted it and sent away thousands of people.

Hearing him leave Truong An, King Dao Hung regretted it so much that he told Dao Hang:

- Buddha Da Bat Da La, because he accepted the important responsibility of propagating Buddhism, came to Central Earth. His teachings made everyone feel impressed and praised. Why, just because of a wrong statement, makes people lose a guru?

Having finished speaking, King Dao Hung sent messengers to chase him and request him to return to Truong An. He told the messenger:

- I know the king's kindness, but unfortunately I cannot obey the order.

He then led his followers south, to Lo Son mountain. Having heard about the reputation of Buddha Da Bat Da La for a long time, Hue Vien happily came out to welcome him. Hue Vien knew that it was only because of his disciples' fault that Buddha Dabat Da La was slandered. Discussing the five boats that will go to Central Earth is just a personal opinion and does not violate the precepts. Therefore, Hue Vien wrote a letter to King Dao Hung and the monks in Truong An to exonerate Buddha Da Bat Da La, then requested him to go to the mountain to translate the Zen scriptures. Having the desire to spread the Dharma in the west, and not wanting to live in seclusion in one place, he soon went to Giang Lang. On the way, he met a foreign boat owner, his disciples asked him, and knew clearly that there were five boats from Thien Truc to Trung Tho. This statement is compatible with His ancient prediction. As soon as he arrived at Giang Lang, all the monks and nuns were racing to worship and make offerings. However, he did not accept any alms offerings, he only carried an alms bowl every day without distinguishing between rich and poor families.

Liu Yu (also known as Emperor Liu Song) led an army to conquer Liu Yi. Liu Yu's official, Yuanbao, in Chen County, also sent troops to Jiangling. One day, he and his disciple Hue Quan went to Vien Bao's mansion to beg for alms. Because Vien Bao did not believe in Buddhism, he treated him and Hue Quan very badly. Not having enough to eat, he and Hue Quan stood up to say goodbye. Vien Bao said:

- You haven't finished eating yet, why are you leaving?

He said:

- Your generosity is limited. However, I used up all the food you served.

Vien Bao then ordered someone to bring more rice, but sure enough, the rice was gone. Vien Bao felt embarrassed and asked Hue Quan:

- What kind of person is that monk?

Hue Quan says:

- He is a person of profound virtue, which ordinary people cannot understand.

Vien Bao was impressed by his miracle and told Liu Yu about it. Liu Yu then sent someone to invite him to come and see him. As soon as he met him, Liu Yu was very respectful and made offerings carefully. Returning to the capital, Liu Yu also invited him to Truong An, to reside at Dao Trang pagoda. His beliefs are true and upright, not the same as ordinary people, but his aspirations are also noble. Mages in the capital often tell each other:

- Zen master Buddha Da Bat Da La at Dao Trang pagoda has achieved the will of heaven, just like a king in Thien Truc.

The monk Chi Phap in Vu Dien requested a part of the Avatamsaka Sutra containing thirty thousand verses, which had not yet been translated. In the year 418, the internal history of Ngo District Manh Tieu, the left guard Tru Thuc Do again requested Buddha Da Bat Da La to translate. Together with more than a hundred monks such as Phap Nghia, Hue Nghia, Hue Nghiem, etc., he translated the first part of the Avatamsaka Sutra at Dao Trang Pagoda. The translated text was very fluent, reaching the essence of the sutra, so it was praised by everyone. The place where the Hoa Nghiem Sutra translation hall is located at Dao Trang Pagoda, is called the Hoa Nghiem Sutra Palace, to commemorate the achievement of the translation of the Sutra.

The sutras translated by Buddha Da Bat Da La are such as the Samadhi Sea Buddha Sutra (6 volumes), the Nirvana Sutra, the Treatise on the Means of Practice, etc. In total there are fifteen volumes, one hundred and seventeen volumes. Everything is compatible with the essential principles of the scriptures, and the translation is also very fluent and clear.

In 429, Buddha Da Bat Da La passed away, at the age of seventy-one years old.

tom_tat: Putra Da La, translated as Merit Flower. He was originally from Ke Tan country, became a monk at a young age, and was strict in his morality, causing everyone to say...
noi_dung:
22. PunyataraPutra Da La, translated as Merit Flower. He was originally from Ke Tan country, became a monk at a young age, and was strict in his morality, making everyone praise him. He thoroughly understood the three canonical sutras, and specialized in reciting the Ten Veritable Rules. He was originally a teacher of monks at home and abroad. People all said that he had attained sainthood.

In the Later Qin Dynasty, the reign of Hongshui (399-415), he carried his staff to Chang'an. King Dao Hung treated his guests with courtesy. Kumarajiva also revered the virtues of Putya Da La. At that time, many sutras had been translated, but the Vinaya Pitaka had not yet been promoted, so as soon as they heard the news of Phat Nha Da La coming to Truong An, everyone admired him. Kumarajiva then gathered all the famous monks in the capital to come and invite him to recite the Ten Sutta Rules. On the seventeenth day of the tenth month in the year 404, at Truong An Dai Temple, Phat Nha Da La recited the Ten Verses of Law; Kumarajiva translated it into Chinese. Of the three parts, just after translating two parts, Venerable Phat Nha Da La became ill and became a citizen. The great karma had not yet been accomplished but the saint passed away, causing the masses to mourn endlessly.

tom_tat: Dam Ma Luu Chi, translated as Phap Lac. He was originally from the Western Regions, left the custom and entered Buddhism, and was famous for regularly upholding the Vinaya.
noi_dung:
23. DharmaruciDam Ma Luu Chi, translated as Phap Lac. He was originally from the Western Regions, left the custom and entered Buddhism, and was famous for regularly upholding the Vinaya.

In the fall of 404, he arrived at Chang'an. Previously, Venerable Phat Nha Da La had not yet finished translating the book Ten Reciting Laws before becoming a citizen. Venerable Hue Vien at Lo Son, heard the reputation of Dam Ma Luu Chi specializing in reciting the Vinaya collection, and attained the final destination of the Vinaya Pitaka, so he wrote a letter to send: "Buddhism first arose in the upper country, gradually spreading to the Western Regions for more than four hundred years. Currently, the precepts of monks are very defective. Previously, the monk Phat Nha Da La from Ke Tan country came here to recite the book Ten Verses of Rules in English. Sanskrit, the learned magician Kumarajiva translated it into Chinese. After only half of it was translated, Phat Nha Da La passed away, leaving the great cause unfinished! Now that I heard that Nhan Gia brought this law, I am very happy to meet it.

Receiving Hue Vien's poem and being requested by King Dao Hung, Dam Ma Luu Chi together with Kumarajiva translated the entire set of the Ten Reciting Laws. After that, this code of law was thoroughly studied by the monks, then censored and edited. Unfortunately, before he could refine the meaning, Kumarajiva had already become naturalized citizen.

While staying at Truong An Dai Tu, Hui Quan invited him to the capital (Nan Kinh), Mr. Dam Ma Luu Chi replied:

- Here, there have been famous and virtuous beings who have passed on the Dharma to benefit people. We have to go to places where there is no religious law.

Therefore, he traveled to another direction, but no one knew where he became naturalized.

tom_tat: Mr. Dam Vo Sam is also called Dam Ma Sam, a person from Thien Truc. At the age of six, he mourned his father, then followed his mother to weave cloth everywhere to make a living...
noi_dung:
24. Dharmaraksa (Dharmaraksa)Mr. Dam Vo Sam is also called Dam Ma Sam, a person from Thien Truc. At the age of six, he mourned his father, then followed his mother to weave cloth everywhere to make a living. At that time, the monk Dat Ma Da Xa (Phap Minh) was very respected by the monks. The poor mother admired the monk Dat Ma Da Xa so she made generous offerings and allowed Dam Vo Sam to follow and study the Dharma. At the age of ten, he and his classmates learned to chant mantras. From there, the supernatural clarity of nature appears; In one day of reciting sutras, he could remember more than ten thousand words, so among the group of disciples, he was highly praised by monk Dat Ma Da Xa.

First, he studied the Hinayana dharma, along with the five enlightenment books of the Thien Truc kingdom. He also had a talent for preaching and the ability to argue with people, which no one could subdue. Later, he argued with Zen master Bach Dau for a hundred days. Finally, he had to admire Zen Master Bach Dau and asked:

- What other scriptures does Zen Master have? Can you show me?

Zen Master Bach Dau then gave him the Nirvana Sutra written on tree bark. Looking through this sutra, he felt even more ashamed of himself:

- I'm so rude. For a long time, I have never known the true path of Mahayana.

Therefore, he requested the public to practice repentance and vow to study Mahayana. At the age of twenty, he recited more than two million words.

Dam Vo Sam's brother specializes in training the king's elephants. One day, the king's white-eared elephant suddenly died, making the king angry, ordered him to kill him, and then issued a decree:

- If anyone dares to look at his body, I will banish the three clans!

Therefore, in the family, no one dared to disobey the king's orders, only he dared to come and pick up the body. When the king found out, he sent troops to arrest him and bring him into the palace to question him. With a naturally calm expression, without showing any signs of fear, He said:

- The Great King killed him according to the law. I also collected his body according to the blood relationship. Both of our actions are ethical, there is nothing wrong! Why are you still angry?

Seeing his noble spirit, the king not only forgave his death, but also kept him in the royal palace to make offerings.

Like Buddha Do Trung, Mr. Dam Vo Sam is proficient in magic spells, often displaying strange and very effective magical powers, causing people in the Western Region to call him 'Great Mantra Master'.

One time, he and the king went into the mountains. The king was thirsty and sent his bodyguards to look for water but could not find it. Seeing a large rock on the side of the road, he chanted a mantra to make water shoot out from that rock. He praised the king's kindness:

- Due to the Great King's grace, a stream of clear water was felt to flow out of this pebble.

Seeing his extraordinary and wonderful teachings, the king was very happy, so he treated him even more favorably. Before long, the king slowly shunned and treated him poorly. Seeing this, he then resigned from the king, then brought twelve volumes of the Great Nirvana Sutra, the Bodhisattva Precepts Sutra, etc. towards the Ke Tan and Kuchar countries. Because the people there originally believed in the Hinayana religion, they did not believe in the Mahayana scriptures. He had to go to Don Hoang again, then to Luong Chau. On the way to Co Tang, while staying at an inn, because he was afraid the sutras would be lost, he put the sutras in his pillow. When evening came, it seemed as if someone had pushed Him to the ground. Waking up, he thought they were thieves. However, this happened three nights in a row. On the fourth night, in the void suddenly a voice said:

- This is the sutra of Tathagata's liberation. Why do you lie down with your head covered?

Hearing these words, he immediately awakened, repented, respectfully worshiped, and placed the scriptures on a high place. That night, a thief came, intending to steal the sutras, but could not carry them because the sutras were too heavy. The next morning, waking up, he took the scriptures and left that place. Seeing Him leisurely carrying the scriptures, the robbers were shocked, praised Him as a saint, and ran to pray for repentance.

At that time, the Ha Tay King Mong Ton finished pacifying Don Hoang. Ha Tay Vuong originally believed in Buddhism, and had the will to propagate the true teachings. Hearing that he was coming to Dunhuang, King Ha Tay immediately invited him to stay in the royal garden in Luong Chau, and made generous offerings, and requested him to translate the sutras. However, because he was not fluent in Chinese and had no one to help him, he could not respond to the request to translate the sutras, but stayed there to study Chinese for three years.

He was revered by Mong Ton because he was a person who often displayed strange magic, just like Buddha Do Trung was respected by Thach Lac and Thach Ho. One time, he told Mong Ton:

- If ghosts and monsters have gathered, disasters will soon arise in the country.

Because he had never seen a ghost, Mong Ton did not believe it. However, thanks to him chanting the blessing mantra, causing the ghosts to appear, Mong Ton was very shocked and shocked. He said:

- You must sincerely maintain the precepts, then chant the mantra, then the ghosts will go away.

Next, he cast a spell for three consecutive days, causing all the demons to leave, so the country was peaceful. Seeing this with his own eyes, Mong Ton knew it was all thanks to his Taoist ability, so he respected him even more.

In 429, Mong Xun crossed the Yellow River and conquered the country of the King of Qin and Qu Fu Mo Mo. Mong Ton sent Crown Prince Hung Quoc to the vanguard. Qu Fu Mo Mat later counterattacked, destroyed the city, and captured Hung Quoc. In 430, Duke Helian of Xia defeated Qu Fu Mo Mo, and caused the destruction of Western Qin. However, during the war, Crown Prince Hung Quoc was killed. Receiving the bad news, Mong Ton was indignant and angry, saying:

- Serving Buddhism, but not getting good results!

Therefore, Mong Ton forced monks under fifty years old to return to the world. When this order was issued, the stone statue of Mong Ton's mother (sixteen meters high) suddenly shed tears. Furthermore, thanks to His best efforts to advise, Mong Ton gradually changed his mind to repent and abolish the above order. Therefore, Buddhism in the Northern Liang region continued to develop.

Tuoba Dao in Northern Wei (i.e. Thai Vo De, 424-451) heard that His mantra was very impressive, so he sent a messenger to the palace to invite Him to the court, and told Mong Ton:

- If we don't allow you to invite Mr. Dam Vo Sam, we will send troops to attack Bac Luong.

Northern Liang was a weak country, so Mong Ton was very afraid of Northern Wei. However, Mong Ton could not bear to let Mr. Dam Vo Sam go. Northern Wei Emperor Thai Vo sent envoys Cong Binh Cong and Quy Thuan to bring nine offerings to Northern Luong, determined to pay homage to Dam Vo Sam:

- I heard that the magician Dam Vo Sam is in the Great King's country. The country wants to invite the Dharma Master to the court to preach Buddhism. Please, Your Majesty, please accept and send away the magician Dam Vo Sam.

At the banquet for the envoy Quy Thuan, Mong Ton said:

- The old Tay Phien official Mong Ton served in the Northern Wei court, never daring to disobey, but Thien Tu listened to other people's mistakes, forcing me to hand over Dam Vo Sam. Previously, the ministers of Northern Wei had come here to make a request, and now they sent an envoy to make a request. Dam Vo Sam is a master, so we decided to live and die together.

Quy Thuan said:

- The Northern Wei court brought many gifts to the Northern Liang king. Why did Your Majesty abandon your industry for a long time because of a Thien Truc monk? Please think carefully, Your Majesty. The King of Northern Wei was truly sincere and devoted.

Because he was still determined not to give in to Mr. Dam Vo Sam, Mong Ton said:

- Your words are so clever, just like To Qin during the Warring States period. I'm afraid it's not a true statement.

Mong Ton told the messenger that because Dam Vo Sam was a master, they decided to live and die together. In fact, Mong Ton just wanted to take advantage of Dam Vo Sam's spells to maintain the throne, so he did not want to let him go to Northern Wei.

In 433, because he wanted to return to the Western Regions to request the last part of the Nirvana Sutra, he said goodbye to Mong Ton. Suspicious that he left Northern Liang to go to Northern Wei, Mong Ton secretly sent someone in disguise to bring him treasure and food, then plotted to kill him. Before the day of departure, He tearfully announced to the crowd:

- My karma is about to come, and even a saint cannot save me. However, I decided to follow my vow, that is, go to the West Region to pray for the last part of the Nirvana Sutra, so I cannot continue to stay here!

After traveling about forty miles, Mong Ton sent assassins to kill Mr. Dam Vo Sam on the way. At that time, Dam Vo Sam was forty-nine years old.

As soon as the news spread, monks from near and far came to mourn and pity him. Later, the court mandarins left and right during the day clearly saw many ghosts and gods carrying swords to slash Mong Ton. In April 433, Mong Ton fell ill and died.

Mr. Dam Vo Sam, himself knowledgeable in precepts, has the talent to translate classics, and has extraordinary supernatural powers.

According to the book 'Gao Tang's Story', while staying in Co Tang, there were many people who sincerely and seriously requested Mr. Dam Vo Sam to ordain the Bodhisattva precepts. The monk Dao Tan at Truong Dich wanted to seek the Bodhisattva precepts. He said:

- Temporarily repent of your sins, then discuss later!

Hearing these words, for seven days and nights, Dao Tan diligently repented. On the eighth day, Dao Tan came to seek precepts. As soon as he saw Dao Tan, he became extremely angry. Seeing that his karma had not been eliminated, Dao Tan devoted all his energy to practicing meditation for three consecutive years, then diligently repented. One night, Dao Tan dreamed of Shakyamuni Buddha and Bodhisattvas coming to give the precepts. The next day, Dao Tan came again to seek ordination. Seeing Dao Tan coming from far away, Mr. Dam Vo Sam said:

- How good! You have been inspired to receive the Dharma precepts, that is, you have attained the precepts! Today, I will prove it to you!

Having finished speaking, in front of the Buddha statue, he explained the precepts to Dao Tan. Dao Lang, who composed the preface to the Maha Nirvana Sutra, also saw that dream clearly that night. Although he had a high level of maturity, he felt that his morality was crude, so Dao Lang vowed to become Dao Tan's junior brother. Before and after Dao Tan, more than a thousand people followed him to receive the Bodhisattva precepts.

According to the book 'Exit Tripitaka', the sutras translated by Mr. Dam Vo Sam are as follows: Mahaparinirvana Sutra (36 volumes), Paragonal Mahaparinirvana Sutra (29 volumes), Yangtzegarbha Sutra (5 volumes), Paragonal Great Cloud Sutra (4 volumes), Compassionate Flower Sutra (10 volumes), Golden Light Sutra (4 volumes), Sea Dragon King Sutra (4 volumes). (4 volumes), Bodhisattva Earthly Precepts Sutra (8 volumes), Bodhisattva Precepts (1 volume), Upasaka Precepts Sutra (7 volumes), Bodhisattva Precepts Sutra (8 volumes), Bodhisattva Precepts Upasaka Sutra (1 volume).

In the middle of the fourth century, Kumarajiva was studying in Ke Tan, and the Nirvana Sutra had not yet been transmitted there. When he returned to Quy Tu country, Kumarajiva had not yet seen the Nirvana Sutra. From 350 to 400, there were many different versions of the Nirvana Sutra. Phap Hsien once brought back a book of the Nirvana Sutra. In 417, Buddha Da Bat Da La and Master Bao Van translated six volumes of the Nirvana Sutra.

In 433, when he heard the Dharma Master Dam Vo Phat say that the Nirvana Sutra had not been fully translated, Dam Vo Sam decided to return to the Western Regions to pray for the second part of the Nirvana Sutra, but met with an accident and died.

Inheriting the wish to seek the second part of the Nirvana Sutra, there was Master Dao Pho (originally from Cao Xuong country, fluent in the languages ​​of six countries) at Dao Trang pagoda. According to Emperor Van De's decree, Master Dao Pho led a delegation of ten people along the boat to go to Tay Vuc. However, the boat encountered wind and waves midway, so the boat drifted to Quang District. Master Dao Pho injured his foot, then became ill and passed away. Before his death, Master Dao Pho said:

- The Song Dynasty has no relationship with the later part of the Nirvana Sutra.

During the reign of Duong Lan Duc (664-665), lawyer Hoi Ninh in Thanh Do, in Ich Chau, followed a boat to seek the Dharma, that is, from Nam Hai to Ha Lang Chau (Java), and stayed there for three years, then together with the monk Nha Na Bat Da La (Tri Hien) translated the latter part of the Nirvana Sutra. The disciple of monk Nha Na Bat Da La, Van Ky, brought this part of the Nirvana Sutra to Truong An. The last part of the Nirvana Sutra includes: Kieu Tran Nhu Pham Residual Product, Di Giao Pham, Responding Completely Complete Product, Co Feel Tea Spleen Product, Saint Khufu Diffuser Product.

After the Nirvana Sutra was translated, the idea that 'all sentient beings have Buddhas' developed strongly, causing Dao Sanh to develop the policy of 'sudden enlightenment to become a Buddha', and the gradual practice theory of Hue Quan was born.

Mong Ton not only invited Venerable Dam Vo Sam to translate the Nirvana Sutra and other sutras, but he also invited the Buddhist monk Buddhavarman from Thien Truc to translate the Maha Bhikkhu Sutra. Monk Phu Da Bat Ma; The Chinese translation is Dao Thai, outstanding talent, temperament, calm, outstanding intelligence than others, often learning many languages. Seeing that the Prajnaparamita Sutra had been translated and disseminated in Central Earth, but the three and nine Abhidharma collections of the Hinayana had not yet been fully translated, the monk Phu Da Bat Ma, not afraid of the dangerous and remote road, crossed Thong Linh mountain, passed through Ke Tan country, requested more than a hundred thousand verses of the Sanskrit sutra, and then went to Luong Chau. Mong Ton heard the sound and invited monk Phu Da Bat Ma to translate the sutras. Because the defenses around Luong Chau citadel were not solid, Mong Ton invited the monk Phu Da Bat Ma to enter Nhan Du Cung pagoda (where Dam Vo Sam once translated the Maha Nirvana Sutra and other scriptures). From the middle of April 425 to the beginning of July 427, the Mahabhāsa Sutra was translated into one hundred volumes. At that time, there were more than three hundred people such as monks Dao Lang, Tri Sung, etc. who took on the responsibility of examining the scriptures.

Mong Ton often invited monks from Thien Truc, Tay Vuc, etc. to come to Luong Chau to translate the scriptures. He often discussed mystical meaning with monks and monks. Regarding religion, one side he took advantage of, and the other side supported.

Mong Ton has a younger brother, named An Duong Hau. He recited many sutras, and often kept the five precepts carefully. Because he had the will to seek the Dharma, he went to Vu Dien country, went to Cu Ma De Dai Tu pagoda, and studied with the monk Buddha Tu Na (Buddhasena) from Thien Truc. Later, he went to Cao Xuong country, requested the Avalokiteshvara and Avalokiteshvara sutras, and translated these two sutras. He returned to Luong Chau again. In 439, when Northern Wei attacked Liangzhou, he took refuge in Jiangnan region, and did not communicate with anyone, only often visiting temples and pagodas. At the request of nun Hue Tuan at Truc Vien Pagoda, he translated the Essential Meditation Sutra on Secrets of Healing in the year 455. Because he was fluent in Sanskrit and Chinese, he translated many sutras such as: Buddha's Theory of the Eight Trai Precepts, Buddha's Theory of Maitreya Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva Tu Suitatā, Buddha's Theory of Pure Sanskrit Prajnaparamita King, Buddha's Theory of Matara Vuong, Buddha's Theory of the Vietnamese Kingdom of Chien Dau, Buddha's Theory King Ma Dat Quoc, Buddha's Teaching of the Great Sangha Sutra of Buddha, Buddha's Teaching of Da Ky, Buddha's Teaching of the Five Non-Returns, Buddha's Teaching of Enlightenment, Resurrection of the Dead Disciple, Buddha's Teaching of the Forbidden Precepts of Kasyapa, Buddha's Teaching of the Five Worlds of Terror, Essential Meditation on the Secret of Curing Sickness.

tom_tat: He is from Ke Tan country (where the theory of Sarvastivada is very practiced). He often sought out a famous teacher and was extremely knowledgeable...
noi_dung: 25. Sanghabhata (Sanghabhata, translated as All Appearances)He is from Ke Tan country (where the theory of Sarvastivada is very practiced). He often sought out famous teachers and learned all the scriptures. He clearly understood the essential teachings of the Abhidharma and Vaibhava collections. In 381, he went to Chang'an. Arriving there, Sangha Bat Trang along with monks such as Dam Ma Nan De, Sangha Deva, Buddha Do La Sat translated the treatise Abhidharma Piba Sa (or Abhidhamma Abhidharma).

tom_tat: Mr. Dam Ma Da Xa, translated as Phap Minh, was originally from Ke Tan country and was studious since childhood. At the age of fourteen, he studied with Venerable Phat Nha Da La....
noi_dung:
26. Dharmayasas (Dharmayasas)Mr. Dam Ma Da Xa, translated as Phap Minh, was originally from Ke Tan country and was studious since childhood. At the age of fourteen, he studied with Venerable Phat Nha Da La. When he grows up, his spirit is high, his wisdom is clear; When you read the scriptures, you will understand them more deeply than others; Cultivate your thoughts, enter the door of meditation, and place your mind in the seven parts of enlightenment. People often called him Phu Dau Ba Da. He often went to ravines and wild forests, without fear of tigers and wolves, to contemplate alone his delusional thoughts. At that time, every time he sat under the tree, he always blamed himself that he was thirty years old and had not yet attained fruition, so why did he indulge! Therefore, do not eat or sleep, day and night diligently repent of your karma. One night, he dreamed of Uncle Xoa Thien Vuong saying:

- Monks must often have the will to propagate Buddhism and help people. Why do you care so much about details, just cultivating yourself alone? If the conditions are complete, they will mature. You should not force your mind to seek, making it impossible to attain results.

When he woke up, he set out to travel throughout neighboring countries to spread the word. In the early years of Tan Long An's life (397-401), he came to Guangzhou and stayed at Bach Sa Pagoda. He often recited the Vinaya Vinaya code, making people so impressed that they called him Maha Vaibhava. At that time, He was eighty-five years old, and had about eighty-five followers. At the request of good believers such as the young lady Truong Pho Minh, he preached about the dharma of dependent origination. At that time, he also translated a sutra.

During the reign of Nghia Hi (405-418), he went to Truong An, and met the Thien Truc monk Dam Ma Quat Da who also went there. At that time, King Dao Hung respected Buddhism very much, so when he saw him coming, he warmly welcomed him and made offerings. He, together with Dam Ma Quat Da, translated the Sariputta Abhidharma set, from 407 to 414, it was completed, with twenty-two volumes. Crown Prince Dao Hoang personally reviewed it. Master Dao Tieu wrote the foreword.

Later, he moved to the south, to Giang Lang, stayed at Tan Tu Pagoda, and strongly propagated Zen. At that time, three hundred monks came to listen to him preach the Dharma. At first they did not believe, but as soon as they met Him, they were all joyful and grateful. He often said that one teacher and one disciple, cultivating the path, would attain Arhatship. One time, while he was closing the temple door to meditate, he suddenly saw five or six monks coming in from outside, then flying back and forth, coming under a tree to meditate. He often communicated with gods. Although he had footprints but no image, people said that he had attained sainthood.

During the reign of Song Nguyen Gia (424-453), he said goodbye and returned to the Western Regions, and then no one knew what the end would be.

Dam Ma Da Xa has a disciple named Phap Do. Phap Do was originally the son of Truc Ba Lac. Truc Ba Lac often goes to Guangzhou to do business. On the way to Nam Khang, she gave birth to a son, so Truc Ba Lac named him Nam Khang. When he grew up, he changed his name to Kim Gia. After becoming a monk, his dharma name was Phap Do. Phap Do is fluent in Sanskrit and Chinese, so he often helps Venerable Dam Ma Da Xa translate the sutras. Phap Do was the first disciple to receive dharma initiation from Dam Ma Da Xa. When Dam Ma Da Xa returned to the Western Regions, Phap Do took the initiative to specialize in studying the Hinayana teachings, without reading and reciting the Sutras of the Equal Way; only bow to Shakyamuni Buddha, not to the Buddhas of the ten directions; They often bring copper bowls to eat and not use anything else, and then force the nuns to regularly repent of their karma. At that time, nuns in Dong Do and Giao Chau such as Phap Hoang (daughter of mandarin Y Nhan Thuan in Don Duong) and Pho Minh (daughter of governor Truong Muc in Giao Chau), etc. often came to receive dharma at Phap Do.

tom_tat: Cau Na Bat Ma, translated as Cong Duc Khai, was from the Sat Loi lineage and was the king of Ke Tan country. Grandfather's name is Ha Le Bat Da, (translated as Lion...
noi_dung:
27. Gunavarman (Gunavarman)Cau Na Bat Ma, translated as Cong Duc Khai, was from the Sat Loi lineage and was the king of Ke Tan country. Grandfather's name is Ha Le Bat Da, (translated as Gentle Lion), with a straightforward personality. Father is Sangha Ananda, (translated as All Good). Thanks to often secluding himself in forests, mountains and streams, at the age of fourteen, Cau Na Bat Ma's knowledge base was exceptionally deep and profound. His personality is kind, devoted to morality, and often performs good deeds. The mother often slaughtered wild animals and then told Him to eat them. He said:

- Any animal that has a life should not be eaten.

The angry mother said:

- Just eat. Mom will take the blame for it.

One day, while frying boiling oil, he suddenly spilled it and burned his finger, so he said to his mother:

- Mom, please bear the pain for me.

The mother said:

- My body hurts, how can I replace it?

- The suffering in front of you cannot replace you, let alone the suffering in the three evil paths!

Hearing this, the mother came to her senses, repented, and no longer killed anyone in her life.

At the age of eighteen, he met a fortune teller who said:

- At the age of thirty, he will go to a great country in the south, and be proclaimed a master. If you do not enjoy the glory and wealth of this world, you will attain sainthood.

At the age of twenty, he became a monk, received full ordination, mastered nine sets of sutras, thoroughly understood the four sets of A Ham sutras, often recited more than a million words of sutras, mastered the rules of the law, and wonderfully entered the essential teachings of meditation, causing people to call him Tripitaka Dharma Master.

When he was thirty years old. The king of Ke Tan country died without any descendants. The meeting of ministers said to each other:

- Mr. Cau Na Bat Ma was originally from a royal lineage, had profound intelligence, and high virtue. We should invite Him to come back to earth and ascend to the throne.

After the discussion, more than a hundred officials came to appeal three times, but he did not accept. After that, he left the capital, stayed away from the world, lived in the wild mountains and forests, and practiced alone. Next, he went to the Lion Kingdom to propagate Buddhism, causing the true teaching to flourish. People with knowledge often say that he has attained sainthood. His dignified dignity makes animals also develop the mind to practice the Way.

Later, he came to Xa Ba country. One day before, the queen mother dreamed of a Taoist monk flying into the kingdom by boat. The next day, she sure enough saw Him coming. The Queen Mother respected the holy body, then asked for refuge and received the five precepts. The Queen Mother advised the king:

- Because of predestined relationships in previous lives, I became a mother and child. I have received the precepts but you still do not believe in Buddhism. I'm afraid that from now on, because of this life, motherhood and love will be destroyed in the next life.

Because the queen mother forced him to, the king had to listen to his mother's words and take the precepts, then gradually believed in Buddhism and practiced diligently. One time, a neighboring country sent troops to invade the border. The King then asked Him:

- Outside enemies depend on their power to invade the land. If we fight with them, it will definitely hurt our lives a lot. If we do not resist, the disaster of losing our country will come. Now I only rely on the Master. I wonder if He has any plans.

- A tyrant starts an army to take over land, which means he has an aggressive personality. However, please, Great King, please develop a compassionate mind and do not create thoughts of wanting to kill.

The king then led the soldiers, arranged the battlefield, raised drums and flags to engage the enemy, causing them to all lose and flee. However, the king was stabbed in the thigh with a spear. He then blessed the water with a mantra, then gave it to the king to drink. The next day, the king completely recovered, so he became even more trusting and grateful. The king wanted to become a monk and practice Buddhism, so he told his officials:

- I want to become a monk. You guys, please find another wise lord.

Because the officials begged and begged three times, the king could not bear to leave, but told them:

- I have three prayers. If you can manage, I will stay and rule the country. The first vow is that in the kingdom, everyone must believe in worshiping the monks. Second, everyone in the country must eliminate all killing. Third, all assets in the country will be provided for the poor and sick.

When the courtiers heard these words, they were all delighted and believed in him. Therefore, the whole country took refuge. To show respect, the king personally built a monastery for him to reside in. While building the monastery, the king suddenly injured his arm, so he had to recite the blessing mantra, causing him to recover the next day.

His reputation for transforming Buddhism spread far and wide, causing neighboring kings to send messengers to request him to go to those places to propagate Buddhism.

At that time, in Nanjing, Hue Quan, Hue Thong, etc., hearing the reputation and virtue of Cau Na Bat Ma, they wrote a note to present to the court. In the ninth month of the Nguyen Gia year (424), they presented a petition to Song Emperor Van De, requesting the court to invite Cau Na Bat Ma to Trung Tho to propagate the Dharma. Song Emperor Van De approved, then ordered the governor in Giao Chau to prepare ships, along with monks Phap Truong, Dao Sung, etc., to bring the king's poems to Xa Ba country, requesting Venerable Cau Na Bat Ma to come to Song country to promote the true teachings. Because he wanted to promote the holy teaching, Cau Na Bat Ma accepted this request and, regardless of the distance, came to Song land.
