Therefore, he followed the boat of merchant Truc Nan De, headed to a small country, then followed the wind to Guangzhou. Upon arriving, he wrote a letter to Emperor Wen:

- The wind of karma blows to the Song land. Now please let me know.

Emperor Wen received that letter and knew that he had arrived in the South Sea, so he ordered the governor of Chau District to escort him back to the capital. On the way, he stopped temporarily at Thuy Hung. The Thuy Hung mountain area is full of tigers and wolves. The shape of that mountain range is towering. Therefore, He changed the name of the mountain to Linh Thuu. A few miles away from the temple on the mountain, he built a meditation room for himself, but the sound from the temple could not reach there. However, every time there was a sound of bells beating, he heard it and returned to the temple. Both monks and laity are respectful. Inside the pagoda there is Bao Nguyet Palace. On the west side of that palace, he personally painted the image of Venerable Rahula and the statue of Buddha Dinh Quang. After painting, every evening, the statue emitted light endlessly, making the Thai Mau governor in Thuy Hung respect and admire him even more. Later, Thai Mau died. He himself went to the palace to comfort him. A few days later, the servants dreamed that Thai Mau and the monks were preaching in the temple. However, everything is blessed by His divine power.

People in the Thuy Hung mountain area often suffer from tiger and wolf disasters. Since residing there, walking day and night, many times he encountered tigers and wolves. He used his staff to pat them on the head, making them all go away. From then on, visitors are no longer hindered. Thanks to his dignity, out of every ten people, seven or eight people were inspired to believe in Buddhism.

One time, he had been meditating for many days without letting go, so the monks in the temple sent a novice monk there to serve him. As soon as the novice arrived, he saw a white lion standing on the roof of the hermitage, and blue lotus flowers flying everywhere in the sky. The little monk screamed in horror, then all the apparitions disappeared. The strange omens are truly incalculable, but most of them are like that. Later, Emperor Van De again issued a decree, urging him to return to the capital. He followed the boat to the capital Kien Nghiep in January 441. Emperor Wen himself personally welcomed and greeted him. At that time, Emperor Wen asked:

- Disciples often maintain the precepts of not killing. The Dharma Master came from far away to teach and transform this world, so what method did he use to instruct?

- The Way lies in the mind, not in things. The Dharma depends on you, not on others. The Emperor's religious practice is different from that of ordinary people. Their relatives are not famous, their commanding language is not authoritative. If they do not practice self-discipline and practice, how can they become virtuous people? For His Majesty, the four seas are his home, and all people are his children. A gentle word from Him immediately made the people happy. If He often promulgates good and righteous teachings, it will make all the gods happy. If He did not constantly strengthen the punishment of innocent people, he would cause the rain to flow smoothly, the cold and hot air to follow the weather, and hundreds of kinds of rice, grain, and grass to flourish. Observing the precepts like that is generous, and the virtue of observing the precepts of not killing also covers everywhere. Why do you think that if you don't kill any animal for half a day, you call it filial piety!

- The minds of secular people are confused and far away from the infinite principles, so they often say that the teachings of Buddhism are false words. On the contrary, monks often cling to chapters, sentences and verses. The words of the Dharma Master truly enlighten the mind, and are in accordance with the words of gods and humans!

Emperor Van De took him back to stay at Ky Hoan pagoda and made generous offerings. Famous kings and scholars are all revered. There, he opened the Lotus Sutra and the Ten Grounds. Many people came to listen to the Dharma.

At the request of Master Hue Nghia in the temple, he translated the book Bodhisattva Precepts, which has twenty-eight chapters. Later, the disciple translated two more chapters. There are thirty chapters in total, called the Bodhisattva Precepts.

The deputy historian Vuong Trung Duc in Banh Thanh invited a foreign monk, Y Diep Ba La, to translate the Ca Tam Sutra. Because of obstacles, Y Diep Ba La translated it to Trach Pham and then stopped. Therefore, Vuong Trung Duc invited him to translate Hau Pham, causing the Ca Tam Sutra to be translated into thirteen volumes. He again translated the Four Parts of the Law of Yet-Ma, Uu Ba Tac Five Precepts, and Compendium of Uu Ba Tac twenty-four precepts. A total of twenty-six volumes. The writing is clear, and the Sanskrit-Chinese are error-free.

Nuns such as Hue Qua, Tinh Am, etc. from Anh Phuoc pagoda came to tell him:

- Six years ago, eight nuns from the Lion country came to the capital and said that in the Song country, there were no nuns yet. Therefore, when the nuns take the vows on the altar, I am afraid that the precepts will not be fully attained.

He said:

- The precepts come from the great monks (nuns must only follow the great monks to receive the precepts). If you do not practice the Dharma to overcome demons according to your duty, you will not be able to attain the precepts. Let's review the fate of Ms. Dai Ai Dao to become a monk and we will understand clearly.

The nuns were afraid that their precepts were not yet perfect, so they kindly asked him to give them the dharma precepts. He then happily accepted. However, because the nuns in the Song Dynasty did not have enough years, they had to invite more foreign nuns to follow the monks and ordain the ordination.

In the summer of that year, he spent the summer in retreat at Bon Lam Ha Tu pagoda. At that time, there was a Vietnamese group offering flowers. The flower petals next to His throne, after many days, were still fresh, causing everyone to worship the holy body.

After summer, he returned to Ky Hoan Pagoda. On the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month of that year, before he had finished eating, he returned to the palace. Later, a disciple came and saw him peacefully pass away. He lived to be sixty-five years old. Before becoming naturalized citizen, he wrote thirty-six verses, and told himself that he had attained the second state of Arhatship (Stu Da Ham), then gave the poem to his disciple Asa La, saying:

- After I pass away, you can give this letter to the Thien Truc monks and the monks here to read.

At the time of naturalization, he sat cross-legged on the meditation mat, his face still rosy as if he had entered meditation. Thousands of monks and lay people attended the funeral ceremony. They smelled a strange scent again, and saw a forty-meter-long dragon rising from His body into thin air. At that time, four unicorns, phoenix, dragon, and turtle appeared. In front of the Nam Lam Gioi Dan, according to Thien Truc's custom, a tea ceremony was held to honor his body. At that time, five-colored clouds suddenly appeared in the clear blue sky, causing everyone to praise the strange sign. There, the monks built a tower to worship the relics of Cau Na Bat Ma.

When he arrived at the Buddhist monk, Emperor Wen wanted to follow him and receive the Bodhisattva precepts. Because he had to worry about fighting foreign invaders, before Tong Van De had time to pray, Mr. Cau Na Bat Ma became a naturalized citizen, making him heartbroken and regretful. Emperor Wen then ordered the monks to read the verse of the will left by Cau Na Bat Ma. The verse reads: "First, I pay homage to the Three Jewels and the pure precepts, all the monks. The impure world has many defilements, the false ones are not faithful, the delusional ones do not understand the truth, and they despise virtuous people. Therefore, you sages and saints, appearing in the body, are hidden. I pray to Na Bat Ma, my fate has come, I have reaped good merits, now I speak the truth, without using a twisted mind, hoping for those who seek fame, and advising people to entertain and increase the Buddha Dharma; great Dharma. If you have such power, you should listen. Once you lived in the wilderness, you saw the corpses, the intestines and liver were rotting, the blood was flowing foully there. You know that the body is inherently like that, you are deeply greedy and not afraid of fire, there are countless kinds of things like that. Practice contemplation of corpses, let go of what you hear and know, stay diligently in the forest, practice mindfulness and never forget, the realm is like looking at the face of a mirror, so you and I are the same The mind is quiet, the body is light and clear, the mind is peaceful, the joy is growing, the bones disappear, the white bones appear before the eyes, the white bones and limbs are destroyed, the mind is clear, the mind is tamed like that, the body is very pliable, the method of cultivating like this, leads to the destruction of dust and mindfulness, that is the salvation of the body, the cause of greed arises Knowing the cause of life, like a fish greedy for bait, it experiences immeasurable suffering; knowing clearly the place of refuge, karma and karma arise, according to the conditions of mindfulness, there are many different types of thoughts, that is, practicing mindfulness step by step, this mind transforms clearly; from there, the law of mindfulness arises, and the cause of suffering is like a hot sword. Because of craving, reaching nirvana, seeing clearly throughout the three realms, the body is so small, resting happily in the means, the body gradually becomes full, and patience is the same, because of the right means, gradually reducing the realm, attaining the ultimate dharma, one step at a time, the dharma of suffering, is called the path of delusion and the world leaving; the realm of ultimate meaning, clear of the brain, achieving pure samadhi, leaving behind pure conditions, not slipping away or losing, wisdom as pure as the bright moon, calm and peaceful, pure form of cessation, not a place to preach, only the Buddha's ability to realize, the theory of the five causes and conditions, the true meaning of practice, clinging to names cannot be seen, the practice of all kinds is not two, the sky has good and bad, people can achieve it tranh; tu hành các diệu tướng, nay Ta không tuyên thuyết, sợ người khởi vọng tưởng, cuồng hoặc mê thế gian; nơi kia tu lợi tướng, Ta đã thuyết ít phần; nếu người có trí sáng, biết rằng do duyên khởi; nơi nước Ma La Bà, đắc được sơ quả thánh; A Lan Nhã sơn tự, đạo tích tu viễn ly; sau nơi nước Sư Tử, thôn tên Kiếp Ba Lợi, tấn tu đắc nhị quả, gọi là Tư Ðà Hàm; đó là danh rời nạn, chướng tu đạo ly dục; thấy Ta tu Separation, knowing that there is no leisure, all give birth to a rare mind; I see that it is like poisonous fire, the mind that arises is boring; avoid the chaos of the fleeting sea, Snakes and Lam Ap, the karma of the wind, depending on the conditions of the Song Dynasty; therefore, in all countries, depending on the force of the Buddha's teachings, you should honestly contemplate, now this body is extinguished, like the extinguished fire!

tom_tat: Cau Na Bat Da La is translated as Cong Duc Hien, Thien Truc middle person. When he was old, because he practiced Mahayana, he became famous, making everyone...
noi_dung:
28. GunabhadraCau Na Bat Da La is translated as Cong Duc Hien, Thien Truc middle person. When he was old, because he studied Mahayana, he became famous, causing everyone to call him Maha Dien. He originally belonged to the Brahmin lineage. Regarding astronomy, languages, mathematics, medicine, magic, etc., all types of learning are profound and profound. One time, after thoroughly reviewing the book 'Ati-Damāstra of the Mind', he admired the essential teachings of the great path, so he began to study Buddhism. However, because the family was originally a pagan, it was forbidden to study Buddhism. Because he couldn't argue with his family, he had to leave home and travel everywhere to study Buddhism. Later, he became a monk and concentrated on studying and practicing Buddhism. When he received full ordination at the age of twenty, he had mastered the three canons of sutras, rules, and treatises. When dealing with people, he always has a compassionate, gentle and respectful mind. Towards his original teacher, he often had a sincere heart of service. Not long after, he said goodbye to his original Hinayana teacher, and continued to study Mahayana.

One time, his master told him to go into the chest containing the sutras to bring out the sutras. He then came and took out the 'Great Avatamsaka Sutra' and brought it to the teacher. The original teacher said:

- You and the Mahayana dharma truly have a profound relationship!

Having finished speaking, he encouraged him to review the sutra. After reciting, he then proclaimed this sutra, which no one could question.

After receiving the Bodhisattva precepts, he returned home and advised his parents to take refuge in Buddhism:

- If your parents persist in following a pagan religion, you will not return, because there will be no benefit. On the contrary, if parents take refuge in the Three Jewels, the Teacher will often return home.

Hearing these words, his parents were moved and agreed to abandon pagan beliefs and take refuge in the Three Jewels.

He often passed through countries like Lion, etc., but later felt that he had an affinity with the East, so he followed a merchant ship to the east. One day, the wind suddenly stopped blowing, causing the boat to stop running. The people on the boat were sad and worried because the water reserve had run out. He said:

- Let us join forces and sincerely recite the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions, then we will surely be inspired.

Having finished speaking, he and the people on the boat recited the sutra continuously. Not long after, the wind suddenly blew, dark clouds covered the sky, then rain poured down, giving everyone water to drink. Thanks to His sincere heart, such inspiration is possible.

In 435, he arrived in Guangzhou. Receiving the statement presented by the historian Xa Lang, Emperor Wen of Song sent messengers to welcome him to Kien Khang (ie Nanjing). As soon as he arrived at the capital, Emperor Wen immediately asked famous monks of the time such as Hue Quan, Hue Nghiem, etc. to come back and forth to ask questions and convey his greetings. Seeing his peaceful spirit, Hue Quan and Hue Nghiem both sincerely admired him and communicated and learned. Arriving at the Buddhist monks, he stayed at De Hoan Pagoda, then immediately began to propagate Buddhism, making Emperor Van De even more impressed. At that time, the literary leader Nhan Duyen Chi, a talented scholar, also personally came to worship him. As soon as this news spread, famous scholars from the capital came to worship Him in droves. The general in Pengcheng was Wang Liuyikang, and the prime minister of Namxiao Wang Liuyixuan both honored him as a teacher. Soon, the monks requested him to translate the sutras. Therefore, he gathered famous monks to learn and translate the Tap A Ham Sutra at De Hoan Pagoda, and the Ancient Dharma Sutra at Dong An Pagoda, and the Thang Man Lang Gia Sutra in Dan Duong District. He recruited more than seven hundred people to assist in the translation work. Bao Van specializes in translation; Hue Quan wrote the pen. The meaning of the I Ching is profound but very fluent, clearly showing the tone.

When Nam Tieu Vuong Luu Nghia Tuyen moved to assume command at Kinh Chau, he invited him to follow. Upon arriving, he assisted him in building a monk's room, painting Buddha statues, etc. at Tan Tu. There, he translated the Anathapindika Sutra, the Past Present Cause and Effect Sutra, the Infinite Life Sutra, the Ne Huan Sutra, the Evil Demon Sutra, the Analogical Liberation Sutra, the Paramitas of the Meanings, the Present Name of the Buddha, the First Meaning of the Five Characteristics, the Eight Good Ideas, etc. In total, he translated more than a hundred volumes of sutras.

When he saved people, he often asked his disciple Phap Dung to translate. King Nam Tieu wanted to invite him to preach the Lotus Sutra. However, he thought that his Chinese language was not yet proficient, which made him extremely ashamed, so he worshiped and repented day and night, praying to Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara for protection. One night, he dreamed of a man wearing white clothes, a sword on his back, and a human head in his hand. That person came before Him and asked:

- Why are you so sad?

In the dream, he recounted how he was invited to lecture on the sutras without being fluent in Chinese. That person said:

- There's nothing to worry about!

Having finished speaking, that person pulled out his sword, cut off His head, and then replaced the head he was holding in his hand on his neck. The new head then naturally moved as usual, then asked:

- Does it hurt?

He replied:

- No pain!

Moments later, he suddenly woke up, his heart filled with joy. On the second day, he was fluent in Chinese, so according to Mr. Nam Tieu Vuong Luu's previous request, he took the stage to preach the Lotus Sutra.

At the end of Nguyen Gia's reign, Nam Tieu Vuong Luu often saw strange dreams, so he came to ask. He said:

- Master Sutra, there will surely be chaos and chaos.

Less than a year later, crown prince Liu Shao rebelled and killed Emperor Wen. Song Xiaodi (457-464) ascended the throne. At that time, knowing that Nam Tieu Vuong Luu had a plot to rebel, his appearance was very worried and sad. However, He could not find an opportunity to hinder him. Seeing that His sad face was unusual, he came to ask the reason. He solemnly and thoughtfully advised, but Nam Tieu Vuong Luu still did not give up his plot to rebel. Finally, knowing there was no way to stop Nam Tieu Vuong Luu, he shed tears and said:

- If you don't change your mind, I won't stay here anymore.

Having finished speaking, He intended to leave that place. However, seeing the presence of Mr. Cau Na Bat Da La, the dispatch of troops became righteous, so Nam Tieu Vuong Luu forced him to follow the army and rebel. Later, at Luong Son Mountain, Nam Tieu Vuong Luu's army was defeated, and his boat was also burned down. At that time, the boat was in the middle of the river, very far from the shore, so he thought it would be difficult to escape the great tribulation. He single-mindedly recited the name Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, held a bamboo stick, jumped into the river, and then floated down the stream. At that time, he suddenly turned around and saw a child pulling him to shore. He said:

- You are just a child, how can you help me cross the river!

As soon as he finished speaking, he saw that he had reached the riverbank. He took off his cloak and gave it to the child to repay the favor of saving his life. However, turning around, he saw no one, so he knew that he was saved by the gods.

After the battle at Luong Son Mountain, Song Hieu De ordered Vuong Huyen Mo (the general who killed Nam Tieu Vuong Luu at Luong Son Mountain) that if he captured Ma Ha Dien, he must submit a decree to report the news, and then take him back to the capital immediately. Finding and arresting him, Vuong Huyen Mo followed orders and took him to the capital. As soon as he entered court, Song Hieu De immediately came to greet him, kindly asked questions, expressed his admiration, and said:

- I have admired you for a long time, but now I have met you.

He said:

- My body was injured by soldiers and swords. He should have been torn to pieces, but His Highness was not suspicious and still warmly welcomed him. What a regenerating grace.

- Then who is the rebel plotter?

- Monastics cannot participate in mutinies, so I don't know the people who conspired to rebel. However, I and Truong Suong, Tong Linh Tu, etc. were all forced to join the rebellion. Unexpectedly, because of predestined fate, we encountered this accident.

- Don't be afraid. I do not blame you.

That day, Emperor Song Hieu ordered someone to take him to stay in the back hall, then provide clothes, food, and people and horses to serve him.

After Nam Tieu Vuong Luu's army was defeated, Song Hieu De's army found a letter from Him sent to Nam Tieu Vuong Luu before. When he opened it, De Song Hieu did not see any words related to military matters, so he trusted him even more. Later, during the discussion, Song Hieu De jokingly asked:

- Do you remember Nam Tieu Vuong Luu?

He replied:

- I received his offerings for ten years, how could I forget that kindness? Please, Your Highness, allow me to offer incense to pray for his salvation for three years.

Hearing this, Emperor Song Hieu agreed.

Trung Hung Pagoda had just been completed. Emperor Song Hieu invited him to reside there.

One time, Emperor Hieu of Song held a banquet and invited him to come. At that time, at the party, the princes and ministers were all gathered. At that time, He had not yet had time to shave his hair, so he still had white hair. Emperor Song Hieu looked up into the distance, then turned around and told his superior, Ta Trang:

- This Ma Ha Dien is truly intelligent and talented. However, His old age and death are not far away. I will challenge you. He will definitely know what I mean.

As soon as he climbed the steps of the palace, Emperor Tong Hieu came out to greet him and said:

- Mr. Ma Ha Dien did not waste his time coming from far away, but there was still one thing left unfinished.

He said:

- I have been coming to the capital of China for nearly thirty years. Thien Tu treated me with great kindness and compassion. I'm so ashamed that I don't deserve to be honored. Now I am seventy years old and sick. Now there is only death, which is unfinished business!

Seeing His excellent eloquence, Emperor Song Hieu admired him even more, and ordered Him to sit next to him. The courtiers in the palace all turned to look.

Tay Khoi Pagoda is located on the Phung Hoang Building in Mat Lang. Every night in the middle of the night, the pagoda door often makes a sound, but no one is seen. Some monks often woke up startled, making their minds uneasy, so they came to pray to him. He then offered incense and prayed:

- Your fate is inherently here. Today we build a pagoda at this place, and often worship on your behalf. If you want to stay here, you must become a good deity protecting the dharma. If you can't stay here, please go somewhere else quickly.

That night, more than ten people in the same dream saw ghosts and gods all flying away into the sky. From then on, the monks were no longer disturbed by ghosts and spirits.

In the sixth Dai Minh era (462), everywhere suffered from drought. Even though it's been several months, I haven't received a single drop of rain. Emperor Song Hieu then asked him to pray for rain, and ordered that if he couldn't pray for rain, he should not meet him. He said:

- Relying on Buddha's teachings and relying on the power of His Highness, the heavens will definitely pour out nectar. If I don't succeed, I won't have the face to meet Your Highness!

He then went to Dia Dai in Bac Ho, not bothering to eat or drink, offered incense to pray for rain, silently chanted sutras, and recited mantras continuously. On the morning of the second day, at the hour of death, from the northwest, clouds indeed gathered, then in an instant the wind blew, causing heavy rain. The next day, all the officials and officials came to congratulate him. Emperor Song Hieu also summoned him to the palace to reward him continuously.

From childhood until the end of his life, he was a vegetarian. Hands often carry incense burners. Every time he finished using the mussels, he took the leftover food and distributed it to the birds. Birds often perch on His hands, without any fear.

In January of 468, feeling physically uneasy, he took leave of Emperor Minh De and his officials. On the day of his death, he stood and looked at the sacred statue of the heavenly flower. Near noon, he passed away at the age of seventy-five. Emperor Minh De was deeply saddened, so he offered a profound condolence. The great mandarins also sadly passed away.

tom_tat: Sangha Bat Ma, translated as Public Revelation. He was originally from Thien Truc country, became a monk at a young age, was handsome and virtuous, and understood the three scriptures...
noi_dung:
29. Sanghavarman (Sanghavarman)Sangha Bat Ma, translated as Public Revelation. He was originally from Thien Truc country, became a monk at a young age, was handsome and virtuous, clearly understood the three canonical teachings, and was proficient in the theory of Samsara.

During the Song Dynasty, the twentieth year of Yuanjia (443), he crossed the deserts and came to Kien Nghiep. His serious temperament and speech were in accordance with the precepts, making him respected by the layman and called him 'Tripitaka Dharma Master'. At first, he stayed at Binh Lang pagoda. Hearing the reputation of his pure conduct, Hue Quan invited him to Dao Trang pagoda, and worshiped and made offerings to show his respect for the precepts.

Day and night, he practiced the Dharma, reading and reciting the scriptures tirelessly. The monks gathered under the court, and spread the correct teachings everywhere. First, he preached precepts to the nuns of Anh Phuoc Pagoda such as nun Hue Qua, etc. to learn full ordination. At that time, the two groups of monks and monks were not yet complete. Thanks to him giving the Dharma precepts, they were complete. Nuns from the Lion Kingdom came to the capital of the Song Dynasty to seek precepts from him. The masses unanimously respected him as the Tripitaka master. Hue Nghia from Ky Hoan pagoda went to Kinh Ap and argued with him. He used religion to demonstrate and prove the Dharma. Upon returning, Hue Nghia was impressed by his virtue, so he sent his disciple Hue Co to bring offerings to him.

Hundreds of monks and nuns followed him to practice. Tong Banh Thanh and Vuong Nghia Khang respected his virtues, so they often made offerings to monks. The four groups all flocked to Kinh Ap.

He explained the wonderful Sutra of the Tam Tam Sutra and recited it fluently. Although the three classics have been translated a lot, most of them have not been edited or revised. Therefore, in September of that year, at Truong Thien Pagoda, Hui Quan summoned scholars and invited Venerable Monk Sangha Bat Ma to translate the Samsara Sutra. Translated by Bao Van. Quan Tu took notes. Inspect, research thoroughly, then complete. Next, he translated the book Ma Dac Lac Gia Distinguishing Karma, Summary of Exhorting the Kings, Essential Verses, and Inviting the Holy Monks to Succeed, etc.

His desire to educate is not determined in one direction. After translating the sutras and transmitting the Dharma, he said goodbye and returned to his native country. The crowd all tried to beg him to stay, but they still couldn't. In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia (442), he followed a merchant ship back to the Western Regions. No one knows where he entered citizenship.

tieu_de: 30. Mr. Dam Ma Mat Da (Phap Tu)
tom_tat: Dharmamitra was originally from Ke Tan country. At the age of seven, his mind was clear and his body was dignified. Every time I see monks...
noi_dung:
30. Mr. Dam Ma Mat Da (Phap Tu)Dharmamitra was originally from Ke Tan country. At the age of seven, his mind was clear and his body was dignified. Every time I see monks practicing the Dharma, I am naturally extremely happy. Although his parents loved him very much, they felt that their child was strange, so they allowed him to become a monk. At that time, in Ke Tan country, there were many saints who attained enlightenment. Therefore, he diligently searched for a master, mastered all the scriptures, and especially penetrated the meditation method, that is, entered the door of meditation in the most wonderful and wonderful place.

His personality is pensive and profound but has profound wisdom. Doubt about decency. At birth, two pairs of eyelashes are attached to each other. Therefore, people called him Lien Mi Zen Master. He liked to travel to different places because he had the will to propagate the true teachings. He traveled around the countries and then came to Quy Tu. Before that day, the king of Quy Tu country dreamed of a god who said:

- Tomorrow there will be a person of great merit entering the country. Your Majesty should make offerings to this person.

The next day, the king ordered the border garrison that if he encountered any mutants, he must immediately report them to the court. Sure enough, that day Dam Ma Mat Da arrived, so the king went to the border to welcome him and bring him to the royal palace. Next, the king followed him and took the precepts, and devoted himself to the four offerings. Although he lives in peace, he does not care about profit. Staying there for a while, he planned to go to other countries. The man again reported a dream to the king, saying:

- The virtuous person is about to leave the Great King!

Waking up, the king was horrified and sad, then he and his officials tried to beg him to stay, but to no avail. Next, he crossed the deserts, reached Don Hoang, then established a vihara in the wilderness, planted trees, cleared hundreds of acres of gardens, and built very solemn rooms. Next, he went to Luong Chau. In the old government palace, he built a meditation hall and accepted disciples to learn meditation. Learners of meditation came in droves.

In the Yuanjia era (424), he often wanted to go to Giang Ta to spread the Dharma. From Luong Chau, he went to Thuc land, then stopped at Kinh Chau, building a meditation hall at Truong Sa pagoda. There, due to his sincere request, after a few days, the relics were received, radiating light to fill the entire hermitage, causing his disciples to develop strong minds to practice. Later, he followed the boat to the capital. At first, he stayed at Trung Hung Pagoda, then later went to Ky Hoan Pagoda. His teachings spread throughout the surrounding area, then spread to the capital, causing everyone to worship him. From the Queen Mother, to the Crown Prince, to the Princess, they all raced to request the Dharma precepts and the four offerings from Him. Due to the request, at Ky Hoan Pagoda, he translated the Zen sutras and the main meditation dharma of Samantabhadra, Samantabhadra, etc. He often used Zen to teach. Thousands of miles away from Buddhism, people flock to receive Zen teachings. Everyone called him 'Great Zen Master'.

The governor of Binh Xuong Manh Nghi in Hoi Ke, strongly believes in the Three Jewels, sees Buddhist work as his duty. Thanks to tasting the taste of meditation, the mind becomes more respectful and remembers His grace. One time, he and Mr. Mang Nghi traveled to Ngan Huyen District in Triet Giang, then built a pagoda. In that area, people have a custom of believing in mediumship spells. He went there to educate them, causing them to change their beliefs and take refuge in the Three Jewels.

From east to west, everyone respected him, and often came to his court to take refuge. Later, he returned to the capital and stayed at Dinh Lam pagoda in Chung Son mountain.

His personality is calm, quiet, and likes the scenery of mountains and water. Therefore, he chose high ground, on Chung Son mountain, to build Kien Thuong pagoda. When the monk heard that he was building a pagoda, he offered pure alms. After the meditation hall hall was completed, monks from thousands of miles away gathered to practice meditation and recite sutras, making his legacy even more resounding. His retreat disciple, Dat Zen Master, also propagated his family style, making his sound echo everywhere.

Once upon a time, on the way from Ke Tan country to Quy Tu country, he was protected by the god King Capila. When arriving at Quy Tu country, the god king appeared in his true form right in the middle of the road to say goodbye and return, saying:

- His divine power is freely available everywhere, so there is no need for children to follow him to the south.

Having finished speaking, the king disappeared. Therefore, when he finished building the temple on Chung Son mountain, he painted the statue of the god king Ca Ty La and hung it on the wall. This statue displays many strange omens. Those who sincerely pray for blessings will get their wish.

On the sixth day of the seventh month, the nineteenth year of Yuanjia (442), Mr. Dam Ma Mat Da passed away at the age of eighty-seven. Monks and laity, the four disciples all mourned. His tomb was built in front of Tong Hi Pagoda on Chung Son Mountain. He translated the Avalokiteśvara Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's Conduct Sutra (1 volume), the Void Pitaka Sutra (1 volume), the Secret Meditation Sutra (3 volumes), the Five Doors Meditation Sutra Essentials of the Use of Dharma (1 volume), the Transformation of the Female Body Sutra (1 volume), the Dhammapada Sutra of Courageous Kings (1 volume), the Void Pitaka Bodhisattva Mantra Sutra (1 volume), the Impressions of Change Sutra (1 volume).

tieu_de: 31. Buddha Da La (Buddhajiva, translated as Enlightenment)
tom_tat: He is from Ke Tan country. When he was young, he received his karma from the teachings of the Amitabha Sangha, specialized in the dharma teachings, and mastered the essentials of meditation. Year...
noi_dung: 31. Buddha Da La (Buddhajiva, translated as Enlightenment)He is from Ke Tan country. When he was young, he received his karma from the teachings of the Amitabha Sangha, specialized in the dharma teachings, and mastered the essentials of meditation. In 423, he arrived at Yangzhou. In the past, Phap Hsien requested the Amitabha code in Sanskrit from the Lion Kingdom. Before the translation was finished, Phap Hien passed away. At Kinh Ap, the monks heard that he specialized in this code of law so they requested a translation. In November of that year at Long Quang Pagoda, he translated it into thirty-four volumes, called the Five Parts of Law, and completed it in April of the following year.

noi_dung: 32. Buddhavarman (Buddhavarman, translated as Giac Khai)He was from the Western Regions, well-versed in the Tripitaka, diligent and often recited the Abhidharma commentary, taking it as his heart's essence. In 437, he arrived in Western Liang. In the past, Dao Thai went through Tay Vuc and received the book Ty Sa. He heard that he was proficient in this treatise, so he offered to translate it. In one year, he translated this treatise into one hundred volumes. Currently only eighty volumes exist.

tom_tat: Cuong Luong Da Xa, translated as Thoi Xuong. He was originally from the Western Region. Strong and straightforward personality. He often recited the Abhidhamma, the essence...
noi_dung:
33. Kalayasas (Kalayasas)Cuong Luong Da Xa, translated as Thoi Xuong. He was originally from the Western Region. Strong and straightforward personality. He often read and recited the Abhidharma, was well versed in the Vinaya, and thoroughly understood the scriptures. Although he thoroughly understood the three scriptures, he often specialized in meditation. Every time he entered meditation, he sat for a whole week without getting up. He often used his true samadhi to educate people in neighboring countries.

At the beginning of the reign of Nguyen Gia (424), he crossed many deserts and mountains to Kinh Ap (Jiankang, or Nanjing). Emperor Van De heard the news and was very happy. First, he stopped at Dao Lam monastery in Chung Son mountain. The monk Bao Chi wholeheartedly worshiped and worshiped his meditation method. At the request of the monks, he translated the Medicine King Sutra, the Supreme Medicine Sutra and the Infinite Life Sutra. These two sutras extol the secret to eliminating afflictions to reach the Pure Land. At that time, as soon as it was translated, it was circulated throughout the Song country. Prime Minister Binh Xuong Manh Nghi heard his voice, so he admired him very much and often sent offerings to him. Thai Confessor Nghi Xuat at Hoi Ke requested him to go down the mountain but he did not go. Later, he went to Giang Lang. In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia (442), he went west to the land of Shu. Everywhere they propagated the dharma of meditation. Later, Mr. Cuong Luong Na Xa passed away in Giang Lang, at the age of sixty years old.

At that time, there were two monks from Thien Truc, Sangha Dat Da and Sangha Da La, who also penetrated the Zen method and went to the Song Dynasty to propagate it. One day, while meditating until noon, Sangha Dat Da stopped meditating to have lunch, suddenly a flock of birds brought fruit and placed it in front of him. Venerable Sangha Dat Da thought to himself:

- In the past, monkeys offered honey, but Buddha still accepted it and used it. Today, the birds brought fruit to offer, why didn't I accept it!

After thinking about it, he took the fruit and ate it. In the nineteenth year of Nguyen Gia (442), in response to Vuong Khang's request in Lam Tuyen, Sangha Dat Da went to Giang Lang to settle down. Finally, Sangha Dat Da passed away in Kien Nghiep.

tieu_de: 34. Venerable Sangha Da La (Aggregation of Sacrifices)
tom_tat: At the end of Song Canh Binh's reign, he went to the Buddhist monk (Jian Nghiep), often begged for alms in the human world, and went to the mountains and forests to meditate, far from the world....
noi_dung:
34. Venerable Sangha Da La (Aggregation of Sacrifices)At the end of Song Canh Binh's reign, he went to the Buddhist monk (Jian Nghiep), often begged for alms in the human world, and went to the mountains and forests to meditate, far from the world. In the 11th year of Nguyen Gia (434), the Da La Sangha came to Chung Trac to settle down, then cut thorny grass to build a monastery, that is, Tong Hi monastery.

During the Northern Wei Dynasty, the seventh year of the Taiping Chan Monarch (446), Emperor Taiwu ordered the destruction of Buddhism. In the third month of the Thua Binh era (452), Emperor Thai Vo died, Emperor Van Thanh ascended the throne, and ordered the revival of Buddhism. The second monk, Dam Duc, was responsible for reviving Buddhist teachings, so together with Thien Truc monk Thuong Na Nha Xa, etc., he translated fourteen volumes of sutras. Dam Duc also together with the Thien Truc monk Kiet Ca Da translated the Pho Phap Tang Truyen, the Pure Land Sutra, the Pure Land Samadhi Sutra, the Yang Chu Buddha Merit Sutra, and the Mahayana Bodhisattva Ten Grounds Sutra.

tieu_de: 35. Lord Mandala Tien (Mandra, translated as Hoang Nhuoc)

noi_dung: 35. Lord Mandala Tien (Mandra, translated as Hoang Nhuoc)Mandala Tien from Funan brought many scriptures in Sanskrit to Central Earth. According to the decree of the royal court, Mandala Tien together with the monk Sangha Ba La translated the Bao Van Sutra, the Dharma Realm Sutra of the Undifferentiated Nature, and the Manjushri Prajnaparamita Sutra.

tom_tat: He was originally from Funan and once translated the Mahayana Mahayana Sutra.
noi_dung: 36. Subhuti (Subhuti, translated as Thien Kiet)He was originally from Funan and once translated the Mahayana Mahayana Sutra.

tom_tat: Venerable Sangha Ba La (translated as Tang Khai) was originally from Funan, born in the year 460, intelligent and enlightened from a young age, and soon learned closely...
noi_dung:
37. SanghabhadraSangha Ba La (translated as Tang Khai) was originally from Funan, born in the year 460, intelligent and enlightened from a young age, learned Buddhism closely, became a monk at a young age, focused on the Abhidharma, and his reputation spread throughout the South China Sea. After receiving the precepts, practice fully according to the precepts. He had the will to travel everywhere to propagate the Dharma. Hearing that the Qi country worshiped Buddhism, he took a boat to the capital Kien Khang, stayed at Chanh Quan pagoda, and became a disciple of the monk Cau Na Bat Da (a Thien Truc person). Later, he followed Cau Na Bat Da to thoroughly study the Phuong Dang Sutra. I haven't finished reading it yet, but I've already mastered the basics. He is fluent in many languages. After the Qi Dynasty was destroyed, he cut off all predestined relationships and retreated in the mountains and forests to cultivate his karma.

In the fifth year of Thien Giam (506), decreed by Emperor Wu of Luong, in five places such as Chiem Van Quan, Chanh Quan pagoda, Funan temple, Hoa Lam garden, Tho Quang palace in Duong Do for seventeen long years, he specialized in translating the sutras, a total of 11 sets, and 48 volumes, such as the Maha Asoka sutra, the commentary on the Liberation Path, etc. When he first started working During the translation work at Tho Quang palace, Emperor Luong Vo personally came to the dharma seat to write down the translation, and review and draft all the translated scriptures. The king again ordered the monks Bao Xuong, Hue Sieu, Tang Tri, Phap Van, etc. to assist in the translation, such as checking the words of the sutras, making the texts fluent. The king often received him very warmly. However, He did not keep personal property. Lieutenant Lam Xuyen Vuong Hoang received him very warmly.

In the fifth Universal Era (524), Venerable Sangha Ba La entered the natural life at the main temple, at the age of sixty-five.

tom_tat: He was originally from the royal family of Uthien Ni (Vjjayani) in central Thien Truc. He went to Eastern Wei to propagate. Era name Nguyen Tuong original year...
noi_dung: 38. Udasunya (Udasunya, translated as Cao Khong)He was originally from the royal family of Uthien Ni (Vjjayani) in central Thien Truc. He went to Eastern Wei to propagate. In the reign of Yuan Xiang (538), at the palace of the monk Ton Thang, he translated the Sangha Tra Sutra, recorded by monk Tang Phuong. After the Eastern Wei Dynasty, in the Later Qi Dynasty, the fourth year of Tai Qing (550), He went to Jinling in Jiangnan and translated the Mahayana Sutra. Previously, serving Emperor Wu Di's orders, he went abroad. In 548, he met the monk Cau Na Bat Da in the country of Vu Dien, and received the Thang Vuong Prajna Sutra in Sanskrit. Unfortunately, because of the Hau Canh chaos, which made society insecure, He had no way to translate. By the Thien Gia era (565) of the Tran dynasty, at Hung Nghiep pagoda in Giang Chau, he was able to translate the book Thang Thien Vuong Prajna, and it was recorded by the monk Tri Han at A Duc Vuong pagoda (Duong Chau). In addition, he was also able to translate the Mahakasyapa sutra and the Qin Brahman King's Prayer to the Buddha Sutra. No one knows what year he passed away.

tom_tat: Dam Ma Luu Chi, (translated as Phap Hy), was originally a Tripitaka shaman in southern Thien Truc. When he arrived at Luoyang, he was invited by Emperor Xuanwu (499-515)...
noi_dung: 39. DharmaruciDam Ma Luu Chi, (translated as Phap Hy), was originally a Tripitaka shaman in southern Thien Truc. When he arrived in Luoyang, he was requested by Emperor Xuanwu (499-515) to translate the sutras. In the second Canh Minh era (501), at Bach Ma pagoda, recorded by the monk Dao Bao, Mr. Dam Ma Liu Chi translated the Tathagata Sutra Entering the All Buddha Realms and the Tathagata Adorned Light Wisdom Sutra Entering All Buddha Realms. In 504 and 507, he translated the Sutra of the Power of Faith Entering the Seal of Dharma, and the Sutra of the Golden King. In 542, at Dich Hoa Pagoda, he translated the Eight Buddha Sutras. I don't know what year he became a naturalized citizen.

tom_tat: Bodhisattva Luu Chi (translated as Dao Hy) was originally from the North of Thien Truc, well versed in the three classics, wonderfully entered into general practice, and had the will to propagate the Dharma. Enter...
noi_dung:
40. Bodhidharma (Bodhiruci)Bodhisattva Luu Chi (translated as Dao Hy) was originally from the North of Thien Truc, well versed in the three classics, wonderfully entered into general practice, and had the will to propagate the Dharma. In the Northern Wei dynasty, at the beginning of the reign of Vinh Binh (508), he crossed Thong Linh mountain and reached Dong Ha. Hearing this news, Emperor Tuyen Vo issued an order to welcome him to Vinh Ninh Dai Tu, thoughtfully making offerings. He again sent seven hundred Sanskrit monks to assist him in translating the sutras.

At first, according to the decree, he translated the Sutra of the Ten Grounds. Emperor Tuyen Vo personally recorded it. Monks like Tang Bien, etc. discussed and approved the translation. Buddhism flourished, and talented men appeared, from the time of spreading these sutras. Emperor Tuyen Vo ordered the scholar Ly Khuc to compile and write a table of contents of the sutras that had just been translated by Bodhi Liuzhi. The wise monk Ly Khuech had already learned profound meanings and thoroughly contemplated the sutras. Venerable monk Ly Khuech wrote that the Tripitaka Dharma Master Bodhi Liuzhi in Luoyang and Nghiep Do, over twenty years, translated thirty-nine sets of sutras, and one hundred and twenty-seven volumes such as the Buddha's Name Sutra, Lankavatara, Phap Tap, Tham Mat, etc. and the treatises Thang Tu Duy, Phap Hoa, Nirvana, etc. recorded by Samana Tang Lang, Dao Tram, etc.

In the book 'Inner Classics' of the Tang Dynasty, Ly Khuc wrote that in the room of the Tripitaka Master Bodhi Liuzhi there were thousands of Sanskrit sutras, and translated sutras, filling the entire room. The wisdom of the Tripitaka of Dharma Master Bodhi Liuzhi is similar to that of the monk Lac Na Ma De, and his enlightenment is lucid, and he is proficient in magic spells, which no one can compare to.

One time, he was about to take a bath but the water in the well dried up. The disciples did not have time to bring water. He then took a willow branch, blessed it a few times, and then put it in the well. Moments later, water suddenly sprayed out from the bottom of the well everywhere. The monks there, seeing His magical magic like that, were all in awe, so they proclaimed him 'Great Saint'. He immediately said:

- Don't give false praise like that. Only this method is not commonly practiced, but foreign monks always practice this method. How dare you call him a saint!

He was afraid of confusing people, so he did not teach magic spells. The sutras translated by Bodhisattva Liuzhi are as follows: Vajra Prajna Paramita Sutra (1 volume), Vajra Prajnaparamita Sutra (3 volumes), Entering the Mausoleum Sutra (10 volumes), Sutra of the Tantra of Liberation (5 volumes), Dharma Collection Sutra (8 volumes), Brahman So Inquiry Sutra (6 volumes), Mahasattva Prajnaparamita Sutra (10 volumes), Buddha Name Sutra (12 volumes), Sutta Never Increase, Never Die (2 volumes), the Sutra of the Sai Ma Three Truths of Life (10 volumes), the commentary on the Infinite Life Sutra of Upasāsā (1 volume), the commentary on the Jādaṇāṇa Sutra (2 volumes).

He passed away in 527.

tieu_de: 41. Tripitaka of Dharma Master Lac Na Ma De (Ratnamati, translated as Bao Hy)

noi_dung: 41. Tripitaka of Dharma Master Lac Na Ma De (Ratnamati, translated as Bao Hy)He was a native of Thien Truc. He was humble in his literature, scholarly, had extensive knowledge, recited more than a million verses (each verse had thirty-two words), and thoroughly understood and often propagated Zen dharma. During the Northern Wei Dynasty, the first year of Chanh Thuy (504), Lac Na Ma De came to Luo Duong and translated scriptures in the palace. At first, Lac Na Ma De assisted Bodhi Liu Chi in translating. Because there were disagreements in the translation, I later translated it myself. Monks Tang Lang, Giac Y, etc. took notes. Venerable Lac Na Ma De translated the following sutras: Sutra of the Bhikkhu-Da-Ba-Van (2 volumes), Nagarjuna Bodhisattva Hoa Huong Phuong (1 volume), treatise on the Ten Grounds Sutra (12 volumes), treatise on the Treasure Sutra (4 volumes), treatise on the Endless One Vehicle Precious Nature (4 volumes), treatise on the Lotus Sutra (1 volume).

Tipiṭaka of Dharma Master Buddha Phan DaBuddha Da Phin Da (translated as Giac Dinh), from the north of Thien Truc; From 525 to 539, at the Bach Ma Pagoda in Lac Duong and the Golden Flower Pagoda in Nghiep Do, he translated ten sets of sutras such as: Vajra Sutra of the Supreme Da La Ni (1 volume), Tathagata's Roar Sutra (1 volume), Transformation of Existence Sutra (1 volume), Ten Dharmas Sutra (1 volume), Silver-Colored Lady Sutra (1 volume), Reverence of the Dharma Sutra (1 volume), Fearless Lady Sutra (1 volume), Wushu Sutra (1 volume). noi_dung: 43. Venerable Gotama Prajna Liu ChiCu Dam Prajna Luu Chi (translated as Tri Hy), a man from Thien Truc, came from a Brahmin lineage, in the city of Ba La Nai (Baranasi), came to Central Earth in the year of Hy Binh (516) of the Northern Wei Dynasty. From the original Yuanxiang era (538) to the final Hung Hoa era (542), in Do Thanh, he translated: Sutra on the Dharma and Mindfulness of the Places (70 volumes), Sutra of the Good Dwelling of Intentions (3 volumes), Sutra of the Uncontained World (1 volume), Sutra of the Uncontained Upadādi (1 volume), Treatise on the Return to War (1 volume), Treatise on the Accomplishments of Karma (1 volume), Liberation of the Obligatory Precepts (1 volume).

tom_tat: The Supreme Being in Sanskrit is called Paramada, and his nickname is Cau La Na Tha (translated as Body Y). He was born in the west of Thien Truc, the country of Uu...
noi_dung:
44. ParamathaThe Supreme Being in Sanskrit is called Paramada, and his nickname is Cau La Na Tha (translated as Body Y). He was born in the west of Thien Truc, the country of Ujjaini. Intelligent nature, extraordinary temperament, extraordinary natural talent, proficient in Buddhism, clear understanding of external scriptures, full of supernatural abilities, is a famous monk and scholar with excellent virtue and virtue.

Emperor Wu of Liang (502-549) revered the Three Jewels, so Buddhism naturally flourished. The kingdoms in the South Sea region also came to pay a lot of tribute. When meeting with the envoy of Funan (Cambodia), Emperor Wu of Liang requested the country of Funan to send the Tripitaka masters, famous monks, Mahayana sutras, etc., to Central Earth.

He came from Thien Truc, traveled to neighboring kingdoms, and often went to Funan. The Liang Dynasty and Funan had a very close relationship. Agreeing to Emperor Wu's request, the king of Funan ordered Chan De to bring the sutras to China.

The True Emperor followed the sea route to Guangzhou on the full moon day of the eighth month of the year 546, the reign of Dai Dong, then arrived at Kien Khang in the eighth month of the year 548. Emperor Wu of Liang graciously treated him warmly and invited the True Emperor to enter Bao Van Palace to make generous offerings.

On the tenth day of the eighth month in the year 548, Hou Canh sent troops to rebel in Tho Duong, then crossed the Truong Giang River and led his army to surround Kien Khang. Emperor Wu of Liang did not resist and died of starvation. Kien Khang citadel suffered a war, fires burned everywhere, people died of starvation. Therefore, Mr. Chan De had to leave that place to go to Phu Xuan. At Luc Nguyen Triet's district residence, he began translating the sutras. Luc Nguyen Triet also invited monk Bao Quynh and more than twenty other people to assist in the translation. However, because of the change, the translation of only five sutras had to be stopped.

In 552, in response to Hau Canh's request, Chan De returned to Kien Khang to receive offerings. The next year, Hou Canh was killed. King Tuong Dong ascended the throne and took the title of Emperor Luong Nguyen. At that time, Chan De stayed at Chanh Quan Pagoda in Kien Khang, then together with Zen Master Nguyen and more than twenty others translated the Golden Light Sutra. In February 554, Chan De left Kien Khang and went to Bao Dien pagoda in Du Chuong. Here he once stayed temporarily on the route from Guangdong to Kien Khang. At that time, he often interacted with the monk Canh Thieu (508-583), who was a monk in the Du Chuong area. He highly praised Canh Thieu, a talented and virtuous monk. He said:

- I have traveled to many countries, but rarely meet people like Canh Thieu.

At Du Chuong, he translated the Tan Kim Quang Minh Sutra, the Only Consciousness Sutra, the Nirvana Sutra, etc.

In 554, the third year of Thua Thanh, he left Du Chuong, went to Tan Ngo to stay at My Nghiep Pagoda, then to Thuy Hung to stay at Kien Hung Pagoda. Later, he passed through Guangdong, entered Jiangxi, and then came to stay at Tinh Do Pagoda in Nam Khang. He continuously wandered around, never having had a fixed residence to focus on translating the sutras.

In 558, the second year of Vinh Dinh, he returned to Du Chuong, staying at The-an pagoda. At that time, he traveled throughout Lam Xuyen, crossed the Vo Di mountain range, then went through many miles of long and arduous road, reaching Tan An. There, seeing that the sea route was favorable, he decided to follow the boat and return to his homeland. There, he met famous monks such as Tri Van, Tang Tong, Phap Chuan, etc. Tri Van was proficient in the Ten Reciting Laws. Because he fled at the end of the Liang dynasty, he went to Min Nam area, and was invited by Tang Tong and Phap Chuan to preach the Dharma. There, Tri Van also inspired many people, causing them to take refuge in the Three Jewels, make offerings to monks, and eliminate bad habits such as smoking, drinking alcohol, and gambling. Thanks to their faith and understanding of Buddhism, the fishermen burned their nets, quit fishing, and kept the precept of not killing. When he met him, Tri Van studied Buddhism together.

The Emperor's ambition was to go to Central Earth to propagate the Dharma and translate the scriptures. However, when times were chaotic, people's hearts were in turmoil, and accidents were constant, he became discouraged and followed the boat back to Thien Truc. On the way, he stopped by Guangdong, to Luong An district. Prefect Vuong Phuong Xa and people in the area begged him to stay. Although he accepted their request to stay there, he did not intend to stay there for a long time. From the first of the fifth month to the twenty-fifth of September in the year 562, he translated the Vajra Prajnaparamita Sutra (10 volumes), and the Vajra Prajnaparamita Sutra, commented by Vasubandhu.

Finally, in September 562, he boarded a boat from Liang'an to return to Thien Truc. On the way, there was a storm, so the wind blew the boat back to Guangdong in December. Thai Thu Au Duong Nguy then requested him to return to stay at Che Chi Pagoda and continue his work of translating the scriptures. From then on, he no longer had the idea of ​​returning to his homeland. With the help of his disciple Hue Khai, he translated the Quang Nghia Dharma Gate Sutra, the Only Consciousness Commentary. Prefect Au Duong Nguy also took refuge, received the Bodhisattva precepts, and became his disciple.

During that year, Au Duong Nguy passed away, and his son Au Duong Hot became the guest host. Hue Tri, the abbot of Che Chi pagoda, and the chief of the southern historical school Vien Kinh, played the Vietnamese harp. He finished translating the book The Mahayana Commentary. The monks in Tan An followed him to practice in the past, traveling to the Lanh Nam area in Guangzhou to listen to him explain the new Buddhist teachings.

In January 564, at the request of Hui Khai, Dharma Ren, etc., he translated Pham Hao in the treatise Cau Xa. Before the translation was finished, something suddenly happened, so he temporarily went to Nam Hai district to reside. By October of that year, he finished translating, producing twenty-two volumes of essays, one volume of verses, and fifty-three volumes of commentaries. Later, in response to the request of the governor, he entered the city to lecture on the sutras and preach the Dharma. Seeing that the old translations had many errors and omissions, he re-translated the book Cau Xa from February 565 to December 567 and completed it. In January of the following year, he finished translating the book The Twenty-Twelve Laws of Wisdom.

Throughout his life, he propagated the Dharma to benefit living beings, but he did not have the opportunity to find good ashrams and temples to live and practice the Dharma, and encountered many unsatisfactory things, so he intended to commit suicide. While lecturing Cau Xa, hearing this news, Hue Khai immediately returned to the temple to prevent it. Monks and lay people came to comfort him. The governor Au Duong Hot also sent people to attend to him, then personally came to take care of him for three consecutive days. He arranged for him to temporarily reside at Vuong Vien pagoda. Disciples of Tang Tong, Tang Khai, etc. intended to take him back to Kien Khang. However, the scholars there, fearing that once he returned, their reputation and power would be tarnished, so they jointly presented a statement to King Tran Van De:

- In the Lanh Nam region, Chan De translated Duy Thuc Vo Tran Thuyet. That monk both promoted the Dharma and pursued political power. This is not only inappropriate but also contrary to our country's teachings. Please, the king, please drive this type of person out of the capital to far away places.

Emperor Tran Van De naturally approved it, so he could not return to the capital. The book 'New Duy Thuc Treatise' was translated by the King and was not circulated outside.

In the past, Emperor Wu of Liang worshiped Dai Luan because he himself studied Thanh That Luan. Tran Van De is not like that. He often made efforts to propagate the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra, and emphasized the Three Treatises.

Despite experiencing the two dynasties of Luong and Tran, the study movement in Kien Khang still favored the principles of Prajna and Tam Luan.

Phap Thai, a disciple of the True Truth, preached the Commentary on Consciousness Only, which monks and laity could not comprehend. Therefore, everyone was cold and no one wanted to study the Yogācāra teachings.

Hue Khai at Tri Hue Pagoda preached nine volumes of the Cau Xa treatise, the Karma Pham Commentary and then passed away. Therefore, Mr. Chan replaced and continued to preach three more volumes. Before the teachings were completed, he passed away the next year, on the eleventh day of the first month of the year 568. He entrusted his disciples, Tri Huu and Phap Hai, at Tam Tang Pagoda to receive the teachings. On the twelfth day, the disciples performed the cremation ceremony and then built the worship tower. On the thirteenth day, Tang Tong, Phap Chuan, etc. discussed going to Lo Son. His disciple Tri Kieu wrote: "As soon as the Noble Truth of the Tripitaka passed away, all his Dharma companions dispersed. The sect had no successors."

Mr. Chan De put all his heart and soul into translating the book The Mahayana Abhidharma. At that time, disciples like Tang Tong and Hue Khai also tried their best to research and support.

One day, the weather was bitterly cold, but the True Deity only wore light clothes and had menstrual fluids all night long, so his health was weak. Just when he was about to sleep, Hue Khai gently took the back of his robe and covered his feet to keep them warm, but he scolded him again. This represents his spirit of contentment, his will to endure hardship, and his diligence in propagating the Dharma. Therefore, the disciples became more and more admired and respected.

He also often lamented that his luck was unfortunate, causing many obstacles to his cause for spreading the Dharma. Fortunately, he was wholeheartedly respected by his disciples and wholeheartedly supported in the work of translating the sutras, so he was somewhat comforted. Hue Khai was afraid that the Yoga-Only-Consciousness Dharma would be lost in the future. He pointed to the northwest and said:

- There is a great country there, neither near nor far. After I pass away, people in that land will promote this Dharma, causing it to prosper.

The Truth's prediction was not wrong. Later, in the north, there was Mr. Dam Tuyen who propagated the Nhiep Luan Luan, and used this method as the foundation for the Nhiep Luan sect.

Mr. Chan De in Central Earth translated the sutras from 546 to 569. Over the course of twenty-three years, Mr. Chan De translated sixty-four volumes, and two hundred and seventy-eight volumes of sutras. The Buddha's merits greatly influenced later Buddhism.

The sutras translated by the True Emperor are as follows: The Sutra of Light and Brightness (7 volumes), the Maitreya Sutra in Lower Birth (1 volume), the Sutra of Human King Prajna (1 volume), the treatise on the Seventeen Grounds (5 volumes), the treatise on Mahayana Arising Faith (1 volume), the Middle Treatise (1 volume), the treatise on True Truth (1 volume), the treatise on the Void of the Origin of Existence (1 volume), the treatise on the Three Distinctions of the Three Worlds (1 volume), the Sutra of the Golden Light (13 volumes), the Sutra of the Golden Light (1 volume). Prajnaparamita (6 volumes), Mahayana Arising Faith commentary (2 volumes), Middle Commentary (2 volumes), Nine Consciousness Notes (2 volumes), Zhuan Falun Meanings (1 volume), Abhidharma Sutra (9 volumes), Supreme Medicine Sutra (2 volumes), Explanation Sutra (1 volume), Vajra Prajna Paramita Sutra (1 volume), Extensive Dharma Door Sutra (1 volume), Anguttara Sutra (1 volume), Practice of Concentration Meditation (1 volume), treatise on the Sakyas (21 volumes), Abhidhamma Abhidhamma (10 volumes), treatise on Mahayana Photography (15 volumes), treatise on Buddha Nature (4 volumes), treatise on the Four Noble Truths (4 volumes), treatise on the Sangha (3 volumes), Treatise on the Mahayana Abhidharma (3 volumes), treatise on Great Emptiness (3 volumes), treatise on the Middle Boundary Distinction (3 volumes), treatise on the Golden Seventeen (2 volumes), Sentences Commentary on the Verses (1 volume), treatise on Vajra Prajna (1 volume), treatise on the Twenty-Twelve Insights (1 volume), treatise on the Mahaparinirvana Sutra (1 volume), treatise on Digha (1 volume), treatise on the Three Non-Natives (1 volume), treatise on the Reflection of Nature (1 volume), treatise on Sui Sui (1 volume), treatise on Praying for Na Ma Sui Tu Tuu (1 volume), treatise on the True King of Happiness (1 volume), treatise on the Accomplishment of the Three Vehicles (1 volume), treatise on the Perfect Wheel The Doctrine of the Doctrine (1 volume), the Treatise on Meaning (1 volume), the Treatise on the Different Paths (1 volume), the Consciousness-Only Treatise on Meaning (1 volume), the Right Wheel Thich Nghia (5 volumes), the Buddha Nature Meaning (3 volumes), the Zen Definition of Meaning (1 volume), the commentary on Cau Xa (16 volumes), the commentary on Vajra Prajna (11 volumes), the commentary on the Eighteen Commentaries (10 volumes), the commentary on the Explanation Sutra (4 volumes), the commentary on the Supreme Sutra (1 volume). Medicine (4 volumes), commentary on the True Truth (3 volumes), commentary on the Four Noble Truths (3 volumes), commentary on Destroying the Self (1 volume), commentary on the Central and Sixteen Truths (1 volume), the story of Ba Tau Ban Dau (1 volume), the Sutra Sutra (2 volumes), the Foreign Translation of the National Language (7 volumes), the Nhan Tho Luc (volume I), the treatise on the Eighteen Emptiness (1 volume), the treatise on Tu Tran (1 volume), the commentary on Explanation of Power (1 volume). volumes), the Treatise on Concentration Tripitaka (2 volumes), the Treatise on Manifestation (1 volume), the Treatise on Transformation of Consciousness (1 volume).

Yogācāra and Consciousness-Only studies had a great influence on Chinese Buddhism, and the Tripitaka master who had the most merit in translating and propagating those sutras was Chan De. Although he had the will to propagate the Dharma and save sentient beings, the True Truth's life encountered many contradictory and tragic scenes: He was not supported by many great donors; There was no certain place of residence, no proper ashram to translate, etc. However, despite all the hardships and frustrations, the True Deity's desire to propagate the Dharma remained steadfast. He translated and explained the scriptures until the last minute of his life. Truly worthy of being a great man in the history of Buddhism.

Later, in the Tang Dynasty, the general Xuanzang presided over a new translation of the Mind-Only Sutras, causing Chan De's previous translated works to be obscured and lost. However, Chan De's career of translating the classics will forever be recorded in the history of Buddhism.

tieu_de: 45. Venerable Na Lien De Le Da Xa (Narendrayasas, translated as Ton Xuyen)
tom_tat: He is from the O Truong country in the north of Thien Truc, of the same ethnicity as Buddha, that is, the Shakyamuni family, the Sat De Loi lineage. At the age of seventeen, he made up his mind...
noi_dung:
45. Venerable Na Lien De Le Da Xa (Narendrayasas, translated as Ton Xuyen)He is from the O Truong country in the north of Thien Truc, of the same ethnicity as Buddha, that is, the Shakyamuni family, the Sat De Loi lineage. At the age of seventeen, he made up his mind to become a monk, then went to study with a wise master. In the twenty-first year of full ordination. Hearing the nobles often praising the Buddha's relics, such as this country having Buddha's alms bowl, that country worshiping Buddha's monk's robe, that country worshiping Buddha's Name, etc., he made a wish to go to those places to admire and worship. As soon as I received the full precepts, I clearly knew the Vinaya Pitaka. After a year of summer, he traveled to various places. All relics such as stone steps, stone platforms, dragon temples, stupas, etc. He went to those places to pay homage and worship. When he arrived at Truc Vien Pagoda, he stayed there for ten years, understanding the monkhood well.

His character is straightforward and his virtue is shining. There was a venerable person who often knew the inborn qualities of others and told him:

- If you specialize in pure practice, you can attain sainthood; I'm just afraid that if you like to travel, it will be difficult for you to achieve anything. If you don't understand this today, you won't have time to regret it when you get old!

He went everywhere: North to Tuyet Son mountain; south to Su Tu country to worship Buddha's relics.

At that time, the king of O Truong used kindness to treat the people and believed in the Three Jewels. Every day, in the morning of the year of the year, the king wakes up, pays homage to the Three Jewels, offers flowers and incense, and makes sincere offerings. When the sun rose, we went up to the palace to review the affairs of the royal court. At the hour of the dragon (from seven in the morning to nine in the evening), the king uses perfume to wash the Buddha statue. Every day, in the palace there are usually hundreds of monks receiving food. The king and his wife personally offered food to the monks. After serving his son, the king practiced martial arts. At sunset, he personally copied the sutras, discussed the meaning of Buddhism with the highly virtuous monks, and then held a conference with the courtiers to discuss political matters. At night, go into the main Buddha hall to light a lamp, worship, and recite sutras, then go to rest. For more than thirty years, the king has always acted like that.

Legend has it that in the country of O Truong, at a mountain in the Tuyet Son range, there are two paths: One is the path of humans, and the other is the path of demons. The path of humans is steep and dangerous, but the path of demons is clear and easy to follow. Passengers arriving there, seeing the other two roads, often mistakenly enter the devil's path, so they are killed by demons. Once upon a time, there was a holy king who made a stone statue of Pi Sa Thien Vuong, whose arms clearly showed the path of mankind. One time, Venerable Na Lien De Le Da Xa and his companions strayed into the path of demons. As soon as he realized he was going astray, he chanted the mantra. The companions were all killed by demons. Thanks to him chanting the mantra, he was able to escape. Therefore, He went back out, but again encountered robbers. He concentrated on reciting mantras, so he was protected by gods. The robbers were about to come and plunder him, but suddenly he was nowhere to be seen. He went east again, through neighboring countries. Because of the military disaster, the road back to the west was cut off, so he had no way to return to his native country.

Therefore, depending on the wind, He reached the Ne Hai Sea, then traveled seven thousand miles to the south. That place was also not safe, so he went to the state of Qi and resided in the capital in the year (556). When Emperor Van Tuyen met him, he respectfully worshiped and made profound offerings. At that time, He was forty years old. Emperor Van Tuyen then assured him to stay at Thien Binh Pagoda and requested to translate the sutras. The king also ordered to bring more than a thousand Sanskrit scriptures from the palace to Thien Binh Pagoda, placing them in a room above. The king also built a magnificent and solemn ashram for him, to show his respect. He again ordered the great monk Master Zhao Xuan, Phap Thuong, and more than twenty other people to assist him in translating the sutras. After he finished translating more than fifty volumes of sutras, Emperor Van Tuyen then circulated them to spread the Dharma.

Emperor Van Tuyen believed in Buddhism very specifically. Every time he held a Sanskrit sutra, he often told his officials that this was a priceless Dharma Jewel that I always respected.

Whenever he finished translating sutras, he often performed magic spells, supported the court, and made many achievements. Whenever he was offered gifts, he did not keep them as his own, but gave them to monks and the poor. He often starts from a kind heart, brings good karma, and helps and saves those who are imprisoned; At the market, they dug wells and personally drew water for people. At the District level in Tay Son, he built three large, solemn pagodas. He also nourished men and women with leprosy, and provided them with adequate supplies. He often went into inns, advised people to observe six days of fasting, and liberated living beings. One time, He was sick for a hundred days but still could not recover. Emperor Wen Tuyen and the queen personally came to greet him. He tried to sit up to respond, saying:

- The poor monk was originally a foreigner and his virtues were not yet perfect. Now the Holy Supreme Saint has come here to offer condolences, making the Poor Monk feel extremely embarrassed.

Ly Kien Duc overthrew the Qi dynasty and took the throne as Emperor Wu of Zhou. He strongly destroyed Buddhism. Wearing three robes inside and wearing secular clothes outside, he took refuge here and there without finding any peace. The people were also devastated, hungry and miserable. Although his strength was tired, his spirit was still full, and he urged himself to help the suffering and hungry people, and preached unceasingly.

Four years later, the Sui Dynasty ascended the throne and revived Buddhism. At the beginning of the reign of Khai Hoang (581), the king appointed translators to translate the Sanskrit sutras, hoping to propagate the Dharma. In the seventh month of the following year, his disciples invited him to the capital and stayed at Dai Hung Thien pagoda. That year, Ly Dong Thao summoned monks to translate the sutras, ordering the monk Huyen Thuong Dam Duyen and more than thirty other people to assist him in translating the sutras. The king often came to worship, warmly greet people, and make generous offerings.

After many years of traveling around the country, he still diligently cultivated the Dharma, often wearing the robe of Sariputra Da La Ni. One night, he dreamed that he himself had become a Buddha. He also often dreams of good omens.

Later, he came to Quang Te pagoda, became the monk of foreign monks, and often greeted guest monks, and was respected and loved by everyone. One day, he suddenly told his disciples:

- I am old and weak, so I will soon die. Today I want to remind you that the Buddha Dharma is difficult to find, so you should diligently practice and study it. The human body is difficult to obtain, so don't let time pass in vain.

Having finished speaking, he passed away on the twenty-ninth day of the second month of the ninth year of Khai Hoang (589), at the age of one hundred years. Previously, He had said:

- I will live to be a hundred years old, and be the same as Dang Tien.

Indeed, as he said, he lived to be a hundred years old before becoming a citizen. (Dang Tien is a master of virtue. His explanations are profound, making it difficult for others to understand. His appearance is very unusual. On the top of his head there is a lump of flesh. His voice resonates far into the clouds. His ears are large and long. His eyes only look straight or down, not looking east or west. His majestic and virtuous appearance is unmatched.)

Venerable Na Lien De Le Na Xa translated a total of 15 sets and more than 80 volumes of sutras such as Bodhisattva View of the Moon Treasure, Nikaya Tripitaka, Phap Thang Bhikkhu, etc.

He traveled for more than forty years, visited about fifty kingdoms, traveled more than one hundred and fifty thousand miles, visited the places of famous and virtuous monks, and many excellent temples and monasteries. All famous monks in the mountains, valleys, and all over the world all worship him.

tom_tat: Xa Na Quat Da is translated as Duc Chi Bac Hien Dau. Hien Dau comes from the sound Nhan Da La Ba Da Na (translated as Vuong Xu, meaning the place where God Thich...
noi_dung:
46. ​​JnanaguntaXa Na Quat Da is translated as Duc Chi Bac Hien Dau. Hien Dau comes from the sound Nhan Da La Ba Da Na (translated as Vuong Xu, meaning the place where Thich Thich often protects).

He was originally from Kien Da La country (translated as Huong Hanh country). The family often resides in Phu Luu Sa Luu La citadel (translated as Truong Phu palace). He originally belonged to the Sat De Loi lineage, his natural name was Kim Bo, translated as Hang (ie like the neck of a giant bird), belonging to the noble family in that country. The father's name is Bat Xa La Ba La (translated as Kim Cang Kien). As a child, he had lofty ambitions; When he grew up, he was noble enough to become a prime minister. He had five children, of whom Xa Na Quat Da was the youngest.

As a child, Mr. Xa Na Quat Da had the virtue of honesty and integrity, soon developed a spiritual mind, liked to shave his head, and vowed to become a monk. My parents knew clearly, but did not allow me to become a monk. That country has a large monastery called Dai Lam. He often went there to take refuge, hoping to be saved. Later, he only followed the monk Xa Nha Na Bat Dat La (translated as Tri Hien), mastered the three Pitakas, and clearly understood the Vinaya Pitaka.

After becoming a monk, Xa Na Quat Da was respectful and devoted to the teachings of his original teacher, only mastering the scriptures. At that time, the sacred relics in Hien Dau still existed. Therefore, he followed his original teacher to admire and worship. At the age of twenty-seven, when he was a third-year-old, he and his master and other monks agreed to travel abroad to spread the Dharma. At first, a total of ten monks set out together. On the way, they stopped by Ca Ty Thi country and stayed there for several years. The king requested Sarya Na Bat Dat La (the original teacher of Sara Quat Da) to be the national teacher, bringing many benefits to the nation.

Later, they came to Tay Tuc mountain in the Dai Tuyet Son range. Tay Tuc mountain is towering, reaching into the blue sky. Next, they passed through the country of Yemdad. That place is wild, sparsely populated, and no one offers food. Therefore, Mr. Xa Na Quat Da gave up his precepts and tried his best to find food and protect the group to propagate the Dharma. Some time later, protected by the gods, they escaped famine in the wilderness. They continued to the country of Kiet La Ban Da and Vu Dien. There, they encountered cold rain, wind and snow, so they temporarily stopped, but did not propagate. Not long after, they went to Thien Chau again. At that time, it was during the Western Wei Dynasty, the reign of Dai Tong Nguyen (535). Even though he encountered many difficulties and dangers, his mind was still strong and diligent. From the time of departure, there were ten people, but when they got there, only four people were still alive. In the reign of Emperor Zhou Ming, the reign of Vo Thanh (557-560), they came to Truong An and temporarily stayed at Thao Duong pagoda. There, Mr. Xa Na Quat Da ascended to the altar, received full precepts, then diligently practiced, slowly learning Chinese. Knowing the reputation of the original teacher (ie Xa Nha Na Bat Dat La), Emperor Chu Minh invited him to the royal palace to ask questions, discuss Buddhism, and then make offerings in the forbidden palace. Seeing that they could not have freedom in the forbidden palace, his teacher and disciples, Xa Na Quat Da, reported it to Emperor Chu Minh. The king then ordered the construction of the Four Heavenly Kings Pagoda for his teachers and students to reside in, and started the work of translating classic scriptures, such as the Thap Nhat Quan Am Sutra, Golden Tien Van, etc.

Later, Tieu Vuong Tu Van Kiem came to take over the land of Thuc, so he invited him to accompany him. So, they followed him there, staying at Long Uyen Pagoda. Venerable Sarya Na Bat Dat La assumed the position of Monk in Ich Chau, and translated the Avalokiteshvara, Buddhist scriptures, etc.

At that time, King Wu De admired Buddhism and destroyed Buddhism, forcing the monks to return to the secular world. He again forced Mr. Xa Na Quat Da into the capital and forced him to drink wine and perform rituals, but he still persevered in keeping the precepts, not showing any fear. Emperor Wu saw his strong will and released him back to the temple. From Cam Chau towards Dot Quyet, the original master (ie Xa Nha Na Bat Dat La) wanted to return to the west to enter nirvana. Arriving at Dot Quyet, teachers and students stayed. Not long after, Sarya Na Bat Da La entered nirvana. Mr. Xa Na Quat Da is a form and a shadow, with no place to stay.

He came to the Bac Dich region, depending on the means to spread benefits. By the fifth year of Khai Hoang (585), at Dai Hung Thien pagoda, monk Dam Duyen and more than thirty other monks began to translate. Hearing that Xa Na Quat Da was staying in Bac Dich, they made a petition to him to return to the capital. The king immediately issued a decree and requested him four times, but he still did not go and stayed there for ten years. Later, because he felt that the world appreciated the Three Jewels, he returned to the capital. At that time, Emperor Wen was residing in Luoyang. He heard that he was coming to the capital, so he was very happy, came to greet him, and invited him to translate the sutras. Seeing that the new scriptures had just been translated, the text was very rudimentary, and the meaning was not clear, so he tried his best to review, sharpen, and refine them. At that time, Venerable Na Lien De Le Da Xa passed away, so only Venerable Xa Na Quat Da was left to take on the responsibility of censoring the scriptures.
