He also invited two Brahman brothers, Cao Thien Thu and Cao Hoa Nhan, to help review the Sanskrit text. There were also ten famous monks such as monks, Dharma Sutras, etc. who helped him edit and determine the principles.

Two thousand miles southeast of Vu Dien, there is a country called Gia Cau Gia. The king believes in Mahayana Buddhism. In the middle hall, there are three sutras of Ma Ha Prajna and the Great Collection of Avatamsaka. The king often divides his time to recite and offer incense and flowers. In the southeast of the country there is a towering Coa mountain. Inside there is a dark cave, containing the eight sutras of the Great Collection, Hoa Nghiem, Phuong Dang, Bao Tich, Lang Gia, Phuong Quang, Sariputra Sariputra, Two Dala Nido La Tang, Ma Ha Prajna. Prajnaparamita and Mahayana have twelve collections, about one hundred thousand verses. The national law is said to protect and protect. In addition, there are three Arhats entering nirvana in that cave. Every fortnight, the monks on the mountain go there and shave the three Arahants. The king of that country uses human law to rule. The people all devoted themselves to worshiping Buddhism.

Mr. Xa Na Quat Dao is pure and kind, his spirit is strong and righteous, and he loves virtue; never tire of seeking the Dharma, learning the three classics, studying the profound principles of the true essence; Learn all the five wisdoms and understand the world; Practicing the Dharma, one obtains the teachings of animals and masters the understanding of mantras; Throughout his life, he often wears three robes and wears them once a day. He benevolently saves people and sacrifices without waiting for requests; Always diligently reading and reciting the scriptures, earning the respect of the monks and the worship of the layman. It was up to Vuong Dang to revere and admire his virtue, so he honored him as a teacher.

In the twelfth year of Khai Hoang (592), Xa Na Quat Da passed away at the age of seventy-eight. Since coming to Dong Do, he has translated thirty-seven sets of sutras, and one hundred and seventy-six volumes, such as the Buddha's Original Conduct Sutras, Tap Phap Cu, Oai Duc Ho Niem, Hien Ho, etc. The translation is fluent, in accordance with the teachings. In the past, Sui Cao To issued an edict to the monk Xa Na Quat Da and the monk Nha Na Kiet Da (from the Western Regions), etc., in the internal history of the province, to translate classical Sanskrit texts. By the twelfth reign of Khai Hoang, it was completed.

tom_tat: Dat Ma Level Da was originally from Hien Dau La La country, belonged to the Sat De Loi lineage, his natural name was Te Na Gia La (called Ho De), was the oldest person, had...
noi_dung:
47. Dharmagupta (Dharmagupta, translated as Dharma Secret)Dat Ma Level Da was originally from Hien Dau La La country, belonged to the Sat De Loi lineage, his natural name was Te Na Gia La (called Ho De), was the eldest, had four younger siblings. My parents were reluctant and did not allow me to become a monk. However, he had full faith and admiration for the dharma, and deeply wished to become a monk and leave the secular world. At the age of twenty-three, he came to the city of Kien Noa Cuu Bat Do (translated as Nhi Xuat). In Cuu Ni area (translated as Hoang Sac Hoa Vien), there is a famous Sangha Lam temple. There, Venerable Dama Level Da was ordained as a monk. At the age of twenty-five, he received full ordination, and remained at the temple to study for three years. In the temple, there was an A Xa Le named Pho Chieu, who was well-versed in the sutras of the Mahayana and Hinayana, often begged, and practiced meditation. At that time, Pho Chieu was requested by the king of Tra Ca to go there to preach the Dharma. Venerable Bodhidharma also followed through that country. One year later, Pho Chieu returned to his native country. Bodhisattva Bodhidharma remained there for four years, at De Ba Ti Ha La Pagoda (translated as Thien Du). This is the temple where Mahayana and Hinayana monks from all four directions gather to practice and study, hoping for an increase in insight.

Merchants traveling north of Thien Truc often passed through this area. They often tell each other that in the Eastern Region there is Dai Chi Na (or Chan Dan) country. At first, although he heard the name of that country, he did not pay attention to it. Later, he and six other monks went to Ca Ty Thi country and stayed at Vuong Tu pagoda. He and four other monks stayed in that city for two consecutive years. During this time, he traveled around monasteries to study the scriptures. This country was originally a place where merchants often gathered, because it was located on the northern route. Merchants also often talk about the people in Dai Chi Na who believe in worshiping the Three Jewels. Twice hearing about the country of Dai Chi Na made him intend to travel there to propagate the Dharma. Therefore, he, along with a few monks accompanying him, went to Tay Tuc mountain in the Tuyet Son range, Bac Khu La country, Ba Da Xa Noa, and Dat Ma Tat Tu Da country. In these countries, although he did not stay long, he clearly understood the customs and rituals of practice in the monasteries. He came to Kiet La Ban Da again, stayed for a year, and still did not preach the Dharma. He came to Sa Lac country again. A fellow monk returned to his native country, while the remaining three companions resided at Vuong Tu pagoda. This temple was built by King Sa Lac. During his two years of residence, for the sake of the monks at that temple, he preached two thousand verses of the Niem Pha treatise to explain the three seals and destroy the theories of pagans. He again preached As It Is, also with two thousand verses, to break down the world's meanings and arguments.

Next, he went to Quy Tu country and stayed at Vuong Tu pagoda for two years. He also preached Thich Tien Luan for the monks there. Because he believed in the Mahayana, when he heard Bodhisattva Bodhisattva explain that treatise, the king of Quy Tu was also greatly enlightened, so he often came day and night to ask questions. Because he had a wish to go to Dong Do, he did not want to stay there. Therefore, he and another monk secretly went to Wu Qi country, stayed at A Lan Noa pagoda, lectured on Thong Tien and sutras for two years, then slowly went to Cao Xuong country, visiting monasteries. In that country, many monks specialize in learning Chinese. Although he stayed for two years, he did not preach anything. Next, he went to Y Ngo country. On the way to that country, He crossed a desert without grass and water. Because of thirst, the companions all died in the desert. He alone carried the sutras and tried to follow the roads and mountains to find drinking water. Unable to find water, he tried his best to recite the name of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and chant mantras. At night, it suddenly rained, making his body and mind full of joy. He then returned to the old path, but it was deserted on all sides, and he lost track and direction. However, he still moved forward, and then when he reached Qua Chau, he realized that the northern road was curved. Along the way, some of the accompanying monks either returned to Thien Truc, stayed in neighboring kingdoms, or lost their lives.

Having gone through many hardships and hardships, he finally reached the capital city of Central Earth alone. Hearing the news of his arrival, the king warmly welcomed him, made offerings, and invited him to stay at major monasteries. In the tenth month of the tenth year of Khai Hoang (590), before he had finished resting, he was given a decree by the king to translate the scriptures. He went to Dai Hung Thien Pagoda and immediately started translating. There, he often preached the profound meanings of the Mahayana and Hinayana sutras. Even though some old-schoolers were skeptical, he still propagated the teachings and commentaries. His nature is gentle and merciful. The mind does not leave the religion, the words and actions are compatible. Pure morality. Deep and profound wisdom. Understand the source of the scriptures. His appearance is dignified, majestic and majestic, the sound of reciting scriptures is as loud as thunder, his reason is clear inside and out, he likes to live in quiet places, does not like hesitation, often teaches people without tiring, does not care about money and material things, making people who have not met him have a heart of admiration, and making people who meet him have deep trust.

Duong De Dinh respected and made offerings to him deeply. Because he wanted Buddhism to prosper, he issued a decree to establish a sutra translation center at Thuong Lam Vien on the banks of the Lac Thuy river, so that he could translate the sutras and spread the Dharma. Famous scholars suddenly flocked to study with him. One time, a sutra had just been translated, with a few passages missing. Because he thoroughly understood the scriptures, he added it himself to make it full of meaning. In total, he translated seven sets of sutras, combined into thirty-two volumes, such as Dependent Origination of the World, Medicine Master's Original Vows, Mahayana Bodhisattva's Reception, etc. The text is neat, clear, and clear. The sutras translated by him are all placed in the 'Duong Trinh Quan Inner Canon Luc'. In the second year of Vo Duc's reign, he translated fifteen more volumes of the Pho Lac Sutra.

There was a monk Ngan Tong, fluent in Sanskrit-Chinese, based on the words of the Venerable Bodhisattva Dharma about the events he saw and heard on the route from Thien Truc to Trung Tho, he wrote a set of 'Tai Sui Tay Vuc Tales'. In this series, it is divided into ten parts: 1/ direction, things, 2/ climate, 3/ residence, 4/ politics, 5/ education, 6/ etiquette, 7/ food, 8/ clothes, 9/ resources, 10/ mountains and rivers, cities, villages, and people.

tom_tat: He is a native of Ma Kiet De country in the middle of Thien Truc, well-versed in the Tripitaka, knowledgeable in worldly philosophy and medical techniques. One time, in that country there was...
noi_dung:
48. Mr. Xa De Tu NaHe is a native of Ma Kiet De country in the middle of Thien Truc, well-versed in the Tripitaka, knowledgeable in worldly philosophy and medical techniques. One time, there was a violent earthquake in that country, causing the ground to crack, revealing a stone stele, written: "In the East, there is the country Chan Dan, named Dai Sui, the city is called Dai Hung, the king Kien Y proposed to build a pagoda and tower to worship the Three Jewels."

Seeing this stone stele, the king and the people were very happy and thought it was a rare good omen. At that time, in Trung Tho it was the fourteenth year of Khai Hoang (594). Venerable Xa De Tu Na, along with fifty monks and lay people, set out from the Royal Palace to the east to find the spirit. On the way they were killed by bandits, only a few people escaped.

After nine years, he arrived in Central Earth in the second year of Nhan Tho (602). At that time, Emperor Van De Sui requested a lot of relics and built an offering tower. As soon as he arrived, the king immediately invited him into Dai Bao's inner palace. While talking with Him, the king suddenly raised four fingers and asked his servants:

- Do you know what I mean?

No one among the gods could answer. The king turned to ask Him. He replied:

- The meaning of Dan Viet is to say that the poor man has attained the four stages of Arhatship. But, this is not true.

Hearing this, the king was horrified. Next, the king invited him to stay at a palace inn. One time, the king asked again:

- Create spiritual towers throughout the districts. However, there are two prefectures, Xiem Chau and Cao Chau, which have the most auspicious omens. So who should we worship?

He said:

- Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva should be worshiped in Siam Chau. In Cao Chau, Bodhisattva Quan Hoa Khong Tang should be worshiped.

- What is the heavenly flower like?

- Like a thin piece of mica.

The king then secretly took thin mica to make heavenly flowers. Whoever looks in, no one will know. Later, the queen passed away, and there was loud music in the void, and a strange scent spread everywhere. The king brought this matter up for questioning. He replied:

- The Queen was reborn in the Western Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha, so the gods played heavenly music to welcome her.

The king thought it was a special omen, so he offered gifts and rewards, but he did not accept it.

After that, no one knew when he passed away.

tom_tat: Mr. Ba La Pha Ca La Mat Da La (translated as Minh Tri Thuc) is a Thien Truc person, belongs to the Sat De Loi lineage, follows the Sat Loi De family, ordained from...
noi_dung:
49. Prabhakaramitra (Prabhakaramitra)Venerable Ba La Pha Ca La Mat Da La (translated as Minh Tri Thuc) is a middle-class person from Thien Truc, belongs to the Sat De Loi lineage, follows the Sat De Loi nature, became a monk at the age of ten, recites hundreds of thousands of verses of the Mahayana sutras. After receiving the full precepts, he diligently studied the Vinaya, was knowledgeable in the precepts, and liked meditation, so he followed the masters to practice meditation, without abandoning the scriptures for twelve long years. Later, he went to Na Lan Da monastery in the country of Maga Da (or Ma Kiet Da). There, when the commentator Gioi Hien was promoting the theory of Truly That Land, he stayed to listen to the explanation. This treatise clearly demonstrates the teachings of small-mindedness. He recited and read the Hinayana treatises thoroughly. Thanks to his intelligent and scholarly temperament, he thoroughly researched the teachings of Mahayana. He also became a teacher for his fellow students, and also converted monks, and often lectured on sutras such as Prajnaparamita Da La Bat Ma, etc., making the students deeply understand the mysterious meanings. His fame and reputation made all kings, officials, and courtiers admire him. However, monastics do not permanently reside in one direction. Depending on the dharma, about every six months, he moved once. Because the people of Northern Dich Dot Quyet did not know Buddhism, he went there to teach. Gradually, he, along with about ten monks and laity, went north, to the west of Khahan Thong Diep Ho (Jabgu), and used the Buddha Dharma to educate those who had never known the true religion, causing the Lord to deeply admire him, so he gave twenty people to serve day and night. The accompanying monks and laity saw his teaching grace like that, so they became even more convinced.

In 626, King Cao Binh sent messengers to Phien land, so he met him and was saved. The messenger brought back the words he had been taught and told them to King Cao Binh. Therefore, King Cao Binh sent an envoy to request him to come to Dong Do, but Diep Ho's military officials were reluctant to let him go. The king heard Cao Binh Vuong's performance and ordered Nhung Lord to take him to Trung Tho. Seeing his weakness, Lord Nhung had to give in and let him enter Trung Tho with Vuong Cao Binh.

That year, in December, he arrived at the capital. The king granted him a decree to stay at Dai Hung Thien Pagoda, and he often went there to visit and discuss the mysterious meaning. Depending on the occasion, he answered thoroughly, causing the king to respect him very much, so he sent five monks to be his attendants. His words and explanations are not beyond the scriptures. The king again granted him an order to translate the sutras, and invited nineteen famous and virtuous monks to assist, such as monk Hue Thua (in charge of comparing meanings), monk Huyen Mo (in charge of translating), monks Hue Tinh, Hue Minh, etc. (in charge of polishing the text), along with the royal servant and crown prince (in charge of editing assumptions), and Quang Loc, chief physician of Khanh Tieu Chuong (in charge of guardianship). The court officials together made profound offerings. First, he translated the Bao Tinh Sutra, then the Thang Quang Sutra, and the Prajnaparamita Dignity Sutra; A total of three series and thirty-five volumes. Six years later, he reviewed and refined the writing to make it fluent, then presented it to the king for consideration. After reviewing thoroughly, the king ordered ten volumes to be copied for circulation in the country. The king highly rewarded him, and ordered the crown prince to write prefaces for the newly translated scriptures. He also often preached sutras to famous mandarins and scholars.

The monk Hue Giai, a monk of extraordinary talent, said to the guardian historian:

- Venerable Ba La Pha Ca La Mat Da La came from thousands of miles away to Dong Ha not for profit and fame, but only because he wanted to make the teachings spread for thousands of years, and the Dharma's sound resonate throughout the ages. In the past, during the reigns of King Phu Kien and Dao Hung, there were three thousand scholars who translated the sutras. Currently, in the Tang Dynasty, there are only more than twenty people involved in translating. So please report this matter to the Emperor, so that he can help translate the sutras, so that future generations will not be suspicious.

Due to his vow to propagate Buddhism, he did not care about hardships and dangers, traveled more than forty thousand miles, crossed Thong Linh mountain, crossed deserts and dangerous mountains and rivers, brought the scriptures to Chan Dan country to translate. However, his wish was not fulfilled, and he did not know who to confide in, so he fell ill. Knowing that he could not be cured, he distributed the materials, created pure karma, then sat upright in front of the main hall of Thang Quang pagoda, with his right mind contemplating the Buddha statue, then passed away, at the age of sixty-nine in the year 633. The crown prince of the East Palace sent twenty people to take his body to the mountain for the cremation ceremony. After that, monk Huyen Mo collected the relics and placed them in the worship tower at Thang Quang pagoda, on the sixth day of the fourth month, the seventh Trinh Quan year. For many years he devoted his efforts to translating, hoping that the torch of Dharma would illuminate the ignorant. However, his vow to propagate the Dharma was not yet fulfilled and he passed away, leaving posterity in shock, sadness, and admiration.

tieu_de: 50. Tripitaka Dharma Master Na De (Punyopaya, translated as Phuoc Sanh)
tom_tat: He was originally from Trung Thien Truc, became a monk at a young age, was enlightened by famous masters, and had the will and ambition to propagate the Dharma far away. Because...
noi_dung:
50. Tripitaka Dharma Master Na De (Punyopaya, translated as Phuoc Sanh)He was originally from Trung Thien Truc, became a monk at a young age, was enlightened by famous masters, and had the will and ambition to propagate the Dharma far away. Therefore, He traveled throughout the kingdoms to enlighten the people. Later, he went to Su Tu country, to Lang Gia mountain in the southeast, through countries in the South China Sea, and taught depending on the conditions. Thanks to his fluency in many languages ​​of different countries, he often recited sutras and preached Dharma, saving people to set up temples. In Thiem Chau, east of Chi Na country, he propagated the Mahayana teachings, causing Buddhism to flourish. He brought one thousand five hundred Mahayana sutras to the capital Trung Tho in the sixth year of Vinh Huy (655).

At that time, the reputation of magician Huyen Trang resounded everywhere, no one could compare. Therefore, Mr. Na De had to resign himself to seclusion. In the original year of Hien Khanh (656), Emperor Cao Tong issued a decree for Mr. Na De to go to the Kunlun countries to find strange medicines. Arriving at the South Sea, the kings together welcomed him, took refuge, and established pagodas so that he could educate and educate the people. Dharma propagation industry is evident. However, because he followed King Tang's orders to visit the countries in the South China Sea, and because he wanted to return to Central Earth to study more scriptures in Sanskrit, in the third year of Long Soc (663), he returned to Tu An pagoda in Dong Do. There, he could only translate three sutras such as Entering the Mantra of La Ceremony with Buddha Dharma, A Tra Na Wisdom, etc. The meaning is profound, the writing is skillful.

That year, due to His teachings, the King of Chenla sent famous monks to Central Earth to request:

- Our country has many strange medicines, but only Mr. Na De knows how to find them. Please bestow the honor of Mr. Na De to his native country.

Emperor Cao Tong intended to issue an edict for Mr. Na De to go, but was told by court officials and famous scholars:

- Tripitaka Dharma Master Na De was originally a disciple of Bodhisattva Nagarjuna, so his understanding of the Formless is truly far beyond that of Xuanzang.

The Sanskrit monks of the Western Region also confessed:

- After the Great Master (Bodhisattva Nagarjuna) passed away, Venerable Na De was a profound interpreter of the True Form, reaching the bottom of the source of Hinayana means of the five Bhikkhus and four Vedas of pagans. He was intelligent in language and meaning, words were like pearls, and his voice was like thunder. More than forty volumes of previous Mahayana treatises were about to be translated.

Thousands of years ago, thousands of miles away, he brought the religion to the north but was not well-received, but was taken to the south and encountered blue mountains and miasma, causing him to catch a cold and pass away. What a pity for a dragon statue of the Dharma.

tieu_de: 51. Venerable Nha Na Bat Da La (Jnanabhadra, translated as Wisdom)
tom_tat: He is from the country of Ha Lang and is well-versed in the three classics. During the reign of Lan Duc (664-665), the monk Hoi Ninh in Chengdu wanted to go to Thien...
noi_dung: 51. Venerable Nha Na Bat Da La (Jnanabhadra, translated as Wisdom)He is from the country of Ha Lang and is well-versed in the three classics. During the reign of Lan Duc (664-665), the monk Hoi Ninh in Chengdu, because he wanted to go to Thien Truc to worship the relics, followed a merchant ship to the west. In the middle of the road, the boat is in Ha Lang country. The monk Hoi Ninh and Venerable Nha Na Bat Da La translated the last two volumes of the Nirvana Sutra, from the Agama Sutra. This part talks about the events that happened after the Buddha's funeral ceremony, such as collecting relics, etc., but is not consistent with the translated Nirvana Sutra. After being translated, this sutra was sent to Giao Chau (Vietnam). Giao Chau Admiral Luong Nan Dich asked monk Van Ky to bring this sutra to the capital. Hoi Ninh monks went to Tay Vuc again.

tieu_de: 52. Buddha Da La (Buddhatrata, translated as Enlightenment)
tom_tat: He is from Ke Tan country north of Thien Truc. He vowed to save the people of Chi Na, so he went to Dong Do to spread the Dharma, staying at Bach Ma Pagoda,...
noi_dung: 52. Buddha Da La (Buddhatrata, translated as Enlightenment)He is from Ke Tan country north of Thien Truc. He vowed to save the people of Chi Na, so he went to Dong Do to spread the Dharma, stayed at Bach Ma Pagoda, and translated the Dai Phuong Quang Vien Giac Lieu Nghia Sutra.

tom_tat: He is from Ke Tan country north of Thien Truc. Forgetting his life and life, he devoted himself to religion, went to admire and worship all the holy relics. Listen to Bodhisattva Manjushri...
noi_dung:
53. Buddha Bodhisattva (Buddhapali, translated as Enlightenment)He is from Ke Tan country north of Thien Truc. Forgetting his life and life, he devoted himself to religion, went to admire and worship all the holy relics. Hearing that Bodhisattva Manjushri was hiding in Thanh Luong mountain, regardless of the distance, he traveled all the way to Ngu Dai mountain. During the reign of Emperor Gao Tong, the original year of Nghi Phuong (676), he carried a staff to Ngu Dai mountain, sincerely worshiped, tears fell like buying, longing to see the Bodhisattva's appearance. Moments later, an old man came out of the mountain, speaking in Brahman (ie Sanskrit):

- What do you ask for?

He replied:

- I heard Bodhisattva Manjushri was hidden in this mountain, so I came here from Thien Truc to worship.

- Teacher came from Thien Truc. So do you bring along the Sutra of the Buddha's Name, Venerable Da La Ni? Here, sentient beings create a lot of evil karma. Monastics also violate the precepts a lot. Buddha's birth mantra can secretly help them eliminate their bad karma. If you don't bring this sutra, then coming here will be useless. Even if you meet Bodhisattva Manjushri, you still cannot recognize him. You should go to the Western Regions to request that sutra, hoping to pass it on in this country. That is to obey the teachings of the saints, to often help sentient beings, that is, to directly repay the Buddhas' kindness.

Having finished speaking, the old man disappeared. He bowed even more deeply and immediately returned to Thien Truc. I requested that prayer book and then returned to Dong Do. Emperor Cao Tong saw that he sincerely worshiped that secret sutra, so he invited the monk Dien Khach at Hong Lu pagoda and the Tripitaka shaman Nhat Chieu to come to the capital to collaborate on the translation. After the translation, the king rewarded him with thirty bundles of silk, which he kept at the royal palace. He tearfully told the king:

- I sacrificed my life because I had the will to benefit living beings. Please, Your Majesty, please allow this sutra to be published.

The king saw that he was very sincere, so he returned the scripture in Sanskrit and kept the translated text. Having regained the original Sanskrit text, he happily went to Tay Minh pagoda and together with monk Thuan Trinh (fluent in Sanskrit) offered a petition for translation. As soon as the king approved, he and the monk Thuan Trinh and the monks co-translated it, calling it the Sutra of the Buddha's Name Ton Thang Da La Ni. This translation, in terms of the mantra's mantra, is different from the previous translators (i.e. monks Dien Khach and Nhat Chieu). After translating, he brought the Sanskrit scripture to Ngu Dai, then retreated to Vajrayana cave. Currently, at Vinh Hung Long Thu Vong, the relics of Buddha Da Ba Loi are still worshiped.

In the Dai Lich era (766-779), monk Phap Chieu stayed at Van Phong pagoda at Nam Nhac mountain, went to Ngu Dai mountain, and worshiped in Vajra cave. Just as it was dusk, Phap Chieu suddenly saw a Sanskrit monk seven meters high, speaking clearly in Sanskrit, and calling himself Buddha Da Ba Loi, asking:

- The priest worships hard here, so what do you want?

Phap Chieu said:

- I wish to see Bodhisattva Manjushri.

- If you are sincere and solid, true and not false, then you can step through this wall, and within an inch of your life you will clearly see the Bodhisattva's face.

As soon as Phap Chieu closed his eyes, he entered a deep cave and saw a large courtyard with the words 'Vajra Prajna Pagoda' written on it. These words radiate a brilliant light. That great hall is indescribably solemn and magnificent. Bodhisattva Manjushri's residence is extremely solemn. Bodhisattva spoke words of comfort and poured tea for Phap Chieu to drink. After that, Buddha Da Ba Loi led the Dharma Edict out of the courtyard. Although the Phap Chieu requested to stay in the great monastery, Buddha Da Ba Loi did not promise, but advised that one must make an effort to practice diligently so that when he returns, he can stay in the great monastery. As soon as Phap Chieu stepped outside the wall and turned around, he no longer saw Buddha Da Ba Loi.

tieu_de: 54. Venerable Brahma Dharma (Bhagavaddharma, translated as Religious Dharma)
tom_tat: He is from the West of Thien Truc, crossed the deserts, traveled thousands of miles to Central Earth, wished to propagate Buddhism, focused on the session...
noi_dung: 54. Venerable Brahma Dharma (Bhagavaddharma, translated as Religious Dharma)He is from the West of Thien Truc, crossed the deserts, traveled thousands of miles to Central Earth, wished to propagate Buddhism, and focused on translating the scriptures. In the reign of Vinh Huy (650-655), he translated the Sutra of Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Bodhisattva, Great Perfection, Great Compassion, Dāla Ni.

tom_tat: He is from Do Hoa La country, became a monk at a young age, traveled all over Thien Truc, learned extremely well the sutras, Lang Gia, and Cau Xa. He comes...
noi_dung: 55. Amitabha Son (Mitrasanata, translated as President)He is from Do Hoa La country, became a monk at a young age, traveled all over Thien Truc, learned extremely well the sutras, Lang Gia, and Cau Xa. He came to Dong Do and together with Truc Soa Nanda translated the Mahayana Sutra Entering the Mausoleum. He, together with Venerable Datama Da La Ni, translated the Uncontained Pure Light Sutra. After that, he returned to his homeland.

tieu_de: 56. Amitabha Buddha (Ratnacinta, translated as Bao Tu Duy)
tom_tat: He is from Ca Thap Di La country in the north of Thien Truc. He became a monk at a young age and often practiced meditation. After receiving the full precepts, he dedicated himself to...
noi_dung: 56. Amitabha Buddha (Ratnacinta, translated as Bao Tu Duy)He is from Ca Thap Di La country in the north of Thien Truc. He became a monk at a young age and often practiced meditation. After receiving the full precepts, he specializes in the dharma, has wisdom that surpasses that of others, understands the ultimate and conventional truths, and is well-versed in magical incantations. Because he wanted to convert, he came to Luoyang in 693, and was decreed to reside at Thien Cung Pagoda, and then began translating the sutras. In 706, he translated seven volumes of the Astounding Sutra of the Da La Ni Sutra. From then on, he no longer translated any sutras, but diligently worshiped, read and recited the sutras, and did virtuous deeds. Every day, he used incense water to clean the Buddha statue. He often carried his alms bowl to beg for alms and also gave alms to the poor. At Long Mon Mountain, he built a pagoda in the Tay Vuc style, and called it Thien Truc Pagoda. Disciples often reside in that temple. Due to his sincere and diligent practice, he achieved many miracles. He passed away in 721, at the age of over one hundred years.

tom_tat: He is a person of Thien Truc, widely learned, knowledgeable in all words, pure and full of virtue, clear on the five wisdoms, penetrating...
noi_dung: 57. Atigupta (Atigupta, translated as Extremely High)He is a person of Thien Truc, widely learned, knowledgeable in all words, pure and full of virtue, clear on the five wisdoms, thoroughly understanding the three classics. In the first month of the third year of Vinh Huy (652), from the west of Thien Truc, he brought the Sanskrit scriptures to Chang'an. The king granted him a decree to stay at Tu Minh Pagoda. Twenty-eight monks and famous scholars such as Mahayana, Anh Cong Ly, etc. at Hue Nhat Pagoda, Phu Do Institute, invited him to establish the Da La Ni altar. He complied with the request and performed the dharma. At that time, there were many people in the crowd who had received many strange omens, so the monks and laity in the capital were joyfully praising them. Therefore, the monks asked him to translate that dharma. He drew from the Vajra Mahayana Sutra and translated each volume into a set of twelve volumes, called the Da La Ni Sutra. Monk Huyen Giai took notes.

tieu_de: 58. The Noble Eightfold Tantra (Pramiti, translated as Supreme Being)
tom_tat: He was a native of Thien Truc and had the ambition to sacrifice and save animals, so he traveled everywhere, then gradually moved to Chi Na, then to Guangzhou to live in...
noi_dung: 58. The Noble Eightfold Tantra (Pramiti, translated as Supreme Being)He was a Thien Truc person, had the ambition to sacrifice and save animals depending on fate, so he traveled everywhere, then slowly went to Chi Na, to Guangzhou to stay at Che Chi Pagoda. There, on the twenty-third day of the fifth month of the year of the Divine Dragon (705) of the Tang Dynasty, according to the request of the masses, he drew from the Empowerment series and translated it into a volume, a set of ten volumes, called the Great Buddha's Name, Tathagata Mat Nhan, Cultivation of Liuyi, Ten Thousand Lives of Bodhisattvas, and Shurangama Sutra. The monk Amitabha Shakyamuni (from O Truong) translated the language. Bodhisattva precepts disciple Tien Chanh Nghi, doctor with the middle book, the lower chapter of the chapter Thanh Ha Phong Dung recorded. Monk Hoai Dich at Nam Lau pagoda, Phu Son mountain, in Tuan Chau, verified the translation. The king in central Thien Truc, when he heard that Bat Lat Mat De translated this sutra in Central Earth, became angry (because this sutra was considered a national treasure) and ordered people to search for it. He then brought the original Sanskrit text back to his native country, and for the sake of sentient beings, he committed the crime to the royal court.

tieu_de: 59. He Truly Xa Nanda (Siksamanda, translated as Learning Joy)
tom_tat: He is a native of Vu Dien country in the north of Thong Linh mountain, with extensive intelligence, extraordinary style, mastery of Mahayana and Hinayana scriptures,...
noi_dung:
59. He Truly Xa Nanda (Siksamanda, translated as Learning Joy)He is a native of Vu Dien country in the north of Thong Linh mountain, with extensive intelligence, extraordinary style, mastery of Mahayana and Hinayana scriptures, and fluent in worldly learnings. Thien Hau (Wu Tac Thien) is devoted to Buddhism and promotes righteous teachings. She originally believed in the Mahayana, but the Avatamsaka Sutra had not yet been translated. Hearing that the country of Vu Dien had a Sanskrit text, Thien Hau sent an envoy there to request the monks to translate. Therefore, he brought this sutra to Central Earth. In the reign of the original year of Witnessing Saint (695), at Dai Van Khong pagoda in the Citadel, in the Eastern region, he began to translate. Thien Hau personally came to the court and wrote the preface. Monk Bodhi Liu Chi (a man from Thien Truc) and monk Nghia Tinh recited Sanskrit words together; monks of Phuc Le, Phap Tang, etc. took notes. The Avatamsaka Sutra was translated into eighty volumes and completed in 699. Next, he translated the Mahayana Sutra Entering the Mausoleum in the year 700. Thien Hau also personally wrote the preface. At Thanh Thien pagoda in Kinh Su and Phat Tho Ky pagoda in Dong Do, he translated the Manjushri Tho Ky sutra, etc. In total, he translated nineteen volumes. Monks Ba Lon, Huyen Quy, etc. took notes. Monk Phuc Le edited the text. Monks Phap Bao, Hang Canh, etc. verify the meaning. Crown Prince Trung Xa Co Ung Phuoc is the guardian.

Staying in Truong An for four years, hearing that his mother had just passed away, he submitted a petition to return to his homeland. The royal historian Or Tu Quang took him back to Vu Dien. Emperor Trung Tong, reigning as Canh Long (708), issued a decree to invite him back to the capital. As soon as he arrived at the capital, the king personally went out to welcome him outside the gate of Khai Vien, and sent soldiers to bring a phan bao rosary to receive the procession, and decorated an elephant board, inviting him to enter the citadel and stay at Dai Tien Phuoc pagoda. Unfortunately, before he could continue to promote the translation of the sutras, he fell ill and passed away on the twelfth day of the ninth month, in the original Canh Van year (710), at the age of fifty-nine. The royal court followed the method of Vu Dien to conduct the cremation ceremony. After cremation, the body is completely destroyed, but the tongue remains intact. His disciples offered prayers and asked his tongue to return to Vu Dien and build an offering tower. The next person built a seven-story tower where the body of That Xoa Nanda was placed. Monks and laymen call it the Hoa Nghiem Tripitaka tower.

tom_tat: He is from Thien Truc. He was a prodigy, only eight years old and already mastered the five intelligences. After receiving great precepts, he diligently and strictly...
noi_dung:
60. Divakara (translated as Sunlight)He is from Thien Truc. He was a prodigy, only eight years old and already mastered the five intelligences. After receiving great precepts, he diligently maintained the noble precepts, was profound in learning, and was proficient in spells. During the reign of Emperor Cao Tong (674-683), he went to Central Earth. In May, in the fourth year of Nghi Phuong (679), the court granted him a decree to translate the sutras that had just been brought over. According to the custom in Xuanzang's life, the court allowed him to reside alone in a large temple, and then accompanied five famous monks to translate the scriptures. At the two eastern and western pagodas of Thai Nguyen in the two capitals, he translated sixteen sets of sutras such as Mahayana Manifestation, Mahayana Five Aggregates, etc. Translated by the monk Chien Da Prajna Deba. Monk Hue Tri verified Sanskrit words. The court also bestowed honors on monks of great merit and virtue to assist him in translating. Thien Hau also personally wrote the foreword. He together with the monk Giac Ho translated the Buddha's Birth Sutra. The translation is neat and flexible, the content is meaningful, and the meaning is clear.

Later, he entered naturalization right in the translation room, at the age of seventy-five. Thien Hau ordered troops to carry his coffin to bury it on Huong Son mountain in Long Mon, Lac Duong, and build a tower to make offerings.

tieu_de: 61. Venerable Devaprajna (Devaprajna, translated as Thien Tri)
tom_tat: He is a native of Vu Dien country, well-versed in Mahayana and Hinayana teachings, thoroughly understands the two dharmas of ultimate truth and conventional truth, thoroughly understands meditation and...
noi_dung: 61. Venerable Devaprajna (Devaprajna, translated as Thien Tri)He is a native of Vu Dien country, proficient in Mahayana and Hinayana teachings, thoroughly understands the two dharmas of ultimate truth and conventional truth, and thoroughly understands meditation and mantras. In 689, he arrived in Lac Duong. Thien Hau granted him a residence at the Wei Quoc Dong Tu pagoda to translate the sutras. From that year to 691, he translated six volumes and seven volumes of the Avatamsaka Sutra of the Infinite Dharma Realm. After that, no one knows where he passed away.

tieu_de: 62. Thi La Dharma (Siladharma, translated as Dharma)
tom_tat: He is from Vu Dien and is fluent in Sanskrit and Chinese. He is the Great Dharma Master in Bac Dinh (Dsimsa). During the reign of Trinh Quan...
noi_dung: 62. Thi La Dharma (Siladharma, translated as Dharma)He is from Vu Dien and is fluent in Sanskrit and Chinese. He is the Great Dharma Master in Bac Dinh (Dsimsa). During the reign of Trinh Quan (627-649), Wukong, on his way back from Thien Truc, stopped by Bac Dinh, where Long Hung pagoda was, to request Dharma, and asked him to become the Master of Teachings. He translated the Ten Grounds Sutra and the Wheel of Prayer Sutra. Monk Phap Nhuoc read and translated. Dharma Super beauty. Monk Thien Tin verified the meaning. Wukong verified the Sanskrit text.

tom_tat: He is from Ma Lai Da country in the south of Thien Truc. That kingdom is near Bo Da Lac Tien mountain (where the Quan Am palace is located). The father belongs to...
noi_dung:
63. Vajrabodhi (Vajrabodhi, translated as Vajra Wisdom)He is from Ma Lai Da country in the south of Thien Truc. That kingdom is near Bo Da Lac Tien mountain (where the Quan Am palace is located). The father was originally from the Brahman lineage, was proficient in the Five Insights, and was the teacher of King Kien Chi.

Just a few years after he was born, Venerable Bat Nhat La Bodhi recited tens of thousands of words in one day. Concentrate and sincerely read the sutras all the time without getting tired. At the age of sixteen, he was enlightened to the Buddha's teachings, but did not like the Ni Kien Tu treatises. Not long after, he became a monk and practiced diligently day and night. Later, he followed his original teacher to Na Lan Da monastery, studying sutras such as Asura Abhidharma, Madhyamika, Only Consciousness, etc. He mastered the precepts, thoroughly understanding the eighteen codes of law. He came to the west of Thien Truc to study the Hinayana sutras and the Dharma Yoga Sutra. He went to the south of Thien Truc to follow Mr. Long Tri to study the Vajra Avalokiteshvara System (belonging to Tantric thought) for seven years. More than ten years later, he completely mastered the three canonical collections. He also went to worship all the relics. Next, he went to the Lion country, climbed Lang Gia mountain, and then passed through more than twenty countries in the east. When he arrived at Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara's holy land at Pho Da Lac mountain in southern Thien Truc, and saw the Bodhisattva appearing majestically, he suddenly vowed to spread Buddhism in Chi Na country. Furthermore, hearing that Buddhism was flourishing in Chi Na, he followed a merchant ship to Guangzhou in the year 719. When Emperor Huyen Tong heard the news, he issued a decree inviting him to stay at Tu An pagoda. At Tien Phuoc Pagoda, he built the Dai Manh Noa La Quan Danh altar to save the four disciples. The two Zen masters Dai Tri and Dai Hue, along with the Tripitaka Bat Khong, jointly worshiped him as their teacher.

Later, the king invited him to Luoyang. During that year, from January to May, there was drought everywhere. The king set up an altar to pray for rain but it didn't work. Therefore, the king invited him to set up a rosary to pray for rain, and ordered Zen master Nhat Hanh to closely guard him. He used the dharma of Bodhisattva Bat Khong Cau Y and set up an altar right at the temple. He also made a statue of Bodhisattva That Cau Chi made of silk, four elbows long. By Saturday morning, the sky was still cloudless, and the climate was still hot and muggy. After noon, suddenly the wind blew from the northwest, then clouds rolled in, and rain poured down heavily. That day, there were tens of thousands of people coming to the altar. People near and far are amazed at the magical effect of the rosary praying for rain. The monks all said to each other:

- Mr. Kim Cang Tri has captured the dragon.

At that time, the king often paid attention to mysterious principles and not to the method of no door. Hearing the scandal, the king ordered the foreign monks of the Phien tribe to return to their native country. The attendant heard this news and returned to the temple to tell him. He said:

- I am a Sanskrit monk, not a Phien monk. The decree is not clear, so I won't go!

A few days later, at Nhan Mon, he suddenly delivered a farewell note to the king. The king was horrified and immediately issued an edict to keep him there.

The twenty-fifth princess, Tam Chung, was very loved by the king, but had been sick for a long time and no one could cure her, so she lay in Ham Nghi's house all day long. She kept her eyes closed, and didn't say a word for weeks. Before that, she requested him to give the precepts. You know she must die. However, the king insisted on asking Him to save her life. He then chose two seven-year-old maids, blindfolded them with silk, and let them lie down on the ground. Next, he told Niu Tien Dong to draw an amulet, then burn it right where Princess Tam Chung was lying. Next, he recited the mantra. At that time, the two maids read after Him without making a single mistake. He then entered samadhi (samadhi), and used his incomprehensible divine power to order two maids to bring an edict to King Diem Ma. In a moment, Princess Tam Chung woke up, opened her eyes and spoke as usual. When the king heard the news, he immediately rode his horse to the inn alone. Princess Tam Chung confessed:

- Karma is difficult to transfer. Today, King Diem Ma sent me back to see the face of the saint again.

Having finished speaking, around noon, he passed away. From then on, the king began to worship the Three Jewels.

In the six palaces, the king was very gracious and loved Vo Quy Phi like a pearl. He advised Ms. Vo Quy Phi to quickly create a statue of Bodhisattva Vajra Longevity. He advised the district in Ha Dong to make a silk Buddha statue and place it inside the Vairocana Buddha tower. He told his disciples:

- The lifespan of these two people is not long.

A few months later, it was exactly as He predicted. He often spoke prophecies like that a lot, and they all came true.

He is knowledgeable in reason, knowledgeable in the scriptures, precepts, and mantras. If anyone asked anything, He would explain clearly. Whoever he meets, he will never forget. The favorable and unfavorable scenes, happiness, sadness, anger, and love did not disturb His mind, making everyone respect and admire him. He often followed the Dharma formula to set up the mandala (or mandala) ashram, and it was all inspiring.

Monk Nhat Hanh admired his teachings and received initiation.

For the sake of profit, and according to the king's decree in 723, at Tu Thanh pagoda, he translated two books of Vajra-Dhatuji Compendium of Reciting and Chanting the Dharma (belonging to the Vajra system of Esoteric Buddhism), and two books of That Cu Chi Da La Ni. At Dai Tien Phuoc Pagoda in the year 730, he translated a book called Manjusri That Benefits Five Self-Minds Dharani Avalokiteshvara Yoga Essentials. Translated by monk Tri Tang. Monk Nhat Hanh copied and polished it into writing. Seeing that there were many shortcomings in this book, He added them to make them complete. The seals of general maintenance contracts translated by Him are all effective. Thanks to him, the secret mantra was spread everywhere, causing many people to be saved.

In August 732, at Quang Phuoc Pagoda in Luoyang, he told his disciples:

- When the moon is full, I will pass away.

Having finished speaking, he went to worship the statue of Vairocana Buddha, circumambulating it three times. Returning to his monastery, he offered incense and made a vow, respectfully entrusted to his disciples the newly translated teachings, then peacefully passed away, at the age of seventy-one years old, and fifty-one years old. On the seventh day of the eleventh month of that year, his followers buried his body at Long Mon in Nam Y, and set up a worship tower. He was given the title of national teacher Sac Thuy by the king. The disciple received the Dharma as Non-emptiness.

tieu_de: 64. Tipiṭaka Dharma Master Amu Kubattāra (Amonghavajra, translated as Vajra of No Emptiness)
tom_tat: He originally belonged to the Brahmin lineage in northern Thien Truc. When he was young, he followed his uncle to Quang Dong country. At the age of fifteen, he studied Buddhism...
noi_dung:
64. Tipiṭaka Dharma Master Amu Kubattāra (Amonghavajra, translated as Vajra of No Emptiness)He originally belonged to the Brahmin lineage in northern Thien Truc. When he was young, he followed his uncle to Quang Dong country. At the age of fifteen, he studied with Venerable Bat Nhat La Bodhi (Vajra Wisdom). At first, he studied the Siddhartha Chapter and the Thanh Minh treatise in Sanskrit. In just a few weeks, he achieved complete enlightenment, surprising Bat Nhat La Bodhi. Later, he received the Bodhisattva precepts, then was introduced to the Vajra Precepts of Mahamandala, achieving many spiritual inspirations, so Venerable Bat Nhat La Bodhi knew that Bat Nhat La Bodhi would later prosper the teachings.

After receiving full ordination, he mastered Sarvāstivāda doctrine and knew many languages ​​fluently. He often translated scriptures with his master. For three consecutive years, Bat-Kong requested to study Tan Yoga Five Triads of Dharma, but Bat-sati-La Bodhi still did not accept. Therefore, Mr. Bat Khong intended to return to Thien Truc. One night, Bat Nhat La Bodhi dreamed that the Buddha and Bodhisattva statues in the temples in the capital were all flying to the east. Waking up, Bodhidharma knew that Bat-Kong was a true Dharma weapon, so he accepted the old request, then transmitted the five sets of Ho Ma A Xa Le Empowerment methods along with the Vairocana Sutra, and the To Tat Dia rules. Later, Bat Nhat La Bo De went to Luoyang, so Bat Khong also followed as an attendant. When Bodhisattva Bat Nhat La Bodhi passed away in the twentieth year of Khai Nguyen (732), Bat Khong established a Photo Hall to commemorate him. Next, Mr. Bat Khong sent royal honors to Ngu Thien Truc (East Thien Truc, Tay Thien Truc, Nam Thien Truc, Bac Thien Truc, Trung Thien Truc), and the Lion country. When he arrived at Nam Hai district, the governor Liu Cu Lan urgently requested him to give the initiation. At Phap Tanh Pagoda, he helped hundreds of thousands of people. Because of his sincerity, he felt the presence of Bodhisattva Manjushri.

In the twelfth month of the twenty-ninth year of Khai Nguyen (741), from Kunlun, he boarded a boat and left Nam Hai. The boat arrived at Ha Lang country when it encountered a hurricane. The merchants were scared, so they followed local customs and prayed, but it was ineffective. Therefore, they knelt down and begged for help. He said:

- Now I have the dharma. Don't worry.

Having finished speaking, in his right hand he held the Five Thai Bodhi Mind pestle, and in his left hand he held the Prajnaparamita Sutra, then chanted the sutra once. Immediately the wind stopped and the sea calmed down. Later, a whale appeared, its head as big as a mountain. Merchants entrust karma. He also practiced the Dharma and chanted sutras as before, and told his disciples to chant the Sutra of Ba Kiet Long Vuong. After a while, all troubles were eliminated. Later, the boat arrived at the Lion country. The king sent messengers to welcome him and sent bodyguards to serve on both sides of the road. As soon as he saw him, the king bowed his head and paid homage, then invited him to the royal palace and made offerings for seven days. Every day, the king filled a golden chest with agarwood water and then personally bathed him. The queen, crown prince, concubines, ministers, and mandarins all respectfully worshiped Him as their king.

As soon as he saw Samantabhadra Samantabhadra, Bat Khong offered silk and brocade cloth, and invited him to open and establish the eighteen Dharma altars of Vajra Empowerment Yogācā and the Vairocana Bodhisattva Pitaka. Mr. Bat Khong also sought to learn more from Mr. Wu Chang about the secret teachings, along with more than five hundred volumes of sutras, Original Samadhi, secret seals of the venerable monks, dharma formations, images, flags, literature, nature, etc.

One day, the king organized a festival to tame elephants. People watching filled the entire palace. He stood in the middle of the crossroads, chanting mantras, shaking hands, and entering concentration. The elephants were running madly and suddenly fell down.

Second, he traveled to the Five Heavens. In 746, he returned to the capital Dong Do. At court, he offered gifts sent by King Thi La Me Gia Bieu of the Lion Kingdom such as gold, silver, lapis lazuli, jewels, Prajnaparamita sutras, etc. Next, he wore a crown and entered the inner court to perform the initiation ceremony for the king. Later, he moved to Tinh Anh pagoda. At that time, it was sunny all summer. The king then ordered him to pray for rain:

- If you can't pray, don't meet me.

He then followed the edict and established the Confucius King altar. In less than three days, the rain poured down everywhere, making the king very happy. He personally brought a treasure chest, a purple-yellow robe, and two hundred bundles of silk to offer to him.

One time, a hurricane suddenly blew. The king again called on Him to stop the wind. He took a silver vase and an apple to perform blessings. In an instant the wind stopped. Suddenly, a goose ran forward, knocking over the silver water bottle, causing the wind to blow even more violently than before. He blessed the mantra again, causing the wind to stop again. The king saw that and gave him the title: "Tri Tang."

He intended to return to his native country, so he rode a horse to Nam Hai district in 749. There, because he received an edict, he had to stay, and then had to go to Ha Lung. In the year 753, at the request of the monk Ca Thu Han, he came to stay at Khai Nguyen Pagoda in Vo Tru. Bodhisattva Tan Tung prayed for empowerment. Thousands of monks all took the throne to receive Dharma. Disciples Ham Quang, etc. also received five sets of empowerments. Opening the Ly Hoan Tong palace, he received the Vajra Precepts Great Mandala Dharma. That day, the land where the ashram was established suddenly had an earthquake. He said:

- This is due to the sincerity of the believers.

Later, he returned to the capital and stayed at Dai Hung Thien pagoda. Next, in the year 756, the king announced the price at Linh Vo Phuong Tuong. He also followed the secret mantra. Tang Tuc Tong also secretly sent messengers to seek secret dharma. In the reign of Can Nguyen (758-759), the king invited him to the palace and established the Ho Ma Phap ashram. He imparted the Seven Jewels Empowerment to the king. In 760, the king fell ill. He then blessed the mantra to eliminate the seven misfortunes. A few days later, the illness completely healed, making the king admire and respect him even more. Later, he submitted a request to enter the mountain as a hermitage. The king granted him permission to enter Chung Nam Son mountain and stay at Tri Cu pagoda. There, day and night he cultivated merit, chanted mantras, and was moved by Bodhisattva Great Bliss to manifest himself and radiate light and witness. He said to himself:

- Sentient beings have not yet been saved, but I have already saved myself.

Tang Tuc Tong ceded the throne to Tang Dai Tong. After ascending the throne, Tang Dai Tong revered him even more deeply. He had just finished translating the two volumes of the Secret Sutra and Nhan Vuong, so the king wrote the preface. On the day these two sutras were released, auspicious clouds appeared, causing the whole court to congratulate him.

In the third Dai Lich era (768), at Dai Hung Thien pagoda, he set up an altar to practice dharma. The king also offered many offerings such as phan bao cai, and alms to male monks for twenty-seven days, issued a decree forbidding court officials from using soldiers, and then entered the altar to receive empowerment.

In the summer of the fifth Dai Lich year (770), the king issued an edict inviting him to Ngu Dai mountain to do Buddhist work. At that time, a comet appeared. As soon as the magic was finished, the comet also disappeared. In the fall, from Ngu Dai, he returned to the capital. The king personally rode a white horse to the city gate to welcome him.

Later, he submitted a request to translate the scriptures. Ten great monks also came to support. By the sixth Dai Lich era (771), in total he had translated one hundred twenty books and seventy sets of sutras. The king gave gifts again.

At that time, in the capital, both spring and summer were suffering from drought. Tang Dai Tong wrote an edict and sent it to him, saying:

- If it rains within three days, then it is the Venerable's miraculous magical power. If after three days there is no rain, then the Venerable Master has no magical power at all.

Serving the decree, he set up an altar to pray for rain. By the second day, it was pouring rain. The king then offered the golden robe, and gave his disciples the seven-element robe (seven pieces of robe), and set up offerings for male monks for a thousand monks, to repay him for his merits. He requested the king to build a pavilion to worship Bodhisattva Manjushri. The king immediately agreed, and spent money from the royal treasury to build it. He again translated the King's Tea King's Sutra.

In the ninth year of the Great Calendar (774), from spring to summer, he praised the wonderful Dharma and admonished his disciples. He often preached and expounded the Samantabhadra Sutra, Praying for Boundless Birth, and also advised his followers to recite and recite that sutra.

One night, he told his disciple Trieu Tuyen to bring a pen and ink, then said:

- Now I briefly write about the nirvana cremation ritual to set a framework for the next life.

After finishing writing, he gave it to Trieu Tuyen so that he could follow it and prepare for burial at the time of his death. Trieu Tuyen then bowed his head and prayed three times:

- Please be compassionate and stay in this world for a long time. On the contrary, sentient beings know who to rely on!

He just smiled. Not long after, he became ill and offered his farewell prayer. The king immediately sent an envoy to bring medicine, and also gave him the position of Qi Quoc Cong, along with three thousand food hamlets. He did not accept it, and was not pleased, saying:

- The saints give up their bodies like they stretch out their arms. When the moon is full I will pass away. When you are about to die, why are you still thinking about fame and fortune?

On the full moon day of the sixth month, he took a bath in incense water, then lay down on the bed, placed his head to the east, face to the north, entered the great mudra samadhi and passed away, at the age of seventy, with fifty monks. The disciple who followed the Dharma was Hue Lang. The king then stayed in court for three days, gave alms, and built a worship tower. Before he entered nirvana, monks often dreamed of Manjushri Bodhisattva's collapse; Vajra mace flew up into the sky. The lake behind Dai Hung Thien Pagoda suddenly dried up. The flowers in Truc Lam Bao Dinh garden are all withered.

On the sixth day of the seventh month, the cremation ceremony is held. The king bestowed the Dharma title of Great Bodhisattva and Perfect Wisdom of the Tripitaka. After the cremation, he collected hundreds of relics. In eighty seeds, the core is still intact. In it there is a color particle that is half hidden and half visible. The king decreed the establishment of a tower to worship relics at the temple.

Throughout his life of propagating the Dharma, Mr. Bat Khong always worked to benefit living beings and things. His Dharma teachings are so profound that no one can measure their depth.

In the past, Duong Huyen Tong respected him very much. One year, there was a drought and the king summoned him to pray for rain. He said that after another day, you can pray for rain. If you keep forcing yourself to pray, the rain will cause many troubles. The king again issued a decree inviting his original teacher (that is, Bat Nhat La Bodhi) to set up an altar to pray for rain. Sure enough, the wind and rain did not stop. The streets were flooded and many trees fell. The king again called on Him to stop the rain. He then recited the mantra in Sanskrit. For a moment it stopped raining.

At Bac Mang mountain there is a magical snake. Every evening often blows fog. One time, He passed by there. Seeing Him coming, the snake god appeared and said:

- The disciple is receiving evil retribution. I wonder if the Venerable Master can save him? I often want to make the river flood Luoyang city for fun!

He then preached the three refuges and five precepts and the principle of cause and effect to the snake god, saying:

- Because of your anger, you must receive this retribution. Now that I'm starting to feel resentment again, I don't have any dharma power to save me. If you follow My teachings, you will be able to give up your snake body.

Later, surrounding villagers saw the carcass of a large dragon, the foul smell wafting up for several miles.

One time, during the reign of Thien Bao, Tay Phien general Dai Thach Khang raised an army to besiege Tay Luong. The King summoned Him to ask for help. He then set up an altar, offered incense, and recited the Human King Secret Mantra twenty-seven times. The king saw about five hundred soldiers in the palace, so he was horrified and asked questions. He replied:

- Thien Vuong Bhikkhu led the army to save An Tay. Please, Your Majesty, please quickly set up the food offering ceremony.

The next day, thirty miles northeast of the city, in the fog saw a majestic and majestic soldier carrying spears, causing the mountains to quake. Seeing this, the soldiers were horrified and frightened. In the Phien soldiers' barracks, there were many yellow rats. The crossbow strings were all bitten off by them. On the pavilion of the northern city gate, Quang Minh Thien Vuong appeared, his eyes raised in anger, causing the Phien soldiers to flee in panic. After the enemy was defeated, the king issued a decree to thank him. From then on, the king ordered a statue of the heavenly king to be painted and placed on the castles of the city gates on all four sides.

Through three generations of kings, he was always respected and respected by them for his outstanding achievements.

tieu_de: 65. Tipiṭaka the Dharma Master Vāyāt La Tang Ha (Subhakarasimha, translated as Fearless Goodness)
tom_tat: He was originally from Central India, and was a descendant of King Cam Lo Phan Vuong, (father of Shakyamuni Buddha). His famous Sanskrit Dharma is...
noi_dung:
65. Tipiṭaka the Dharma Master Vāyāt La Tang Ha (Subhakarasimha, translated as Fearless Goodness)He was originally from Central India, and was a descendant of King Cam Lo Phan Vuong, (father of Shakyamuni Buddha). His famous Sanskrit Dharma is Thu Ba Yet La Tang Ha; The Chinese name is Tinh Su Tu, and the translation is Thien Vo Uy. He is also known as Du Ba Ca La, translated as Fearless. His father was originally the king of Trung Thien Truc. Martial arts are virtuous and complete. At the age of ten, he commanded three armies. At the age of thirteen, he ascended the throne and was admired by his ministers and people. Because His brothers were jealous, they started a rebellion. After quelling the rebellion, he ceded the throne to his brother to become a monk. When he arrived at the South China Sea, he met the monk Thu Thang Chieu De, who taught him the way to practice and attain samadhi, then used sand to build a tower of ten thousand.

He followed a merchant ship to travel around the world. He practiced meditation in secret. The mouth often chants sutras emitting bright white light. In three days, even though there was no wind, the boat traveled tens of thousands of miles. One day, a merchant ship suddenly encountered pirates. He then silently recited the mantra. Bodhisattva That Cu Chi appeared in full form, causing the robbers to abandon their teachings and take refuge.

His natural nature is intelligent and enlightened, his intelligence is outstanding, and he deeply understands the principles of the five teachings and three studies; Willow reaches the Dharma of total retention and meditation to the source; adept at the art of magic.

First, he went to Na Lan Da monastery (called Thi Vo Yem). This monastery is the meeting place of saints and monks. In the temple, there was Elder Dat Ma Cuc Da, who often meditated in secret and received secret seals from Tathagata, who was a disciple of Bodhisattva Nagarjuna. Elder Dat Ma Cuc Da's appearance appeared to be only forty years old, but in reality he was eight hundred years old. Tripitaka Master Xuanzang once met him.

Mr. Thien Vo Uy then bowed his head in respect and was honored as his original teacher. Later, Elder Dat Ma Cuc Da transmitted to Thien Fearless the Dharma of General Yogacara Samantabhadra. At that time, dragon gods were flying and crowded before our eyes. In an instant, Venerable Thien agreed to receive all the secret seals. That day, he received empowerment and became a teacher of gods and humans, that is, he was called a Tripitaka Dharma Master. The meaning of the Tripitaka is to enter the precepts and wisdom within; Outwardly, he thoroughly understands the three canonical sutras, and uses the dharani to summarize them all. Da La Ni is the Bodhisattva wheel and the auspicious ocean of liberation. Three generations of Buddhas were born in this method, and it is said that the torch of wisdom shines. Because the nature of living beings is different, the torch of wisdom is also immeasurable. Therefore, the Buddha has hundreds of billions of motes of Samadhi. The Bodhisattvas took refuge in the samadhis and immediately ascended to the level of dignity and entered the ocean of great enlightenment.

At that time, Mr. Thien Vo Uy went to admire and worship the holy relics, without caring about the hardships and dangers. At each place, he visited the relics three times. He again went to Mount Ketu, shaved the hair of Venerable Ma Ha Kasyapa, and received empowerment from Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. He often resides during the summer on Linh Thuu Mountain. Tigers often come to seek enlightenment from Him. He went deeper into the mountain cave and saw the shadow of Shakyamuni Buddha and his two attendants, as if they were still alive.

At that time, the country of Trung Thien Truc was suffering from drought, so the king asked him to pray for rain. When he set up the altar, the crowd saw Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara appearing in the bright sky, holding a vase in his hand and pouring water down, causing heavy rain to pour down. When the crowd saw this, they were all happy and achieved unprecedented results.

In Five Heavens, after Buddha passed away, pagans emerged. Ninety-six wrong views are said to follow each other. Depending on their views and attachments, he cleared away their doubts and errors, causing them to open their evil minds, let go of their delusions, and follow the path of enlightenment. The clouds of Mahayana and Hinayana dharma permeate. Samadhi water is square and round as a dharma weapon. Knock down heresy and raise the flag of Dharma. Establishing a superior mind-king ashram, causing their crazy minds to stop, and personally bowing to the Buddha.

One time, the Elder Dat Ma Cuc Da told Venerable Thien:

- Hey Thien Nam Tu! You have a good relationship with Chan Dan country. Go over there and educate sentient beings.

Listening to his master's instructions, Mr. Thien Vo Uy said goodbye and departed. One day, encountering a river in Ca Low Di La, without a bridge, he skimmed across the water to cross the river. Another time, a rich man invited him to his house to eat dinner. At the same time, that rich man also invited an Arhat to have dinner with him. As soon as he met him, the Arhat said:

- I am a follower of the Hinayana teachings, and the Venerable has achieved Bodhisattva status.

Therefore, the Arhat gave up the main seat to Him. After eating the mussels, the Arhat then flew into space and disappeared.

When he came to Wu Truong, he often preached the Pi Lo dharma in the Dot Quyet palace; peacefully meditate under the trees. On the way, He met robbers. They were slashed three times by their swords but were not harmed. The knife cut into His body as if touching bronze and iron. Previously, when he saw the towering Snow Mountain, he did not want to cross it. Elder Dat Ma Cuc Da flew from nowhere and said:

- Bodhisattva's body is similar to the world, but does not let go of birth and death. You've been gone for a long time, so is your body sick?

Having finished speaking, Elder Dat Ma Cuc Da then flew into the sky and disappeared. So He moved forward, without any hesitation. On the way, he passed through the country of Tibet (Tibet), and was accompanied by merchants. He again encountered robbers blocking the way, so he secretly took the seal, forcing them to bow their heads and apologize. That night, approaching the border of Central Earth, the god appeared and said:

- This is the eastern border, not within the scope of discipleship, but is the land of Dong Do protected by Bodhisattva Manjushri.

Having finished speaking, the deity bowed and then disappeared. That is the god Kapila, who used to protect him.

He used camels to carry the scriptures to Tay Chau. As soon as he reached a river bank, the dragon god pulled the camel's legs into the water. He also entered the dragon palace for three consecutive days, preaching Dharma to educate and enlighten the water tribe. After that, he led the camel back to the river bank, but the scriptures were not wet at all.

In the past, he was traveling in Bac Thien Truc, and his virtue spread to Central Earth. Era name: Khai Nguyen Nguyen (713) Duong Huyen Tong dreamed of conversing with a true monk, his appearance was extremely majestic.

In the fourth year of Khai Nguyen (716), at the age of eighty, he brought the Sanskrit scriptures to Chang'an. It was in accordance with the good dream, so the king was very happy to decorate the ashram for him to reside in, and honored him as a teacher. The princes also bowed their heads in respect. The king granted him a decree to reside in the southern monastery at Dai Hung Thien pagoda, then invited him to go to Tay Minh pagoda. The king himself came to greet him and was extremely respectful. At Thien Cung, the king invited him to sit on a high throne, then prostrated and proclaimed him a national teacher. He then taught the king about Tathagata's teachings. From then on, the majestic method flourished extremely.

At that time, there was a magician who could command ghosts and spirits and do many transformations. He wanted to enter the royal palace to compete in magic. He still sat motionless, but the wizard's arms and legs could not move, so he had to retreat.

Next year, in accordance with the edict, he began translating the sutras at the Bodhi Institute, and submitted a petition to invite famous monks to review the Chinese translation. Initially, he translated a book called Void Store Seeking Dharma. Translated by monk Siddhartha. Vo Truoc took notes, then brought them to the inner palace. The king looked very happy and praised him.

In the past, the monk Vo Hanh went to Tay Vuc and Thien Truc to study the languages ​​of those places, translate the scriptures, and then return. Unfortunately, Vo Hanh passed away in the north of Thien Truc. Vo Hanh's translations were brought back and placed at Hoa Nghiem Pagoda. Venerable Thien Thien and Zen Master Nhat Hanh selected a few books belonging to the general Buddhist teachings, which have not yet been translated.

In the twelfth year of Khai Nguyen (724), he came to stay at Phuoc Tien pagoda in Lac Duong, then translated the Sutra book Ty Lo Gia Na. This sutra has one hundred thousand chants. He also translated seven volumes of the Maha-Bhikkhu Vairocana Buddha Sutra of Divine Power and Transformation of Blessings (or Mahavairocana Sutra, belonging to the Taigarbha Precepts system of Esoteric Buddhism). Translated by monk Bao Nguyet. Zen Master Nhat Hanh took notes and edited. The translation is appropriate, wonderful and profound; The above is in accordance with Buddha's will, the bottom is in accordance with the fate of living beings, making the benefits universal everywhere. He also translated three volumes of the To Ba Ho Dong Tu Sutra, and three volumes of the To Tat Dia Yet La Sutra. These two sutras are full of the mantras of Vinaya, or the Secret Mantra of the Forbidden World. People who have not yet entered the Mandala La cannot recite them, just like people who have not fully received the precepts cannot listen to monks reciting the precepts. The Sutra of Void Store Bodhisattva's Fulfillment of the Supreme Vows to Win the Mind of Dārani Praying for Dharma-Treatment is a small part of the book Vajra Sutra to Achieve the Complete Path.

By nature, he likes quiet and peaceful places. At that time, he opened the method of meditation and encouraged beginners. At that time, Zen Master Nhat Hanh was a sage, penetrating the wisdom of concentration, understanding the wonderful principles of yin and yang, and was respected by kings and mandarins. However, because there were still doubts, Nhat Hanh often came to ask Thien Vo Uy for advice. At his monastery, he often cast bronze towers, more sophisticated than the heavens and humans, to serve as models for future generations. The masses in the temple also imitated him and cast the tower. One time, a big wind blew, causing the fire to spread. He told the crowd not to be afraid. Sure enough, in a moment, snow fell, causing the fire to go out, and a flower suddenly appeared in the tower. The crowd were all happy and praised.

Another time, when there was a drought, the king sent messengers to ask him to pray for rain. He said:

- Nowadays, there is a drought, of course. If you continue to force it and pray for the dragon to spray rain, you will be hit by storms and floods, causing self-destruction.

The king kept pleading, saying:

- People are sick and suffering because of the drought. Having wind and lightning (lightning) is pleasant enough.

He couldn't refuse forever, so he had to build an altar to pray for rain. When the military officer brought out the rosary and conch, he said that it was not enough to pray for rain. He then took a bowl of water, used a small knife to stir inside, and recited hundreds of mantras in Sanskrit. In an instant, there was a red dragon with a red body, as long as a finger, swimming and diving at the bottom of the bowl of water. He again stirred the water and chanted the mantra. A moment later, a white smoke rose from the bowl of water, flew dozens of meters high and then disappeared. He told the bodyguards:

- Let's go quickly. Rain will fall!

The bodyguards had just left, then turned their heads and looked back, seeing the white smoke suddenly fly back to dance on the roof of the lecture hall, then a gust of wind blew, accompanied by an explosion of thunder. The bodyguards had just returned to Thien Tan Bridge when the rain poured in and followed the horse's hooves. Trees on both sides of the road were blown down by the wind. The bodyguards entered the court to complain, but their clothes were covered in mud. The king trusted Him even more.

Once, there was a dragon that lived on a mountain. He came there, saw it, and shouted:

- Quickly go to Lac Duong city!

Having finished speaking, he recited the mantra several hundred times. A few days later, the dragonfly died. That was an omen of An Loc Son chaos. One day, he visited lawyer Dao Tuyen. As soon as Dao Tuyen saw him, he felt disdain. At night, cockroaches and bugs crawled into Dao Tuyen's room door. Venerable Thien then repeatedly shouted:

- The lawyer's servant killed the Buddhists.

Only then did Dao Tuyen know that he was an incarnate Bodhisattva, so he put on the saffron robe and solemnly worshiped and repented.

In the twentieth year of Khai Nguyen (732), he submitted a request to return to Thien Truc, but the king refused. On the seventh day of the tenth month, the twenty-third year of Khai Nguyen (735), he became naturalized citizen, lived ninety-nine years old, and received eighty monks. Clergy throughout the country are sad and regretful. New Lawyer took charge of the burial. Three days later, the monks buried his body at Quang Hoa pagoda in Long Mon on Tay Son mountain. Due to the power of concentration and wisdom, his whole body did not deteriorate. On the day of his body's burial ceremony, the sky and earth were gloomy and sad, the mountains all changed color. Dharma successor disciples are Zen master Bao Uy, Zen master Hue Uy, etc.

tom_tat: He is from Ca Tat Thi country in the north of Thien Truc, his customary name is Kieu Dap Ma De. At the age of seven, he had the intention to leave his parents and take refuge in Tam...
noi_dung:
66. Prajnaparamita (Wisdom)He is from Ca Tat Thi country in the north of Thien Truc, his customary name is Kieu Dap Ma De. At the age of seven, he had the intention to leave his parents and take refuge in the Three Jewels. At that time, he often followed the monks' teachings and studied one hundred thousand verses of the four Agama sutras, and thirty thousand verses of the Abhidharma sutra. When he reached adulthood, he followed his master to another country to receive full ordination. At that time, he recited nearly forty thousand verses of the Tat Ba Da series, and twenty-seven thousand verses of the Cau Xa series. He recited the Mahabharata again and understood its meaning. For seven years, he stayed there to specialize in studying Hinayana teachings, then went to Na Lan Da monastery in central Thien Truc. There, he studied the sutras of Mahayana teachings such as Only Consciousness, Yogācāra, Vajra, Prajna, Vinaya, and the Five Insights. He only studied under three great contemporary commentators such as Tri Ho, Tien Huu, and Tri Huu. Later, he came to worship the Song Lam forest, where the Buddha entered nirvana, and the eight large stupas worshiping the Buddha's relics. For eighteen years, he often went back and forth to admire and worship the relics.

Hearing the voice of a famous master in southern Thien Truc, he went there to learn the Dharma. There was an empowerment master named Dat Ma Da Xa. As soon as he saw Prajnaparamita, Venerable Dama Da Xa knew that this was a Dharma weapon, so he taught the Yogacara Sutra of the Dharma of Entering the Mantra of La Matita to Protect the Body of the Five Seals. In one year, he memorized three thousand five hundred verses. Hearing that Bodhisattva Manjushri was living in the country of Chi Na, he held up a staff and headed east to spread the Dharma. So, he followed the boat to Dong Do. As soon as the boat entered the border of Guangzhou, the wind blew it back to the east of Lion country. He boarded a big boat again and traveled around the countries in the South China Sea. As soon as he entered the coastal area of ​​Guangdong province, a storm blew in, causing the boat to break and everyone to die, leaving only him alive. By the evening of the fifth watch, the wind was calm. At that time, the scriptures that he brought with him were also lost. When he waded ashore, he saw scriptures scattered on the beach. Therefore, he took a bamboo tree and searched for sutras in the sand of the sea. He said to himself:

- Probably the nature of the Chi Na people is not yet mature enough to receive this Mahayana teachings.

He then brought the scriptures and walked for half a month until he arrived in Guangzhou. At that time, it was during the reign of King Duc Tong.

In the eighth year of Trinh Nguyen (792), the king issued a decree allowing him to enter the capital and begin translating the scriptures. At that time, famous monks also gathered to accompany the translation. The monk Prajna (from Ke Tan country), recites Sanskrit scriptures. The monks at Quang Trach Pagoda translated. Monk Vien Chieu at Tay Minh pagoda took notes.

During the years he stayed there, he always participated in translating the scriptures. The writing was so fluent that the king also had to order the writing of prefaces for the sutras that he had just finished translating.

Later, he passed away in Lac Duong. The grave is buried in Tay Vong of Long Mon. The tower still exists today.

tom_tat: He is from Thien Truc. In 784, the monk went to visit Emperor Duc Tong and asked for a bell to bring back to Thien Truc to make...
noi_dung: 67. Lord LotusHe is from Thien Truc. In 784, he gathered a staff to visit Tang Duc Tong and asked for a bell to bring back to Thien Truc to do Buddhist work. The king bestowed a decree for the warlord Ly Phuc in Guangzhou to cast bronze bells. After casting, the king ordered people to bring it to the south of Thien Truc to keep it at Kim Doi Pagoda. He brought this bell to the kingdom of Bao Quan (Ratnasena), and placed it in the Vairocana tower. Later, he brought the last part of the Avatamsaka Sutra to the capital.
