The Tripitaka by Master Bat Nha at Sung Phuoc Pagoda translated it into forty volumes.

tieu_de: 68. Venerable Muni That Loi (Munisri, translated as Tich Mac)
tom_tat: He is from the north of Thien Truc and became a monk at Na Lan Da monastery. In 793, he started from Na Lan Da monastery, then went to Truong An in...
noi_dung: 68. Venerable Muni That Loi (Munisri, translated as Tich Mac)He is from the north of Thien Truc and became a monk at Na Lan Da monastery. In 793, he set out from Na Lan Da monastery, then arrived at Truong An in 800. After that, he was granted a decree by the king to stay at Tu An pagoda, and together with the Tripitaka Dharma Master Bat Nha, translated ten volumes of National Guardian Da La Ni.

tom_tat: He was from the Western Regions, came to Chan Dan, and took on the responsibility of translating the scriptures. He thoroughly understood the Yoga dharma, and had divine power...
noi_dung: 69. PurnasomaHe was from the Western Regions, came to Chan Dan, and took on the responsibility of translating the scriptures. He thoroughly understood the Yogācāra dharma and had strange divine powers. During the reign of Emperor Van Tong, the reign of Khai Thanh (836-840), he brought the Sanskrit scriptures to Central Earth, and together with the monk Vajra All Earth, etc., translated four volumes of Da La Ni Tap and one volume of Thu Da Thien Tu Thuyet of Ton Thang Sutra. At that time, Tri Huyen, the national teacher Ngo Dat, respected Man Nguyet as his teacher.

tom_tat: In addition, from the first to the tenth century, there were many translators from Thien Truc, Dai Nhuc Chi, Tay Vuc, etc. to Truong An,...
noi_dung:
Appendix: Other Translators & ReferencesIn addition, from the first to the tenth century, there were many translators from Thien Truc, Dai Nhuc Chi, Tay Vuc, etc. to Chang'an, Luoyang, Kien Nghiep, etc. translating the classics as follows:

Mr. An Phap Kham, a native of An Xi country, in Luoyang from 281 to 306, translated the Sutra of the Infinite Transformation of the Divine Path, the Sutra of Manjushri Showing Treasures, the Sutra of Ajatasatru King, and the story of King Asoka.

Venerable Chi Phap Do, a native of Dai Nhuc Chi country, translated the Dong Tu Sutra, etc. in Luoyang in the year 301.

Venerable Nha La Nghiem, from Thien Truc, translated the Sutra in Luoyang around the year 316.

Mr. Chi Dao Can, a native of Dai Nhuc Chi country, came to Kien Nghiep in 335, translating the Phuong Dang Sutra, Phap Hoa, etc.

Mr. Truc Dam Vo Lan (Dharmaranya, translated as Phap Chanh), a native of Thien Truc country, translated the sutras at Kien Nghiep from 381 to 395.

Venerable Chi Thi Lon, a native of Dai Nhu Chi country, translated two volumes of the Illusory Samadhi Sutra, Upper Golden Light Sutra, and two volumes of Shurangama Sutra in the Former Liang Dynasty, year 373.

Kumarabodhi, translated as Dong Giac, a native of Thien Truc country, translated the sutras at Chang'an from 369 to 371. Dharmapriya, translated as Phap Ai, translated the sutras at Chang'an in 382.

Kalodaka, translated as Thoi Thuy, a native of Thien Truc country, translated the sutra at Kien Nghiep in the year 392.

Mr. Jiang Daohe, a native of Jiangju, translated the sutra at Jianye in 396.

Sangha Da (Sanghata, translated as Nhieu Thien) was a native of Tay Vuc, translating sutras in Beijing from 402 to 412.

Truc Nan De (Nandi, translated as Van Hy), a Thien Truc layperson, translated the sutra at Kien Nghiep in 419.

Venerable Chi Da Mat (Gitamita, translated as Ca Huu) from the Western Regions, translated the sutra at Kien Nghiep in the year 420.

Gunaila, a native of the Western Regions, came to Jingzhou to translate scriptures in 462.

Sanghavarman, a native of the Lion country, translated the sutra at Kien Nghiep in 478.

Mr. Vat De De San Ngu (translated as Pure Lotus Flower) is from Quy Tu country. Wukong from Thien Truc passed through Quy Tu country, met Venerable De De San at Lien Hoa Pagoda, and asked him to translate the Ten Powers Sutra.

Mr. Bat Nha is from Ke Tan country. In 795, he translated ten volumes of the last part of the Avatamsaka Sutra, Samantabhadra's Prayer, which he brought from O Tra to Dong Do.

Mr. Vo Neng Thang was from A Chat Dat Tan in Thien Truc, and also translated the classics at the end of the Tang Dynasty.

According to the book Khai Nguyen Thich Giao Luc Tai, from the Later Han Dynasty to the Tang Dynasty, the reign of Khai Nguyen, the translators, including monks and lay people, were about 171, translating 2,278 volumes and 7,046 volumes of sutras. These classics include some true and false, some are lost. According to the book Khai Nguyen Thich Giao Luc Tai, the true and extant sutras are 968 sets and 4,507 volumes. During the Song Dynasty, more than five hundred volumes were translated. In total, there are about five thousand volumes of dharma scriptures. From 67 to 789 was the time when the vast majority of the sutras were translated. Before and after that time, they are all extra parts.
